summary: Pilloni constructs p-adic families of Siegel modular forms of genus two in all degrees of coherent cohomology, for the forms of weight (k, 2) whose archimedean component is a non-degenerate limit of discrete series and which live in H⁰ and H¹ of Ω^(k,2)(−D) on Siegel threefolds. Theorem 1.1 (higher Hida theory): there is a perfect complex M of Λ-modules, Λ = Z_p⟦Z_p^×⟧, of amplitude [0, 1], whose specialisation at every k ≥ 0 is the U-ordinary part of the cohomology at Klingen level over Q_p, whose H⁰ with Q_p/Z_p coefficients is the T-ordinary part at spherical level for k > p + 1, and which carries the prime-to-p Hecke action. Theorem 1.2 (= Theorem 15.2.1): for a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal m, M_m has trivial Euler characteristic; the proof uses Arthur's classification for GSp₄. The method: integral Hecke operators T and U at p through paramodular and Klingen correspondences, with trace maps from Grothendieck–Serre duality (§§4, 7, 10); a second Hasse invariant and the p-rank ≥ 1 locus, whose image in the minimal compactification is covered by two affines (§6; the covering is proved in §14.8, p. 101); Λ-adic sheaves 𝔉^κ on the Klingen tower, built from the Hodge–Tate reduction of ω_{H∞} (§9); and higher Coleman theory, meaning overconvergent cohomology with U compact, finite-slope families and classicality of small-slope classes (Theorems 14.7.1 and 14.8.1), which gives control over Q_p in all weights. The atlas plans the Siegel threefold at hyperspecial level (PELModuli, ShimuraCompactifications, AutomorphicBundles, ShimuraData), adic and formal models, Banach modules and compact operators, and group-independent ordinary projectors and eigenvariety gluing (PadicFamilies L0a, L2a), with Hida and Coleman families only for modular curves and totally real fields, in a single degree (L0, L2, L5). It plans no Hecke operators at p on coherent cohomology in all degrees, no parahoric-level integral models, no second Hasse invariant, no Λ-adic interpolation of automorphic sheaves, and no higher Hida or higher Coleman theory. Routes: a Part II of PadicFamilies for the paper's core (HigherHidaAndColemanTheory, 271 items); additions to proposals made by other extractions, joined under the same ids: SiegelModularFormsModPn and GSp4NonregularModularityLifting (PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20), IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes (PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18 and -20), ShimuraVarietiesHondaTatePartII and ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary; and source routes to nineteen existing roadmaps, chiefly AdicSpacesPartII, HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups, PadicFamilies L0a and L2a, and AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry. 175 mistakes are recorded, none previously known. Among them: Theorem 5.1.7.1(5) has the wrong sign on the cyclotomic exponent; Theorem 6.1.5.1(2) states the boundary ideals under a refinement the wrong way round; Lemma 11.1.1.4 fails at n = 0; the perfectness of M (Theorem 11.3.1(2)) has no written proof; the prime-to-p Hecke operators are not shown to commute in D(Λ); and the proof of Theorem 15.2.1 specialises at a single weight, where each of the p − 1 components of weight space needs one.

items.name: Siegel threefold X_K over Z_p and the boundary divisor D
items.statement: Fix a prime p (§6.1). Let K = ∏_ℓ K_ℓ ⊂ GSp4(A_f) be a neat compact open subgroup with K_p = GSp4(Z_p). The introduction omits neatness, but it is the standing assumption of §5.2.1 (p. 23) and §6.1.1 (p. 26). Y_K = Y_{K,Z_(p)} ×_{Z_(p)} Z_p is the moduli space of triples (G, λ, ψ) up to prime-to-p quasi-isogeny. Here G is an abelian surface, λ: G → G^t is a Z_(p)^×-multiple of a polarization of degree prime to p, and ψ is a K^p-level structure (§6.1.1); Y_K is smooth over Z_p (Prop. 6.1.4.1). X_K → Spec Z_p denotes a toroidal compactification X_{K,Σ} of Y_K for a Γ-admissible good polyhedral cone decomposition Σ (§6.1.5, Theorem 6.1.5.1). It is normal and lci over Z_p. The cohomology of the automorphic bundles does not depend on Σ (§6.2.1, p. 30). Over C, Siegel threefolds are finite unions of arithmetic quotients of the three-dimensional Siegel upper half space; they are moduli spaces of abelian surfaces with polarization and level structure, and they have canonical models over number fields. X_K carries the universal semi-abelian scheme G. D is the boundary, i.e. the reduced complement of Y_K in X_K, which is a relative Cartier divisor; D is defined in the same way in X_{Kli(p)K} (the same letter is used for both). F(−D) = F ⊗ O(−D).
items.note: The good-level Siegel threefold over Z_p, its toroidal compactification with universal semi-abelian scheme, neat level, the boundary divisor D and the twist F(−D) = F ⊗ O(−D) on X_K are all planned. The mapping follows PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20: siegel-threefold-Y-K went to PELModuli M1/M2/M5, toroidal-compactification-hodge-bundle to ShimuraCompactifications C5/C3. The complex description (arithmetic quotients of the Siegel space) is A5, and the canonical model is V5. The same notation D on X_{Kli(p)K} depends on the Klingen-level model, which is missing (klingen-level-cover-XKli). Neither library has Siegel moduli or compactifications.

items.name: Klingen parahoric level X_{Kli(p)K} → X_K
items.statement: Kli(p) ⊂ K_p = GSp4(Z_p) is the Klingen parahoric subgroup: the elements whose reduction mod p lies in the Klingen parabolic P_Kli(F_p), the stabilizer of the line ⟨e1⟩ (§5.1.4, p. 21). Y_{Kli(p)K} → Y_K is the moduli space of subgroups H ⊂ G[p] of order p (§6.1.2). Y_{Kli(p)K} is regular, flat and lci over Z_p (Prop. 6.1.4.1). Over Y_{Kli(p)K} there is a chain of isogenies G → G/H → G/H^⊥ → G whose composite is multiplication by p; H^⊥ is the orthogonal of H for the Weil pairing on G[p]. X_{Kli(p)K} is the toroidal compactification of Y_{Kli(p)K} for a Γ_{Kli(p)}-admissible good polyhedral cone decomposition Σ' refining the Σ of X_K. With this choice p1 extends to a proper map p1: X_{Kli(p)K} → X_K (Theorem 6.1.5.1(3)). The introduction calls p1 a covering that parametrizes a subgroup of order p of the semi-abelian scheme, at least where that scheme is abelian. p1 is not finite: it is not quasi-finite over the p-rank-0 locus of the special fibre, because p-rank-0 abelian surfaces can have infinitely many subgroups of order p (§7.1, p. 38).
items.note: The group Kli(p) is planned: it is the parahoric fixing a line of F_p^4, so ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.3 covers it ('For a facet construct the smooth affine O_E-group scheme ...'), as in PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20/parahoric-subgroups-P-Pi-I. No layer plans the integral model of level Kli(p)K^p over Z_p, its moduli interpretation by a subgroup of order p, or its toroidal compactification. PELModuli:M2 requires 'no nontrivial level at p'. M4 only normalizes at higher p-level and says 'Do not assert smoothness, a fine moduli interpretation, or a universal abelian scheme on such a normalization without a separate theorem'. C5 keeps 'the good-prime assumptions'. The SiegelModularFormsModPn brief (PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20, proposed, not in the atlas) records the same gap: 'PELModuli M2 has no p-level, M4 no moduli interpretation'. The source is Pilloni §6 (local models, pp. 26–37).

items.name: Coherent realization of limits of discrete series (Harris)
items.statement: Automorphic forms for GSp4/Q whose component at infinity has singular Harish-Chandra parameter and is a non-degenerate limit of discrete series can be realized in the coherent cohomology of an appropriate automorphic vector bundle over a Siegel threefold. Those with Hodge–Tate weights (k+1,k+1,0,0) realize in H^0 and H^1 of Ω^{(k,2)}.
items.note: No atlas layer plans Harris's realization of limits of discrete series in coherent cohomology. AF.1 plans only (g,K)-cohomology. In PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20 the same input (thm-5-2-harris-diagram, ext-harris-limit-ds-lie-algebra-cohomology) is missing; it was routed to the IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes Part II (layer 6, 'Harris's comparison') and to an AF source route. External input: [28] M. Harris, Automorphic forms and the cohomology of vector bundles on Shimura varieties, in Automorphic forms, Shimura varieties and L-functions, vol. 1, Academic Press, 283–415

items.name: Integral correspondences U1, U2, T1, T2 and their cohomological action
items.statement: The cocharacter of the torus of GSp4 underlying the double coset of diag(p^2,p,p,1) is not minuscule, so the moduli problem for U and T involves the p^2-torsion. Using the factorization diag(p^2,p,p,1) = diag(p,p,p,1)·diag(p,1,1,1) (in GL4(Q_p)), the correspondence underlying U (resp. T) is factored into two correspondences U1 and U2 (resp. T1 and T2) through paramodular level. Their moduli problems are defined integrally and are described locally by local models. These correspondences are not finite flat over the Siegel threefold. The trace maps in cohomology are defined using Grothendieck–Serre duality in coherent cohomology, subject to a normalization.
items.note: Missing. No layer plans local models for GSp4 at Klingen or paramodular level; PerfectoidShimuraVarieties:S2's local models serve Scholze's perfectoid tower. Trace maps along correspondences that are not finite flat, obtained from Grothendieck–Serre duality, are not planned either. Coherent duality is planned only for curves (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3). CG20 serre-duality-automorphic-bundles is missing. CG18 gave its general-dimension duality a source route to AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:A0-extension. The correspondence formalism of EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.8 ('c₂* K→c₁^!K') is étale, not coherent. Pilloni §4 ('Correspondences and coherent cohomology', pp. 15–19) and §§7, 10 are the source.

items.name: Ordinary parts (U-ord, T-ord)
items.statement: For a complex or module on which U (resp. T) acts, the exponent U−ord (resp. T−ord) denotes the ordinary part for the action of U (resp. T). This is the direct factor cut out by the ordinary projector of §2 (e = lim_N U^{N!}), defined when the action is locally finite.
items.note: The ordinary part is planned in the settings where Theorem 1.1 uses it. There the projector e = lim U^{N!} acts on perfect Z_p-complexes (RΓ of a proper scheme, then ⊗Q_p) and on H^0(X_K, Ω(−D)⊗Q_p/Z_p), a union of finite U-stable pieces. The precedents are PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/lemma-7-3 (L0a + IHG.2) and PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20/ordinary-idempotent-and-ordinary-part (L0a, via the union argument for K/O). Three things are not covered: the operators U and T themselves (hecke-operator-U-klingen, hecke-operator-T-spherical); the locally finite generality of §2 used to define M (def-2-1-1-locally-finite-action and following); and, in Mathlib, anything beyond the finite Fitting decomposition LinearMap.eventually_isCompl_ker_pow_range_pow.

items.name: Theorem 1.1 (main theorem): existence of the perfect complex M
items.statement: There is a perfect complex M of Λ-modules of amplitude [0,1] satisfying points 1–3 of Theorem 1.1. In the body, M = f RΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_{Kli(p)K}, 𝔉^κ ⊗ ω^2(−D)), with ω^2 = Ω^(0,2) (Theorem 11.3.1(2)). For every k ∈ Z, M ⊗^L_{Λ,k} Z_p is a perfect complex of Z_p-modules concentrated in degrees 0 and 1. For every k ∈ Z≥0, point 1 gives (M ⊗^L_{Λ,k} Z_p) ⊗^L_{Z_p} Q_p ≅ RΓ(X_{Kli(p)K}, Ω^(k,2)(−D) ⊗^L_{Z_p} Q_p)^{U−ord}, so M ⊗^L_{Λ,k} Z_p is an integral structure of this complex.
items.note: Main theorem (Theorem 11.3.1 and Part III). No layer plans p-adic families in higher coherent cohomology. It depends on the missing F^κ, U and §2 projector items.

items.name: Theorem 1.1(1): control theorem over Q_p in all weights k ≥ 0
items.statement: For all k ∈ Z≥0 there is a canonical quasi-isomorphism M ⊗^L_{Λ,k} Q_p ≅ RΓ(X_{Kli(p)K}, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D) ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p)^{U−ord}, where U−ord means the ordinary part for the action of U.
items.note: Proved in Part III through M†, small-slope classicality and a dimension argument (see M-dagger-quasi-isomorphism-all-weights). No layer plans it.

items.name: Theorem 1.1(2): integral control of H^0 with Q_p/Z_p coefficients for k > p+1
items.statement: For all k ∈ Z with k > p+1 there is a canonical isomorphism H^0(M ⊗^L_{Λ,k} Q_p/Z_p) ≅ H^0(X_K, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D) ⊗ Q_p/Z_p)^{T−ord}, where T−ord means the ordinary part for the action of T.
items.note: Integral control for k > p+1 (§11, Theorem 11.2.1). It needs the T-operator (missing) and integral coherent cohomology with Q_p/Z_p coefficients (the proposed IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes, not in the atlas).

items.name: Theorem 1.1(3): prime-to-p Hecke action on M
items.statement: The perfect complex M carries an action of the prime-to-pN spherical Hecke algebra H^{Np} = ⊗'_{ℓ∤Np} H_ℓ, where H_ℓ = Z[T_{ℓ,0}, T_{ℓ,0}^{−1}, T_{ℓ,1}, T_{ℓ,2}] (§5.1.3). In the body, H_ℓ is constructed for ℓ ≠ p with K_ℓ = GSp4(Z_ℓ) (Prop. 15.1.1), with the normalizations T_{ℓ,2} = ℓ^{−3}T'_{ℓ,2} and T_{ℓ,i} = ℓ^{−6}T'_{ℓ,i} for i = 0,1. Theorem 1.1(3) asserts that the isomorphisms of points 1 and 2 are equivariant for this action.
items.note: Prime-to-p Hecke action on M and on the control isomorphisms. The prime-to-p operators T_γ on integral coherent cohomology in all degrees are missing in every layer (CG18/CG20 coherent-hecke-operator-T-gamma and hecke-operators-T-x-i, routed to the proposed IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes, layer 3). Their action on M adds the compatibility with F^κ and U.

items.name: Remark 1.1: p-stabilization is an isomorphism on ordinary H^0 for k > p+1
items.statement: For any k ∈ Z with k > p+1, the natural map (a p-stabilization map) H^0(X_K, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D) ⊗ Q_p)^{T−ord} → H^0(X_{Kli(p)K}, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D) ⊗ Q_p)^{U−ord} is an isomorphism. This is the compatibility between points 1 and 2 of Theorem 1.1.
items.note: The p-stabilization H^0(X_K)^{T-ord} → H^0(X_{Kli(p)K})^{U-ord} is an isomorphism for k > p+1. This needs the missing T, U, Klingen model and their comparison.

items.name: The formal schemes X_{Kli(p)K}, X^{≥1}_{Kli(p)K}, X^{≥2}_{Kli(p)K}, X^{≥1}_K
items.statement: 𝔛_{Kli(p)K} is the p-adic formal completion of the Z_p-scheme X_{Kli(p)K}. 𝔛^{≥1}_{Kli(p)K} ⊂ 𝔛_{Kli(p)K} is the open formal subscheme where the p-rank of the semi-abelian scheme is at least 1 and the universal subgroup H_1 of order p is multiplicative. In the body it is the moduli, over 𝔛^{≥1}_K, of subgroups H_1 ⊂ G[p] that are étale-locally isomorphic to μ_p (§9.1.1, §9.2). Mod p it is a strict open subscheme of X_{Kli(p),1} ×_{X_1} X_1^{≥1} (Remark 9.1.1.1). It strictly contains the ordinary locus 𝔛^{≥2}_{Kli(p)K}, where the p-rank is 2. 𝔛^{≥1}_K ⊂ 𝔛_K is the open formal subscheme where the multiplicative rank of G is at least 1 (p-rank ≥ 1). Its complement is the p-rank-0 (supersingular) locus.
items.note: p-adic formal completion is AdicSpacesPartII:F0 ('Completion along a closed subscheme is functorial'). The p-rank stratification of the Siegel threefold mod p, the ordinary locus X^{≥2}, and the Klingen-level locus where the universal subgroup is multiplicative are planned nowhere. CG20 notes that 'the p-rank stratification of the Siegel 3-fold mod p' is planned nowhere, and its proposed SiegelModularFormsModPn layer 2 takes the strata S = V(h) ⊃ Z. The Hasse neighbourhoods in HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T3 and ShimuraCompactifications:C6 are Hilbert.

items.name: Supersingular isogenies of type T factor through Frobenius; T is topologically nilpotent off X^{≥1}_K
items.statement: Heuristic (§1, p. 4). Let λ: A → A' be an isogeny of 'type' T between abelian surfaces over a discrete valuation ring O_K with maximal ideal m_K. If A and A' have supersingular reduction, the reduction of λ factors through the Frobenius of A, so dλ: ω_{A'} → ω_A vanishes modulo m_K. The introduction uses this to explain why, over the complement of 𝔛^{≥1}_K (the supersingular locus), T acts topologically nilpotently on Ω^(k,2) for k large enough. The precise statements proved in the body are two. First, if A is an abelian surface of p-rank 0 over a field of characteristic p and L ⊂ A[p] is a subgroup scheme of order p^3, then Ker(F) ⊂ L, so the isogeny with kernel L factors through Frobenius (Lemma 7.4.2.6). Second, there is a constant C, independent of the prime-to-p level K^p, such that for all k ≥ C and all r ≥ p^2 + p the cohomological correspondence T1: p2^*Ω^(k,r)|_{X^{=0}_{par,1}} → p1^!Ω^(k,r)|_{X_1^{=0}} vanishes, where X_1^{=0} is the p-rank-0 locus of the special fibre (Proposition 7.4.2.2).
items.note: A statement about isogenies of type T between supersingular abelian surfaces, and the topological nilpotence of T off X^{≥1}_K (§§7–8). No layer plans it.

items.name: Overconvergent complex M†, compactness of U and finite slope families
items.statement: Over Q_p, M† is obtained by taking the ordinary part for U of an overconvergent cohomology of the analytic fibre 𝒳^{≥1}_{Kli(p)K} of X^{≥1}_{Kli(p)K}, with values in a huge Banach sheaf. U is compact on this cohomology, and a theory of finite slope families is developed (Remark 1.2; Part III).
items.note: Part III (§§12–13). The compact-operator and Fredholm machinery is planned (LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L4, PadicFamilies:L2a), and overconvergent coefficient sheaves are planned for Hilbert varieties and Siegel anticanonical domains (OverconvergentAutomorphicForms O1–O8). Overconvergent higher coherent cohomology on the Klingen p-rank ≥ 1 locus, with a compact U, is planned nowhere.

items.name: M† → M ⊗ Q_p is injective on H^0 and surjective on H^1
items.statement: By construction there is a map M† → M ⊗^L_{Z_p} Q_p, which is injective on H^0 and surjective on H^1. This is a 'degeneration' of the classical statement that all ordinary p-adic modular forms are overconvergent.
items.note: Depends on the missing M† and M. No layer plans it.

items.name: Ordinary classicality: M† ⊗^L_{Λ,k} Q_p ≅ RΓ(X_{Kli(p)K}, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D) ⊗^L Q_p)^{U−ord}
items.statement: In the ordinary case, for all k ≥ 0: M† ⊗^L_{Λ,k} Q_p = RΓ(X_{Kli(p)K}, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D) ⊗^L_{Z_p} Q_p)^{U−ord}.
items.note: Ordinary case of small-slope classicality (§14). No layer plans it.

items.name: M† → M ⊗ Q_p is a quasi-isomorphism in all weights k ≥ 0
items.statement: Three inputs are combined: the integral control theorem for k ≫ 0, the injectivity (H^0) and surjectivity (H^1) of M† → M ⊗^L_{Z_p} Q_p, and ordinary classicality. Together they show that M† → M ⊗^L_{Z_p} Q_p is a quasi-isomorphism at weights k ≫ 0, and then, by an elementary dimension argument, at all weights k ≥ 0.
items.note: Assembles the integral control theorem, the H^0/H^1 comparison and ordinary classicality with a dimension argument. No layer plans it.

items.name: Hida's control theorem for ordinary p-adic Siegel cusp forms (degree 0, all weights)
items.statement: Let Λ2 be the two-dimensional Iwasawa algebra, with specialization morphisms (k,r): Λ2 → Z_p for (k,r) ∈ Z≥0 × Z. Let ord' denote the ordinary part for the usual ordinary idempotent attached to diag(p^3,p^2,p,1) ∈ GSp4(Q_p), and let X^{≥2}_{Kli(p)K} be the ordinary locus in X^{≥1}_{Kli(p)K}. Then there is a finite free Λ2-module M' such that for all (k,r) ∈ Z≥0 × Z, M' ⊗_{Λ2,(k,r)} Z_p = H^0(X^{≥2}_{Kli(p)K}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D))^{ord'}.
items.note: No layer plans Hida theory for GSp4. PadicFamilies L0 covers modular forms and L5 totally real fields. OverconvergentAutomorphicForms:O7 is Hilbert and says 'Hida's ordinary-projector/control theorems require additional hypotheses and are not claimed'. AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L4 and AutomorphicCongruences:L1 are unitary. The two-variable Iwasawa algebra Λ2 itself is planned (Tau Ceti ProfiniteProPGroups layer 9, PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1). External input: [34] H. Hida, Control theorems for coherent sheaves on Shimura varieties of PEL type, J. Inst. Math. Jussieu 1 (2002); [3] F. Andreatta, A. Iovita, V. Pilloni, p-adic families of Siegel modular cuspforms, Ann. of Math. 181 (2015); using [62] V. Pilloni, Prolongement analytique sur les variétés de Siegel, Duke Math. J. 157 (2011)

items.name: Classicality of ordinary p-adic Siegel forms of weight (k,r), r ≥ 4
items.statement: For all (k,r) ∈ Z≥0 × Z≥4, H^0(X^{≥2}_{Kli(p)K}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D))^{ord'} is a subspace of the space of classical modular forms of Iwahori level at p. The control theorem holds for weights with r ≥ 4. After localization it can sometimes be improved to r ≥ 3, which is exactly the condition under which the corresponding automorphic forms are discrete series at infinity. In singular weight (k,2) no such classicality is expected: Galois representations attached to eigenforms in M' ⊗_{Λ2,(k,2)} Z_p may fail to be de Rham at p.
items.note: No layer plans classicality of ordinary p-adic Siegel forms, which uses Pilloni, Duke 2011 (analytic continuation). The singular-weight remarks (possible failure of the de Rham property) are expectations. External input: [34] H. Hida (2002); [3] Andreatta–Iovita–Pilloni (2015); [62] Pilloni (2011)

items.name: Injective comparison H^0(M ⊗^L_{Λ,k} Z_p) → M' ⊗_{Λ2,(k,2)} Z_p
items.statement: Eigenforms in H^0(M ⊗^L_{Λ,k} Z_p) correspond to classical automorphic forms. There is a natural injective map H^0(M ⊗^L_{Λ,k} Z_p) → M' ⊗_{Λ2,(k,2)} Z_p. Expected but not proved: the subspace of M' ⊗_{Λ2,(k,2)} Z_p spanned by eigenforms with de Rham associated Galois representations is 'generated' by the image of this map, and the classical eigenforms in M' ⊗_{Λ2,(k,2)} Z_p are exactly those whose associated Galois representation is de Rham.
items.note: Needs M and Hida's module M' (ext-hida-control-ordinary-p-adic-siegel-forms), both missing. The 'expected' statements are unproved and must be recorded as expectations.

items.name: de Rham property of Galois representations of classical forms (Mok)
items.statement: For eigenforms in H^0(M ⊗^L_{Λ,k} Z_p), which correspond to classical automorphic forms, one often knows that the associated Galois representation is de Rham.
items.note: Mok, Prop. 4.16 (GSp4 Galois representations are de Rham) is missing, like PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20/ext-mok-galois-reps-for-GSp4. AG2.6 plans de Rham and crystalline properties only for its polarized unitary systems ('For the polarized systems, apply the actual crystalline/semistable/log-crystalline comparison'). External input: [54] C.-P. Mok, Galois representations attached to automorphic forms on GL(2) over CM fields, Compositio Math. 150 (2014), Prop. 4.16

items.name: Modularity conjecture for abelian surfaces over Q
items.statement: Conjecture: for every simple abelian surface A over Q there exists a cuspidal automorphic form π on GSp4/Q such that the spin L-function of π coincides with the L-function of H^1(A). This is known when End(A) ≠ Z ([85], [42]); [8] gives a precise conjecture when End(A) = Z. The component at infinity of such a π should be a limit of discrete series, and π should realize in the cuspidal coherent cohomology of Ω^{(0,2)}.
items.note: The conjecture is registered as an endpoint with conjectural status, following PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20/conj-automorphy-of-motives (planned at ML.5/ML.0). The known cases End(A) ≠ Z (Yoshida-type lifts [85]; Kisin [42] for GL2-type modularity) are not planned as proofs in any layer, and nor are the Brumer–Kramer paramodular refinement [8] or the claim that such π realize in coherent cohomology of Ω^{(0,2)} (see ext-harris-coherent-realization). External input: [8] A. Brumer and K. Kramer, Paramodular abelian varieties of odd conductor, Trans. AMS 366 (2014); [85] H. Yoshida, Invent. Math. 60 (1980); [42] M. Kisin, Invent. Math. 178 (2009)

items.name: Modularity lifting to ordinary p-adic modular forms (Pilloni 2012)
items.statement: Under many technical assumptions, an abelian surface whose associated p-adic Galois representation is residually modular arises from a p-adic modular form. The Taylor–Wiles system lets Galois deformation rings act on the module H^0(X^{≥2}_{Kli(p)K}, Ω^{(0,2)}(−D))^{ord'} of ordinary p-adic modular forms. Congruences are unobstructed for ordinary p-adic modular forms. They are obstructed for classical forms of weight (0,2) because H^1 does not vanish.
items.note: Cited only as motivation (Crelle 2012). No layer plans Taylor–Wiles patching for ordinary p-adic Siegel forms of weight (0,2) = CG (2,2). Its Hida-theory input is ext-hida-control-ordinary-p-adic-siegel-forms (missing). External input: [61] V. Pilloni, Modularité, formes de Siegel et surfaces abéliennes, J. reine angew. Math. 666 (2012), 35–82

items.name: Calegari–Geraghty conditional modularity lifting in weight (0,2)
items.statement: Calegari and Geraghty modify the Taylor–Wiles method so that it applies in obstructed situations. They prove a conditional modularity lifting theorem: under technical conditions, an abelian surface whose associated p-adic Galois representation is residually modular arises from a weight (0,2) modular form. The Galois deformation ring acts on a localization of H^0(X_K, Ω^{(0,2)}(−D) ⊗ Q_p/Z_p). The theorem requires the localized cohomology to vanish in degrees ≥ 2, and this vanishing is not known.
items.note: This is PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20's Theorem 9.1/1.1 (missing, routed to the proposed GSp4NonregularModularityLifting) with CG18's method. The balanced-module patching engine is planned at DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.5. The required vanishing of localized H^{≥2} is CG20 Assumption 7.7 (open in weight (2,2)). External input: [11] F. Calegari and D. Geraghty, Modularity lifting beyond the Taylor–Wiles method, Invent. Math. 211 (2018), 297–433; [12] F. Calegari and D. Geraghty, Modularity lifting for non-regular symplectic representations (preprint; Duke Math. J. 169 (2020))

items.name: p-divisible classes of H^0(M ⊗^L_{Λ,0} Q_p/Z_p) are classical
items.statement: As a replacement for H^0(X_K, Ω^{(0,2)}(−D) ⊗ Q_p/Z_p) in the Calegari–Geraghty method, the paper proposes H^0(M ⊗^L Q_p/Z_p) specialized at the weight corresponding to Ω^{(0,2)}, i.e. k = 0 (printed 'Λ,2'). Its p-divisible classes come from cohomology classes in H^0(X_{Kli(p)K}, Ω^{(0,2)}(−D)), and hence from classical automorphic forms.
items.note: Needs M and the U-ordinary classicality of H^0 in weight (0,2). The printed subscript 'Λ,2' on p. 6 means the specialization k = 0 for Ω^{(0,2)}; HAL v3 prints the same (see clusterNotes). No layer plans it.

items.name: Standing hypothesis of §2 on the coefficient ring R
items.statement: Throughout §2, R is a complete local noetherian ring with maximal ideal m_R such that R/m_R is a finite field.
items.note: The hypothesis is expressed by Mathlib predicates: [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) R] [Finite (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R)]. Mathlib/RingTheory/AdicCompletion/LocalRing.lean:127 also provides the completion instance for Noetherian local rings. DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.1 plans the coefficient categories built on this.

items.name: The category Mod^comp(R) of m_R-adically separated complete modules
items.statement: Mod(R) is the abelian category of R-modules. Mod^comp(R) is its full subcategory of m_R-adically separated and complete R-modules, and it is not abelian in general. A complex of objects of Mod^comp(R) is exact if its image in Mod(R) is exact. Every arrow M → N in Mod^comp(R) has a kernel in Mod^comp(R), namely its kernel in Mod(R), which is an object of Mod^comp(R).
items.note: The objects are m_R-adically separated and complete modules, which is Mathlib's IsAdicComplete (= IsHausdorff + IsPrecomplete); the full subcategory is a wrapper. Not in the libraries: the stated fact that the kernel of a map between complete separated modules is again complete and separated. It holds because m_R is finitely generated: derived-complete modules are closed under kernels, and a separated derived-complete module is adically complete. Derived completeness is planned in DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1. The kernel lemma should join the §2 source route (P7).

items.name: Definition 2.1.1: locally finite action
items.statement: Let M be an object of Mod^comp(R) and T ∈ End_R(M). The action of T on M is locally finite if for all n ∈ N and all v ∈ M/m_R^n M, the elements {T^k v}_{k∈N} generate a finite R/m_R^n-submodule of M/m_R^n M. Equivalently, for all n ∈ N, M/m_R^n M can be written as an inductive limit of finite T-stable R-modules.
items.note: The notion of a locally finite action is not defined in any layer or library. L0a gap (see clusterNotes): L0a plans the U^(n!) projector only for finite modules, inverse limits of finite discrete quotients and 'finite perfect/cohomological complexes'. Pilloni needs locally finite actions on m_R-adically complete, non-finite modules, where M/m^n M is only a union of finite T-stable pieces.

items.name: Lemma 2.1.1(1): local finiteness is stable under extensions
items.statement: Let 0 → M1 → M2 → M3 → 0 be an exact sequence in Mod^comp(R), and let T be an R-linear endomorphism acting equivariantly on M1, M2 and M3. If the action of T is locally finite on M3 and on M1, then it is locally finite on M2.
items.note: Needs Definition 2.1.1, which is missing. L0a gap (see clusterNotes).

items.name: Lemma 2.1.1(2): local finiteness passes to quotients
items.statement: Let 0 → M1 → M2 → M3 → 0 be an exact sequence in Mod^comp(R), and let T be an R-linear endomorphism acting equivariantly on M1, M2 and M3. If the action of T is locally finite on M2, then it is locally finite on M3.
items.note: Needs Definition 2.1.1, which is missing. L0a gap (see clusterNotes).

items.name: Lemma 2.1.1(3): local finiteness passes to submodules when m_R^n kills M2
items.statement: Let 0 → M1 → M2 → M3 → 0 be an exact sequence in Mod^comp(R), and let T be an R-linear endomorphism acting equivariantly on M1, M2 and M3. If there exists n ∈ N with m_R^n M2 = 0 and T is locally finite on M2, then T is locally finite on M1.
items.note: Needs Definition 2.1.1, which is missing. L0a gap (see clusterNotes).

items.name: Remark 2.1.1: local finiteness does not pass to kernels in general
items.statement: The assumption m_R^n M2 = 0 in Lemma 2.1.1(3) is necessary. Take R = Z_p, M2 = ∏_{i∈Z≥0} Z_p, M3 = ∏_{i∈Z≥0} Z/p^{i(i+1)/2}Z, M1 ≃ ∏_{i∈Z≥0} Z_p the kernel of the natural map M2 → M3, and T the endomorphism of M2 sending (a_i)_{i≥0} to (0, pa_0, p^2a_1, ..., p^i a_{i−1}, ...). Then T is locally finite on M2, T(M1) ⊂ M1, and T is not locally finite on M1.
items.note: The counterexample should be an acceptance test of the locally finite projector. L0a's current failure test (R = C, U = 2) targets a different hypothesis. L0a gap (see clusterNotes).

items.name: Lemma 2.1.2: local finiteness can be checked modulo m_R
items.statement: Let M be an object of Mod^comp(R) and T an endomorphism of M. The action of T on M is locally finite if and only if it is locally finite on M/m_R M.
items.note: Needs Definition 2.1.1, which is missing. L0a gap (see clusterNotes).

items.name: Lemma 2.1.3: the ordinary projector e = lim T^{N!}
items.statement: Assume that T acts locally finitely on an object M of Mod^comp(R). Then there is a unique ordinary projector e ∈ End_R(M) such that: (1) for all v ∈ M, ev = lim_{N→∞} T^{N!} v, the limit being taken in the m_R-adic topology; (2) e and T commute, and there is a T-stable decomposition M = eM ⊕ (1−e)M, with T bijective on eM and topologically nilpotent on (1−e)M.
items.note: The finite core that the proof reduces to ('We reduce to the situation where M is a finite R/m_R^n-module') is L0a's finite projector; Mathlib has only the Fitting decomposition LinearMap.eventually_isCompl_ker_pow_range_pow (Mathlib/RingTheory/Artinian/Module.lean:317), and AUDIT-15 rates L0a 'partly built'. The statement for locally finite actions is not planned. L0a gap (see clusterNotes).

items.name: Lemma 2.1.4(1): equivariant maps respect the ordinary decomposition
items.statement: Let f: M1 → M2 be a morphism in Mod^comp(R). Let T be an R-linear endomorphism acting equivariantly on M1 and M2, with locally finite action on both, and let e denote the ordinary projector of T on M1 and on M2. Then f(eM1) ⊂ eM2 and f((1−e)M1) ⊂ (1−e)M2. Equivalently, f commutes with e and decomposes as the direct sum of ef and (1−e)f.
items.note: L0a plans 'naturality for maps commuting with U' only for finite modules and profinite limits. L0a gap (see clusterNotes).

items.name: Lemma 2.1.4(2): ordinary part of a cokernel
items.statement: In the situation of Lemma 2.1.4, assume that M3 = coker f is an object of Mod^comp(R). Then coker(eM1 → eM2) = eM3, where e on M3 is the ordinary projector of the induced action of T.
items.note: L0a plans 'exactness first for U-equivariant exact sequences of finite modules, then for inverse-limit sequences', not for locally finite actions on complete modules. L0a gap (see clusterNotes).

items.name: Lemma 2.1.4(3): ordinary part of a kernel
items.statement: In the situation of Lemma 2.1.4, let M0 = ker f and assume that T is locally finite on M0. Then ker(eM1 → eM2) = eM0.
items.note: The same gap as Lemma 2.1.4(2). The hypothesis that T is locally finite on ker f is needed because of Remark 2.1.1. L0a gap (see clusterNotes).

items.name: Categories of complexes C^comp(R), C^flat(R), C^perf(R) and K^perf(R)
items.statement: C^comp(R) is the category of bounded complexes of m_R-adically complete and separated R-modules, with morphisms the morphisms of complexes of degree 0. C^flat(R) is the full subcategory of C^comp(R) of bounded complexes of m_R-adically complete, separated and flat R-modules. C^perf(R) is the full subcategory of C^flat(R) of complexes of finite free R-modules, called perfect complexes. K^perf(R) is the homotopy category: its objects are those of C^perf(R), and its morphisms are homotopy classes of morphisms in C^perf(R).
items.note: C^perf(R) and the homotopy category K^perf(R) are planned in P7. AUDIT-17: 'No perfect complex, `Perf` subcategory or pseudo-coherence notion exists in either tree', while the homotopy and quasi-isomorphism API is in Mathlib (HomotopyCategory, CochainComplex.IsKProjective). C^comp and C^flat are full subcategories of bounded complexes cut out by termwise Mathlib predicates (IsAdicComplete, Module.Flat), which P7 does not name. They are bookkeeping for P7's 'explicit derived completeness' hypotheses, with derived completeness from DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1.

items.name: Derived subcategories D^comp(R), D^flat(R), D^perf(R)
items.statement: D(R) is the derived category of Mod(R). D^comp(R), D^flat(R) and D^perf(R) are the full subcategories of D(R) generated by the objects of C^comp(R), C^flat(R) and C^perf(R) respectively, i.e. the objects of D(R) isomorphic to such complexes.
items.note: D(R) is Mathlib's DerivedCategory (Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/DerivedCategory/Basic.lean:87, available for ModuleCat R through HasDerivedCategory.standard). D^perf is P7's perfect objects. D^comp and D^flat are essential images of termwise-defined classes, subject to the same bookkeeping as complexes-C-comp-C-flat-C-perf.

items.name: K^perf(R) → D^perf(R) is an equivalence
items.statement: The functor K^perf(R) → D^perf(R) is an equivalence of categories.
items.note: Mathlib proves that a bounded-above cochain complex of projectives is K-projective (isKProjective_of_projective), and that for K-projective K the functor Qh : K(C) → D(C) is bijective on Hom(K, L) for every L (Qh_map_bijective). Finite free modules are projective (ModuleCat.projective_of_free). So the functor from bounded complexes of finite free R-modules up to homotopy into D(R) is fully faithful, and it is an equivalence onto its essential image, which is D^perf by definition. AUDIT-17 records this API as 'library: mathlib' for P7. Only the names K^perf and D^perf are missing; they are P7's perfectness definition. External input: [83] C. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Cambridge Stud. Adv. Math. (1994), Cor. 10.4.7

items.name: Proposition 2.2.1: perfectness criterion for complexes of complete flat modules
items.statement: Let M• be an object of C^flat(R) concentrated in degrees [a,b]. Assume that M• ⊗_R R/m_R has finite cohomology groups. Then M• is quasi-isomorphic to a perfect complex concentrated in degrees [a,b].
items.note: A bounded complex of flat m_R-adically complete modules is derived complete and has Tor-amplitude in [a,b]. Finiteness of H^*(M•⊗R/m_R) lifts to pseudo-coherence under derived completeness, and pseudo-coherence with Tor-amplitude [a,b] gives a finite projective (here free) representative in degrees [a,b], by the P7 node. Pilloni's proof instead uses Mittag-Leffler, topological Nakayama and the Künneth spectral sequence; all three are planned (see those items). Neither library has derived Nakayama (AUDIT-17: 'absent').

items.name: Mumford's lemma: complexes with finite cohomology have finite free models
items.statement: As used in Proposition 2.2.1: if M• is a complex of flat R-modules concentrated in degrees [a,b] whose cohomology groups H^n(M•) are all finite R-modules, then M• is quasi-isomorphic to a perfect complex (finite free modules, R local) concentrated in degrees [a,b].
items.note: Precedent PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/mumford-lemma-1 (planned at P7). The P7 node plans the representation by finite projectives in the Tor-amplitude range. Over the local ring R finite projective means free: Mathlib Module.free_of_flat_of_isLocalRing (Mathlib/RingTheory/LocalRing/Module.lean:304). CG18 notes that the node should add 'bounded complex with finitely generated cohomology over a Noetherian ring is pseudo-coherent'. External input: [55] D. Mumford, Abelian varieties, TIFR (2012 edition), §5, Lemma 1, p. 44

items.name: Cohomology commutes with inverse limits under Mittag-Leffler (EGA 0_III 13.2.3)
items.statement: As used in the proof of Proposition 2.2.1. Let M• ∈ C^flat(R) be concentrated in degrees [a,b], and assume that M• ⊗_R R/m_R has finite cohomology groups. The inverse system of complexes (M•/m_R^n M•)_n has surjective transition maps, and its limit is M• because the terms of M• are m_R-adically complete and separated. The exact sequences 0 → m_R^{n−1}/m_R^n ⊗_R M• → M•/m_R^n → M•/m_R^{n−1} → 0 and induction on n show that each H^i(M•/m_R^n) is a finite R/m_R^n-module, hence of finite length. So the systems (H^i(M•/m_R^n))_n satisfy the Mittag-Leffler condition for every i. By EGA 0_III, Prop. 13.2.3, H^i(M•) = lim_n H^i(M•/m_R^n) for all i.
items.note: AUDIT-17 rates this target 'partial'. Mathlib's Mittag-Leffler condition (CategoryTheory.Functor.IsMittagLeffler, Mathlib/CategoryTheory/CofilteredSystem.lean) is for Type-valued systems, and neither library has lim¹ or a cohomology-of-limits theorem. External input: [EGA] A. Grothendieck and J. Dieudonné, EGA III, chap. 0, Prop. 13.2.3

items.name: Topological Nakayama lemma
items.statement: As used: let X be an m_R-adically complete and separated R-module (X ≅ lim_n X/m_R^n X). If X/m_R X is a finite R-module, then X is a finite R-module.
items.note: Planned at L5. AUDIT-26 rates it absent ('Only algebraic Nakayama for finitely generated modules is available'). Mathlib does have the surjectivity step: surjective_of_mkQ_comp_surjective (Mathlib/RingTheory/AdicCompletion/Functoriality.lean:448) says that if M is I-adically precomplete, N is I-adically Hausdorff, and M → N → N/IN is surjective, then M → N is surjective. Applied to R^n → X it gives the lemma, once one knows that R^n is precomplete for complete R; no instance for that was found. IntegralIwasawaTheory:L2 also proves a compact version. External input: standard (topological Nakayama lemma; not cited by the paper)

items.name: Künneth spectral sequence
items.statement: For a bounded complex M• of flat R-modules there is a spectral sequence E_2^{p,q} = Tor^R_{−p}(H^q(M•), R/m_R) ⇒ H^{p+q}(M• ⊗_R R/m_R), with d_2: E_2^{p,q} → E_2^{p+2,q−1}.
items.locator: §2.2, proof of Proposition 2.2.1, p. 9 (also in the proof of Proposition 2.2.2)
items.note: AUDIT-17 rates this target 'partial': Mathlib has spectral objects and their spectral sequences, but no Tor spectral sequence or derived tensor product. External input: [83] C. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra (1994), Thm. 5.6.4

items.name: Proposition 2.2.2: Nakayama's lemma for complexes
items.statement: Let f: M• → N• be a map in C^flat(R). Assume that f ⊗ 1: M• ⊗_R R/m_R → N• ⊗_R R/m_R is a quasi-isomorphism. Then f is a quasi-isomorphism.
items.note: The cone of f is a bounded complex of flat complete modules, so it is derived complete, and cone(f)⊗^L R/m_R = cone(f ⊗ 1) is acyclic. Conservativity of reduction on derived complete objects (derived Nakayama) then gives cone(f) = 0. Neither library has it (AUDIT-17: derived Nakayama 'absent').

items.name: Definition 2.3.1: locally finite chain endomorphism and its projector
items.statement: Let M• ∈ C^flat(R) and T ∈ End_{C^flat(R)}(M•). T is locally finite on M• if T acts locally finitely on each M^i. In that case Lemma 2.1.3 attaches to T a projector e ∈ End_{C^flat(R)}(M•), giving a direct factor eM• ∈ C^flat(R) of M•.
items.note: L0a plans the degreewise projector only on 'finite perfect/cohomological complexes'. Complexes in C^flat(R) have huge, non-finite terms (the Čech complexes of F^κ). L0a gap (see clusterNotes).

items.name: Definition 2.3.2: locally finite endomorphism in D^flat(R)
items.statement: Let M• ∈ D^flat(R) and T ∈ End_{D^flat(R)}(M•). T is locally finite if there exist a representative M0• ∈ C^flat(R) of M• and a representative T0 ∈ End_{C^flat(R)}(M0•) of T which is locally finite in the sense of Definition 2.3.1.
items.note: Needs Definition 2.3.1, which is missing. IHG.2 compares chain, homotopy and derived actions only on bounded perfect complexes. L0a gap (see clusterNotes).

items.name: Proposition 2.3.1: characterization of locally finite endomorphisms
items.statement: Let M• ∈ D^flat(R) and T ∈ End_{D^flat(R)}(M•). The following are equivalent: (1) T is locally finite; (2) T is locally finite on the cohomology groups H^i(M• ⊗^L_R R/m_R), and there exist representatives M0• ∈ C^flat(R) of M• and T0 ∈ End_{C^flat(R)}(M0•) of T.
items.note: Needs Definitions 2.3.1–2.3.2 and the minimal subcomplex (minimal-subcomplex-differentials-zero-mod-m), which are missing. L0a gap (see clusterNotes).

items.name: Minimal direct-factor subcomplex with differentials zero mod m_R
items.statement: Let M0• ∈ C^flat(R). There is a subcomplex N• ⊂ M0•, N• ∈ C^flat(R), such that: (1) all differentials d: N^i → N^{i+1} are 0 modulo m_R; (2) the inclusion i: N• → M0• has a section s: M0• → N•; (3) i and s are quasi-isomorphisms. In particular H^i(M0• ⊗_R R/m_R) = N^i/m_R N^i.
items.note: P7's node 'Perfect complexes, Tor-amplitude and minimal complexes over local rings' covers only pseudo-coherent K with finite free terms R^{d_i}. The analogue for complexes of flat m_R-adically complete modules of infinite rank (a direct-factor subcomplex N• with differentials zero mod m_R, quasi-isomorphic to M0•) is not planned. AUDIT-17 rates minimal representatives 'partial' (two-term pieces only).

items.name: Lemma 2.3.1: splitting a map of flat complete modules into an isomorphism and a map zero mod m_R
items.statement: Let f: M → N be a map in Mod^comp(R), with M and N flat. There are decompositions M = M1 ⊕ M2 and N = N1 ⊕ N2 such that f(M_i) ⊂ N_i for i ∈ {1,2}, f|_{M1}: M1 → N1 is an isomorphism, and f|_{M2}: M2 → N2 is zero modulo m_R.
items.note: No layer or library splits a map of flat m_R-adically complete modules into an isomorphism plus a map that is zero modulo m_R. It is the key step of the minimal-subcomplex construction.

items.name: Flat m_R-adically complete modules are topologically free
items.statement: Let M be a flat object of Mod^comp(R), let {ē_i}_{i∈I} be a basis of M/m_R M over R/m_R, and let {e_i}_{i∈I} be lifts to M. Let R̂^{(I)} be the m_R-adic completion of the free module ⊕_{i∈I} R, i.e. families (r_i) with r_i → 0 along the filter of complements of finite subsets. The map ⊕_I R → M, (r_i) ↦ Σ r_i e_i, induces an isomorphism R̂^{(I)} ≅ M. The family {e_i} is called a topological basis of M.
items.note: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L0 plans the DVR/Banach case: 'For Banach spaces whose nonzero norm values lie in the coefficient value group, prove the orthonormal-basis theorem ... by lifting a basis of the integral lattice modulo varpi and completing the successive expansions.' The case needed here is a general complete local Noetherian R, including the components of Λ = Z_p[[Z_p^×]], which are not DVRs, and it is not planned. Proof: M/m^n M is flat, hence free, over the Artinian ring R/m^n (Stacks 051G, absent from the libraries by CG18 lemma-7-5), then pass to the limit. The page-10 text writes R^I and its completion for the free module R^{(I)} (see clusterNotes).

items.name: Ordinary projector and ordinary direct factor attached to a locally finite representative
items.statement: Setting of §2: R is a complete local noetherian ring with maximal ideal m_R and finite residue field R/m_R; C^flat(R) is the category of bounded complexes of m_R-adically complete and separated flat R-modules; D^flat(R) ⊂ D^comp(R) ⊂ D(R) are the full subcategories generated by C^flat(R) and C^comp(R); D^perf(R) is generated by bounded complexes of finite free R-modules. Let M• ∈ D^flat(R) and let T ∈ End_{D^flat(R)}(M•) be locally finite (Definition 2.3.2: it has a representative T0 ∈ End_{C^flat(R)}(M0•), M0• ∈ C^flat(R) representing M•, acting locally finitely on every term). For every such locally finite representative (M0•, T0), Lemma 2.1.3 applied termwise gives the ordinary projector e0 ∈ End_{C^flat(R)}(M0•) (e0 v = lim_{N→∞} T0^{N!} v, m_R-adically) and the direct factor e0M0• of M0•. Let ē0 be the image of e0 in End_{D^comp(R)}(M•); the associated direct factor ē0M• of M• in D^comp(R) is represented by e0M0•. Under the hypothesis of Lemma 2.3.2 the paper speaks of 'the projector associated to a locally finite endomorphism' (denoted e): it may depend on the representative, but two representatives give canonically isomorphic direct factors.
items.locator: §2.3, paragraph between Lemma 2.3.1 and Lemma 2.3.2 and paragraph after Lemma 2.3.2, pp. 10–11
items.note: PadicFamilies:L0a plans the U^(n!) projector only for 'a finite underlying module' and for 'a complete separated module M presented as an inverse limit of finite discrete quotient modules M/J', applied 'degreewise to finite perfect/cohomological complexes with commuting U and differential'. Pilloni's Definition 2.1.1 (p. 7) asks only that M/m_R^n be an inductive limit of finite T-stable submodules. M/m_R^n itself can be infinite, for example the completion of an infinite-rank free module. The construction is also made for complexes in C^flat(R) and lives in D^flat(R), where it may depend on the representative. Neither the ind-finite step nor the D^flat(R) construction is planned. The libraries have only the finite case: mathlib:LinearMap.eventually_isCompl_ker_pow_range_pow (Mathlib/RingTheory/Artinian/Module.lean:317, the Fitting decomposition). AUDIT-15 records that the element lim U^(n!) itself is not constructed.

items.name: Lemma 2.3.2 (independence of the ordinary direct factor from the representative)
items.statement: Setting as in §2 (R complete local noetherian, R/m_R finite). Let M• ∈ D^flat(R), T ∈ End_{D^flat(R)}(M•), and let (M0•, T0) and (M1•, T1) be two locally finite representatives of (M•, T), with associated projectors e0, e1 and their images ē0, ē1 ∈ End_{D^comp(R)}(M•). Assume that ē0M• is an object of D^perf(R). Then the canonical map ē0M• → ē1M• (the composite ē0M• → M• → ē1M•) is a quasi-isomorphism; in particular ē1M• is also perfect.
items.note: Lemma 2.3.2 is planned nowhere. Its proof inputs are Prop. 2.2.1, a perfectness criterion for flat complete complexes with finite reduction, and Prop. 2.2.2, derived Nakayama. Those inputs are close to DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:P7 ('Prove derived Nakayama and specialization/extension results under explicit derived completeness and finiteness hypotheses'). P7 works with complexes of finite projective modules, however, not with complexes of flat complete modules of possibly infinite rank.

items.name: Ordinary projector on perfect complexes (Khare–Thorne) and compatibility
items.statement: For M• ∈ D^perf(R) and T ∈ End_{D^comp(R)}(M•) there is an ordinary projector attached to T, and it is unique; uniqueness rests on the fact that the algebra End_{D^comp(R)}(M•) is finite over R when M• is perfect. For M• ∈ D^perf(R) the condition of being locally finite is automatically satisfied, and the projector of §2.3 is compatible with that of Khare–Thorne.
items.note: For perfect M, End_{D(R)}(M) is a finite R-module (P7/IHG.2). L0a applied to it, with U = left multiplication by T, gives e = lim T^(n!) and its uniqueness. This is how PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/lemma-7-3 (ordinary part of a perfect complex) was marked planned. Caveat: the clause saying this projector is compatible with Pilloni's locally-finite projector depends on the missing item ordinary-direct-factor-of-locally-finite-endomorphism. External input: C. Khare, J. Thorne, Potential automorphy and the Leopoldt conjecture, Amer. J. Math. (reference [41]), Lemma 2.12

items.name: Standing conventions of §3 (base field, adic spaces, pseudo-uniformizer)
items.statement: k is a complete non-archimedean field with ring of integers O_k and maximal ideal m_{O_k}. In §3.1–§3.2 (the paper says 'in this section' at the start of §3.1), the adic spaces 𝒳 considered are over Spa(k, O_k), of finite type (in particular quasi-compact) and separated, and O_𝒳 is the structure sheaf. §3.3 and §3.4 state their own hypotheses. In §3.3, f: 𝒳 → 𝒴 is a quasi-compact map of finite type adic spaces, but 𝒵 is an arbitrary adic space over Spa(k, O_k). In §3.4 the spaces T^an_Σ over Spa(Q_p, Z_p) are locally of finite type but not quasi-compact. From §3.2 on, p denotes a topologically nilpotent unit of k. Ȟ^i denotes Čech cohomology and Ȟ^i_𝒰 Čech cohomology relative to a covering 𝒰.
items.note: These are conventions only: finite-type separated adic spaces over Spa(k, O_k), a topologically nilpotent unit p, and Čech notation. Each piece is planned.

items.name: The subsheaves O^+ and O^{++} of O_𝒳
items.statement: For every open U ⊂ 𝒳: O^+_𝒳(U) = {f ∈ O_𝒳(U) : |f|_x ≤ 1 for all x ∈ U} and O^{++}_𝒳(U) = {f ∈ O_𝒳(U) : |f|_x < 1 for all x ∈ U}. These are subsheaves of O_𝒳.
items.note: O^+ is planned in Tau Ceti AdicSpaces Layer 3.3: 'Define 𝒪_X⁺(U) = {f ∈ 𝒪_X(U) : v_x(f_x) ≤ 1 for every x ∈ U}'. No layer defines O^{++} = {f : |f|_x < 1 for all x}. A search of the atlas for O^{++} or for a sheaf of topologically nilpotent sections finds nothing. The item bundles both sheaves, so it is marked missing; only the O^{++} half is new.

items.name: Sections of O^+ and O^{++} on an affinoid
items.statement: If U = Spa(A, A^+) with A a complete Tate algebra topologically of finite type over k, A° the subring of power-bounded elements of A and A°° the ideal of A° of topologically nilpotent elements, then O^+_𝒳(U) = A^+ = A° and O^{++}_𝒳(U) = A°°.
items.note: The O^+ half is planned. Tau Ceti AdicSpaces Layer 2.3 plans Prop. 7.52(1), 'A⁺ = {a ∈ A : v(a) ≤ 1 for every v ∈ Spa(A,A⁺)}'. Layer 3.5 plans 'Prove that 𝒪_X(X) ≅ A'. Layer 2.4 plans classical affinoids with plus ring A°. Neither is proved at the pinned commit. The identification O^{++}(U) = A°° (Huber, Lemma 4.4) is planned nowhere. The paper cites Huber [35], lem. 4.4 for both identifications, O^+_𝒳(U) = A° and O^{++}_𝒳(U) = A°°. External input: R. Huber, A generalization of formal schemes and rigid analytic varieties, Math. Z. 217 (1994) (reference [35]), Lemma 4.4

items.name: Proposition 3.1.1 (1): Čech cohomology computes H^i(𝒳, O^+)
items.statement: Let 𝒳 be a separated adic space of finite type over Spa(k, O_k). For all i the natural map Ȟ^i(𝒳, O^+_𝒳) → H^i(𝒳, O^+_𝒳) from Čech cohomology to cohomology is an isomorphism.
items.note: No layer studies the cohomology of O^+. DiamondsAndVStacks:D0 plans generic Čech-to-sheaf spectral sequences, and AdicSpacesPartII R2/F0 plan formal models, but Proposition 3.1.1 itself is planned nowhere. The proof also needs the missing O-plus-as-limit-of-formal-models and cohomology-of-limit-of-formal-models.

items.name: Proposition 3.1.1 (2): Čech cohomology computes H^i(𝒳, O^{++})
items.statement: Let 𝒳 be a separated adic space of finite type over Spa(k, O_k). For all i the natural map Ȟ^i(𝒳, O^{++}_𝒳) → H^i(𝒳, O^{++}_𝒳) is an isomorphism.
items.note: This is the same as Prop. 3.1.1(1) for O^{++}, and O^{++} itself is missing. Planned nowhere.

items.name: (𝒳, O^+) as the projective limit of the formal models
items.statement: There is an isomorphism of locally ringed spaces (𝒳, O^+_𝒳) ≅ lim_𝔛 (𝔛, O_𝔛), where 𝔛 runs over all formal models of 𝒳 (formal schemes topologically of finite type over Spf O_k with generic fibre 𝒳) ([69], thm. 2.22). For such 𝔛 let X̄ be its special fibre over Spec O_k/m_{O_k}, X̄^red its reduction, and I_𝔛 = ker(O_𝔛 → O_{X̄^red}). Under the above isomorphism O^{++}_𝒳 = colim_𝔛 I_𝔛. (The paper calls O_𝔛 → O_{X̄red} a map of coherent sheaves. This holds for discretely valued k. In general I_𝔛 ⊇ m_{O_k}O_𝔛 need not be finitely generated, so I_𝔛 and O_{X̄red} need not be coherent O_𝔛-modules.)
items.note: AdicSpacesPartII:R2 plans 'admissible formal schemes, formal completion, admissible blow-ups, and the adic generic-fibre functor'. Nothing plans (𝒳, O^+) = lim over formal models (Scholze, Perfectoid spaces, Thm 2.22) or O^{++} = colim I_𝔛. AdicEtaleGeometry:A2 warns 'do not assume AdicSpaces already includes a Raynaud equivalence'. TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure:TC.0 compares integral structure sheaves only 'on the specified covers' of Shimura towers. External input: P. Scholze, Perfectoid spaces, Publ. IHES 116 (2012) (reference [69]), Theorem 2.22 (the first assertion); the description of O^{++} is asserted in the proof

items.name: Cohomology of O^+ as a direct limit over formal models
items.statement: With 𝔛 running over the formal models of 𝒳 (quasi-compact), H^i(𝒳, O^+_𝒳) = colim_𝔛 H^i(𝔛, O_𝔛) (cohomology of a projective limit of coherent spaces with the colimit sheaf is the direct limit of the cohomologies).
items.note: Fujiwara–Kato Prop. 3.1.10, that the cohomology of a projective limit of coherent spaces is the colimit of the cohomologies, is planned nowhere. ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0's 'continuity under the cofiltered limits used in the classical proofs' concerns étale sheaves only. External input: K. Fujiwara, F. Kato, Foundations of rigid geometry (reference [19]), Prop. 3.1.10 (as cited)

items.name: Čech cohomology via finite coverings; Leray's acyclic covering theorem
items.statement: (a) On a quasi-compact space Čech cohomology can be computed using only finite coverings. (b) If 𝒰 is a covering of X such that the sheaf F has vanishing higher cohomology on all finite intersections of members of 𝒰, then Ȟ^i_𝒰(X, F) → H^i(X, F) is an isomorphism.
items.locator: §3.1, proofs of Proposition 3.1.1 and Corollary 3.1.1, p. 12
items.note: Leray's acyclic-cover theorem (b) is planned generically in D0. Part (a), that on a quasi-compact space finite coverings are cofinal for Čech cohomology, is an elementary cofinality remark inside the same development. Neither library has Čech-to-derived comparisons for sheaves of modules. External input: R. Godement, Topologie algébrique et théorie des faisceaux (reference [26]), p. 224 and Corollaire p. 213

items.name: Formal models of separated rigid spaces are separated
items.statement: If 𝒳 is separated, every formal model 𝔛 of 𝒳 is separated.
items.note: This is the separatedness comparison of Bosch–Lütkebohmert, Prop. 4.7, named in F0. External input: S. Bosch, W. Lütkebohmert, Formal and rigid geometry I. Rigid spaces, Math. Ann. 295 (1993) (reference [7]), Prop. 4.7 (as cited)

items.name: Theorem 3.1.1 (Bartenwerfer), part 1: bounded torsion of H^i(𝒳, O^+) on smooth affinoids
items.statement: Let 𝒳 be a smooth affinoid adic space of finite type over Spa(k, O_k). For all i > 0, H^i(𝒳, O^+_𝒳) is annihilated by a non-zero element c(𝒳) ∈ O_k.
items.note: Bartenwerfer's bounded-torsion theorem is planned nowhere. The only integral-acyclicity statements in the atlas are for perfectoid affinoids: PerfectoidSpaces:P2, 'all-degree almost acyclicity on affinoids and their integral structure sheaves'. A search for 'Bartenwerfer' or 'bounded torsion' finds nothing. External input: W. Bartenwerfer, Die höheren metrischen Kohomologiegruppen affinoider Räume, Math. Ann. 241 (1979) (reference [2])

items.name: Theorem 3.1.1 (Bartenwerfer), part 2: vanishing of H^i(𝒳, O^{++}) with good reduction
items.statement: Let 𝒳 be a smooth affinoid adic space of finite type over Spa(k, O_k) which admits a smooth affine formal model. Then H^i(𝒳, O^{++}_𝒳) = 0 for all i > 0.
items.note: Planned nowhere; see the previous item. External input: W. Bartenwerfer (reference [2])

items.name: Corollary 3.1.1: H^i(𝔛, m O_𝔛) = H^i(𝒳, O^{++}) for smooth formal schemes
items.statement: Let 𝔛 be an admissible (topologically of finite type and flat over Spf O_k) smooth and separated formal scheme with generic fibre 𝒳. Then for all i the canonical map H^i(𝔛, m_{O_k}O_𝔛) → H^i(𝒳, O^{++}_𝒳) is an isomorphism.
items.note: The comparison H^i(𝔛, m O_𝔛) = H^i(𝒳, O^{++}) for smooth formal schemes is planned nowhere. It depends on the missing Bartenwerfer vanishing and on O^{++}.

items.name: Lemma 3.2.1: H^i(𝒳, O) = lim_n H^i(𝒳, O/p^n O^+) on smooth affinoids
items.statement: Let 𝒳 be a smooth affinoid adic space (over Spa(k, O_k), p a topologically nilpotent unit of k). For every i ≥ 0 the map H^i(𝒳, O_𝒳) → lim_n H^i(𝒳, O_𝒳/p^nO^+_𝒳) is an isomorphism. (For i > 0 both sides vanish: lim_n H^i(𝒳, O_𝒳/p^nO^+_𝒳) = 0.)
items.note: Acyclicity of O on affinoids is planned: Tau Ceti AdicSpaces Layer 4 ('exactness in every degree of the augmented Čech complex for every finite rational cover') and AdicSpacesPartII:R3 ('acyclicity'). Lemma 3.2.1 also needs Bartenwerfer's bounded torsion of H^i(O^+), which is missing.

items.name: Locally free sheaf F with integral structure F^+
items.statement: F is a locally free sheaf of O_𝒳-modules (of finite rank, as is implicit in Proposition 3.2.1) together with a locally free O^+_𝒳-submodule F^+ ⊂ F such that F = F^+ ⊗_{O^+_𝒳} O_𝒳. One considers the sheaves F^+ and F/p^nF^+ for n ∈ N.
items.note: R3 plans 'locally free sheaves' of O_𝒳-modules. No layer plans locally free O^+-lattices F^+ ⊂ F.

items.name: Lemma 3.2.2 (1): Čech-to-derived comparison for F/p^nF^+ up to bounded torsion
items.statement: Assume 𝒳 is a smooth and separated adic space (finite type over Spa(k, O_k)), F^+ ⊂ F as above, and let 𝒰 be a finite affinoid covering of 𝒳 such that F^+ is trivial on each member of 𝒰. There is a non-zero c ∈ O_k, depending on 𝒰 (the same c serving in Lemma 3.2.2 (2) and (3)), such that for all n ∈ N and all i the map Ȟ^i_𝒰(𝒳, F/p^nF^+) → H^i(𝒳, F/p^nF^+) has kernel and cokernel annihilated by c.
items.note: Planned nowhere; it rests on the missing Bartenwerfer bounds.

items.name: Lemma 3.2.2 (2): Čech-to-derived comparison for F^+ up to bounded torsion
items.statement: In the situation of Lemma 3.2.2 (𝒳 smooth separated, 𝒰 a finite affinoid covering trivializing F^+, c ≠ 0 as there), the map Ȟ^i_𝒰(𝒳, F^+) → H^i(𝒳, F^+) has kernel and cokernel killed by c.
items.note: Planned nowhere.

items.name: Lemma 3.2.2 (3): the limit comparison map is surjective with bounded kernel
items.statement: In the situation of Lemma 3.2.2, the map lim_n Ȟ^i_𝒰(𝒳, F/p^nF^+) → lim_n H^i(𝒳, F/p^nF^+) has kernel killed by c and is surjective.
items.note: Planned nowhere. The proof shows that the cokernel is killed by c² and then uses p-divisibility.

items.name: Proposition 3.2.1 (1): H^i(𝒳, F) → lim_n H^i(𝒳, F/p^nF^+) is surjective
items.statement: Let 𝒳 be a smooth and separated adic space (finite type over Spa(k, O_k)) and F^+ ⊂ F as in §3.2. For all i the map H^i(𝒳, F) → lim_n H^i(𝒳, F/p^nF^+) is surjective.
items.note: Planned nowhere.

items.name: Proposition 3.2.1 (2): H^i(𝒳, F) = lim_n H^i(𝒳, F/p^nF^+) for proper 𝒳
items.statement: Let 𝒳 be a smooth, separated and proper adic space over Spa(k, O_k) and F^+ ⊂ F as in §3.2. For all i the map H^i(𝒳, F) → lim_n H^i(𝒳, F/p^nF^+) is an isomorphism.
items.note: Planned nowhere. Its inputs are partly planned: Kiehl finiteness (R3), properness of formal models (F0), and Raynaud models (missing).

items.name: Lemma 3.2.3: cohomology of a limit of complexes surjects onto the limit of cohomology up to c
items.statement: Let (K•_α)_{α∈N} be a projective system of complexes of O_k-modules and K• = lim_α K•_α. Assume there is c ∈ O_k such that the cokernel of K^n → K^n_α is killed by c for all n and α. Then for all i the cokernel of H^i(K•) → lim_α H^i(K•_α) is killed by c.
items.note: This is plain homological algebra for inverse systems of complexes of O_k-modules, with O_k possibly non-noetherian. DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:P7 plans derived Mittag–Leffler comparisons only over complete Noetherian local rings. The libraries have no lim^1 for modules.

items.name: Raynaud's theory: formal models adapted to a finite affinoid covering
items.statement: Given 𝒳 (quasi-compact, quasi-separated, over Spa(k, O_k)) and a finite affinoid covering 𝒰 of 𝒳, there is a formal model 𝔛' of 𝒳 admitting an affine covering 𝔘' whose generic fibre refines 𝒰.
items.note: R2 plans admissible formal schemes and blow-ups, but not the existence of a formal model whose affine cover refines a given affinoid cover. AdicEtaleGeometry:A2: 'do not assume AdicSpaces already includes a Raynaud equivalence'. External input: Raynaud's theory of formal models (e.g. Bosch–Lütkebohmert [7])

items.name: Formal models of proper rigid spaces are proper
items.statement: If 𝒳 is proper, a formal model 𝔛 of 𝒳 (here: the normalisation of 𝔛' in 𝒳) is automatically proper.
items.note: This is Lütkebohmert's Lemma 2.6, an instance of F0's properness comparison. External input: W. Lütkebohmert, Formal-algebraic and rigid-analytic geometry, Math. Ann. 286 (reference [52]), Lemma 2.6

items.name: Finiteness of coherent cohomology of proper rigid spaces and proper formal schemes
items.statement: (a) If 𝒳 is a proper adic space over Spa(k, O_k) and F a coherent (here locally free) O_𝒳-module, then H^i(𝒳, F) is a finite-dimensional k-vector space. (b) If 𝔛 is a proper admissible formal scheme over Spf O_k and F a locally free O_𝔛-module of finite rank, then H^i(𝔛, F) is a finite O_k-module.
items.note: Part (a) is Kiehl's theorem, named in R3. Part (b) is part of F0's formal-functions package. Caveat: F0 opens with 'complete separated Noetherian adic rings'. For a non-discretely valued k, O_k is not noetherian, and F0's blueprint must then cover proper formal schemes of finite presentation over non-noetherian O_k (Fujiwara–Kato, Abbes). External input: Kiehl's finiteness theorem for (a); finiteness of coherent cohomology of proper formal schemes for (b); both used without citation

items.name: Setting for base change of O^{++}/p^n (§3.3)
items.statement: f: 𝒳 → 𝒴 is a quasi-compact morphism of finite type adic spaces over Spa(k, O_k); i: 𝒵 → 𝒴 is a morphism of adic spaces over Spa(k, O_k) inducing a homeomorphism from 𝒵 onto i(𝒵) and, for all z ∈ 𝒵, a bijection (k(i(z)), k(i(z))^+) → (k(z), k(z)^+) of residue pairs. 𝒳_𝒵 = 𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒵 with projections i': 𝒳_𝒵 → 𝒳 and f': 𝒳_𝒵 → 𝒵.
items.note: This setting defines morphisms that are homeomorphisms onto their image and bijective on residue pairs (for example, inclusions of points or fibres). Planned nowhere.

items.name: Lemma 3.3.1: (i')^{-1}(O^{++}/p^n) = O^{++}_{𝒳_𝒵}/p^n
items.statement: In the setting of §3.3, for all n ∈ N the canonical map (i')^{-1}(O^{++}_𝒳/p^n) → O^{++}_{𝒳_𝒵}/p^n is an isomorphism.
items.note: Planned nowhere; O^{++} is missing.

items.name: Proposition 3.3.1: base change for Rf_*(O^{++}/p^n)
items.statement: In the setting of §3.3 (f quasi-compact of finite type, i a homeomorphism onto its image inducing bijections on residue pairs), for all n ∈ N the base change map i^{-1} Rf_*(O^{++}_𝒳/p^n) → Rf'_*(O^{++}_{𝒳_𝒵}/p^n) is an isomorphism.
items.note: Planned nowhere. ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology plans base change only for étale torsion sheaves.

items.name: Tori, toric embeddings and their analytic and formal versions (§3.4)
items.statement: T is a split torus over Spec Z; 𝔗 is the formal torus over Spf Z_p (completion of T along T × Spec F_p); T^an → Spa(Q_p, Z_p) is the analytification of T × Spec Q_p (T^an = Spa(Q_p, Z_p) ×_{Spec Q} T, [35] Prop. 3.8); T^rig ⊂ T^an is the generic fibre of 𝔗 ([35] Prop. 4.2); X_*(T) is the cocharacter group. For a rational polyhedral cone decomposition Σ of X_*(T)_R (printed 'rational polyhedral cone'), T → T_Σ is the associated toric embedding over Spec Z (KKMS [40]) and T_Σ^an, T_Σ^rig, 𝔗_Σ are defined in the same way; similarly for a refinement Σ' of Σ. Σ' is called smooth if T_{Σ'} is smooth.
items.note: The item is notation only: T_Σ over Z, 𝔗_Σ, T^an_Σ and T^rig_Σ, with smooth refinements. Every piece is planned. The printed 'rational polyhedral cone' should read 'rational polyhedral cone decomposition'.

items.name: Proposition 3.4.1: Rf_*O^{++} = O^{++} for smooth toric refinements
items.statement: In the notation of §3.4, let Σ' be a smooth refinement of Σ and f: T^an_{Σ'} → T^an_Σ the natural morphism. Then the natural map O^{++}_{T^an_Σ} → Rf_*O^{++}_{T^an_{Σ'}} is a quasi-isomorphism, i.e. f_*O^{++}_{T^an_{Σ'}} = O^{++}_{T^an_Σ} and R^if_*O^{++}_{T^an_{Σ'}} = 0 for all i > 0.
items.note: Proposition 3.4.1 is planned nowhere. ShimuraCompactifications:C3 keeps 'separately stated higher-direct-image vanishing for the exact coefficient sheaves and hypotheses used by consumers' (RS-32), but on algebraic toroidal models and not for O^{++} on adic spaces.

items.name: Kempf's vanishing for toric resolutions (KKMS)
items.statement: For a refinement Σ' of Σ with T_{Σ'} smooth, the proper birational toric morphism π: T_{Σ'} → T_Σ satisfies π_*O_{T_{Σ'}} = O_{T_Σ} and R^iπ_*O_{T_{Σ'}} = 0 for i > 0; the paper uses it for the analytic spaces over Q_p and for the formal completions with coefficients k(x)^{00} ⊗̂_{Z_p} O (giving H^i(𝔗_{2,Σ''}, k(x)^{00} ⊗̂ O) = H^i(𝔗_{2,σ}, k(x)^{00} ⊗̂ O)).
items.note: The toric statement Rπ_*O = O is not stated in any layer. C3 plans the global analogue for toroidal compactifications: 'Prove the structure-sheaf pushforward ... Where higher direct images are required, make their vanishing a separate theorem with the relevant coefficient hypotheses.' AUDIT-10 records f_*O = O and higher direct images as absent. Tau Ceti AnalyticToricGeometry L5 has only toric maps and properness. This follows CG-20/coherent-cohomology-independent-of-compactification, which was routed to C3. External input: G. Kempf, F. Knudsen, D. Mumford, B. Saint-Donat, Toroidal embeddings I, LNM 339 (reference [40]), Cor. 1 on p. 44

items.name: Stalks at non-maximal points equal stalks at the maximal generisation
items.statement: For x ∈ T^an_Σ not a maximal point, with maximal generisation x̃, (R^if_*O^{++}_{T^an_{Σ'}}/p)_x = (R^if_*O^{++}_{T^an_{Σ'}}/p)_{x̃}.
items.note: The equality of stalks at a point and at its maximal generisation, for these overconvergent-type sheaves, is planned nowhere. External input: M. van der Put, Cohomology on affinoid spaces, Compositio Math. 45 (1982) (reference [82]), Prop. 1.4.10 and Example 1.5.2

items.name: Derived categories D_qcoh, D^±_qcoh, D^b_qcoh, D^b_qcoh(O_X)_{fTd}; the base S
items.statement: For a scheme X, D_qcoh(O_X) ⊂ D(O_X) is the full subcategory of complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves; D^+_qcoh(O_X) (resp. D^−_qcoh(O_X)) consists of objects with vanishing cohomology sheaves in sufficiently negative (resp. positive) degrees; D^b_qcoh(O_X) of objects with only finitely many non-zero cohomology sheaves; D^b_qcoh(O_X)_{fTd} ⊂ D^b_qcoh(O_X) of objects quasi-isomorphic to bounded complexes of flat O_X-modules ([32] Def. 4.3 p. 97). If X is locally noetherian, D^+_qcoh(O_X) is also the derived category of bounded-below complexes of quasi-coherent sheaves ([32] Cor. 7.19). For the rest of §4, S is a fixed noetherian affine scheme.
items.note: The ambient D(O_X) is planned (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1, 'For morphisms of sites and ringed topoi, construct the enhanced pullback/pushforward adjunction'). Mathlib has DerivedCategory and SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent. Nothing plans D_qcoh, D^±_qcoh, D^b_qcoh(O_X)_fTd, or Hartshorne's comparison D^+_qcoh(O_X) ≃ D^+(QCoh(X)) for locally noetherian X. AUDIT-01 (A0-extension) says Tor-amplitude and perfect complexes on schemes are absent.

items.name: Embeddable and projectively embeddable morphisms
items.statement: A morphism of S-schemes f: X → Y is embeddable if there exist a smooth S-scheme P and a finite morphism i: X → P ×_S Y such that f is the composite of i and the second projection ([32] p. 189). f is projectively embeddable if it is embeddable and P can be taken to be a projective space over S ([32] p. 206).
items.note: Coherent duality is planned only for curves (Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge Layer B, StableReduction Layer 2, SF.3). Searching the atlas for 'Residues and Duality', 'Grothendieck duality', 'f^!' and 'dualizing' finds only étale or diamond six-functor layers.

items.name: The functor f^! for embeddable morphisms (Hartshorne)
items.statement: For an embeddable morphism of S-schemes f: X → Y there is a functor f^!: D^+_qcoh(O_Y) → D^+_qcoh(O_X), compatible with composition of embeddable morphisms ((gf)^! ≅ f^!g^!) and with restriction to open subschemes (part 5 of the theorem); Rf_*: D_qcoh(O_X) → D_qcoh(O_Y) is the derived direct image.
items.note: Hartshorne's f^! for embeddable morphisms is planned nowhere. The f^! in DiamondSixOperations, EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves and AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons is étale, not coherent. External input: R. Hartshorne, Residues and Duality, LNM 20 (reference [32]), III Thm. 8.7

items.name: Trace map Rf_*f^! ⇒ Id for projectively embeddable f
items.statement: If f: X → Y is projectively embeddable, there is a natural transformation (trace map) Tr_f: Rf_*f^! ⇒ Id of endofunctors of D^+_qcoh(O_Y).
items.note: Planned nowhere. CG18's Grothendieck–Serre duality with trace was also marked missing and routed to A0-extension. External input: R. Hartshorne, Residues and Duality (reference [32]), III Thm. 10.5

items.name: Grothendieck duality for projectively embeddable morphisms
items.statement: If f: X → Y is projectively embeddable, the trace map induces an isomorphism Hom_{D_qcoh(O_X)}(F, f^!G) ≅ Hom_{D_qcoh(O_Y)}(Rf_*F, G) for all F ∈ D^−_qcoh(O_X) and G ∈ D^+_qcoh(O_Y).
items.note: Planned nowhere; see PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/verdier-serre-duality. External input: R. Hartshorne, Residues and Duality (reference [32]), III Thm. 11.1

items.name: Proposition 4.1.2.1: f^!F ⊗^L Lf^*G = f^!(F ⊗^L G)
items.statement: Let f: X → Y be an embeddable morphism of S-schemes. For F ∈ D^+_qcoh(O_Y) and G ∈ D^b_qcoh(O_Y)_{fTd} there is a functorial isomorphism f^!F ⊗^L Lf^*G ≅ f^!(F ⊗^L G).
items.note: Planned nowhere for coherent f^!. External input: R. Hartshorne, Residues and Duality (reference [32]), III Prop. 8.8

items.name: Local complete intersection morphisms, cotangent complex L_{X/S} and ω_{X/S}
items.statement: A morphism f: X → S is a local complete intersection (lci) if locally on X it factors as X →^i Z → S with i a regular immersion (EGA IV 16.9.2) and Z smooth over S. For f lci the cotangent complex L_{X/S} is a perfect complex concentrated in degrees −1 and 0, and ω_{X/S} denotes its determinant in the sense of Knudsen–Mumford [43].

items.name: Cotangent complex of an lci morphism
items.statement: If f: X → S is lci, its cotangent complex L_{X/S} is defined and is perfect of amplitude [−1, 0]; for a regular immersion i: X → Z into a smooth S-scheme with ideal I it is represented by [I/I² → i^*Ω^1_{Z/S}].
items.note: The statement is affine-local; DD.0 plans the localization compatibility needed to globalize it. Caveat: DD.0's amplitude criterion is stated 'in its finite-presentation/flatness range', whereas Pilloni's lci maps need not be flat. The regular-quotient computation plus transitivity covers Pilloni's local factorization X ↪ Z → S. External input: L. Illusie, Complexe cotangent et déformations I, LNM 239 (reference [37]), Prop. 3.2.9

items.name: Proposition 4.1.3.1: h^!O_S = ω_{X/S}[n] for lci h
items.statement: If h: X → S is an embeddable morphism which is a local complete intersection of pure relative dimension n, then h^!O_S ≅ ω_{X/S}[n], where ω_{X/S} is the determinant of the cotangent complex L_{X/S}. (Printed: 'f^!O_X = ω_{X/S}[n]'.)
items.note: Planned nowhere; this needs coherent f^!. The paper prints 'f^!O_X = ω_{X/S}[n]'; h^!O_S is meant.

items.name: Corollary 4.1.3.1: f^!O_Y = ω_{X/S} ⊗ f^*ω_{Y/S}^{-1}
items.statement: Let h: X → S and g: Y → S be embeddable morphisms of S-schemes which are lci of pure relative dimension n, and let f: X → Y be an embeddable morphism of S-schemes. Then f^!O_Y ≅ ω_{X/S} ⊗ f^*ω_{Y/S}^{-1}; in particular f^!O_Y is an invertible sheaf (in degree 0).
items.note: Planned nowhere.

items.name: Fundamental class Θ: f^*O_Y → f^!O_Y and the trace Tr: Rf_*f^*O_Y → O_Y
items.statement: Let X, Y be embeddable S-schemes and f: X → Y an embeddable morphism. A fundamental class of f is a map Θ: f^*O_Y (= O_X) → f^!O_Y constructed ad hoc in the situations of Construction 1 (4.2.1) or Construction 2 (4.2.2). If f is moreover projectively embeddable, applying Rf_* and composing with the trace Rf_*f^!O_Y → O_Y gives Tr: Rf_*f^*O_Y → O_Y.
items.note: Planned nowhere. AutomorphicBundles:B5 plans 'trace along Hecke correspondences' only on sections in characteristic 0. AUDIT-13 records 'no coherent pullback/trace'.

items.name: Construction 1: fundamental class as determinant of the differential
items.statement: Let f: X → Y be an embeddable morphism of embeddable S-schemes. Assume X and Y are local complete intersections over S of the same pure relative dimension, X is normal, and there are an open V ⊂ X smooth over S whose complement has codimension ≥ 2 (printed 'codimension 2') and an open U ⊂ Y smooth over S with f(V) ⊂ U. Over V the fundamental class is det(df), the determinant of df: f^*Ω^1_{U/S} → Ω^1_{V/S}, a section of ω_{V/S} ⊗ f^*ω_{U/S}^{-1} = f^!O_Y|_V (Cor. 4.1.3.1); since f^!O_Y is invertible and X is normal, it extends uniquely to Θ: O_X → f^!O_Y.
items.note: Planned nowhere. Printed 'codimension 2' means codimension ≥ 2, as the item states.

items.name: Construction 2: fundamental class of a finite flat morphism is the trace
items.statement: If f: X → Y is finite flat, then f^!O_Y = Hom_{O_Y}(f_*O_X, O_Y) (as an f_*O_X-module) and the fundamental class Θ: O_X → f^!O_Y is defined by Θ(1) = tr_f, the trace morphism tr_f: f_*O_X → O_Y of the finite locally free algebra f_*O_X.
items.note: The affine ingredient is in Mathlib: mathlib:Algebra.trace (Mathlib/RingTheory/Trace/Defs.lean:71, 'the trace of (s * ·)'). AdicSpacesPartII:R3 plans the trace for finite locally free algebras on adic spaces. Nothing plans the scheme-level identification f^!O_Y = Hom(f_*O_X, O_Y) with Θ(1) = tr_f.

items.name: Lemma 4.2.3.1 (1): cotangent complex of a finite flat map between smooth S-schemes
items.statement: Let X, Y be smooth S-schemes and f: X → Y finite flat (hence lci). Then L_{X/Y} is represented by the two-term complex [Ω^1_{Y/S} ⊗_{O_Y} O_X →^{df} Ω^1_{X/S}] (degrees −1, 0).
items.note: This is an immediate corollary of the planned transitivity triangle L_{Y/S}⊗O_X → L_{X/S} → L_{X/Y}, with L = Ω¹ for smooth maps. Pilloni's proof instead uses the regular immersion X ↪ X ×_S Y, which is also covered by DD.0.

items.name: Lemma 4.2.3.1 (2): det(df) is the trace (Constructions 1 and 2 agree)
items.statement: Let X, Y be smooth S-schemes and f: X → Y finite flat. Then det(df) ∈ ω_{X/Y} = f^!O_Y equals the trace map tr_f ∈ Hom(f_*O_X, O_Y); hence the fundamental classes of Construction 1 and Construction 2 coincide.
items.note: Planned nowhere. It needs residues (Hartshorne, property R6).

items.name: Residues and the trace (Hartshorne, property (R6))
items.statement: Let X, Y be smooth S-schemes of relative dimension n and f: X → Y finite flat. The map f_* det L_{X/Y} = Hom(f_*O_X, O_Y) → O_Y is the residue map. It sends ω ∈ f_*Ω^n_{X/S} = f_*ω_{X/S} (printed Ω^1_{X/S}) and local generators (t_1, …, t_n) of the ideal I_X of the graph X → X ×_S Y to Res[ω; t_1, …, t_n]. By [32], property (R6) on p. 198, the determinant of [Ω^1_{Y/S} ⊗_{O_Y} O_X → Ω^1_{X/S}] maps to the usual trace map tr_f.
items.note: The residue symbol of Residues and Duality is planned nowhere. External input: R. Hartshorne, Residues and Duality (reference [32]), property (R6) on p. 198

items.name: Lemma 4.2.4.1 (1): fundamental class respects boundary divisors (Construction 1)
items.statement: Let D_X ⊂ X and D_Y ⊂ Y be effective reduced Cartier divisors relative to S such that f restricts to D_X → D_Y and D_X → f^{-1}(D_Y) is a homeomorphism. In the setting of Construction 1, assume moreover that D_X ∩ X^sm is a normal crossings divisor in the smooth locus X^sm of X and D_Y ∩ Y^sm is a normal crossings divisor in Y^sm. Then the fundamental class Θ: O_X → f^!O_Y restricts to a morphism O_X(−D_X) → f^!O_Y(−D_Y) (:= f^!O_Y ⊗ f^*O_Y(−D_Y) = f^!(O_Y(−D_Y))).
items.note: Planned nowhere. The logarithmic differentials used in the proof are planned only for dagger spaces (AdicSpacesPartII:F1) and log geometry (CrystallineCohomology CR.5), not for this statement.

items.name: Lemma 4.2.4.1 (2): fundamental class respects boundary divisors (Construction 2)
items.statement: With D_X, D_Y as in Lemma 4.2.4.1 (effective reduced Cartier divisors relative to S, f(D_X) ⊂ D_Y, D_X → f^{-1}(D_Y) a homeomorphism) and f finite flat (Construction 2), the fundamental class Θ: O_X → f^!O_Y restricts to O_X(−D_X) → f^!O_Y(−D_Y).
items.note: Planned nowhere.

items.name: Proposition 4.2.5.1 (1): base change of f^!O_Y
items.statement: Assume f: X → Y is in the situation of Construction 1 or 2, and consider a cartesian square with i: Y' → Y, j: X' = X ×_Y Y' → X and f': X' → Y'. Assume that i is an open immersion or that f is finite flat. Then there is a natural isomorphism of sheaves j^*f^!O_Y ≅ (f')^!O_{Y'}, with j^* the non-derived pullback.
items.note: Planned nowhere for coherent f^!.

items.name: Proposition 4.2.5.1 (2): base change of the fundamental class
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 4.2.5.1 (i an open immersion or f finite flat), under the isomorphism j^*f^!O_Y ≅ (f')^!O_{Y'}, the pullback j^*Θ: O_{X'} → (f')^!O_{Y'} of the fundamental class of f is the fundamental class of f'.
items.note: Planned nowhere.

items.name: Definition 4.3.1 (1): correspondence
items.statement: Let X, Y be S-schemes. A correspondence C over X and Y is a diagram of S-morphisms p_2: C → X and p_1: C → Y.
items.note: Definition 4.3.1(1) is exactly a span C → X, C → Y of S-schemes, and the libraries express it directly. No named 'correspondence' structure exists. Hecke correspondences of Shimura varieties are separately planned (ShimuraVarieties:V1, ShimuraCompactifications:C3).

items.name: Definition 4.3.1 (2): cohomological correspondence and its action on cohomology
items.statement: Let C (p_2: C → X, p_1: C → Y) be a correspondence, F a coherent sheaf on X and G a coherent sheaf on Y. A cohomological correspondence from F to G is a map T: R(p_1)_*p_2^*F → G. The associated map on cohomology, also denoted T, is the composite RΓ(X, F) →^{p_2^*} RΓ(C, p_2^*F) = RΓ(Y, R(p_1)_*p_2^*F) →^{T} RΓ(Y, G).
items.note: Coherent cohomological correspondences T: R(p1)_*p2^*F → G are planned nowhere.
