Tau Ceti has only absolute H^i(X, M) with long exact and Mayer–Vietoris sequences; there are no higher direct images (AUDIT-01). CG18's coherent Hecke operators (coherent-hecke-operator-T-gamma) were routed to IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes.

items.name: Remark 4.3.2: cohomological correspondences as maps p_2^*F → p_1^!G
items.statement: If p_1 is projectively embeddable, then by duality (adjunction between Rp_{1*} and p_1^!) cohomological correspondences T: R(p_1)_*p_2^*F → G correspond to maps p_2^*F → p_1^!G.
items.note: Planned nowhere; it needs coherent Grothendieck duality.

items.name: 4.3.1: constructing cohomological correspondences from a sheaf map and a fundamental class
items.statement: Let C (p_2: C → X, p_1: C → Y) be a correspondence with p_1 projectively embeddable, and let F, G be locally free sheaves of finite rank on X, Y. Given a morphism φ: p_2^*F → p_1^*G and a map p_1^*O_Y → p_1^!O_Y (typically a fundamental class), tensoring the latter with G and using Proposition 4.1.2.1 gives p_1^*G → p_1^!G; the composite T: p_2^*F → p_1^*G → p_1^!G is a cohomological correspondence (Remark 4.3.2).
items.note: Planned nowhere.

items.name: Remark 4.3.3: renormalizing a cohomological correspondence by a power of the uniformizer
items.statement: Let O be a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer ϖ, S = Spec O, and X, Y, C flat over S. If T: p_2^*F → p_1^!G factors as p_2^*F → ϖ^k p_1^!G ⊂ p_1^!G for some integer k ≥ 0, one defines the normalized correspondence ϖ^{−k}T: p_2^*F → p_1^!G.
items.note: Planned nowhere.

items.name: The group scheme GSp_4 over Z
items.statement: V = Z^4 with canonical basis (e_1, …, e_4); J = (0 A; −A 0) with A the 2×2 anti-diagonal matrix with entries 1 on the anti-diagonal; J is the matrix of a symplectic form ⟨ , ⟩ on V (⟨e_1, e_4⟩ = ⟨e_2, e_3⟩ = 1). GSp_4 → Spec Z is the group scheme GSp(V, ⟨ , ⟩) of symplectic similitudes, ν: GSp_4 → G_m the similitude character, and Sp_4 = ker ν its derived subgroup.
items.note: Same status as PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20/def-gsp4-similitude-and-sp4. The libraries supply only Sp4 as a partial input.

items.name: Diagonal torus of GSp_4 and its character lattice
items.statement: T^der = {diag(t_1, t_2, t_2^{−1}, t_1^{−1})} is the diagonal maximal torus of Sp_4, Z = {diag(s, s, s, s)} the centre of GSp_4, T the diagonal torus of GSp_4; T^der × Z → T is surjective (as fppf sheaves) with kernel μ_2. X^*(T) = {(a_1, a_2; c) ∈ Z^3 : c ≡ a_1 + a_2 mod 2}, where (a_1, a_2; c)·diag(st_1, st_2, st_2^{−1}, st_1^{−1}) = s^c t_1^{a_1} t_2^{a_2}; basis e_1 = (1, 0; 1), e_2 = (0, 1; 1), e_3 = (0, 0; 2) = ν.
items.note: The coordinates (a1,a2;c) with c ≡ a1+a2 mod 2, and T^der × Z → T with kernel μ2, are a coordinate choice on planned objects. PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20/def-diagonal-torus-and-character-lattice was marked the same way.

items.name: Positive roots, simple roots and ρ for GSp_4 (corrected)
items.statement: The positive system is tied to the Shimura datum: the non-compact positive roots −2e_1 + e_3, −e_1 − e_2 + e_3, −2e_2 + e_3 lie in g_C/p_Si (Remark 5.1.2.1). The positive system consistent with the rest of the paper (§5.1.6, §5.3, §15, and the matrix of i) is {e_2 − e_1, −2e_1 + e_3, −e_1 − e_2 + e_3, −2e_2 + e_3}, with simple roots α_1 = e_2 − e_1 (the compact root) and α_2 = −2e_2 + e_3, and ρ = (−2, −1; 0). Printed: positive roots {e_1 − e_2, −2e_1 + e_3, −e_1 − e_2 + e_3, −2e_2 + e_3}, α_1 = e_1 − e_2, α_2 = −2e_2 + e_3, ρ = (−1, −2; 0).
items.note: The general root datum is planned in Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups Layer 7, but no layer states the GSp4 root datum in these coordinates (PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20/thm-root-datum-of-gsp4-in-coordinates: missing, routed to D5). I checked the correction on the p. 20 image. In the printed positive system, −2e2+e3 = 2(e1−e2) + (−2e1+e3), so the printed α2 is not simple there, while the printed ρ = (−1,−2;0) does match that system. The corrected system {e2−e1, −2e1+e3, −e1−e2+e3, −2e2+e3} has simple roots e2−e1 and −2e2+e3 and ρ = (−2,−1;0). Its dominance condition λ2−λ1 ≥ 0 ≥ λ2 agrees with the holomorphic condition 0 ≥ λ2 > λ1 of §5.1.6.

items.name: Cocharacter lattice, dual basis and coroots of GSp_4 (corrected)
items.statement: X_*(T) = {(b_1, b_2; d) ∈ ½Z^3 : b_1 + d ∈ Z, b_2 + d ∈ Z}, acting by (b_1, b_2; d)·t = diag(t^{b_1+d}, t^{b_2+d}, t^{−b_2+d}, t^{−b_1+d}); the pairing with X^*(T) is ⟨(a_1, a_2; c), (b_1, b_2; d)⟩ = a_1b_1 + a_2b_2 + cd, and f_1 = (1, 0; 0), f_2 = (0, 1; 0), f_3 = (−½, −½; ½) is the basis dual to e_1, e_2, e_3. For the corrected base, α_1^∨ = f_2 − f_1 and α_2^∨ = −f_2, Δ^∨ = {α_1^∨, α_2^∨}, and (X^*(T), Δ, X_*(T), Δ^∨) is the based root datum of GSp_4. Printed: α_1^∨ = f_1 − f_2, α_2^∨ = f_2.
items.note: X_*(T) and the pairing are planned (Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups Layer 4) and partly in the library (tauceti:TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.cocharPoints, Cocharacter.lean:107; tauceti:TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.pairing, :172). The coroots and the based root datum of GSp4 in coordinates are planned nowhere. I checked: ⟨−2e2+e3, f2⟩ = −2, so the printed α2^∨ = f2 has the wrong sign whichever positive system is chosen. With the corrected base, α1^∨ = f2−f1 and α2^∨ = −f2 pair to 2 with α1 and α2.

items.name: GSp_4 is its own Langlands dual: the isomorphism i
items.statement: The map i: X^*(T) → X_*(T) with matrix ((1,1,1),(1,0,1),(1,1,2)) in the bases e_1, e_2, e_3 and f_1, f_2, f_3 (i(e_1) = f_1 + f_2 + f_3, i(e_2) = f_1 + f_3, i(e_3) = f_1 + f_2 + 2f_3) is an isomorphism of root data (X^*(T), Φ, X_*(T), Φ^∨) ≅ (X_*(T), Φ^∨, X^*(T), Φ); for the corrected base it is based (i(α_1) = −f_2 = α_2^∨, i(α_2) = f_2 − f_1 = α_1^∨). It induces an identification of the dual group of GSp_4 with GSp_4(C).
items.note: ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.5 plans 'a pinned split dual group over ℤ from the dual root datum'. The explicit self-duality i of GSp4 (Roberts–Schmidt, Lemma 2.3.1) is planned nowhere. I checked with the printed matrix (columns are the images): i(−2e2+e3) = f2−f1 and i(e2−e1) = −f2, as the item says. External input: B. Roberts, R. Schmidt, Local newforms for GSp(4), LNM 1918 (reference [65]), Lemma 2.3.1

items.name: Parabolic subgroups P_W; Klingen and Siegel parabolics
items.statement: For a totally isotropic direct factor W ⊂ V, P_W is the parabolic subgroup of GSp_4 stabilizing W (printed 'stabilizes P_W'), U_W its unipotent radical and M_W its Levi quotient; M_W = M_{W,l} × M_{W,h} with M_{W,l} = GL(W) and M_{W,h} the group of symplectic similitudes of W^⊥/W (M_{W,h} = G_m when W = W^⊥). W = ⟨e_1⟩ gives the Klingen parabolic P_Kli with M_Kli ≅ G_m × GL_2; W = ⟨e_1, e_2⟩ gives the Siegel parabolic P_Si with M_Si ≅ GL_2 × G_m. Remark 5.1.2.1: with g_C, p_Si, m_Si the Lie algebras of GSp_4/C, P_Si, M_Si, the positive compact root lies in m_Si and the positive non-compact roots in g_C/p_Si.
items.note: Same status as CG-20's Siegel and Klingen parabolic items. Remark 5.1.2.1 (compact roots in m_Si, noncompact roots in g_C/p_Si) depends on the positive system, which is missing (see gsp4-positive-roots-simple-roots-rho). Printed 'stabilizes P_W' should read 'stabilizes W'.

items.name: Spherical Hecke algebra H_ℓ of GSp_4 and the operators T_{ℓ,i}
items.statement: For a prime ℓ, GSp_4(Z_ℓ) ⊂ GSp_4(Q_ℓ) is a (hyperspecial) maximal compact subgroup, and H_ℓ = C_c^0(GSp_4(Q_ℓ)//GSp_4(Z_ℓ), Z). It is a commutative algebra isomorphic to Z[T_{ℓ,0}, T_{ℓ,0}^{−1}, T_{ℓ,1}, T_{ℓ,2}], generated by the characteristic functions of the double cosets T_{ℓ,2} = GSp_4(Z_ℓ)diag(ℓ, ℓ, 1, 1)GSp_4(Z_ℓ), T_{ℓ,1} = GSp_4(Z_ℓ)diag(ℓ², ℓ, ℓ, 1)GSp_4(Z_ℓ), T_{ℓ,0} = ℓGSp_4(Z_ℓ).
items.note: The integral spherical Hecke algebra and the double-coset operators are planned. The presentation H_ℓ ≅ Z[T0^{±1}, T1, T2] is a GSp4 instance of SR.4's integral Satake theory. SR.4 names only 'split tori and GL_n' as explicit verifications, so its blueprint should add the GSp4 example. §15.2 (p. 107) works with the abstract Hecke algebra H^{Np} = ⊗'_{ℓ∤Np} H_ℓ, the restricted tensor product of these spherical Hecke algebras over the primes ℓ ∤ Np (N the product of the primes ℓ with K_ℓ ≠ GSp_4(Z_ℓ)). The paper names it without writing out this formula; it is the analogue of H^N = ⊗'_{ℓ∤N} H_ℓ of §5.3 (p. 24, see hecke-algebra-action-on-coherent-cohomology), and its action on the p-adic complexes comes from §15.1 (p. 106). The Hecke polynomial Q_ℓ(X) of §5.1.3 is recorded in hecke-polynomial-gsp4.

items.name: The Hecke polynomial Q_ℓ(X)
items.note: IHG.3 plans only the GL_n polynomial: 'Do not assert this GL_n polynomial for a general reductive group without choosing a representation of its L-group.' This matches PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20/hecke-polynomial-Q-x, which was marked missing and routed to IHG.

items.name: Twisted Satake isomorphism; Θ(Q_ℓ(X)) = det(1 − X c_Θ)
items.statement: There is a twisted Satake isomorphism H_ℓ ⊗ C ≅ C[X_*(T)]^W, W the Weyl group of GSp_4 acting on X_*(T). To a homomorphism Θ_ℓ: H_ℓ → C it associates (via the identification of the dual group with GSp_4(C)) a semisimple conjugacy class c_{Θ_ℓ} ⊂ GSp_4(C), and Θ_ℓ(Q_ℓ(X)) = det(1 − X c_{Θ_ℓ}) (standard 4-dimensional representation). Remark 5.1.5.1: for spherical π_ℓ, c_{Θ_{π_ℓ}} is the class attached to π_ℓ ⊗ |ν|^{−3/2} by the usual (untwisted) Satake isomorphism.
items.note: SR.4 plans the Satake isomorphism, including 'the integral unnormalized form', and 'Identify Hecke eigencharacters with unramified semisimple parameters'. The GSp4 identity Θ(Q_ℓ(X)) = det(1 − X c_Θ), through the identification of the dual group with GSp4(C), is not planned, because Q_ℓ is missing. External input: A. Genestier, J. Tilouine, Système de Taylor–Wiles pour GSp4, Astérisque 302 (2005) (reference [25]), p. 193 and Remark 3 on p. 196

items.name: Klingen parahoric Kli(ℓ) and the algebra H^+_{Kli(ℓ)} with operators U_{Kli(ℓ),i}
items.statement: Kli(ℓ) ⊂ GSp_4(Z_ℓ) is the Klingen parahoric subgroup of elements whose reduction mod ℓ lies in P_Kli(F_ℓ). H^+_{Kli(ℓ)} is the subalgebra of C_c^0(GSp_4(Q_ℓ)//Kli(ℓ), Z) generated by the double cosets U_{Kli(ℓ),2} = Kli(ℓ)diag(ℓ, ℓ, 1, 1)Kli(ℓ), U_{Kli(ℓ),1} = Kli(ℓ)diag(ℓ², ℓ, ℓ, 1)Kli(ℓ), U_{Kli(ℓ),0} = ℓKli(ℓ); the paper asserts it is a polynomial algebra in these variables.
items.note: The Klingen parahoric itself is planned (ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.3; CG-20/parahoric-subgroups-P-Pi-I planned). The algebra H^+_{Kli(ℓ)}, its U-operators, and the claim that it is polynomial are planned nowhere (compare CG-20/remark-gsp4-parahoric-oldforms, missing).

items.name: Hecke parameters of a spherical representation
items.statement: Let π_ℓ be an irreducible complex smooth admissible representation of GSp_4(Q_ℓ) which is spherical (π_ℓ^{GSp_4(Z_ℓ)} ≠ 0, necessarily one-dimensional), and Θ_{π_ℓ}: H_ℓ → C the corresponding character. The Hecke parameters of π_ℓ are the W-orbit of (α, β, γ, δ), the roots of the reciprocal polynomial of Θ_{π_ℓ}(Q_ℓ(X)) (i.e. Θ_{π_ℓ}(Q_ℓ(X)) = (1 − αX)(1 − βX)(1 − γX)(1 − δX)), ordered so that αδ = βγ; then diag(α, β, γ, δ) represents c_{Θ_{π_ℓ}}, and W acts on such quadruples with orbit all diagonal representatives of c_{Θ_{π_ℓ}}.
items.note: SR.4 plans unramified parameters in general. The GSp4 definition through Q_ℓ, with the ordering αδ = βγ, is not planned.

items.name: Lemma 5.1.5.1: eigenvalues of T_{ℓ,0}, T_{ℓ,1}, T_{ℓ,2} in terms of Hecke parameters
items.statement: For π_ℓ spherical with Hecke parameters (α, β, γ, δ) (αδ = βγ), the eigenvalues of T_{ℓ,0}, T_{ℓ,1}, T_{ℓ,2} on π_ℓ^{GSp_4(Z_ℓ)} are respectively ℓ^{−3}αδ, ℓ^{−1}(αβ + αγ + αδ + βδ + γδ) − ℓ^{−3}αδ, and α + β + γ + δ.
items.note: This GSp4 computation is planned nowhere.

items.name: Generic spherical representations and their characterization
items.statement: A spherical irreducible smooth admissible representation π_ℓ of GSp_4(Q_ℓ) is generic if it is an irreducible (unramified) principal series representation. With Hecke parameters (α, β, γ, δ), this is equivalent to: ξ^{−1}ξ' ≠ ℓ for all ξ, ξ' ∈ {α, β, γ, δ}.
items.note: SR.2 plans parabolic induction in general. The GSp4 irreducibility criterion ξ^{-1}ξ' ≠ ℓ is not planned. The source is cited as '[24], prop. 3.2.3', but [24] is Gan–Takeda in this version; Genestier–Tilouine [25] is meant (compare CG-20/ext-genestier-tilouine-unramified-at-TW-primes, missing, routed to SR). External input: Equivalence cited as '[24], prop. 3.2.3' (reference [24] is Gan–Takeda in this version; apparently Genestier–Tilouine [25], Prop. 3.2.3 is meant — see mistakes)

items.name: Proposition 5.1.5.1: Klingen-invariants of a generic spherical representation
items.statement: Let π_ℓ be a generic spherical representation of GSp_4(Q_ℓ) with Hecke parameters (α, β, γ, δ). Then π_ℓ^{Kli(ℓ)} is 4-dimensional, and the eigenvalues of (U_{Kli(ℓ),0}, U_{Kli(ℓ),1}, U_{Kli(ℓ),2}) acting on π_ℓ^{Kli(ℓ)} are the Weyl orbit of (ℓ^{−3}αδ, ℓ^{−1}αβ, α + β) (i.e. U_{Kli(ℓ),1} has eigenvalues ℓ^{−1}αβ, ℓ^{−1}αγ, ℓ^{−1}βδ, ℓ^{−1}γδ).
items.note: Planned nowhere; the same gap as CG-20/remark-gsp4-parahoric-oldforms and ext-borel-casselman. External input: Cited as '[24], coro. 3.2.2' (apparently Genestier–Tilouine, Astérisque 302, Cor. 3.2.2; HAL v3 cites the same corollary to Genestier–Tilouine)

items.name: Hecke parameters of a representation with Klingen-fixed vectors
items.statement: Let π_ℓ be an irreducible complex smooth admissible representation of GSp_4(Q_ℓ) with π_ℓ^{Kli(ℓ)} ≠ 0. Then there is (α, β, γ, δ) ∈ C^4 with αδ = βγ (printed 'αβ = γδ') such that π_ℓ^{Kli(ℓ)} contains a simultaneous eigenvector for U_{Kli(ℓ),0}, U_{Kli(ℓ),1}, U_{Kli(ℓ),2} with eigenvalues ℓ^{−3}αδ, ℓ^{−1}αβ, α + β. The W-orbit of (α, β, γ, δ) is again called the Hecke parameters of π_ℓ.
items.note: Planned nowhere. Printed 'αβ = γδ' should read 'αδ = βγ'.

items.name: Proposition 5.1.5.2: regular Klingen parameters force generic spherical
items.statement: Let π_ℓ be an irreducible complex smooth admissible representation of GSp_4(Q_ℓ) with π_ℓ^{Kli(ℓ)} ≠ 0 and Hecke parameters (α, β, γ, δ). Assume ξ^{−1}ξ' ≠ ℓ for all ξ, ξ' ∈ {α, β, γ, δ}. Then π_ℓ is a generic spherical representation with Hecke parameters (α, β, γ, δ).
items.note: Planned nowhere. This is Genestier–Tilouine Prop. 3.2.3, cited as [24]. External input: Cited as '[24], prop. 3.2.3' (apparently Genestier–Tilouine, Prop. 3.2.3)

items.name: Lemma 5.1.5.2: spherical line ≅ the ℓ^{−1}αβ-eigenline of U_{Kli(ℓ),1}
items.statement: Let π_ℓ be a generic spherical representation with Hecke parameters (α, β, γ, δ); let (π_ℓ^{Kli(ℓ)})_{αβ} be the ℓ^{−1}αβ-eigenspace of U_{Kli(ℓ),1} in π_ℓ^{Kli(ℓ)} and π_{αβ}: π_ℓ^{Kli(ℓ)} → (π_ℓ^{Kli(ℓ)})_{αβ} the projection along the other eigenspaces. Assume the set {αβ, βδ, αγ, γδ} has 4 distinct elements. Then the composite π_ℓ^{GSp_4(Z_ℓ)} ⊂ π_ℓ^{Kli(ℓ)} →^{π_{αβ}} (π_ℓ^{Kli(ℓ)})_{αβ} is an isomorphism (of one-dimensional spaces).
items.note: Planned nowhere. External input: Injectivity from '[24], corollary 3.2.2' (apparently Genestier–Tilouine, Cor. 3.2.2)

items.name: (Limits of) discrete series π(λ, C) of GSp_4(R) and their parameters
items.statement: Given λ = (λ_1, λ_2; c) ∈ X^*(T) + (−1, −2; 0) ⊂ X^*(T)_C with −λ_1 ≥ λ_2 > λ_1 [printed '−λ_1 ≥ λ_2 ≥ λ_1', which admits the compact wall λ_2 = λ_1, where there is no (limit of) discrete series; sourceIssues E23] and a Weyl chamber C positive for λ, there is a (limit of) discrete series representation π(λ, C) ([28], 3.3); its infinitesimal character is the W-orbit of λ. If moreover λ_2 ≠ 0 and λ_2 ≠ −λ_1, λ determines C uniquely and π(λ, C) is a discrete series. The central character is normalized by c = −λ_1 − λ_2 + 3.
items.note: AF.1 plans only (g,K)-module foundations. Harish-Chandra's π(λ, C) for GSp4(R) is planned nowhere (CG-20/harish-chandra-parameterization, missing, routed to AF). The printed region '−λ1 ≥ λ2 ≥ λ1' includes the compact wall λ2 = λ1, which carries no (limit of) discrete series; the statement uses the strict inequality λ2 > λ1, after which the uniqueness sentence is correct as printed (sourceIssues E23). §15.2.1 (p. 107) restates this definition with the coset X^*(T) + (2, 1; 0). This is the same coset as X^*(T) + (−1, −2; 0), because (3, 3; 0) ∈ X^*(T) (X^*(T) = {(a_1, a_2; c) : c ≡ a_1 + a_2 mod 2}, p. 20). There the region is printed '−λ_1 ≥ λ_2 > −λ_1', which is empty; it should read −λ_1 ≥ λ_2 > λ_1 (sourceIssues E151). §15.2.1 then uses only the case λ_2 = 0 > λ_1. External input: M. Harris, Automorphic forms and the cohomology of vector bundles on Shimura varieties (reference [28]), 3.3 (construction of π(λ, C))

items.name: Harish-Chandra isomorphism and infinitesimal characters
items.statement: Let 𝔷 be the centre of the enveloping algebra U(g). The Harish-Chandra isomorphism identifies 𝔷 with the W-invariant polynomial functions on X^*(T)_C, i.e. Sym(X_*(T) ⊗ C)^W (printed 'C[X_*(T)]^W'; sourceIssues E25), so infinitesimal characters are W-orbits in X^*(T)_C; the infinitesimal character of π(λ, C) is W·λ.
items.note: Tau Ceti plans the semisimple case; gsp4 is sp4 plus a centre, a routine extension. Mathlib has UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra but no Harish-Chandra isomorphism. The clause about the infinitesimal character of π(λ, C) depends on the missing limits-of-discrete-series-gsp4. The printed 'C[X_*(T)]^W' should be the W-invariant polynomial functions on X*(T)_C (sourceIssues E25). The paper restates the Harish-Chandra isomorphism and the infinitesimal character of π(λ, C) in §15.2.1, p. 107, in the same notation. External input: Harish-Chandra isomorphism, recalled in Faltings–Chai [18], p. 229

items.name: Holomorphic (limit of) discrete series
items.statement: If 0 ≥ λ_2 > λ_1 and C is the dominant chamber for the positive roots of §5.1.1 (in the corrected convention, positive system {e_2 − e_1, −2e_1 + e_3, −e_1 − e_2 + e_3, −2e_2 + e_3}), π(λ, C) is called a holomorphic (limit of) discrete series; it is a limit of discrete series exactly when λ_2 = 0.
items.note: Planned nowhere (compare CG-20/def-5-7-regular-and-lds-weights, missing, routed to AF).

items.name: Theorem 5.1.7.1 (1): the Hecke eigenvalues of a discrete series cusp form generate a number field
items.statement: Let π = π_∞ ⊗ π_f be a cuspidal automorphic representation of GSp_4 such that π_∞ = π(λ, C) is in the discrete series with λ = (λ_1, λ_2; −λ_1 − λ_2 + 3). Let N be the product of the primes ℓ at which π_ℓ is not spherical, H^N = ⊗'_{ℓ∤N} H_ℓ, and Θ_π: H^N → C the character by which H^N acts on ⊗_{ℓ∤N} π_ℓ^{GSp_4(Z_ℓ)}. Then the image of Θ_π generates a number field E.
items.note: A discrete-series π_∞ = π(λ, C) is cohomological, so part (1) is an instance of AF.4's rationality statement. The GSp4 instance still has to be checked in AF.4's blueprint. Parts (2)–(5) are missing. External input: R. Taylor [77], G. Laumon [47], R. Weissauer [84], E. Urban [80]; for general type also C. Sorensen [73] completed by C.-P. Mok [54] and Chenevier–Harris [13]

items.name: Theorem 5.1.7.1 (2): existence of ρ_{π,λ} and unramified local–global compatibility
items.statement: With π, N, Θ_π, E as in Theorem 5.1.7.1 (1): for every finite place λ of E there is a semisimple continuous Galois representation ρ_{π,λ}: G_Q → GSp_4(Ē_λ), unramified away from N and the prime p below λ, such that for all primes ℓ ∤ Np, det(1 − Xρ_{π,λ}(Frob_ℓ)) = Θ_π(Q_ℓ(X)) (Frob_ℓ a geometric Frobenius).
items.note: No layer attaches Galois representations to cuspidal representations of GSp4 (CG-20/ext-mok-galois-reps-for-GSp4 and galois-rep-of-regular-weight-cuspidal-eigenform, missing, routed to AG2). The paper's second proof, via the lift to GL4 (Sorensen, Mok, Chenevier–Harris), runs through AG2's GL_n systems. External input: Taylor [77], Laumon [47], Weissauer [84], Urban [80]; Sorensen [73], Mok [54], Chenevier–Harris [13]

items.name: Theorem 5.1.7.1 (3): ρ_{π,λ} is de Rham with Hodge–Tate weights (0, −λ_2, −λ_1, −λ_1 − λ_2)
items.statement: With π as in Theorem 5.1.7.1, ρ_{π,λ} is de Rham at p with Hodge–Tate weights (0, −λ_2, −λ_1, −λ_1 − λ_2) (cyclotomic character of Hodge–Tate weight −1).
items.note: Planned nowhere for GSp4 (CG-20/galois-rep-crystalline-at-p, missing). External input: Taylor [77], Laumon [47], Weissauer [84], Urban [80]

items.name: Theorem 5.1.7.1 (4): crystallinity at p ∤ N and the crystalline characteristic polynomial
items.statement: With π as in Theorem 5.1.7.1, if p ∤ N then ρ_{π,λ} is crystalline at p and det(1 − Xφ | D_crys(ρ_{π,λ})) = Θ_π(Q_p(X)).
items.note: Planned nowhere for GSp4. External input: Taylor [77], Laumon [47], Weissauer [84], Urban [80]

items.name: Theorem 5.1.7.1 (5): symplectic self-duality up to twist
items.statement: With π as in Theorem 5.1.7.1, ρ_{π,λ} ≅ ρ_{π,λ}^∨ ⊗ χ_p^{λ1+λ2} ω_{π,λ} for some finite-order character ω_{π,λ}. Here χ_p is the p-adic cyclotomic character, of Hodge–Tate weight −1. Equivalently, ν∘ρ_{π,λ} = χ_p^{λ1+λ2}ω_{π,λ}. (Printed: χ_p^{−λ1−λ2}, which is inconsistent with part (3).)
items.note: Planned nowhere for GSp4. AG2.2 recovers polarizations only for GL_n systems. External input: Taylor [77], Laumon [47], Weissauer [84], Urban [80]

items.name: Remark 5.1.7.1: normalizations of Galois representations
items.statement: Geometric Frobenii are used. Artin reciprocity is normalized by sending p to the geometric Frobenius at p, and the cyclotomic character has Hodge–Tate weight −1. ρ_{π,λ} is the Galois representation attached to the L-algebraic automorphic representation π ⊗ |ν|^{−3/2} (Buzzard–Gee [10], Conj. 3.2.2); the twist by |ν|^{−3/2} matches the twisted Satake isomorphism. The Hodge–Tate weights are given by the infinitesimal character (λ1, λ2; −λ1 − λ2) of π_∞ ⊗ |ν|^{−3/2}, and the Hodge cocharacter is t ↦ diag(1, t^{−λ1}, t^{−λ2}, t^{−λ1−λ2}). For consistency with these conventions and Theorem 5.1.7.1 (3), the central character of π ⊗ |ν|^{−3/2} is |·|^{λ1+λ2} ⊗ ω_π with ω_π of finite order (printed |·|^{−λ1−λ2}). ω_{π,λ} is the λ-adic character of G_Q attached to ω_π by class field theory, so ν∘ρ_{π,λ} = χ_p^{λ1+λ2}ω_{π,λ}.

items.name: Arthur's classification: ρ_{π,λ} is reducible unless π is of general type
items.statement: π is of general type if it has a transfer (printed 'base change') to a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_4. By Arthur's classification, π as in Theorem 5.1.7.1 falls into six categories; if π is not of general type, ρ_{π,λ} is reducible: it is a sum of Galois representations attached to algebraic automorphic forms on GL_1 (cases e), f)), a sum of ones attached to algebraic forms on GL_1 and regular algebraic forms on GL_2 (cases c), d)), or a sum of ones attached to regular algebraic forms on GL_2 (case b)). If π is of general type, ρ_{π,λ} is expected to be irreducible.
items.locator: §5.1.7, paragraph after Remark 5.1.7.1 and footnote 4, p. 23
items.note: Arthur's GSp4 classification is not among ML.4's named sources (CG-20/ext-arthur-gsp4-classification, missing, routed to ML.4). Printed 'base change' means transfer to GL4. External input: J. Arthur, Automorphic forms for GSp_4 (reference [1])

items.name: Siegel datum and the complex Siegel threefold S_K
items.statement: h: Res_{C/R}G_m → GSp_4/R, h(a + ib) = a·1_4 + bJ; K_∞ ⊂ GSp_4(R) is the centralizer of the image of h, and H = GSp_4(R)/K_∞ is the Siegel space. For a neat compact open subgroup K ⊂ GSp_4(A_f), S_K = GSp_4(Q)\H × GSp_4(A_f)/K is the complex analytic Siegel threefold of level K; it is a moduli space of abelian surfaces with additional structures (Laumon [47], sect. 3).
items.note: Compare CG-20/complex-uniformization (planned: V1, M3, A5).

items.name: Remark 5.2.1.1: Hodge decomposition of g and the choice of positive roots
items.statement: ad(h) defines a Hodge structure on g_R with g_C = g^{(0,0)} ⊕ g^{(−1,1)} ⊕ g^{(1,−1)}; set p_h = g^{(0,0)} ⊕ g^{(1,−1)}. The parabolic p_h is conjugate to p_Si by some g ∈ GSp_4(C) (printed 'g ∈ g_C'), and the positive roots lie in Ad(g)(g^{(0,0)} ⊕ g^{(−1,1)}).
items.note: The Hodge decomposition of g_C and p_h are planned in ShimuraData D2/D3 (CG-20/def-hodge-decomposition-and-p-plus-minus). The point of the remark, that the positive system of §5.1.1 lies in Ad(g)(g^{(0,0)} ⊕ g^{(−1,1)}), is planned nowhere (CG-20/def-compact-noncompact-roots-and-positive-system, missing, routed to AF). Printed 'g ∈ g_C' should read g ∈ GSp4(C).

items.name: Minimal compactification S_K^* and its boundary strata
items.statement: S_K^* is the minimal compactification of S_K (Pink [64], sect. 3), with stratification S_K^* = S_K ⊔ S_K^{(1)} ⊔ S_K^{(0)}. With H^{(1)} = C \ R and H^{(0)} = {1, −1}: S_K^{(1)} = P_Kli(Q)\H^{(1)} × G(A_f)/K is a union of modular curves and S_K^{(0)} = P_Si(Q)\H^{(0)} × G(A_f)/K is the union of their cusps; P_Kli(Q) and P_Si(Q) act diagonally, on H^{(1)} and H^{(0)} through M_{Kli,h}(Q) and M_{Si,h}(Q). S_K^{(1),*} = S_K^{(1)} ⊔ S_K^{(0)} is a union of compactified modular curves.
items.note: The Siegel threefold strata (modular curves and cusps) are an instance. The proof of Corollary 15.2.3.1 (p. 109) recalls this stratification and uses the projection π: S^tor_{K,Σ} → S^*_K from the toroidal to the minimal compactification, which induces a projection D → S^{(1),*}_K of the boundary divisor onto the union of compactified modular curves. External input: R. Pink, On l-adic sheaves on Shimura varieties and their higher direct images in the Baily–Borel compactification, Math. Ann. 292 (1992) (reference [64]), sect. 3

items.name: Toroidal compactifications S^tor_{K,Σ} and the semi-abelian surface G
items.statement: For an auxiliary polyhedral cone decomposition Σ one has a toroidal compactification S^tor_{K,Σ} of S_K, over which there is a semi-abelian surface G → S^tor_{K,Σ} extending the universal abelian surface.
items.note: Compare CG-20/toroidal-compactification-hodge-bundle (planned: C5, C3). External input: M. Harris, Functorial properties of toroidal compactifications of locally symmetric varieties, Proc. LMS 59 (1989) (reference [29]), sect. 2

items.name: Automorphic vector bundles Ω^{(k,r)}, boundary divisor D and cuspidal subsheaf
items.statement: ω_G → S^tor_{K,Σ} is the conormal sheaf of the semi-abelian surface G along the unit section; it is locally free of rank 2. For (k, r) ∈ Z_{≥0} × Z, Ω^{(k,r)} = Sym^k ω_G ⊗ det^r ω_G. D_{K,Σ} = S^tor_{K,Σ} \ S_K (printed 'S^tor_{K,Σ} \ S_{K,Σ}') is a Cartier divisor, and Ω^{(k,r)}(−D_{K,Σ}) (also written Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) is the cuspidal subsheaf of Ω^{(k,r)}. The paper's main focus is r = 2 and the groups H^i(S^tor_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)), i ∈ {0, 1}.
items.note: Same status as CG-20/automorphic-bundles-omega-a-b.

items.name: Independence of coherent cohomology from the cone decomposition
items.statement: The coherent cohomology groups H^i(S^tor_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) are independent of the choice of Σ.
items.note: B3 plans only 'independence of spaces of sections from the chosen sufficiently fine admissible fan'. Independence of all H^i needs Rπ_*O = O for refinements. C3 leaves that as a separately stated theorem, and AUDIT-10 records it as absent. This is the same decision as CG-20/coherent-cohomology-independent-of-compactification (missing, routed to C3). External input: M. Harris, Automorphic forms of ∂̄-cohomology type as coherent cohomology classes, J. Diff. Geom. 32 (1990) (reference [30]), Prop. 2.4

items.name: Holomorphic (limit of) discrete series cusp forms embed into H^0
items.statement: If π = π_∞ ⊗ π_f is cuspidal automorphic with π_∞ = π(λ, C) a holomorphic (limit of) discrete series, λ = (λ_1, λ_2; −λ_1 − λ_2 + 3) (so 0 ≥ λ_2 > λ_1), there is a natural embedding π_f^K ⊂ H^0(S^tor_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(λ_2−λ_1−1, 2−λ_2)}(−D)).
items.note: B4 plans classical forms as sections, with the transformation-law comparison. The passage from an automorphic representation with holomorphic (limit of) discrete series π_∞ to H^0 is not planned. Compare CG-20/thm-5-2-1 and automorphic-representation-of-eigenform, both routed to IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes layer 6.

items.name: Decomposition of H^0(S^tor, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) for r ≥ 2
items.statement: For all k ≥ 0 and r ≥ 2, H^0(S^tor_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) = ⊕_{π_f} π_f^K, where π_f runs over the admissible representations of GSp_4(A_f) such that π(λ, C) ⊗ π_f is cuspidal automorphic for λ = (1 − k − r, 2 − r; k + 2r) (printed '1 − k + r') and π(λ, C) the holomorphic (limit of) discrete series.
items.locator: §5.3, p. 24 (the case r ≥ 3 is restated in the proof of Theorem 5.3.1, p. 25)
items.note: Planned nowhere. It uses Schmidt's classification of lowest-weight representations. Printed '1 − k + r' should read 1 − k − r; this is confirmed by p. 25 and by λ2 − λ1 − 1 = k. External input: Deduced from the description of representations with a lowest weight in R. Schmidt, Archimedean aspects of Siegel modular forms of degree 2 (reference [67]), p. 12, diagram (44)

items.name: Action of the prime-to-N Hecke algebra on coherent cohomology
items.statement: Let N be the product of the primes ℓ with K_ℓ ≠ GSp_4(Z_ℓ) and H^N = ⊗'_{ℓ∤N} H_ℓ. Then H^N acts on H^i(S^tor_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,r)}) and on H^i(S^tor_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)).
items.note: B5 plans Hecke pullback and trace on sections in characteristic 0. Hecke actions on H^i for i > 0, and on the cuspidal sheaves over toroidal compactifications, are planned nowhere. AUDIT-13: 'no coherent pullback/trace'. Compare CG-20/hecke-operators-T-x-i, routed to IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes. External input: M. Harris [30], Prop. 2.6

items.name: Normalized Hecke operators T_{ℓ,i} on coherent cohomology via cohomological correspondences
items.statement: For ℓ ∤ N and i ∈ {0, 1, 2}, let d_{ℓ,i} be the diagonal matrix defining the double coset T_{ℓ,i} and K(ℓ, i) = K ∩ d_{ℓ,i}^{−1}Kd_{ℓ,i}. For suitable cone decompositions Σ, Σ', Σ'' there is a Hecke correspondence p_2: S^tor_{K(ℓ,i),Σ''} → S^tor_{K,Σ'}, p_1: S^tor_{K(ℓ,i),Σ''} → S^tor_{K,Σ} (Faltings–Chai [18], p. 253) with an isogeny p_1^*G → p_2^*G whose differential gives p_2^*Ω^{(k,r)} → p_1^*Ω^{(k,r)}. Tensoring with the fundamental class p_1^*O → p_1^!O of p_1 (Construction 1) gives a cohomological correspondence T'_{ℓ,i}: p_2^*Ω^{(k,r)} → p_1^!Ω^{(k,r)} (printed 'p_1^!O_{S^tor_{K,Σ}}'). Set T_{ℓ,2} = ℓ^{−3}T'_{ℓ,2} and T_{ℓ,i} = ℓ^{−6}T'_{ℓ,i} for i ∈ {0, 1}; the same names denote the induced operators on H^i(S^tor, Ω^{(k,r)}) and (by Lemma 4.2.4.1) on H^i(S^tor, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)).
items.note: C3 plans the toroidal Hecke correspondences: 'For a morphism of data or a Hecke translation, choose compatible source and target fans and construct the extension'. The fundamental-class construction and the normalizations ℓ^{-3} and ℓ^{-6} are planned nowhere. Printed 'p_1^!O' should read p_1^!Ω^{(k,r)}.

items.name: Theorem 5.3.1: Galois representations attached to Hecke eigensystems in coherent cohomology
items.statement: Let K ⊂ GSp_4(A_f) be neat, (k, r) ∈ Z_{≥0} × Z, N the product of primes ℓ with K_ℓ ≠ GSp_4(Z_ℓ), and let Θ: H^N → C be a system of eigenvalues of H^N (normalized as in §5.3) acting on H^i(S^tor_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,r)}) or on H^i(S^tor_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) for some i. Then the image of Θ generates a number field E, and for every finite place λ of E there is a semisimple continuous Galois representation ρ_{Θ,λ}: G_Q → GL_4(Ē_λ), unramified away from N and the prime p below λ, such that det(1 − Xρ_{Θ,λ}(Frob_ℓ)) = Θ(Q_ℓ(X)) for all ℓ ∤ Np.
items.note: Theorem 5.3.1, for eigensystems in all degrees and all weights, rests on Taylor [76] and the Pilloni–Stroh Hasse-invariant interpolation [63]. It is planned nowhere. TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure covers Betti torsion, not coherent cohomology. The introduction (§1, p. 2) also recalls this result: the coherent realization shows that the Hecke parameters of these automorphic forms are defined over number fields, and congruences give compatible systems of 4-dimensional Galois representations, citing the same sources [76] and [63]. External input: Deduced from Theorem 5.1.7.1 using R. Taylor, Galois representations associated to Siegel modular forms of low weight, Duke Math. J. (1991) (reference [76]) and V. Pilloni, B. Stroh, Cohomologie cohérente et représentations galoisiennes, Ann. Math. Québec 40 (2016) (reference [63]), by p-adic interpolation

items.name: Cohomological weights (footnote 5)
items.statement: A weight (k, r) is cohomological if r ≠ 2, k + r ≠ 1 and k + 2r ≠ 3, i.e. the Hodge–Tate weights 0, r − 2, r + k − 1, k + 2r − 3 are pairwise distinct; then the coherent cohomology group appears in the Hodge decomposition of the cohomology of an automorphic local system on the Shimura variety.
items.note: AF.4 plans cohomological representations in general. The GSp4 condition in terms of (k, r) is not planned (compare CG-20/def-5-7-regular-and-lds-weights, missing, routed to AF).

items.name: Proposition 6.1.4.1 (1): Y_K is smooth over Z_p
items.statement: The scheme Y_K is smooth over Spec Z_p.
items.note: This is good-level smoothness.

items.name: Remark 5.3.2 (end): expected crystallinity, and the Newton polygon lying above the Hodge polygon
items.statement: (An expectation; the paper does not prove it.) Let Θ be a system of Hecke eigenvalues occurring in H^i(S^tor_{K,Σ}, Ω^(k,r)) or H^i(S^tor_{K,Σ}, Ω^(k,r)(−D)), and let ρ_{Θ,λ} be the attached Galois representation (Theorem 5.3.1). One expects ρ_{Θ,λ} to be de Rham with Hodge–Tate weights (0, r−2, r+k−1, k+2r−3), and crystalline at p if (N,p)=1. In particular, suppose (N,p)=1 and (α,β,γ,δ) are the Hecke parameters of a local representation π_p contributing to H^i(S^tor_{K,Σ}, Ω^(k,r)) or H^i(S^tor_{K,Σ}, Ω^(k,r)(−D)). Then the Newton polygon of (α,β,γ,δ) is expected to lie above the Hodge polygon with the same initial and end points. This last statement follows from the main theorem of V. Lafforgue [45] when the weight is cohomological (footnote 5: r ≠ 2, k+r ≠ 1, k+2r ≠ 3).
items.locator: §5.3, Remark 5.3.2, pp. 25–26 (only the last sentences are on p. 26)
items.note: The item has two parts. (a) The expectation (de Rham with HT weights (0, r−2, r+k−1, k+2r−3), crystalline when (N,p)=1, Newton polygon above Hodge polygon) is a conjecture in singular weight. The paper does not prove it, so it should be a conjecture predicate, not a target. (b) In cohomological weight (footnote 5: r ≠ 2, k+r ≠ 1, k+2r ≠ 3), the Newton-above-Hodge statement is V. Lafforgue's theorem [45]. It is planned nowhere. Only the last sentences of the remark are on p. 26. Remark 5.3.2 (p. 25) says that the de Rham and crystalline statement 'seems accessible' when the weight is cohomological, but the author knows no reference for it. Only the Newton-above-Hodge statement is attributed, in cohomological weight, to V. Lafforgue [45]. Footnote 5 explains the cohomological condition: it makes the Hodge–Tate weights distinct, so that the coherent cohomology group appears in the Hodge decomposition of the cohomology of an automorphic local system. External input: [45] V. Lafforgue, Estimées pour les valuations p-adiques des valeurs propres des opérateurs de Hecke, Bull. SMF 139 (2011), 455–477 (the cohomological-weight case)

items.name: The smooth Siegel threefold Y_K over Z_p (hyperspecial level at p)
items.statement: Fix a prime p. Let V = Z^4 with basis e_1,…,e_4 and the symplectic form ⟨,⟩ with matrix J = [[0,A],[−A,0]], where A is the 2×2 antidiagonal matrix with entries 1 (§5.1); GSp_4 = GSp(V,⟨,⟩). Let K ⊂ GSp_4(A_f) be a neat compact open subgroup with K = K^p K_p and K_p = GSp_4(Z_p). Y_{K,Z_(p)} → Spec Z_(p) is the moduli space representing the functor that sends a locally noetherian Z_(p)-scheme S to the set of isomorphism classes of triples (G, λ, ψ), taken up to prime-to-p quasi-isogeny, where: (1) G is an abelian surface over S; (2) λ: G → G^t is a Z_(p)^×-multiple of a polarization of degree prime to p (G^t the dual abelian scheme); (3) ψ is a K^p-level structure, i.e. for S connected with geometric point s, a K^p-orbit of symplectic similitudes H_1(G_s, A_f^p) ≃ V ⊗_Z A_f^p invariant under π_1(S,s). This is independent of s; on disconnected S one chooses a geometric point in each connected component. There is an isomorphism (Y_{K,Z_(p)} × Spec C)^an ≃ S_K. Set Y_K := Y_{K,Z_(p)} ×_{Spec Z_(p)} Spec Z_p.
items.note: This is the Siegel PEL moduli problem with hyperspecial level at p and neat K^p, with triples taken up to prime-to-p quasi-isogeny (Kottwitz [44]). The status matches PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20/siegel-threefold-Y-K (planned via M1, M2, M5). M2 gives an algebraic space; C5 makes it a scheme. The complex comparison (Y_{K,Z_(p)} × C)^an ≃ S_K is M3. The base change to Z_p is formal. External input: R. Kottwitz [44], Points on some Shimura varieties over finite fields, JAMS 5 (1992): representability

items.name: Klingen level at p: Y_Kli(p)_K and the chain G → G/H → G/H^⊥ → G
items.statement: p_1: Y_Kli(p)_K → Y_K is the moduli space of the data (G, λ, ψ) of §6.1.1 together with a (finite flat) subgroup scheme H ⊂ G[p] of order p. Over Y_Kli(p)_K there is a chain of isogenies of abelian surfaces G → G/H → G/H^⊥ → G. Here H^⊥ ⊂ G[p] is the orthogonal of H for the Weil pairing on G[p] given by the polarization, and the composite G → G is multiplication by p.
items.note: The moduli interpretation of Klingen level at p (an order-p subgroup H ⊂ G[p] and the chain G → G/H → G/H^⊥ → G) is planned nowhere. Representability as a finite scheme over Y_K would come from a Hilbert-scheme argument (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.2).

items.name: Paramodular level: Y_{par,K} and the map p_2: Y_Kli(p)_K → Y_{par,K}
items.statement: Y_{par,K} → Spec Z_p is the moduli space of isomorphism classes of triples (G', λ', ψ): G' is an abelian surface, λ': G' → (G')^t is a Z_(p)^×-multiple of a polarization of degree p^2, and ψ is a K^p-level structure. The natural map p_2: Y_Kli(p)_K → Y_{par,K} sends (G, λ, H, ψ) to (G/H^⊥, λ', ψ'). Here λ' is the polarization of G/H^⊥ obtained by descending p^2λ along G → G/H^⊥, and ψ' is induced by the isomorphisms G[N] = (G/H^⊥)[N] for every N prime to p.
items.note: The item has three parts: the moduli space Y_{par,K} over Z_p of surfaces with a Z_(p)^×-multiple of a degree-p² polarization, the descended polarization λ' of G/H^⊥, and the map p_2. The Klingen item above has the same gap.

items.name: Proposition 6.1.4.1 (ii): Y_Kli(p)_K is regular, flat and lci
items.statement: The scheme Y_Kli(p)_K is regular, and it is flat and a local complete intersection over Spec Z_p.
items.note: The proof cites Tilouine [79] §2.2 Thm 3 for the local model computation. Both the object (klingen-level-moduli-YKli) and its local model are missing. Proposition 6.1.4.1 (pp. 26–27) is an unnumbered list of claims: Y_K is smooth over Spec Z_p; Y_{par,K} and Y_Kli(p)_K are regular, flat and local complete intersections over Spec Z_p; the non-smooth locus of Y_{par,K} is a finite set of characteristic-p points. This item records the Klingen claim only. The other claims are YK-smooth-over-Zp and Ypar-regular-flat-lci-finite-nonsmooth-locus, and the paramodular local model used in the proof is paramodular-local-model-and-singularity. External input: [79] J. Tilouine, Siegel varieties and p-adic Siegel modular forms, Doc. Math. (2006), §2.2, Thm. 3 (local model computation)

items.name: Proposition 6.1.4.1 (iii): Y_{par,K} is regular, flat and lci, with finitely many singular points
items.statement: The scheme Y_{par,K} is regular, and it is flat and a local complete intersection over Spec Z_p. Its non-smooth locus is a finite set of points of characteristic p.
items.note: The proof uses the local model of paramodular-local-model-and-singularity (de Jong [17]; Yu [86] Thm 4.4). The local-model data used in the proof (V_1 = pe_1Z ⊕ e_2Z ⊕ e_3Z ⊕ e_4Z, the only singular point L_0 = ⟨pe_1, e_4⟩ ⊂ V_1 ⊗ F_p of the local model, and its formal deformation ring Z_p[[X,Y,W,Z]]/(XY − WZ + p)) is recorded in paramodular-local-model-and-singularity. External input: Local model theory: [17] A. J. de Jong, J. Algebraic Geom. 2 (1993); [86] C.-F. Yu, Kottwitz–Rapoport strata in the Siegel moduli spaces, Thm. 4.4

items.name: Local model of Y_{par,K} and its unique singularity
items.statement: Let V_1 = pe_1Z ⊕ ⊕_{i=2}^4 e_iZ ⊂ V. The local model of Y_{par,K} is the moduli space of totally isotropic direct factors L ⊂ V_1 of rank 2. Its only singular point is L_0 = ⟨pe_1, e_4⟩ ⊂ V_1 ⊗ F_p. The formal deformation ring at L_0 is Z_p[[X,Y,W,Z]]/(XY − WZ + p), and the universal deformation of L_0 is ⟨pe_1 + Xe_2 + We_3, Ze_2 + Ye_3 + e_4⟩.
items.note: This is a concrete computation: the local model is the moduli of totally isotropic rank-2 direct factors L ⊂ V_1, with singular point L_0 = ⟨pe_1, e_4⟩ and deformation ring Z_p[[X,Y,W,Z]]/(XY − WZ + p). I checked isotropy: with ⟨e_1,e_4⟩ = ⟨e_2,e_3⟩ = 1, the pairing of the two displayed generators is p + XY − WZ. External input: [17] de Jong; [86] Yu, Thm. 4.4

items.name: Arithmetic groups Γ, Γ_par, Γ_Kli(p) and the paramodular group scheme GSp'_4
items.statement: Γ = GSp_4(Z_(p))^+ is the group of automorphisms of (V ⊗ Z_(p), ⟨,⟩) up to a positive similitude factor. With V_1 = pe_1Z ⊕ ⊕_{i=2}^4 e_iZ, GSp'_4 → Spec Z is the group scheme GSp(V_1, ⟨,⟩), the paramodular group, and Γ_par = GSp'_4(Z_(p))^+ is the subgroup of GSp'_4(Z_(p)) of elements with positive similitude factor. Γ_Kli(p) is the group of automorphisms of (V_1 ⊗ Z_(p) → V ⊗ Z_(p), ⟨,⟩) up to a positive similitude factor. It is a subgroup of both Γ and Γ_par, and all three are subgroups of GSp_4(Q).
items.note: Γ_Kli(p) equals Γ ∩ Γ_par: an element preserving both V⊗Z_(p) and V_1⊗Z_(p) with a positive unit similitude factor. Passing to the '+' subgroups (positive similitude) is elementary. The groups are used as the arithmetic groups acting on the cusp data in §6.1.5.

items.name: Cusp labels 𝔆, cones C(V/W^⊥), the conical complex 𝒞 and the groups P_W, P_{W,h}
items.statement: 𝔆 is the set of totally isotropic direct factors W ⊂ V. For W ∈ 𝔆, C(V/W^⊥) is the cone of positive (semi-definite) symmetric bilinear forms V/W^⊥ × V/W^⊥ → R with radical defined over Q. 𝒞 is the quotient of ∐_{W∈𝔆} C(V/W^⊥) by the equivalence relation induced by the inclusions C(V/W^⊥) ⊂ C(V/Z^⊥) for W ⊂ Z; it carries an action of GSp_4(Q). For W ∈ 𝔆, P_W is the parabolic subgroup stabilising W. Its Levi quotient is M_W = M_{W,l} × M_{W,h}, where M_{W,l} is the linear group of W and M_{W,h} is the group of symplectic similitudes of W^⊥/W (G_m when W = W^⊥) (§5.1.2). P_{W,h} ⊂ P_W is the inverse image of M_{W,h} under P_W → M_W.
items.note: This is the standard Faltings–Chai/Lan cusp-label formalism for GSp4: isotropic direct factors W, positivity cones C(V/W^⊥), the conical complex, P_W and P_{W,h}.

items.name: Boundary charts: moduli of 1-motives M → B → Y at hyperspecial, Klingen and paramodular level, and the toroidal embeddings M̄_σ ⊃ Z_σ
items.statement:
For W ∈ 𝔆 and γ ∈ GSp_4(A_f^p)/K^p there are towers M_{W,γ} → B_{W,γ} → Y_{W,γ}, M_{W,γ,Kli(p)} → B_{W,γ,Kli(p)} → Y_{W,γ,Kli(p)} and M_{W,γ,par} → B_{W,γ,par} → Y_{W,γ,par}.
(a) M_{W,γ} is the moduli space of 1-motives with a polarization of degree prime to p, rigidified by V/W^⊥ ([74] Def. 1.4.3), with K^p-level structure (printed 'K_p'; sourceIssues E34). It is a torsor over B_{W,γ} under a torus T_{W,γ} isogenous to Sym^2(V/W^⊥) ⊗ G_m (since split tori of equal rank are isomorphic, this only fixes the rank; the equivariant description is that T_{W,γ} is isogenous to Hom(Sym^2(V/W^⊥), G_m), so its character group, not its cocharacter group, is a lattice in Sym^2(V/W^⊥) ⊗ Q; sourceIssues E36). B_{W,γ} is an abelian scheme over Y_{W,γ}, the moduli space of abelian schemes of dimension 2 − rank_Z W (printed 'rank_Z W', here and for the Kli(p) and par bases; sourceIssues E35) with a polarization of degree prime to p and level structure away from p.
(b) M_{W,γ,Kli(p)} is the same with in addition a Klingen level structure. It is a torsor under T_{W,γ,Kli(p)} (isogenous to Sym^2(V/W^⊥) ⊗ G_m) over the abelian scheme B_{W,γ,Kli(p)} → Y_{W,γ,Kli(p)}. Y_{W,γ,Kli(p)} is a moduli space of abelian schemes of that genus with a prime-to-p polarization, level away from p and possibly a Klingen level structure at p, depending on the position of W relative to V_1.
(c) M_{W,γ,par} is the moduli space of 1-motives with a polarization of degree Np^2, where (N,p)=1 and N depends on K^p; the toric part has character group ≅ V_1/W^⊥, and there is a K^p-level structure (printed 'K_p'; sourceIssues E34). It is a torsor under T_{W,γ,par} (isogenous to Sym^2(V/W^⊥) ⊗ G_m) over the abelian scheme B_{W,γ,par} → Y_{W,γ,par} (printed 'Y_{W,γ}'; sourceIssues E35, E37). Y_{W,γ,par} is a moduli space of abelian schemes of that genus with either a prime-to-p polarization or a polarization of degree a prime-to-p multiple of p^2, and level away from p.
For a cone σ ⊂ C(V/W^⊥) with affine toroidal embeddings T_{W,γ} → T_{W,γ,σ} (and likewise for Kli(p) and par), set M̄_{W,γ,σ} = M_{W,γ} ×^{T_{W,γ}} T_{W,γ,σ}, M̄_{W,γ,Kli(p),σ} and M̄_{W,γ,par,σ}. Z_{W,γ,σ}, Z_{W,γ,Kli(p),σ} and Z_{W,γ,par,σ} are the closed subschemes corresponding to the closed strata of these affine toroidal embeddings.
items.note: The item is missing only because of parts (b) and (c). Splitting (a) off would make it planned (C0, C4, C5). External input: B. Stroh [74], Bull. SMF 138 (2010), §1 (Def. 1.4.3); K.-W. Lan [48] §6.2, [49], [50]

items.name: Rational polyhedral cone decompositions: smooth, H-equivariant, H-admissible, projective
items.statement:
The set 𝒞 × GSp_4(A_f^p)/K^p carries the diagonal action of GSp_4(Q) and the action of GSp_4(A_f^p) by left translation on the second factor.
- A non-degenerate rational polyhedral cone is a subset of C(V/W^⊥) × {γ}, for some (W,γ), of the form ⊕_{i=1}^k R_{>0}s_i with s_i: V/W^⊥ × V/W^⊥ → Q symmetric pairings.
- For a Z-lattice L_W ⊂ Sym^2(V/W^⊥) ⊗_Z Q, the cone is smooth with respect to L_W if the s_i can be taken to be part of a Z-basis of Hom(L_W, Z).
- A rational polyhedral cone decomposition Σ is a partition 𝒞 × GSp_4(A_f^p)/K^p = ∐_{σ∈Σ} σ into non-degenerate rational polyhedral cones such that (1) the closure of each cone is a union of cones, and (2) if σ ∈ Σ and σ ⊂ C(V/W^⊥) × {γ}, then gσ ∈ Σ for all g ∈ P_{W,h}(A_f^p).
- For H ⊂ GSp_4(Q), Σ is H-equivariant if hσ ∈ Σ for all h ∈ H and σ ∈ Σ; H-admissible if H\Σ is finite; projective if it admits a polarization function ([50] Def. 2.4).
- Each (W,γ) has integral structures given by the tori T_{W,γ}, T_{W,γ,par} and T_{W,γ,Kli(p)}: their character groups X^⋆(T) are lattices in Sym^2(V/W^⊥) ⊗_Z Q, and their cocharacter groups X_⋆(T) = Hom(X^⋆(T), Z) are lattices in Hom(Sym^2(V/W^⊥), Q), the space of rational symmetric bilinear forms on V/W^⊥, whose real span contains C(V/W^⊥) [printed 'X_⋆(T_{W,γ}), X_⋆(T_{W,γ,par}) and X_⋆(T_{W,γ,Kli(p)}) ⊂ Sym^2(V/W^⊥) ⊗_Z Q'; sourceIssues E36]. Σ is smooth with respect to one of them if every cone of Σ is smooth with respect to L_W = X^⋆(T), i.e. its generators s_i can be taken to be part of a Z-basis of X_⋆(T).
items.note: The general notions are planned: non-degenerate rational cones, smoothness with respect to a lattice, H-equivariance, H-admissibility and projectivity via a polarization function. The integral structures X_*(T_{W,γ,par}) and X_*(T_{W,γ,Kli(p)}) come from the paramodular and Klingen boundary charts, which are missing (boundary-charts-via-1-motives). External input: Faltings–Chai [18]; Lan [50] Def. 2.4 (polarization function)

items.name: Existence, common refinements and cofinality of good admissible cone decompositions
items.statement: Let H be Γ, Γ_par or Γ_Kli(p). H-admissible rational polyhedral cone decompositions exist and are naturally ordered by inclusion (refinement), and any two have a common refinement. Those that also satisfy properties (1)–(3) of 'good' (projective; the stabiliser condition; smooth for the integral structure attached to H) form a cofinal subset of all H-admissible rational polyhedral cone decompositions.
items.note: Existence, common refinements and cofinality of projective smooth decompositions are C0's targets (Faltings–Chai [18] p. 97). The blueprint should also state the stabilizer condition (2) of 'good' explicitly, since C0 does not name it. The Γ_par and Γ_Kli(p) lattices depend on the missing boundary charts. External input: [18] G. Faltings and C.-L. Chai, Degeneration of abelian varieties, p. 97

items.name: H-admissible good polyhedral cone decomposition
items.note: C0 covers conditions (1) (projective) and (3) (smooth with respect to a given lattice). Condition (2) (h ∈ H ∩ P_W with hgσ ∩ σ ≠ ∅ acts trivially on C(V/W^⊥)) is the Faltings–Chai admissibility condition and is not named in C0; the C0 blueprint must include it. Condition (3) for Γ_par and Γ_Kli(p) uses the lattices X_*(T_{W,γ,par}) and X_*(T_{W,γ,Kli(p)}) from the missing boundary charts.

items.name: Theorem 6.1.5.1(1): toroidal compactifications of Y_K, Y_Kli(p)_K and Y_{par,K}, with strata, formal charts and Cartier boundary
items.statement:
Let Σ be a good polyhedral cone decomposition which is Γ-admissible (resp. Γ_Kli(p)-, resp. Γ_par-admissible). Then there is a toroidal compactification X_{K,Σ} of Y_K (resp. X_Kli(p)_{K,Σ} of Y_Kli(p)_K, resp. X_{par,K,Σ} of Y_{par,K}) over Z_p, with a stratification indexed by Γ\Σ (resp. Γ_Kli(p)\Σ, resp. Γ_par\Σ). For σ ∈ Σ with σ ⊂ C(V/W^⊥) × {γ}:
- the (σ,γ)-stratum is isomorphic to Z_{W,γ,σ} (resp. Z_{W,γ,Kli(p),σ}, resp. Z_{W,γ,par,σ}), with the 'resp.' order corrected from the printed text;
- the completion of the compactification along this stratum is isomorphic to the completion of M̄_{W,γ,σ} along Z_{W,γ,σ} (resp. M̄_{W,γ,Kli(p),σ} along Z_{W,γ,Kli(p),σ}, resp. M̄_{W,γ,par,σ} along Z_{W,γ,par,σ}).
The boundary D, the reduced complement of Y_K in X_{K,Σ} (resp. of Y_Kli(p)_K, resp. Y_{par,K}), is a relative Cartier divisor.
items.note: The item is missing because of X_par, and in part X_Kli(p). Splitting off the X_K statement would make that part planned (C5), as PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20/toroidal-compactification-hodge-bundle was. External input: K.-W. Lan [50], IMRN 2017, Thm. 6.1 (of which the theorem is stated to be a special case) and Prop. 7.5; Faltings–Chai [18] (Y_K); Lan [49], [50] (Y_{par,K}, via Zarhin's trick: embed into principally polarized abelian 16-folds, compactify, normalize); Stroh [74] and Lan [49], [50] (Y_Kli(p)_K, via normalization in the compactification of Y_{par,K} × Y_K)

items.name: Theorem 6.1.5.1(2): refinement maps, Rπ_*O = O, and pullback of the boundary ideal
items.statement: If Σ' is a refinement of Σ (printed: 'If Σ′ ⊂ Σ is a refinement'), there is a projective map π_{Σ',Σ}: X_{K,Σ'} → X_{K,Σ} with (Rπ_{Σ',Σ})_* O_{X_{K,Σ'}} = O_{X_{K,Σ}}. If I_{X_{K,Σ}} and I_{X_{K,Σ'}} are the invertible ideal sheaves of the boundary in X_{K,Σ} and X_{K,Σ'}, then π_{Σ',Σ}^* I_{X_{K,Σ}} = I_{X_{K,Σ'}}. The same holds for X_{par,K,Σ} and X_Kli(p),K,Σ.
items.note: Over Z_p, the statements (Rπ_{Σ',Σ})_*O = O and π^*I_D = I_{D'} are not planned, even for X_K. They are also needed for X_par and X_Kli(p). External input: Lan [50], Thm. 6.1 and Prop. 7.5

items.name: Theorem 6.1.5.1(3): the projections p_1, p_2 extend to toroidal compactifications
items.statement: If Σ is Γ-admissible and Σ' is a Γ_Kli(p)-admissible refinement of Σ, then p_1: Y_Kli(p)_K → Y_K extends to a map X_Kli(p)_{K,Σ'} → X_{K,Σ}. If Σ is Γ_par-admissible and Σ' is a Γ_Kli(p)-admissible refinement of Σ, then p_2: Y_Kli(p)_K → Y_{par,K} extends to a map X_Kli(p)_{K,Σ'} → X_{par,K,Σ}.
items.note: The source spaces X_Kli(p) and X_par are missing. External input: Lan [50], Thm. 6.1 and Prop. 7.5

items.name: Theorem 6.1.5.1(4): toroidal compactifications are normal and lci over Z_p
items.statement: If Σ is Γ-admissible (resp. Γ_Kli(p)-, resp. Γ_par-admissible) and good, the toroidal compactification X_{K,Σ} of Y_K (resp. X_Kli(p)_{K,Σ} of Y_Kli(p)_K, resp. X_{par,K,Σ} of Y_{par,K}) is normal and a local complete intersection over Spec Z_p.
items.note: The proof uses the charts, Proposition 6.1.4.1 and modular curves.

items.name: Notation X, X_Kli(p), X_par
items.statement: Dropping K and Σ from the notation, X := X_{K,Σ}, X_Kli(p) := X_Kli(p)_{K,Σ} and X_par := X_{par,K,Σ} (printed 'X, X_par and X_Kli(p) for X_{K,Σ}, X_Kli(p)_{K,Σ} and X_{par,K,Σ}', which pairs X_par with X_Kli(p)_{K,Σ} and X_Kli(p) with X_{par,K,Σ}; sourceIssues E41). D (or D_X, D_{X_par}) denotes the boundary divisor.
items.note: The status follows the objects named.

items.name: Automorphic vector bundles Ω^(k,r) = Sym^k ω_G ⊗ det^r ω_G on X and X_par
items.statement: Let G be the semi-abelian scheme over X, with unit section e. Then ω_G := e^* Ω^1_{G/X} is locally free of rank 2. For (k,r) ∈ Z_{≥0} × Z, set Ω^(k,r) := Sym^k ω_G ⊗ det^r ω_G, and write ω^r := Ω^(0,r) and Ω^k := Ω^(k,0) (so Ω^1 = ω_G and ω = det ω_G). Over X_par the same construction with e^* Ω^1_{G'/X_par} (G' the semi-abelian scheme over X_par) gives sheaves also written Ω^1 and Ω^(k,r). Ω^(k,r)(−D) denotes the twist by the ideal of the boundary.
items.note: Split it: the definition on X is planned (AutomorphicBundles:B3, B4; ShimuraCompactifications:C5), and only the X_par instance is missing. Ω^(k,r) is the automorphic vector bundle attached to the representation Sym^k St ⊗ det^r St of GL_2, the Levi of the Siegel parabolic. The introduction (pp. 2–3, Theorem 1.1) also uses these sheaves on X_Kli(p)K. The singular weights studied are (k,2), k ≥ 0; the corresponding Galois representations have (conjectural) Hodge–Tate weights (k+1, k+1, 0, 0) up to twist (p. 2).

items.name: Minimal compactifications X^⋆ and X^⋆_par
items.statement: There are minimal compactifications X^⋆ of Y_K and X^⋆_par of Y_{par,K}, defined as X^⋆ = Proj ⊕_{k≥0} H^0(X, ω^k) and X^⋆_par = Proj ⊕_{k≥0} H^0(X_par, ω^k). The sheaf ω descends to ample invertible sheaves on X^⋆ and X^⋆_par, and there are canonical morphisms π: X → X^⋆ and π_par: X_par → X^⋆_par.
items.note: The item is missing only because of X^⋆_par. Splitting would make the X^⋆ part planned (C5). External input: Faltings–Chai [18]; Lan [49], [50]

items.name: Theorem 6.2.2.1: vanishing of R^iπ_* of the cuspidal sheaves Ω^(k,r)(−D)
items.statement: For all (k,r) ∈ Z_{≥0} × Z and all i > 0: R^i π_* Ω^(k,r)(−D_X) = 0 and R^i (π_par)_* Ω^(k,r)(−D_{X_par}) = 0.
items.note: The theorem is integral over Z_p for all (k,r), for both X and X_par. The theorem is quoted from Lan, [50] thm. 8.6. It is used in the proofs of Proposition 8.1.1 and Lemma 8.2.1 (p. 52), and it is cited again as '[50], thm. 8.6' in the proof of Theorem 11.3.1 (p. 72). The proof of Theorem 11.2.1 (p. 71) uses the same relative acyclicity. External input: [50] K.-W. Lan, Integral models of toroidal compactifications with projective cone decompositions, IMRN 2017, Thm. 8.6

items.name: Conormal sheaf ω_H, Hasse–Witt operator and Hasse invariant Ha(G) of a BT_1
items.statement: Let S be an F_p-scheme. For a group scheme H → S, ω_H is the conormal sheaf of H along the unit section. For a truncated Barsotti–Tate group of level 1 (BT_1) G → S, let V: G^(p) → G be the Verschiebung and V^⋆: ω_G → ω_G^(p) its differential (the Hasse–Witt operator). The Hasse invariant is Ha(G) := det V^⋆ ∈ H^0(S, (det ω_G)^{p−1}).
items.note: The general BT_1 definition Ha(G) = det V^⋆ ∈ H^0(S, (det ω_G)^{p−1}) over any F_p-scheme is planned nowhere.

items.name: Proposition 6.3.1.1 (Fargues): LF: (det ω_G)^{p−1} ≃ (det ω_{G^D})^{p−1} exchanging Hasse invariants
items.statement: Let G be a BT_1 over an F_p-scheme S, with Cartier dual G^D. There is a canonical and functorial isomorphism LF: (det ω_G)^{p−1} ≃ (det ω_{G^D})^{p−1} such that LF(Ha(G)) = Ha(G^D).
items.note: The source is Fargues [21] §2.2.3, Prop. 2. External input: [21] L. Fargues, La filtration canonique des points de torsion des groupes p-divisibles (with Y. Tian), Ann. Sci. ENS, §2.2.3, Prop. 2

items.name: Quasi-polarization of a BT_1
items.statement: A quasi-polarization of a BT_1 G is an isomorphism λ: G ≅ G^D such that λ^D = −λ.

items.name: Lemma 6.3.1.1: LF ∘ λ^⋆ = id for a quasi-polarization λ
items.statement: Let G be a BT_1 over an F_p-scheme S with a quasi-polarization λ: G ≅ G^D. Then the composite (det ω_{G^D})^{p−1} →(λ^⋆) (det ω_G)^{p−1} →(LF) (det ω_{G^D})^{p−1} is the identity.
items.note: Proof: if G is ordinary, Ha(G) and Ha(G^D) generate the two sheaves, λ^⋆Ha(G^D) = Ha(G) by functoriality, and LF(Ha(G)) = Ha(G^D). The general case follows because the stack of quasi-polarized BT_1s is smooth with dense ordinary locus (item stack-quasi-polarized-BT1-smooth-ordinary-dense).

items.name: The stack of quasi-polarized BT_1s is smooth with dense ordinary locus
items.statement: The algebraic stack of quasi-polarized truncated Barsotti–Tate groups of level 1 (over F_p) is smooth, and its ordinary locus is dense.
items.note: Cited without a precise locator in [36]. External input: [36] L. Illusie, Déformations de groupes de Barsotti–Tate (d'après A. Grothendieck), Astérisque 127 (1985)

items.name: Setting of §6.3.2: a p-rank-one BT_1 of height 4, its filtration G^m ⊂ G^o ⊂ G and G^oo = G^o/G^m
items.statement: Let S be a reduced F_p-scheme and G a BT_1 over S of height 4 and dimension 2, whose étale rank and multiplicative rank are constant and both equal to 1 (so Ha(G) vanishes identically). There is a multiplicative–connected filtration G^m ⊂ G^o ⊂ G, and G^oo := G^o/G^m is a BT_1 of height 2 and dimension 1.
items.note: This is the setting of the second Hasse invariant (§6.3.2).

items.name: The invariant Ha'(G^oo) ∈ H^0(S, ω_{G^oo}^{p^2−1})
items.statement: In the setting of §6.3.2, let 𝓔 = Ext^1_cris(G^oo, O_{S/Spec F_p})_S, with Hodge filtration 0 → ω_{G^oo} → 𝓔 → ω^{−1}_{(G^oo)^D} → 0. The map V^⋆: 𝓔 → 𝓔^(p) is zero on ω_{G^oo}, because it is zero pointwise and S is reduced. The map it induces on quotients, ω^{−1}_{(G^oo)^D} → ω^{−p}_{(G^oo)^D} (the differential of Frobenius on the Lie algebra of (G^oo)^D), is also zero. Hence V^⋆ induces an isomorphism V^⋆: ω^{−1}_{(G^oo)^D} → ω^p_{G^oo}. Set Ha'(G^oo) := (V^⋆)^{p−1} ∈ H^0(S, ω^{p(p−1)}_{G^oo} ⊗ ω^{p−1}_{(G^oo)^D}) ≃ H^0(S, ω^{p^2−1}_{G^oo}), identifying ω^{p−1}_{(G^oo)^D} with ω^{p−1}_{G^oo} by LF.
items.note: Uses crystalline Dieudonné theory (CrystallineCohomology, FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.2 and R07.6).

items.name: The second Hasse invariant Ha'(G) ∈ H^0(S, (det ω_G)^{p^2−1})
items.statement: In the setting of §6.3.2, the second Hasse invariant is the invertible (nowhere vanishing) section Ha'(G) := Ha(G^m)^{p+1} ⊗ Ha'(G^oo) ∈ H^0(S, (det ω_G)^{p^2−1}), using det ω_G = ω_{G^m} ⊗ ω_{G^oo}. The Cartier dual G^D satisfies the same assumptions, so Ha'(G^D) is defined, and LF^{⊗(p+1)}: (det ω_G)^{p^2−1} ≃ (det ω_{G^D})^{p^2−1}.
items.note: CG20 records this form, as h̃ on the non-ordinary locus, as missing (secondary-hasse-invariant, routed to the proposed SiegelModularFormsModPn).

items.name: Lemma 6.3.2.1: LF^{⊗(p+1)}(Ha'(G)) = Ha'(G^D)
items.statement: In the setting of §6.3.2 (S reduced; G a BT_1 of height 4 and dimension 2 with constant étale and multiplicative ranks 1), LF^{⊗(p+1)}(Ha'(G)) = Ha'(G^D).
items.note: Proof: S is reduced, so it suffices to check at algebraically closed points. There a quasi-polarization λ: G → G^D exists, LF^{⊗(p+1)} ∘ λ^⋆ is the identity by Lemma 6.3.1.1 (the paper prints the target of this composite as (det ω_G)^{p²−1}; it is (det ω_{G^D})^{p²−1}, so the composite is an endomorphism of (det ω_{G^D})^{p²−1}; sourceIssues E42), and λ^⋆Ha'(G^D) = Ha'(G) by functoriality.

items.name: Setting of §6.3.3: S normal reduced, generic p-rank one, Hasse–Witt of rank one; the open S'
items.statement: Let S be a normal reduced F_p-scheme and G a BT_1 over S of height 4 and dimension 2 whose generic étale rank and generic multiplicative rank are equal to 1. S' ⊂ S is the dense open subscheme where G has étale rank one and multiplicative rank one. Assume moreover that over S the Hasse–Witt map V^⋆: ω_G → ω_G^(p) has rank 1, i.e. Ker V^⋆ is an invertible sheaf and locally a direct factor of ω_G. Lemmas 6.3.3.3 and 6.3.3.5 also need a hypothesis the paper omits: at every point of S the étale rank of G equals its multiplicative rank [sourceIssues E43]. This holds for the p-torsion of polarized abelian surfaces, as in §6.4.
items.note: This is the setting of §6.3.3, including the omitted hypothesis (étale rank equal to multiplicative rank at every point) that the item records.

items.name: Lemma 6.3.3.1: the Hasse–Witt map of G^D also has rank one
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of §6.3.3, the map V^⋆: ω_{G^D} → ω^(p)_{G^D} has rank one, so G^D satisfies the same hypotheses as G.
items.note: Proof: with 𝓔 = Ext^1_cris(G, O_{S/F_p})_S, there is a short exact sequence of perfect complexes (the rows) [ω_G →V⋆ ω_G^(p)] → [(ω^∨_{G^D})^(p) →F⋆ 𝓔 →V⋆ ω_G^(p)] → [(ω^∨_{G^D})^(p) →F⋆ ω^∨_{G^D}], with acyclic middle row. The map F⋆ in the last row is dual to V⋆ of G^D, and the long exact sequence identifies its kernel and cokernel with those of V⋆_G. External input: [21] Fargues, p. 915 (the exact sequence of complexes)

items.name: Hodge–Tate exact sequence for a BT_1
items.statement: For a BT_1 G over an F_p-scheme S there is an exact sequence 0 → Ker F → G →(HT) ω_{G^D} →(F − V^⋆) ω^(p)_{G^D}. Here ω_{G^D} and ω^(p)_{G^D} are viewed as vector group schemes (twisted forms of G_a^2 in the case at hand), F is the Frobenius of G and of ω_{G^D}, and V^⋆ is the Hasse–Witt map of G^D.
items.note: The source is Fargues [21] §2.1.2. External input: [21] Fargues, §2.1.2

items.name: Lemma 6.3.3.2: the multiplicative subgroup G^m ⊂ G[F] over S' extends to a finite flat H ⊂ G[F] over S
items.note: Remark 6.3.3.1 (the referee's alternative proof): since S is reduced, it suffices to check at geometric points that K has rank p, which is an elementary Dieudonné module computation. H is the 'canonical' filtration H ⊂ Ker F used in Lemma 6.4.2.

items.name: Diagrams (6.3.A), (6.3.B) and the maps V^⋆_H, W and Z
items.note: Z is in fact an isomorphism of invertible sheaves (the source is invertible by Lemma 6.3.3.4, the target because V⋆ has rank 1). It is the connecting map from the cokernel of F⋆: (ω^∨_{G^D})^(p) → ω^∨_{G^D} to the cokernel of V⋆: ω_G → ω_G^(p) in the long exact sequence used in the proof of Lemma 6.3.3.1 (pp. 31–32), whose middle complex is exact. Lemma 6.3.3.5 needs this only to see that A does not vanish on S'.

items.name: Lemma 6.3.3.3: V^⋆_H and W vanish on S∖S' to the same order
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of §6.3.3, including the omitted one that étale rank equals multiplicative rank at every point, the maps V^⋆_H and W vanish on S∖S' and have the same order of vanishing at each generic point of S∖S'.
items.note: The item records the omitted hypothesis on ranks.

items.name: Lemma 6.3.3.4: ω^∨_{G^D}/F⋆(ω^∨_{G^D})^(p) = (ω_{G^D[F]/L})^∨
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of §6.3.3 there is a canonical isomorphism ω^∨_{G^D}/F⋆(ω^∨_{G^D})^(p) = (ω_{G^D[F]/L})^∨.
items.note: Proof: F⋆: (ω^∨_{G^D})^(p) → ω^∨_{G^D} is dual to V⋆: ω_{G^D} → ω^(p)_{G^D}, whose kernel is ω_{G^D[F]/L} by the analogue of (6.3.B) for G^D.

items.name: The rational section A = (V⋆_H)^{p+1} ⊗ (W^{−1} ∘ Z)^{p−1}
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of §6.3.3, A := (V⋆_H)^{p+1} ⊗ (W^{−1} ∘ Z)^{p−1} is a rational section of ω_H^{p^2−1} ⊗ ω^{p(p−1)}_{G[F]/H} ⊗ ω^{p−1}_{G^D[F]/L}. W is invertible over S', and Z is read through Lemma 6.3.3.4, so W^{−1} ∘ Z is a rational section of ω^p_{G[F]/H} ⊗ ω_{G^D[F]/L}. Exchanging G and G^D gives B, a rational section of ω_L^{p^2−1} ⊗ ω^{p(p−1)}_{G^D[F]/L} ⊗ ω^{p−1}_{G[F]/H}.

items.name: Lemma 6.3.3.5: A is regular and vanishes exactly on S∖S'
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of §6.3.3 (including the equality of étale and multiplicative ranks at every point of S, which the paper omits; sourceIssues E43), the section A is regular on S and vanishes precisely over S∖S'.
items.note: The printed proof is 'follows from Lemma 6.3.3.3 since p+1 > p−1'. At a generic point x of S∖S', put o = ord_x V⋆_H = ord_x W > 0 (Lemma 6.3.3.3). Z is a morphism of invertible sheaves, so ord_x Z ≥ 0 and ord_x A = (p+1)o + (p−1)(ord_x Z − o) ≥ 2o > 0; regularity elsewhere follows from normality of S. In fact Z is an isomorphism (it is the connecting map of the long exact sequence in the proof of Lemma 6.3.3.1, pp. 31–32), so ord_x A = 2o. Over S', V⋆_H, W and Z are isomorphisms, so A does not vanish there.

items.name: Proposition 6.3.3.1: Ha'(G) extends from S' to S and vanishes exactly on S∖S'
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of §6.3.3, the second Hasse invariant Ha'(G) ∈ H^0(S', (det ω_G)^{p^2−1}) (printed ω_G^{p^2−1}) extends to a section over S, and the extension vanishes precisely on S∖S'.
items.note: This is a special case of Boxer [5] and Goldring–Koskivirta [27]. External input: A very special case of the extension results of G. Boxer [5] and W. Goldring–J.-S. Koskivirta [27]

items.name: Hasse invariants are compatible with étale isogenies
items.statement: Let S be an F_p-scheme and λ: G → G' an étale isogeny of Barsotti–Tate groups over S. Then λ⋆: ω_{G'} → ω_G is an isomorphism and λ⋆Ha(G') = Ha(G). When the second Hasse invariant is defined, λ⋆Ha'(G') = Ha'(G).
items.note: The first clause (Ha) is general. The second (Ha') is specific to genus two.

items.name: Lemma 6.3.4.1: normalized pullback λ̃⋆ for isogenies of multiplicative BT groups
items.statement: Let S be an F_p-scheme, G and G' Barsotti–Tate groups of multiplicative type over S, and λ: G → G' an isogeny of degree p^r. Then there is a canonical isomorphism λ̃⋆: det ω_{G'} → det ω_G with λ̃⋆Ha(G') = Ha(G). Construction: write G = T ⊗_{Z_p} μ_{p^∞} and G' = T' ⊗_{Z_p} μ_{p^∞} with T, T' smooth pro-étale Z_p-sheaves. Then λ induces λ_0: T → T' and an isomorphism p^{−r} det λ_0: det T → det T'. With h the rank of T, ω_G ≅ T^∨ ⊗ ω_{μ_{p^∞}}, so det ω_G ≅ (det T)^{−1} ⊗ ω_{μ_{p^∞}}^{⊗h}, and similarly for G'. λ̃⋆: det ω_{G'} → det ω_G is the transpose of p^{−r} det λ_0, tensored with the identity of ω_{μ_{p^∞}}^{⊗h} [printed 'det ω_G = det T ⊗ ω_{μ_{p^∞}}'; sourceIssues E47]. Using the canonical trivialisation F_p ≃ (det T/pT)^{⊗(1−p)} (and likewise for T'), Ha(G) = 1 ⊗ Ha(μ_{p^∞})^{⊗h} [printed without the exponent h; sourceIssues E47].
items.note: Only the classical Ha is involved.

items.name: Multiplicative Barsotti–Tate subgroup G^m ⊂ G
items.statement: A Barsotti–Tate group G over S (in characteristic p) of constant multiplicative rank has a filtration by a multiplicative Barsotti–Tate subgroup G^m ⊂ G, with G/G^m a Barsotti–Tate group without multiplicative part.
items.note: G^m is the Cartier dual of the étale quotient of G^D. External input: [31] M. Harris and R. Taylor, The geometry and cohomology of some simple Shimura varieties, Cor. II.1.2

items.name: Lemma 6.3.4.2: normalized pullback λ̃⋆ for isogenies whose kernel is a complement to a multiplicative subgroup
items.statement: Let S be an F_p-scheme and G, G' Barsotti–Tate groups over S of constant multiplicative rank. Let λ: G → G' be an isogeny with kernel L ⊂ G[p], and assume that for every geometric point x → S there is a multiplicative subgroup H_x ⊂ G_x[p] with H_x ⊕ L_x = G_x[p]. Then there is a canonical isomorphism λ̃⋆: det ω_{G'} → det ω_G with λ̃⋆Ha(G') = Ha(G), and, when the second Hasse invariant is defined, λ̃⋆Ha'(G') = Ha'(G). Construction: with G^m ⊂ G, (G')^m ⊂ G' and L^m = L ∩ G^m, λ restricts to λ^m: G^m → (G')^m with kernel L^m. The induced isogeny G/G^m → G'/(G')^m is uniquely of the form pμ with μ an isomorphism, because L/L^m ↪ (G/G^m)[p] has the same rank as (G/G^m)[p]. Then λ̃⋆ := (λ̃^m)⋆ ⊗ μ⋆ under det ω = det ω_{(·)^m} ⊗ det ω_{(·)/(·)^m}.
items.note: It includes the Ha' clause.

items.name: Reductions X_n, X_{par,n} and the multiplicative-rank (p-rank) strata X_n^{=r}, X_n^{≤r}, X_n^{≥r}
items.note: The strata on X are defined by the multiplicative rank of the semi-abelian scheme, including its torus part.

items.name: p-rank strata: X_n^{=r} is dense in X_n^{≤r}, of dimension r + 1
items.statement: X_n^{=r} is dense open in X_n^{≤r}, and X^{=r}_{par,n} is dense open in X^{≤r}_{par,n}. These strata have dimension r + 1 [printed '3 − r'; sourceIssues E48].
items.note: The item uses the corrected dimension r+1; the paper prints 3−r. External input: [57] P. Norman and F. Oort, Moduli of abelian varieties, Ann. of Math. 112 (1980), 413–439

items.name: Ha(G) on X_1 and X_{par,1}; the non-ordinary loci X_1^{≤1} := V(Ha(G)) and X^{≤1}_{par,1} := V(Ha(G'))
items.statement: ω denotes the invertible sheaf det ω_G on X_1 (resp. det ω_{G'} on X_{par,1}). The Hasse invariants Ha(G) ∈ H^0(X_1, ω^{p−1}) and Ha(G') ∈ H^0(X_{par,1}, ω^{p−1}) are defined as in §6.3.1, taking the determinant of the differential of the Verschiebung of the semi-abelian scheme (alternatively, extend from the interior by Koecher's principle). X_1^{≤1} is the closed subscheme V(Ha(G)) and X^{≤1}_{par,1} is V(Ha(G')).
items.note: The item also mentions the Koecher alternative. Koecher for Siegel was routed by PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20 to ShimuraCompactifications C5.

items.name: Ha has non-zero differential at every p-rank-one point (Dieudonné/Grothendieck–Messing computation)
items.statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p and x ∈ X_1^{=1}(k) or X^{=1}_{par,1}(k), with p-divisible group H. The contravariant Dieudonné module D of H has a W(k)-basis e_1,…,e_4 with D = W(k)e_1 ⊕ (W(k)e_2 ⊕ W(k)e_3) ⊕ W(k)e_4 (multiplicative ⊕ biconnected ⊕ étale). The printed Frobenius (columns of the printed matrix) is Fe_1 = pe_1, Fe_2 = pe_3, Fe_3 = e_2, Fe_4 = e_4, and the Hodge filtration is Ker(F) = ⟨ē_1, ē_2⟩ ⊂ D/pD. The universal first-order deformation of H (unpolarized, [36]) lives over R = k[X,Y,W,Z]/(X,Y,Z,W)^2, with Fil ⊂ D ⊗ R generated by (1,0,X,W)^T and (0,1,Y,Z)^T. The Hasse invariant of this deformation is det(F | D⊗R/Fil); in the basis ē_3, ē_4 the matrix is [[−Y,0],[−Z,1]], so it equals −Y. The paper takes the principal quasi-polarization to be the form J (⟨e_1,e_4⟩ = ⟨e_2,e_3⟩ = 1); for p odd this is incompatible with the printed F. Normalizing instead Fe_3 = −e_2, which is compatible with J, leaves the Hodge filtration unchanged and makes the Hasse invariant Y. With J: Fil is isotropic iff X = Z, so the tangent space of X_1 at x is {X = Z}; and Fil^⊥ is generated by (1,0,Z,W)^T and (0,1,Y,X)^T. The tangent space of X_{par,1} at x is {Z = 0} or {X = 0}, according as the polarization λ: D → D^t (with D^t identified with D via J) is diag(1,p,p,1) or diag(p,1,1,p). The conditions are λ(Fil) ⊂ Fil^⊥ and λ^∨(Fil^⊥) ⊂ Fil; λ is diagonal and commutes with F, so these conditions do not depend on the sign normalization. In every case the tangent space is not contained in {Y = 0}, so Ha has non-zero differential at x.
items.note: The paramodular tangent-space clause needs the paramodular model. External input: [36] Illusie (Grothendieck–Messing deformation theory)

items.name: Lemma 6.4.1: the schemes X_1^{≤1} = V(Ha(G)) and X^{≤1}_{par,1} = V(Ha(G')) are reduced
items.statement: The closed subschemes X_1^{≤1} = V(Ha(G)) ⊂ X_1 and X^{≤1}_{par,1} = V(Ha(G')) ⊂ X_{par,1} are reduced.
items.note: The proof needs X_par,1 to be Cohen–Macaulay and normal (Proposition 6.1.4.1).

items.name: Ha'(G) on X_1^{=1} and Ha'(G') on X^{=1}_{par,1}, including the boundary
items.statement: On the open subscheme of X_1^{=1} (resp. X^{=1}_{par,1}) where the semi-abelian scheme is abelian, Ha' is defined by §6.3.2 applied to G[p] (resp. G'[p]). It extends over the boundary: the construction of §6.3.2 (Ha(G^m)^{p+1} ⊗ Ha'(G^oo)) applies to the identity components G[p]^o and G'[p]^o, which are truncated BT_1 of height 3, dimension 2 and multiplicative rank 1. This gives Ha'(G) ∈ H^0(X_1^{=1}, ω^{p^2−1}) and Ha'(G') ∈ H^0(X^{=1}_{par,1}, ω^{p^2−1}), with ω = det ω_G (resp. det ω_{G'}).
items.note: X_1^{=1} is open in the reduced scheme X_1^{≤1} (Lemma 6.4.1).

items.name: Finitely many superspecial points on X_1 and X_{par,1}
items.statement: An abelian surface is superspecial if it is isomorphic to a product of two supersingular elliptic curves. X_1 and X_{par,1} contain only finitely many superspecial points; SS denotes this finite set. Outside SS, the Hasse–Witt matrix on X_1^{≤1} and X^{≤1}_{par,1} has rank 1.
items.note: The bibliography entry [56] reads 'Narashiman', 'April 1951'. The paper is Proc. Indian Acad. Sci. Math. Sci. 90 (1981). External input: [56] M. S. Narasimhan and M. V. Nori, Polarizations on an abelian variety, Proc. Indian Acad. Sci. (Math. Sci.) 90 (1981), 125–128

items.name: X_1^{≤1} ∖ SS is smooth: the Iwahori-level local model
items.statement: X_1^{≤1} ∖ SS is smooth. Over it the canonical filtration H ⊂ Ker F (H from Lemma 6.3.3.2) embeds X_1^{≤1} ∖ SS into the moduli space of abelian surfaces with a polarization of degree prime to p and Iwahori level at p. The image is exactly the union of the strata X_0^{m,e} and X_0^{sg,F} of [62]. The closure of X_0^{m,e} is locally isomorphic to Spec F_p[x,y,a,b,c]/(xy, ax+by+abc, a, y, x+bc) ≅ Spec F_p[b,c], with X_0^{m,e} = {bc ≠ 0} and X_0^{sg,F} = {c = 0, b ≠ 0}.
items.note: Verified: with a = y = 0 and x = −bc, both xy and ax+by+abc vanish. The union of the two strata is the open {b ≠ 0} of the plane, hence smooth. Atlas: Iwahori level is planned only for Hilbert varieties (HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:H4). External input: [62] V. Pilloni, Prolongement analytique sur les variétés de Siegel, Duke Math. J. 157 (2011), pp. 186–189 (Iwahori-level local model and its strata)

items.name: X^{≤1}_{par,1} ∖ SS is locally Spec F_p[a,b,c]/(ab)
items.statement:
X^{≤1}_{par,1} ∖ SS is locally isomorphic to Spec F_p[a,b,c]/(ab), with X^{=1}_{par,1} corresponding to {a ≠ 0 or b ≠ 0}. Construction:
- Let K(λ) = ker(λ: G' → (G')^t) and K(λ^t) = ker(λ^t: (G')^t → G') (printed '→ G'). Off SS both are BT_1 of height 2 and dimension 1.
- Set H = K(λ) ∩ Ker F and H' = K(λ^t) ∩ Ker F, both of order p.
- The chain G' → G'/H → (G')^t → (G')^t/H' → G' embeds X^{≤1}_{par,1} ∖ SS into the Iwahori-level moduli space, identifying it with an open subscheme of the union of the closures of the strata X_0^{o,m} and X_0^{et,o} of [62].
- On the local model F_p[x,y,a,b,c]/(xy, ax+by+abc), these closures are F_p[b,c] (x = y = a = 0) and F_p[a,c] (x = b = 0, y = −ac). They are the quotients by a = 0 and by b = 0 of F_p[x,y,a,b,c]/(xy, ax+by+abc, y+ac, x) ≅ F_p[a,b,c].
items.note: Verified: with x = 0 and y = −ac, xy = 0 and ax+by+abc = −abc+abc = 0. External input: [62] Pilloni, Duke 157 (2011) (strata X_0^{o,m}, X_0^{et,o})

items.name: Lemma 6.4.2 (i): Ha'(G) and Ha'(G') extend to X_1^{≤1} and X^{≤1}_{par,1}
items.statement: The second Hasse invariants Ha'(G) ∈ H^0(X_1^{=1}, ω^{p^2−1}) and Ha'(G') ∈ H^0(X^{=1}_{par,1}, ω^{p^2−1}) extend to sections over X_1^{≤1} and X^{≤1}_{par,1} respectively.
items.note: Proof: X_1^{≤1} and X^{≤1}_{par,1} are Cohen–Macaulay (Cartier divisors in CM schemes) and SS is finite, so it suffices to extend off SS. On X_1^{≤1} ∖ SS (smooth), apply Proposition 6.3.3.1. On X^{≤1}_{par,1} ∖ SS, apply it on each smooth irreducible component {a = 0} and {b = 0}; the two extensions glue because both vanish on the intersection.

items.name: Lemma 6.4.2 (ii): the extended Ha'(G), Ha'(G') vanish on the p-rank-0 loci
items.statement: The extensions of Ha'(G) and Ha'(G') vanish on X_1^{≤0} and X^{≤0}_{par,1}, the loci of multiplicative rank 0. Off SS, their zero loci in X_1^{≤1} (resp. in each component of X^{≤1}_{par,1}) are exactly the p-rank-0 loci (Proposition 6.3.3.1).

items.name: Schematic p-rank-0 loci X_1^{≤0} := V(Ha'(G)) and X^{≤0}_{par,1} := V(Ha'(G'))
items.statement: X_1^{≤0} is defined as the vanishing locus (closed subscheme) of Ha'(G) in X_1^{≤1}, and X^{≤0}_{par,1} as the vanishing locus of Ha'(G') in X^{≤1}_{par,1}.
items.note: Together with X_1^{≤1} = V(Ha(G)), this fixes the scheme structures on the p-rank strata used in the higher Hida theory of §§8–10. Lemma 6.4.2 and Remark 6.4.1, stated next to this definition on pp. 36–37, have their own items: second-hasse-invariant-extends-to-nonordinary-locus, second-hasse-invariant-vanishes-on-p-rank-zero and second-hasse-order-two-and-square-root. In §§7.4.2–8.1 (pp. 48–52) the paper writes X_1^{=0} and X_{par,1}^{=0} for these schemes (sourceIssues E61).

items.name: Remark 6.4.1: Ha'(G) vanishes to order 2 along the p-rank-0 locus; square root for p ≥ 3
items.statement: (Remark, proof only sketched.) Using Lemma 6.3.3.5 one checks that the Siegel modular form Ha'(G) vanishes to order 2 along the rank-0 locus. When p ≥ 3, Ha'(G) has a square root, a modular form of weight (p^2−1)/2 vanishing to order 1. When p = 2 it has no square root.
items.note: This is a remark whose proof is only sketched.

items.name: The T-operator as a composite of paramodular double cosets
items.statement: Let T_{p,1} = GSp_4(Z_p) diag(1,p,p,p^2) GSp_4(Z_p); its cocharacter t ↦ diag(t^2,t,t,1) is not minuscule. Using the factorization diag(p^2,p,p,1) = diag(p,p,p,1) × diag(p,1,1,1) in GL_4(Q_p), T_{p,1} is replaced by the composite of double cosets T := GSp_4(Z_p) diag(p,p,p,1) GSp'_4(Z_p) ⋆ GSp'_4(Z_p) diag(p,1,1,1) GSp_4(Z_p), where GSp'_4 is the paramodular group. Each of the two double cosets has a moduli interpretation in terms of parahoric level (Klingen–paramodular). T is to act on RΓ(X, Ω^(k,r)) and RΓ(X, Ω^(k,r)(−D)) for r ≥ 2.
items.note: PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20's proposed SiegelModularFormsModPn layer 4 builds operators at p only on H^0, via Hartogs. Pilloni's integral T on all of RΓ is new.

items.name: T = T_{p,1} + (1+p+p^2+p^3) T_{p,0} as double cosets, and the moduli interpretation of T (footnote 8)
items.statement: At the level of double cosets, T = T_{p,1} + (1 + p + p^2 + p^3) T_{p,0}, where T_{p,0} = p GSp_4(Z_p). Moduli interpretation (footnote 8): T parametrizes chains G → G/H_1 → (G/H_1)/H_2, where H_1 ⊂ G[p] has order p^3 and H_2 ⊂ (G/H_1)[p] has order p and lies in the kernel of the polarization of G/H_1. The component T_{p,1} corresponds to an arbitrary H_1 with H_2 ≠ G[p]/H_1. The component T_{p,0} corresponds to an arbitrary H_1 with H_2 = G[p]/H_1, and has multiplicity p^3 + p^2 + p + 1 = #GSp_4(Z_p)/Kli(p).
items.note: I checked the degrees: deg T = (p³+p²+p+1)(p+1), deg T_{p,1} = p⁴+p³+p²+p and deg T_{p,0} = 1, consistent with multiplicity p³+p²+p+1 = #GSp4(Z_p)/Kli(p). The definition of T as the composite GSp4(Z_p)diag(p,p,p,1)GSp4'(Z_p) ⋆ GSp4'(Z_p)diag(p,1,1,1)GSp4(Z_p) is recorded in T-operator-as-composite-of-parahoric-double-cosets. This item records the comparison with T_{p,1} and the moduli description of footnote 8.

items.name: Hecke parameters of π_p and ordinarity (Newton polygon = Hodge polygon)
items.statement: Let π_p be a spherical irreducible smooth representation of GSp4(Q_p) that contributes to RΓ(X, Ω^{(k,r)}) ⊗^L \bar Q_p or to RΓ(X, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) ⊗^L \bar Q_p. Let Θ_{π_p} be the corresponding character of the spherical Hecke algebra, valued in \bar Q_p. Let (α_p, β_p, γ_p, δ_p) be the Hecke parameters of π_p: the roots of the reciprocal Hecke polynomial evaluated at Θ_{π_p}, ordered by non-decreasing p-adic valuation and with α_pδ_p = β_pγ_p. The Hodge polygon has slopes 0, r−2, k+r−1, k+2r−3. The Hecke parameter is called ordinary if its Newton polygon agrees with this Hodge polygon.
items.note: Checked against pp. 37–38. SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.4 identifies 'Hecke eigencharacters with unramified semisimple parameters'. IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.3 plans only the GL_n Hecke polynomial ('Do not assert this GL_n polynomial for a general reductive group without choosing a representation of its L-group'). PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20 routed the GSp4 spin polynomial there (hecke-polynomial-Q-x).
