No layer plans the Hodge polygon with slopes 0, r−2, k+r−1, k+2r−3 of weight (k,r), or ordinarity as Newton = Hodge for GSp4 Hecke parameters. The first half of the statement, which defines the Hecke parameters (α_p, β_p, γ_p, δ_p) ordered by non-decreasing p-adic valuation with α_pδ_p = β_pγ_p, is also the input to the eigenvalue formula for T on p. 38 (thm-T-eigenvalue-and-ordinarity-criterion).

items.name: The eigenvalue Θ_{π_p}(T) and the criterion 'Θ(T) is a p-adic unit' for r = 2 (motivational)
items.statement: Keep the setting of the previous item and assume that the Newton polygon of (α_p,β_p,γ_p,δ_p) lies above the Hodge polygon (slopes 0, r−2, k+r−1, k+2r−3), with the same initial and ending point. By Lemma 5.1.5.1, Θ_{π_p}(T_{p,1}) = p^{−1}(α_pβ_p + α_pγ_p + α_pδ_p + β_pδ_p + γ_pδ_p) − p^{−3}α_pδ_p and Θ_{π_p}(T_{p,0}) = p^{−3}α_pδ_p. The operator T acts like p^{3−r}(T_{p,1} + (1+p+p^2+p^3)T_{p,0}); the text says the factor p^{3−r} optimizes integrality. Hence Θ_{π_p}(T) = p^{2−r}(α_pβ_p + α_pγ_p + α_pδ_p + β_pδ_p + γ_pδ_p) + p^{1−r}(1+p+p^2)α_pδ_p. When r = 2: (i) Θ_{π_p}(T) is p-integral for all k ≥ 0; (ii) T and pT_{p,1} are congruent modulo p for k ≥ 2; (iii) (α_p,β_p,γ_p,δ_p) is ordinary if and only if α_pβ_p is a p-adic unit; (iv) when k ≥ 1, this is further equivalent to Θ_{π_p}(T) being a p-adic unit.
items.note: Checked against the p. 38 image. The arithmetic checks: p^{3−r}(p^{−1}Σ − p^{−3}αδ + (1+p+p²+p³)p^{−3}αδ) = p^{2−r}Σ + p^{1−r}(1+p+p²)αδ. For r = 2, Θ(T) − pΘ(T_{p,1}) = (p^{−2}+p^{−1}+1+p)αδ with v(αδ) ≥ k+1, which gives (ii) for k ≥ 2. The input Θ(T_{p,i}) comes from Lemma 5.1.5.1 (another cluster). The normalized operator and the ordinarity criteria are planned nowhere.

items.name: The correspondence X ← X_Kli(p) → X_par and the chain of isogenies G → G' → G
items.statement: Consider X, X_Kli(p) and X_par for good polyhedral cone decompositions Σ, Σ', Σ'' (§6.1), with Σ' refining both Σ and Σ''. This gives maps p_1 : X_Kli(p) → X and p_2 : X_Kli(p) → X_par. G is the semi-abelian scheme over X and G' the semi-abelian scheme over X_par. Over X_Kli(p) there is a chain of isogenies G → G' → G: the first isogeny G → G' has degree p^3, the second G' → G has degree p, and the composite is multiplication by p. The map p_1 forgets G' and p_2 forgets G. By Theorem 6.1.5.1, X, X_Kli(p) and X_par are normal and lci over Spec Z_p. Their non-smooth locus lies in the non-ordinary locus of the special fibre, so it has codimension 2. The morphisms p_1 and p_2 are not finite flat, because they are not quasi-finite over the rank 0 loci X_1^{=0} and X_par^{=0}: p-rank 0 abelian surfaces may have infinitely many subgroups of order p. They are also not finite flat over the boundary; the text calls this 'not a serious issue'.
items.note: Checked against p. 38. Good-reduction integral models exclude level at p: PELModuli:M2 requires 'no nontrivial level at p', and ShimuraCompactifications:C5 says 'Keep the good-prime assumptions on the input PEL datum'. PELModuli:M4 only normalizes at higher p-level and forbids 'a fine moduli interpretation, or a universal abelian scheme on such a normalization without a separate theorem'. Three things are therefore unplanned: the Klingen and paramodular toroidal models with the universal chain G → G' → G (degrees p³, p), their normality and lci property (Theorem 6.1.5.1), and the maps p_1, p_2, which are not quasi-finite over the p-rank-0 locus.

items.name: The unnormalized cohomological correspondence T_1' : p_2^*Ω^{(k,r)} → p_1^!Ω^{(k,r)}
items.statement: Let (k,r) ∈ Z_{≥0}^2. The differential of the isogeny G → G' gives a map p_2^*Ω^{(k,r)} → p_1^*Ω^{(k,r)}. Construction 1 (§4.2.1) gives a fundamental class p_1^*O_X → p_1^!O_X, and p_1^!O_X is an invertible sheaf. Tensoring with Ω^{(k,r)} and applying Proposition 4.1.2.1 gives a map p_1^*Ω^{(k,r)} → p_1^!Ω^{(k,r)}. Composing the two maps gives the cohomological correspondence T_1' : p_2^*Ω^{(k,r)} → p_1^*Ω^{(k,r)} → p_1^!Ω^{(k,r)}, which still has to be normalized.
items.note: Checked against p. 38. The only cohomological correspondences planned are étale: EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.8 ('Construct cohomological correspondences c₂* K→c₁^!K'). AutomorphicBundles:B5 plans 'pullback, coefficient identification, and trace along Hecke correspondences' on the characteristic-zero models. Nothing plans the coherent fundamental class p_1^*O → p_1^!O for non-flat lci/CM maps (§4.2.1, Proposition 4.1.2.1; another cluster), or its use with dΨ on the Siegel Klingen correspondence.

items.name: Lemma 7.1.1: T_1' is divisible by p^{2+r}
items.statement: Let (k,r) ∈ Z_{≥0}^2. If k + 2r ≥ 2 + r, the map T_1' : p_2^*Ω^{(k,r)} → p_1^!Ω^{(k,r)} factors through p^{2+r}p_1^!Ω^{(k,r)}.
items.note: Checked against the pp. 38–39 images, including the hypothesis k + 2r ≥ 2 + r. The proof reduces to generic points of the ordinary locus, using normality and the codimension-2 non-ordinary locus. It then computes traces in Serre–Tate coordinates (see ext-serre-tate-local-moduli). None of this is planned.

items.name: The normalized correspondence T_1 = p^{−2−r}T_1' and T_1 : RΓ(X_par, Ω^{(k,r)}) → RΓ(X, Ω^{(k,r)})
items.statement: Assume k + 2r ≥ 2 + r, which holds if r ≥ 2. Define T_1 := p^{−2−r}T_1' : p_2^*Ω^{(k,r)} → p_1^!Ω^{(k,r)}. The same symbol denotes the induced map on cohomology T_1 : RΓ(X_par, Ω^{(k,r)}) → RΓ(X, Ω^{(k,r)}).
items.note: Checked against p. 39. It depends on construction-unnormalized-T1-prime and Lemma 7.1.1, both missing.

items.name: The unnormalized cohomological correspondence T_2' : p_1^*Ω^{(k,r)} → p_2^!Ω^{(k,r)}
items.statement: Exchange the roles of p_1 and p_2. Define T_2' : p_1^*Ω^{(k,r)} → p_2^*Ω^{(k,r)} → p_2^!Ω^{(k,r)}, where the first map comes from the differential of the isogeny G' → G and the second from the fundamental class of p_2, tensored with Ω^{(k,r)}.
items.note: Checked against p. 39. As for T_1': there is no coherent fundamental class or upper-shriek correspondence in any layer (EDC.8 is étale only).

items.name: Lemma 7.1.2: T_2' is divisible by p
items.statement: Let (k,r) ∈ Z_{≥0}^2. If r ≥ 1, the map T_2' factors through p·p_2^!Ω^{(k,r)}.
items.note: Checked against the pp. 39–40 images. The proof uses Serre–Tate parameters at ordinary points of X_par, with matrix (X pZ; Z Y). Misprint on p. 40: 'the map p_2^*O_{X_par} → p_1^!O_{X_par} factors through p p_2^!O_{X_par}'. The p_1^! should be p_2^! (sourceIssues E54).

items.name: The normalized correspondence T_2 = p^{−1}T_2' and T_2 : RΓ(X, Ω^{(k,r)}) → RΓ(X_par, Ω^{(k,r)})
items.statement: Assume r ≥ 1. Define T_2 := p^{−1}T_2' : p_1^*Ω^{(k,r)} → p_2^!Ω^{(k,r)}. The same symbol denotes the induced map on cohomology T_2 : RΓ(X, Ω^{(k,r)}) → RΓ(X_par, Ω^{(k,r)}).
items.note: Checked against p. 40. It depends on T_2' and Lemma 7.1.2, both missing.

items.name: The T-operator T = T_1 ∘ T_2 on RΓ(X, Ω^{(k,r)})
items.statement: For (k,r) ∈ Z_{≥0}^2 with r ≥ 1 and k + 2r ≥ r + 2, define T := T_1 ∘ T_2 ∈ End(RΓ(X, Ω^{(k,r)})). It corresponds to the normalized operator attached to the composite of Hecke operators GSp4(Z_p)diag(p,p,p,1)GSp4'(Z_p) ⋆ GSp4'(Z_p)diag(p,1,1,1)GSp4(Z_p).
items.note: Checked against p. 40. PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20 marked the nearest analogue missing: hecke-operators-T-p1-Q-p2, which is T_{p,1} and Q_{p,2} in degree 0 with K/O coefficients only. It routed it to SiegelModularFormsModPn. Pilloni's T is a normalized integral operator on all of RΓ(X, Ω^{(k,r)}), and no layer plans it. B5 is characteristic zero and IHG.2 is abstract Hecke algebras on complexes. The introduction (p. 2) attaches T to the double coset K_p diag(p², p, p, 1) K_p, i.e. to T_{p,1} (sourceIssues E1). The body (§7, pp. 37–38) replaces T_{p,1} by the normalized composite above, which acts as p^{3−r}(T_{p,1} + (1+p+p²+p³)T_{p,0}). The decomposition, the eigenvalue formula and the ordinarity criterion are in T-equals-Tp1-plus-multiple-of-Tp0, T-operator-as-composite-of-parahoric-double-cosets and thm-T-eigenvalue-and-ordinarity-criterion.

items.name: Proposition 7.2.1: T_1 and T_2 do not depend on the toroidal compactification
items.statement: Assume r ≥ 1 and k + 2r ≥ r + 2. Let Σ, Σ', Σ'' and Λ, Λ', Λ'' be good polyhedral cone decompositions, with a commutative diagram in which X_{par,Λ''} ←(l_2) X_Kli(p)_{Λ'} →(l_1) X_Λ lies over X_{par,Σ''} ←(p_2) X_Kli(p)_{Σ'} →(p_1) X_Σ via vertical maps r, s, t. By Theorem 6.1.5.1 the following pullbacks are isomorphisms: t^* : RΓ(X_Σ, Ω^{(k,r)}) → RΓ(X_Λ, t^*Ω^{(k,r)}); r^* : RΓ(X_{par,Σ''}, Ω^{(k,r)}) → RΓ(X_{par,Λ''}, r^*Ω^{(k,r)}); and s^* : RΓ(X_Kli(p)_{Σ'}, Ω^{(k,r)}) → RΓ(X_Kli(p)_{Λ'}, s^*Ω^{(k,r)}), where Ω^{(k,r)} means p_1^*Ω^{(k,r)} or p_2^*Ω^{(k,r)}. Then the diagrams commute: t^* ∘ T_{1,Σ} = T_{1,Λ} ∘ r^* and r^* ∘ T_{2,Σ} = T_{2,Λ} ∘ t^*.
items.note: Checked against the pp. 40–41 images. ShimuraCompactifications:C3 plans the proper refinement maps and 'the structure-sheaf pushforward'. AutomorphicBundles:B3 plans 'independence of spaces of sections from the chosen sufficiently fine admissible fan', in characteristic zero and for sections only. PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20 marked coherent-cohomology-independent-of-compactification missing and routed it as a source to C3/C5. Compatibility of the Klingen/paramodular correspondences T_1, T_2 with change of fan is unplanned.

items.name: Lemma 7.3.1(1): T_1 preserves cuspidal sheaves
items.statement: Let D_X, D_{X_par}, D_{X_Kli(p)} be the boundaries of the toroidal compactifications X, X_par, X_Kli(p), often written simply D. If k + 2r ≥ r + 2, the cohomological correspondence T_1 : p_2^*Ω^{(k,r)} → p_1^!Ω^{(k,r)} induces a cohomological correspondence T_1 : p_2^*Ω^{(k,r)}(−D_{X_par}) → p_1^!Ω^{(k,r)}(−D_X).
items.note: Checked against pp. 41–42. The proof uses Lemma 4.2.4.1: the fundamental class respects boundary ideals. AutomorphicBundles:B5's 'Identify cuspidality with the appropriate boundary vanishing condition' concerns expansions, not integral correspondences at p.

items.name: Lemma 7.3.1(2): T_2 preserves cuspidal sheaves
items.statement: If r ≥ 1, the cohomological correspondence T_2 : p_1^*Ω^{(k,r)} → p_2^!Ω^{(k,r)} induces a cohomological correspondence T_2 : p_1^*Ω^{(k,r)}(−D_X) → p_2^!Ω^{(k,r)}(−D_{X_par}).
items.note: Checked against p. 41. The paper says the proof is 'similar' to that of point 1. It is unplanned, as for Lemma 7.3.1(1).

items.name: Lemma 7.3.1(3): the cuspidal correspondences do not depend on the cone decomposition
items.statement: The cuspidal cohomological correspondences of Lemma 7.3.1(1) and (2) are functorial with respect to change of polyhedral cone decomposition: the analogue of Proposition 7.2.1 holds for the cuspidal automorphic sheaves Ω^{(k,r)}(−D).
items.note: Checked against p. 41. It is the cuspidal analogue of Proposition 7.2.1, also missing.

items.name: Reduction mod p of T_1, T_2 and T on X_1 and X_{par,1}
items.statement: Work over Spec F_p. Let (k,r) ∈ Z_{≥0}^2 with r ≥ 1 and k + 2r ≥ r + 2, the hypotheses of §7.1 under which T_1 and T_2 are defined; the paper leaves them implicit here. Let p_1 : X_Kli(p)_1 → X_1 and p_2 : X_Kli(p)_1 → X_{par,1} be the reductions mod p of p_1 and p_2. Notation: for a locally closed subscheme i : T ↪ S and a coherent sheaf F on S, F|_T := i^*F. Reduction mod p and Proposition 4.1.2.1 give normalized cohomological correspondences T_1 : p_2^*(Ω^{(k,r)}|_{X_{par,1}}) → p_1^!(Ω^{(k,r)}|_{X_1}) and T_2 : p_1^*(Ω^{(k,r)}|_{X_1}) → p_2^!(Ω^{(k,r)}|_{X_{par,1}}). These give T_1 ∈ Hom(RΓ(X_{par,1}, Ω^{(k,r)}), RΓ(X_1, Ω^{(k,r)})), T_2 ∈ Hom(RΓ(X_1, Ω^{(k,r)}), RΓ(X_{par,1}, Ω^{(k,r)})), and T = T_1 ∘ T_2.
items.note: Checked against p. 42. It is the reduction mod p of the missing T_1, T_2, via Proposition 4.1.2.1.

items.name: Proposition 7.4.1.1: T_1 and T_2 commute with the Hasse invariant
items.statement: Over F_p, for r ≥ 2 and k + r > 2, the following diagrams commute. First, (p_1^*Ha) ∘ T_1 = T_1 ∘ (p_2^*Ha) as maps p_2^*Ω^{(k,r)} → p_1^!Ω^{(k,r+(p−1))}, where T_1 is taken in weights (k,r) and (k, r+(p−1)). Second, (p_2^*Ha) ∘ T_2 = T_2 ∘ (p_1^*Ha) as maps p_1^*Ω^{(k,r)} → p_2^!Ω^{(k,r+(p−1))}. Here Ha is the Hasse invariant of G on X_1, respectively of G' on X_{par,1}; it is a section of ω^{p−1}.
items.note: Checked against the pp. 42–43 images. The nearest item elsewhere is PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20's ext-hasse-commutes-with-Up-operators (h commutes with U_{p,1}, U_{p,2} on mod-p Siegel forms). It is missing and was routed to SiegelModularFormsModPn. This proposition is a sheaf-level statement about the correspondences T_1, T_2, in all degrees. It uses Lemmas 6.3.4.1–6.3.4.2 (another cluster).

items.name: Lemma 7.4.1.1: p_1^*Ha and p_2^*Ha are non-zero-divisors on X_Kli(p)_1
items.statement: The sections p_2^*Ha and p_1^*Ha are not zero divisors in X_Kli(p)_1.
items.note: Checked against p. 43. It rests on X_Kli(p)_1 being Cohen–Macaulay (Theorem 6.1.5.1) with a non-ordinary locus of codimension 1. Neither is planned.

items.name: Correspondences T_1, T_2 and T on the non-ordinary locus X_1^{≤1}
items.statement: Recall that X_{par,1}^{≤1} and X_1^{≤1} are the vanishing loci of the Hasse invariant in X_{par,1} and X_1. By Proposition 7.4.1.1 and Proposition 4.1.2.1, for all r ≥ 2 + p − 1 and k + r > 2 + p − 1 there are cohomological correspondences T_1 : p_2^*(Ω^{(k,r)}|_{X_{par,1}^{≤1}}) → p_1^!(Ω^{(k,r)}|_{X_1^{≤1}}) and T_2 : p_1^*(Ω^{(k,r)}|_{X_1^{≤1}}) → p_2^!(Ω^{(k,r)}|_{X_{par,1}^{≤1}}). They induce T_1 ∈ Hom(RΓ(X_{par,1}^{≤1}, Ω^{(k,r)}), RΓ(X_1^{≤1}, Ω^{(k,r)})) and T_2 ∈ Hom(RΓ(X_1^{≤1}, Ω^{(k,r)}), RΓ(X_{par,1}^{≤1}, Ω^{(k,r)})), and T := T_1 ∘ T_2.
items.locator: §7.4.1, p. 43; restated at the start of §7.4.2, p. 44
items.note: Checked against pp. 43–44, including the hypotheses r ≥ 2+p−1 and k+r > 2+p−1.

items.name: Maps of exact triangles, and the T-equivariant long exact sequence for multiplication by Ha
items.statement: For all r ≥ 2 and k + r > 2 there are maps of exact triangles. The first row is R(p_1)_*p_2^*Ω^{(k,r)} → Ω^{(k,r)}. It maps (by p_2^*Ha on the left and multiplication by Ha on the right) to R(p_1)_*p_2^*Ω^{(k,r+(p−1))} → Ω^{(k,r+(p−1))}, which maps to R(p_1)_*(p_2)^*(Ω^{(k,r+(p−1))}|_{X_{par,1}^{≤1}}) → Ω^{(k,r+(p−1))}|_{X_1^{≤1}}, followed by +1. There are analogous maps of triangles for R(p_2)_*p_1^*Ω → Ω. Consequently, for r ≥ 2 and k + r > 2 there is a long exact sequence H^*(X_1, Ω^{(k,r)}) →(×Ha) H^*(X_1, Ω^{(k,r+(p−1))}) → H^*(X_1^{≤1}, Ω^{(k,r+(p−1))}) → … on which T acts equivariantly.
items.note: Checked against the pp. 43–44 images. PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20's hasse-multiplication-exact-sequences (routed to GSp4NonregularModularityLifting) concerns Hecke operators away from p. T-equivariance at p is unplanned.

items.name: Lemma 7.4.2.1: splitting the base by the type (étale, multiplicative, biconnected) of an order-p subgroup
items.statement: Let N ∈ Z_{≥1}, let S be a scheme of characteristic p, and let G be a truncated Barsotti–Tate group of level N over S whose étale rank and multiplicative rank are constant over S. Let H ⊂ G be a subgroup scheme of order p. Then S is a disjoint union of open and closed subschemes S = S^{et} ⊔ S^m ⊔ S^{oo} such that, at every geometric point of S^{et}, S^m and S^{oo}, the group H is isomorphic to Z/pZ, μ_p and α_p respectively.
items.note: Checked against p. 44. This is a general statement about truncated BT groups in characteristic p. FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.1 plans 'Cartier duality, connected–étale sequences over the allowed bases, ... finite-flat subgroup and quotient constructions'. It does not plan the multiplicative/biconnected/étale type decomposition of the base. Neither library has p-divisible or BT groups (library-coverage: no connected–étale sequence for finite flat groups).

items.name: Lemma 7.4.2.2: X_Kli(p)|_{X_{par,1}^{=1}} splits into étale, multiplicative and bi-infinitesimal components
items.statement: Notation: for a map of schemes S → T and a locally closed subscheme Z ↪ T, write S|_Z := S ×_T Z. Consider the chain G → G' → G over X_Kli(p). The scheme X_Kli(p)|_{X_{par,1}^{=1}} is the disjoint union of three open and closed subschemes. The étale component (X_Kli(p)|_{X_{par,1}^{=1}})^{et} is where the isogeny G' → G has multiplicative kernel. The multiplicative component (X_Kli(p)|_{X_{par,1}^{=1}})^m is where G' → G is étale. The bi-infinitesimal component (X_Kli(p)|_{X_{par,1}^{=1}})^{oo} is where G' → G has bi-connected kernel. Consequently X_Kli(p)|_{X_1^{=1}}, which has the same topological space, is also the union of three types of components: (X_Kli(p)|_{X_1^{=1}})^{et}, (X_Kli(p)|_{X_1^{=1}})^m and (X_Kli(p)|_{X_1^{=1}})^{oo}.
items.locator: §7.4.2, Lemma 7.4.2.2 and the following paragraph, pp. 44–45
items.note: Checked against pp. 44–45. It is specific to the Klingen model over the paramodular p-rank-1 locus, and extends to the boundary through the local charts. Unplanned.

items.name: Lemma 7.4.2.3: X_{par,1}^{=1} = X_{par,1}^{=1,oo} ∪ X_{par,1}^{=1,m−et}
items.statement: The scheme X_{par,1}^{=1} is the union of two types of components. The components X_{par,1}^{=1,oo} are those where the kernel K(λ) of the quasi-polarization G'[p^∞] → (G')^t[p^∞] is a biconnected group. The components X_{par,1}^{=1,m−et} are those where the kernel of the polarization contains a multiplicative group.
items.note: Checked against p. 45. It concerns paramodular (degree-p² polarization) geometry, which no layer plans. PELModuli:M5 asks only for 'at least one non-principal polarization type' at good primes.

items.name: Lemma 7.4.2.4: where p_2 sends the components of Lemma 7.4.2.2
items.note: Checked against p. 45. Unplanned.

items.name: Decompositions T_1 = T_1^m + T_1^{et} + T_1^{oo} and T_2 = T_2^m + T_2^{et} + T_2^{oo} over the p-rank one locus
items.statement: Assume r ≥ p + 1 and k + r > p + 1, so that T_1 and T_2 are defined over X^{≤1} (§7.4.1–7.4.2) and restrict to the open subschemes X^{=1}. The cohomological correspondence T_1 : p_2^*Ω^{(k,r)}|_{X_{par,1}^{=1}} → p_1^!Ω^{(k,r)}|_{X_1^{=1}} is the sum T_1^m + T_1^{et} + T_1^{oo} of its projections on the multiplicative, étale and bi-infinitesimal components of Lemma 7.4.2.2. Similarly, T_2 : p_1^*Ω^{(k,r)}|_{X_1^{=1}} → p_2^!Ω^{(k,r)}|_{X_{par,1}^{=1}} decomposes as T_2 = T_2^m + T_2^{et} + T_2^{oo}. Here T_2^m, T_2^{et} and T_2^{oo} are the projections of T_2 on the étale, multiplicative and bi-infinitesimal components respectively: the roles of étale and multiplicative are switched between T_1 and T_2. By Lemmas 7.4.2.3–7.4.2.4 this gives maps on cohomology H^*(X_1^{=1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) →((T_2^{oo}, T_2^m + T_2^{et})) H^*(X_{par,1}^{=1,oo}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) ⊕ H^*(X_{par,1}^{=1,m−et}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) →((T_1^{oo}, T_1^{et} + T_1^m)) H^*(X_1^{=1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)).
items.note: Checked against p. 45, including the reversed roles of étale and multiplicative components between T_1 and T_2. Unplanned. §11.1.2 (pp. 68–69) recalls these correspondences, restricted to the p-rank-one locus, and their decompositions T_1 = T_1^m + T_1^{et} + T_1^{oo}, T_2 = T_2^m + T_2^{et} + T_2^{oo} on H^0(X_1^{=1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)), under the same hypotheses r ≥ p + 1 and k + r > p + 1. It uses them for Lemma 11.1.2.1 (U = T on H^0(X_1^{=1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) when k + r > 2(p+1) and r ≥ p + 1).

items.name: Proposition 7.4.2.1 (first diagram): T_1 commutes with Ha' on X^{≤1}
items.note: Checked against the pp. 45–48 images. The proof uses completions along p-rank-1 strata, miracle flatness (missing, see ext-miracle-flatness) and Lemma 6.3.4.2. Unplanned.

items.name: Proposition 7.4.2.1 (second diagram): T_2^{et} commutes with Ha' on X^{=1}
items.note: Checked against the pp. 46 and 48 images. Unplanned.

items.name: Proposition 7.4.2.1: T_1^m = T_1^{oo} = 0 and T_2^m = 0
items.statement: For r ≥ 2 + (p − 1) and k + r > 2(p + 1), the component correspondences over the p-rank one locus satisfy T_1^m = T_1^{oo} = 0 and T_2^m = 0.
items.note: Checked against the p. 48 image. On the lift Ã, the vanishing of T_1^{oo} uses the Fargues degree 1/(p+1) (ext-fargues-degree-of-subgroups). The printed formula sums over L ⊂ Ã[p] with L^⊥ biconnected. Unplanned.

items.name: Proposition 7.4.2.1 (last part): for r ≥ p + 2, T_2^{oo} = 0 and T_2 commutes with Ha' on X^{≤1}
items.note: Checked against the pp. 46 and 48 images. Remark 7.4.2.1(1) says the statement fails for r = p+1. Unplanned.

items.name: Corollary 7.4.2.1: T = T_1^{et} ∘ T_2^{et} on the p-rank one locus
items.statement: When r ≥ p + 1 and k + r > 2(p + 1), T = T_1 ∘ T_2 = T_1^{et} ∘ T_2^{et} as endomorphisms of H^*(X_1^{=1}, Ω^{(k,r)}). (The printed text writes ω^{(k,r)}.)
items.note: Checked against the p. 48 image. The printed ω^{(k,r)} should read Ω^{(k,r)}. Unplanned.

items.name: Lemma 7.4.2.5: p_1^*Ha' is a non-zero-divisor on X_Kli(p)_1 ×_{X_1} X_1^{≤1}
items.statement: The section p_1^*Ha' is not a zero divisor in X_Kli(p)_1 ×_{X_1} X_1^{≤1}.
items.note: Checked against p. 48 and footnote 11. It needs the Cohen–Macaulay property of X_Kli(p)_1 ×_{X_1} X_1^{≤1}. Unplanned.

items.name: T_1 on the p-rank zero locus, and the Ha' long exact sequences
items.statement: By Proposition 7.4.2.1 and Proposition 4.1.2.1, for r ≥ p^2 + p = 2 + (p − 1) + (p^2 − 1) and k + r > 2(p + 1) + p^2 − 1 there is a cohomological correspondence T_1 : p_2^*Ω^{(k,r)}|_{X_{par,1}^{=0}} → p_1^!Ω^{(k,r)}|_{X_1^{=0}}. Moreover, for all r ≥ 2 + p − 1 and k + r > 2(p + 1) + p^2 − 1 there is a commutative diagram of long exact sequences, with vertical maps T_1 going from the X_par row to the X row. The X_par row is H^*(X_{par,1}^{≤1}, Ω^{(k,r)}) →(Ha') H^*(X_{par,1}^{≤1}, Ω^{(k,r+(p^2−1))}) → H^*(X_{par,1}^{≤0}, Ω^{(k,r+(p^2−1))}) → …. The X row is H^*(X_1^{≤1}, Ω^{(k,r)}) →(Ha') H^*(X_1^{≤1}, Ω^{(k,r+(p^2−1))}) → H^*(X_1^{≤0}, Ω^{(k,r+(p^2−1))}) → ….
items.note: Checked against the pp. 48–49 images, including both sets of bounds (r ≥ p²+p; r ≥ 2+p−1 with k+r > 2(p+1)+p²−1). Unplanned.

items.name: Proposition 7.4.2.2: T_1 vanishes on the p-rank zero locus for k large
items.statement: There is a constant C, not depending on the prime-to-p level K^p, such that for all k ≥ C and all r ≥ p^2 + p the cohomological correspondence T_1 : p_2^*Ω^{(k,r)}|_{X_{par,1}^{=0}} → p_1^!Ω^{(k,r)}|_{X_1^{=0}} is zero.
items.note: Checked against the pp. 49–50 images. The proof uses Artin–Rees (in Mathlib, see ext-artin-rees) and Lemma 7.4.2.6. On p. 49 it cites Lemma 7.1.1 as giving divisibility 'when r ≥ 1'; the lemma's hypothesis is k + 2r ≥ 2 + r, which is harmless here since r ≥ p²+p. The argument that C is independent of K^p (p. 50) is sound: vanishing descends along the finite étale level-change map away from the boundary, and the p-rank-0 locus avoids the boundary. The proposition itself is unplanned.

items.name: Lemma 7.4.2.6: an order-p^3 subgroup of A[p], for A of p-rank 0, contains Ker F
items.statement: Let A → Spec l be an abelian surface of p-rank 0 over a field l of characteristic p, and let L ⊂ A[p] be a group scheme of order p^3. Then Ker F ⊂ L.
items.note: Checked against the p. 50 image. It is a general fact about p-torsion of p-rank-0 abelian surfaces, proved with the Weil pairing A[p] × A[p]^D → μ_p. AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A3 plans 'the Weil pairing between A[n] and A∨[n]' and adds 'The p-primary torsion in characteristic p is never replaced by its group of geometric points'. It does not state this lemma. FiniteFlatGroups R07.2 supplies Frobenius/Verschiebung and the ordinary/supersingular cases.

items.name: Lemma 8.1.1: T is locally finite on H^0(X_1^{=1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D))
items.statement: For all r ≥ 2 + (p − 1) and all k > p + 1, the action of T on H^0(X_1^{=1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) is locally finite.
items.note: Checked against p. 50. H^0(X_1^{=1}, ·) is written as a colimit over Ha' of H^0(X_1^{≤1}, ·). Unplanned.

items.name: The ordinary projector e for T on H^0(X_1^{=1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D))
items.statement: For k > p + 1 and r ≥ p + 1, e denotes the ordinary projector associated, by §2.3, with the locally finite operator T on H^0(X_1^{=1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)).
items.note: Checked against p. 50. Parts exist but do not cover it. PadicFamilies:L0a plans the projector 'For an endomorphism U of a finite underlying module' and for inverse limits of finite quotients, but not for a locally finite operator on a filtered colimit (§2.3, another cluster). Mathlib has the finite Fitting decomposition, LinearMap.eventually_isCompl_ker_pow_range_pow (Mathlib/RingTheory/Artinian/Module.lean:317). The space and the operator T are missing.

items.name: Lemma 8.1.2(1): Ha'T = THa' on H^0(X_1^{≤1}, ·)
items.note: Checked against the pp. 50–51 images. Unplanned.

items.name: Lemma 8.1.2(2): Ha'T = THa' on H^i(X_1^{≤1}, ·) for r ≥ p + 2
items.statement: If r > 2 + (p − 1) and k > p + 1, then Ha'T = THa' as morphisms H^i(X_1^{≤1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) → H^i(X_1^{≤1}, Ω^{(k,r+(p^2−1))}(−D)) for all i.
items.note: Checked against the pp. 50–51 images. The hypothesis is r > 2+(p−1), i.e. r ≥ p+2. Remark 8.1.1 says r = p+1 is open. Unplanned.

items.name: Vanishing of higher cuspidal cohomology on the p-rank one stratum
items.statement: For all r (and k ≥ 0), H^i(X_1^{=1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) = 0 for i > 0.
items.locator: §8.1, end of the proof of Proposition 8.1.1, p. 52
items.note: Checked against p. 52. It uses relative acyclicity to the minimal compactification (Theorem 6.2.2.1, another cluster) and affineness of the image of X_1^{=1). No layer plans this. AutomorphicBundles:B3 treats the pushforward to the minimal compactification in characteristic zero only. PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20's ext-pilloni-vanishing-large-parallel-weight, a related statement, is missing.

items.name: Proposition 8.1.1 (first part): eH^0(X_1^{≤1}, ·) = eH^0(X_1^{=1}, ·)
items.statement: There is a constant C (see Proposition 7.4.2.2), independent of the level K^p, such that for k ≥ C and r ≥ p + 1 restriction gives isomorphisms eH^0(X_1^{≤1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) = eH^0(X_1^{=1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)).
items.note: Checked against the pp. 51–52 images. Unplanned.

items.name: Proposition 8.1.1 (second part): for r ≥ p + 2, eH^i(X_1^{≤1}, ·) = 0 for i = 1, 2
items.statement: With C as in Proposition 8.1.1, for k ≥ C and r ≥ p + 2: eH^i(X_1^{≤1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) = eH^i(X_1^{=1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) = 0 for i = 1, 2.
items.note: Checked against the pp. 51–52 images. Unplanned.

items.name: Ha-colimit acyclic resolution and the two-term complex computing RΓ(X_1^{≥1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D))
items.statement: Let X_1^{≥1} = X_1 ∖ X_1^{=0}. Over X_1^{≥1} there is a resolution 0 → Ω^{(k,r)}(−D) → colim_{n,×Ha} Ω^{(k,r+(p−1)n)}(−D) → colim_n Ω^{(k,r+(p−1)n)}(−D)/(Ha)^n → 0. All these sheaves are acyclic relative to the minimal compactification (Theorem 6.2.2.1). The support of the middle sheaf is the rank 2 locus and that of the last sheaf is the rank 1 locus, and both are affine in the minimal compactification. So this is an acyclic resolution, and RΓ(X_1^{≥1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) is represented by the complex H^0(X_1^{=2}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) → colim_n H^0(X_1^{≥1}, Ω^{(k,r+(p−1)n)}(−D)/(Ha)^n) in degrees 0 and 1. Moreover H^0(X_1^{=2}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) = colim_n H^0(X_1, Ω^{(k,r+n(p−1))}(−D)), with transition maps multiplication by Ha.
items.note: Checked against the p. 52 image. The paper writes the middle term's weights both as r+(p−1)n and as r+(p²−1)n; the item's (p−1) is the one consistent with multiplication by Ha. Unplanned.

items.name: Lemma 8.2.1: T is locally finite on RΓ(X_1^{≥1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D))
items.statement: The action of T on RΓ(X_1^{≥1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) is locally finite for k > p + 1 and r ≥ 2.
items.note: Checked against p. 52. It uses Lemma 2.1.1 (another cluster) for extensions. Unplanned.

items.name: H^0(X_1^{≥1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) = H^0(X_1, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D))
items.statement: Since X_1^{=0} has codimension 2 in X_1 and X_1 is smooth, H^0(X_1^{≥1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) = H^0(X_1, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) unconditionally. In particular eH^0(X_1^{≥1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) = eH^0(X_1, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)).
items.note: Checked against p. 53. PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20's hecke-at-p-via-almost-ordinary-locus-and-hartogs states the same equality with O/ϖ^m coefficients: H^0(X, ω) = H^0(X′, ω), X′ the p-rank ≥ 1 locus. It records codimension 2 and algebraic Hartogs as 'planned nowhere' and routes them to SiegelModularFormsModPn. TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure:TC.0 states that 'General Hartogs statements without codimension/normality ... are not inferred'. Per library-coverage, Tau Ceti has only one-dimensional algebraic Hartogs. The same codimension-2 extension is used again in the proof of Corollary 11.2.1 (p. 71): since the complement of 𝔛^{≥1} in 𝔛 has codimension 2, the map eH^0(X, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D) ⊗ Q_p/Z_p) → eH^0(𝔛^{≥1}, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D) ⊗ Q_p/Z_p) is an isomorphism.

items.name: Ordinary cohomology of Ω/Ha^n on X_1 and on X_1^{≥1} (steps in the proof of Prop. 8.2.1)
items.statement: Let C be as in Proposition 8.1.1. (i) For Z = X_1^{≥1} and for Z = X_1 there are exact sequences 0 → H^0(Z, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) → H^0(X_1^{ord}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) → colim_n H^0(Z, Ω^{(k,r+n(p−1))}(−D)/Ha^n) → H^1(Z, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) → 0, compatible with restriction. There are also isomorphisms colim_n H^i(X_1, Ω^{(k,r+n(p−1))}(−D)/Ha^n) ≃ H^{i+1}(X_1, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) for i = 1, 2. (ii) eH^i(X_1, Ω^{(k,r+n(p−1))}(−D)/Ha^n) = 0 for all n ≥ 1, k ≥ C, r ≥ 3 and i ∈ {1, 2}. (iii) eH^0(X_1, Ω^{(k,r+n(p−1))}(−D)/Ha^n) → eH^0(X_1^{≥1}, Ω^{(k,r+n(p−1))}(−D)/Ha^n) is bijective for all n ≥ 1, k ≥ C and r ≥ 3.
items.note: Checked against the pp. 53–54 images. Unplanned.

items.name: Proposition 8.2.1 (first part): eRΓ(X_1^{≥1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) is perfect of amplitude [0,1]
items.statement: For all r ≥ 2 and k ≥ C (C as in Proposition 7.4.2.2), eRΓ(X_1^{≥1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) is a perfect complex of amplitude [0,1] of F_p-vector spaces.
items.note: Checked against the p. 53 image. The notion of a perfect complex is planned (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:P7, reviewed node 'Perfect complexes, Tor-amplitude and minimal complexes over local rings'). The theorem is not.

items.name: Proposition 8.2.1 (second part): eRΓ(X_1, ·) ≃ eRΓ(X_1^{≥1}, ·) for r ≥ 3
items.statement: For all r ≥ 3 and k ≥ C, the restriction map eRΓ(X_1, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) → eRΓ(X_1^{≥1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) is a quasi-isomorphism.
items.note: Checked against the p. 53 image. Remark 8.2.1 says the r = 2 case would follow from Remark 8.1.2. Unplanned.

items.name: Proposition 8.2.1 (third part): weight (k,2): eH^0 agrees and eH^1 injects
items.statement: For all k ≥ C, eH^0(X_1^{≥1}, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) = eH^0(X_1, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)), and the map eH^1(X_1, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) → eH^1(X_1^{≥1}, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) is injective. By the proof, both are finite-dimensional F_p-vector spaces.
items.note: Checked against the pp. 53–54 images. On p. 54 the paper calls these spaces 'finite dimensional'. Unplanned.

items.name: Serre–Tate local moduli for ordinary abelian surfaces
items.statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p, and let x : Spec k → X be an ordinary point, with abelian surface G and Tate module T ≅ Z_p^2 (fixed isomorphism). By Serre–Tate theory ([39]) the formal deformation space of x is Hom(Sym^2 T, Ĝ_m). Its underlying ring is W(k)[[X,Y,Z]], where the Serre–Tate parameter is the map Z_p^2 → Z_p^2 ⊗ Ĝ_m given by the symmetric matrix (X Z; Z Y). Deforming isogenies amounts to compatibility of Serre–Tate parameters. At an ordinary point of X_par the parameter is given by the matrix (X pZ; Z Y), again with ring W(k)[[X,Y,Z]].
items.note: Neither plan covers the canonical coordinates. AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A4 plans the Serre–Tate equivalence only: 'Prove the Serre–Tate equivalence for deformations of abelian schemes with endomorphism and polarization structures; identify its tangent map with the Hodge filtration'. Tau Ceti ModularCurves 7F (ST-1) plans it only for elliptic curves (Katz Thm 1.2.1). Katz's coordinates are the formal torus Hom(Sym²T, Ĝ_m) for an ordinary principally polarized abelian variety, with ring W(k)[[X,Y,Z]], and the matching of Serre–Tate parameters along isogenies. Library-coverage: 'SerreTate has zero occurrences'. The paramodular (X pZ; Z Y) chart belongs with the new roadmap. The same Serre–Tate input, the formal torus Hom(Sym^2 T, Ĝ_m) at ordinary points, is used again in §10.3, proofs of Lemmas 10.3.2–10.3.3 (pp. 60–61), and in §14.9, proof of Lemma 14.9.1 (pp. 104–105). In the display of the deformation ring on p. 60 the exponents on X′ and Z′ are swapped (sourceIssues E77). The trace-divisibility computations in the proof of Lemma 14.9.1 are part of that proof, not of this external input. External input: N. Katz, Serre–Tate local moduli, in: Surfaces Algébriques, LNM 868, Springer, 1981 [39]

items.name: Splitting of the multiplicative–connected–étale filtration over a perfect base
items.statement: Over a perfect scheme S of characteristic p, a (truncated) Barsotti–Tate group G with constant étale and multiplicative ranks decomposes as G = G^m ⊕ G^{oo} ⊕ G^{et}, into multiplicative, biconnected and étale parts, splitting its multiplicative–connected–étale filtration.
items.note: Checked against p. 44 ([59], Prop. 1.3). FiniteFlatGroups:R07.1 plans 'connected–étale sequences over the allowed bases', and R07.2 'Frobenius/Verschiebung'. Neither plans the splitting of the multiplicative–connected–étale filtration over a perfect base. IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration:IG.0 builds completely slope-divisible (Oort–Zink) representatives only for its fixed unitary datum. Nothing is in Mathlib or Tau Ceti. External input: F. Oort and T. Zink, Families of p-divisible groups with constant Newton polygon, Doc. Math. 7 (2002), 183–201, prop. 1.3 [59]

items.name: Fargues degree of the order-p subgroups of E[p], for a supersingular E over W(l)
items.statement: For a finite flat group scheme L over O_C with conormal module ω_L ≅ ⊕_i O_C/a_i, the degree (Fargues) is deg L = Σ_i v(a_i), with v(p) = 1. For the lift Ã over W(l) with p-divisible group μ_{p^∞} ⊕ E[p^∞] ⊕ Q_p/Z_p (E[p^∞] the p-divisible group of a supersingular elliptic curve over W(l)), an order-p biconnected subgroup L^0 ⊂ E[p] has degree 1/(p+1). Consequently, for L = L^m ⊕ L^0 ⊕ L^{et} ⊂ Ã[p], the map e^*Ω^1_{Ã/L} → e^*Ω^1_Ã has elementary divisors (p, ϖ) with v(ϖ) = 1/(p+1).
items.note: Checked against the p. 48 image. No layer names Fargues' degree of finite flat group schemes over O_C. The closest are HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T0 ('the integral differential calculations here') and T3 ('integral differential estimates', for BHW canonical subgroups). AInfCohomology:AI.2's 'Fargues' equivalence' is about BKF modules and is unrelated. External input: L. Fargues, La filtration de Harder–Narasimhan des schémas en groupes finis et plats, J. reine angew. Math. 645 (2010) [20]; V. Pilloni, Prolongement analytique sur les variétés de Siegel, Duke Math. J. 157 (2011), example A.2.2 [62]

items.name: Artin–Rees lemma
items.statement: Let A be a Noetherian ring, 𝔞 ⊂ A an ideal, M a finite A-module and N ⊂ M a submodule. There is c ≥ 0 such that 𝔞^nM ∩ N = 𝔞^{n−c}(𝔞^cM ∩ N) for all n ≥ c.
items.note: Pilloni's use on p. 49 (∃C: p²A ∩ ∩_i p_i^C ⊂ p²I) follows from three facts: Artin–Rees for M = A, N = p²A and each ideal p_i; p being a non-zero-divisor on A; and ∩_i p_i^N ⊂ I for N ≫ 0. That consequence is not in the libraries. Tau Ceti's TauCeti.ArtinRees.exists_controlled_lift (TauCeti/RingTheory/Ideal/ArtinRees.lean:78) is a different consequence. External input: Artin–Rees lemma (e.g. Matsumura, Commutative ring theory, Thm. 8.5). Mathlib at 082e2d3: Ideal.exists_pow_inf_eq_pow_smul, Mathlib/RingTheory/Filtration.lean:388, stating ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ k, I ^ n • ⊤ ⊓ N = I ^ (n - k) • (I ^ k • ⊤ ⊓ N) for [IsNoetherianRing R] [Module.Finite R M] (N : Submodule R M).

items.name: Deep Klingen level structure X^{≥1}_Kli(p^m)_n
items.statement: Setting: p a fixed prime, K = K^p·GSp4(Z_p) with K^p neat, X → Spec Z_p a toroidal compactification (good polyhedral cone decomposition) of the Siegel threefold of level K, G → X the universal semi-abelian scheme, X_n = X ⊗ Z/p^nZ, and X_n^{≥1} ⊂ X_n the open subscheme where the multiplicative rank (p-rank) of G is ≥ 1. For m ≥ 1 and n ≥ 1, X^{≥1}_Kli(p^m)_n → X^{≥1}_n is the moduli space of subgroup schemes H_m ⊂ G[p^m] that are étale-locally isomorphic to µ_{p^m}. X^{ord}_Kli(p^m)_n = X^{=2}_Kli(p^m)_n denotes its ordinary locus (the preimage of X_n^{=2}). The transition maps X^{≥1}_Kli(p^m)_n → X^{≥1}_Kli(p^{m'})_n (m' ≤ m) send H_m to H_{m'} = H_m[p^{m'}] (in particular H_1 = H_m[p]); by convention X^{≥1}_Kli(p^0)_n = X^{≥1}_n.
items.note: No layer plans the moduli X^{≥1}_Kli(p^m)_n of subgroups H_m ⊂ G[p^m] étale-locally ≅ µ_{p^m} over the p-rank ≥ 1 locus. The p-rank strata of the Siegel threefold mod p^n are themselves planned nowhere (PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20 routes them to the proposed SiegelModularFormsModPn, not in the atlas). IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration:IG.1 builds Igusa towers over central leaves of its fixed PEL datum ('Construct Ig^X by trivializing the PEL p-divisible group over the leaf'). HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T3–T5 and OverconvergentAutomorphicForms:O7 are Hilbert canonical-subgroup/ordinary towers. Same gap as K1's deep-klingen-tower-H-infinity. Remark 9.1.1.1 (p. 54), which compares X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1 with X_Kli(p)_1 ×_{X_1} X_1^{≥1}, is recorded in deep-klingen-p-vs-klingen-level-open-immersion.

items.name: Remark 9.1.1.1: X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1 inside the Klingen-level compactification
items.statement: Let X_Kli(p) be the toroidal compactification of Klingen level at p (in this remark, with the same polyhedral cone decomposition as X), with chain of isogenies G → G' → G (the first of degree p^3, the composite multiplication by p) and universal order-p subgroup H_1 ⊂ G[p], the orthogonal for the Weil pairing on G[p] of Ker(G → G') (equivalently the kernel of the degree-p isogeny G → (G')^t dual to G' → G). Then X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1 is the open subscheme of X_Kli(p)_1 ×_{X_1} X_1^{≥1} where H_1 is multiplicative of order p, and this open subscheme is strictly smaller than X_Kli(p)_1 ×_{X_1} X_1^{≥1}.
items.note: Needs the Klingen-level compactification X_Kli(p) with its chain G → G' → G, which is missing (K1 klingen-level-cover-XKli: PELModuli:M2 has 'no nontrivial level at p', and M4 gives only normalizations without a moduli interpretation). It also needs the missing deep Klingen space. The comparison of the two spaces is this paper's.

items.name: Finite flat replacement G̃[p^m] of G[p^m] at the boundary
items.statement: Let S be the spectrum of a completed local ring of X_n^{≥1}. There is a finite flat subgroup scheme G̃[p^m] ⊂ G[p^m] over S containing the connected component of G[p^m]. Away from the boundary one takes G̃[p^m] = G[p^m]; at the boundary G̃ is the semi-abelian scheme of constant toric rank occurring in Mumford's construction, whose p^m-torsion is finite flat (whereas G[p^m] is only quasi-finite).
items.note: C4 plans Mumford's construction (the polarized degeneration/1-motive construction, with its Raynaud extension G̃ of constant toric rank) and the formal local description of the universal degeneration over complete local bases. The closed immersion G̃[p^m] ↪ G[p^m], whose image is finite flat and contains G[p^m]^0 = Ĝ[p^m], is a standard property of that construction (Faltings–Chai III). C4 should state it explicitly. The integral Siegel charts come from C5. Borderline: see clusterNotes. For Mumford's construction and the semi-abelian scheme G̃ of constant toric rank, the paper cites Faltings–Chai, [18], chap. III. External input: Mumford's construction of degenerating abelian varieties: G. Faltings and C.-L. Chai, Degeneration of abelian varieties, Ergeb. Math. 22, Springer 1990, chap. III ([18] in the paper).

items.name: Unique lifting of homomorphisms into étale group schemes along nilpotent thickenings
items.statement: Let T ↪ T' be an infinitesimal (nilpotent) thickening, F' a finite flat group scheme over T', and E' an étale group scheme over T' (every étale group scheme over T deforms uniquely to T'). Then every homomorphism ψ_T : F'|_T → E'|_T extends uniquely to a homomorphism ψ_{T'} : F' → E'. As used: the surjection ψ_T : G̃^D[p^m]|_T → H_m^D|_T (H_m^D étale, locally ≅ Z/p^mZ) extends uniquely to ψ_{T'} : G̃^D[p^m]|_{T'} → H_m^D|_{T'} for any deformation G̃^D[p^m]|_{T'}.
items.note: Mathlib has only the affine, ring-level lifting. Algebra.FormallyEtale.comp_bijective gives unique lifts of algebra maps along square-zero ideals (read in Mathlib/RingTheory/Etale/Basic.lean), and Algebra.FormallySmooth.lift handles nilpotent ideals. Neither library has scheme-level infinitesimal lifting for étale morphisms, topological invariance of the étale site, or a group-scheme statement. SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4 ('Develop infinitesimal lifting and obstruction complexes') is generic. FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.2 supplies 'the deformation results needed for p-divisible groups over nilpotent thickenings', not this lemma. The paper cites Illusie's deformation theory for this step: [37], thm VII, 4.2.5 (p. 55). Chapter VII is in Complexe cotangent et déformations II (LNM 283), while [37] is listed as volume I (LNM 239) (sourceIssues E71). External input: Cited as Illusie's deformation theory, '[37], thm VII, 4.2.5' ([37] = L. Illusie, Complexe cotangent et déformations I, LNM 239; chapter VII is in volume II, LNM 283). The statement also follows directly from the formal étaleness of E' → T' (EGA IV 17–18).

items.name: Lemma 9.1.1.1: the deep Klingen transition maps are étale and affine
items.statement: For all m ≥ 1 and n ≥ 1, the map X^{≥1}_Kli(p^m)_n → X^{≥1}_Kli(p^{m−1})_n, H_m ↦ H_m[p^{m−1}] (the target is X_n^{≥1} when m = 1), is étale and affine.

items.name: Remark 9.1.1.2: degrees of the deep Klingen transition maps
items.statement: The map X^{≥1}_Kli(p^m)_n → X^{≥1}_Kli(p^{m−1})_n (m ≥ 1) is not finite: it is an isomorphism over the p-rank-one locus, and over the p-rank-two (ordinary) locus it is finite étale of degree p if m ≥ 2 and of degree p + 1 if m = 1.
items.note: Degree count for the missing deep Klingen tower over the p-rank strata. That tower over the p-rank ≥ 1 locus is planned nowhere (see deep-klingen-level-structure-mod-pn).

items.name: Igusa tower IG(p^m)_n over the deep Klingen tower
items.statement: IG(p^m)_n := Isom_{X^{≥1}_Kli(p^m)_n}(µ_{p^m}, H_m), a (Z/p^mZ)^×-torsor over X^{≥1}_Kli(p^m)_n. There are commutative squares: X^{≥1}_Kli(p^m)_{n−1} → X^{≥1}_Kli(p^m)_n over X^{≥1}_Kli(p^{m−1})_{n−1} → X^{≥1}_Kli(p^{m−1})_n. In them the horizontal maps (reduction mod p^{n−1}) are closed immersions and the vertical maps are étale and affine. Above them lie the commutative squares IG(p^m)_{n−1} → IG(p^m)_n over IG(p^{m−1})_{n−1} → IG(p^{m−1})_n, the vertical maps restricting an isomorphism µ_{p^m} ≅ H_m to µ_{p^{m−1}} ≅ H_{m−1}.
items.note: IG(p^m)_n = Isom(µ_{p^m}, H_m) lives over the missing deep Klingen tower. IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration:IG.1's Igusa varieties are a different object: they trivialize the whole p-divisible group over a central leaf of that roadmap's unitary datum. HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T5 builds Hilbert Igusa torsors of the dual canonical subgroup.

items.name: Formal deep Klingen tower 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^m), 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^∞) and the universal H_∞
items.statement: Let 𝔛 → Spf Z_p be the p-adic completion of X and 𝔛^{≥1} ⊂ 𝔛 the open formal subscheme where the multiplicative rank of G is ≥ 1. For m ≥ 1, 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^m) → 𝔛 is the moduli of subgroups H_m ↪ G[p^m] étale-locally isomorphic to µ_{p^m} (the limit over n of the X^{≥1}_Kli(p^m)_n). The paper asserts that 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^m) → 𝔛 is étale and affine (but not finite). 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^∞) is the inverse limit over m of 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^m), which exists because the transition maps are affine. Over it, H_∞ ↪ G[p^∞] is the universal multiplicative Barsotti–Tate subgroup, étale-locally ≅ µ_{p^∞}, with H_∞[p^m] = H_m.
items.note: p-adic formal completion is planned (AdicSpacesPartII:F0: 'Completion along a closed subscheme is functorial'), and multiplicative p-divisible groups belong to R07.1. The formal tower 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^m), its pro-affine limit and the universal H_∞ are not planned (K1 deep-klingen-tower-H-infinity, missing). The introduction (p. 4) describes the fibres of 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^∞) → 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p): they are isomorphic to 1 + pZ_p ⊂ P^1(Z_p) over the ordinary locus, and the map is an isomorphism over the p-rank-one locus. The finite-level form is Remark 9.1.1.2 (p. 55, deep-klingen-transition-not-finite-degrees): X^{≥1}_Kli(p^m)_n → X^{≥1}_Kli(p^{m−1})_n is an isomorphism over the p-rank-1 locus and has rank p (resp. p+1) over the p-rank-2 locus if m ≥ 2 (resp. m = 1), so it is not finite.

items.name: Formal Igusa tower 𝔍𝔊(p^m), 𝔍𝔊(p^∞)
items.statement: Over 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^m), 𝔍𝔊(p^m) := Isom(µ_{p^m}, H_m), a (Z/p^mZ)^×-torsor. Over 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^∞), 𝔍𝔊(p^∞) := Isom(µ_{p^∞}, H_∞), a Z_p^×-torsor.
items.note: Z_p^×-torsor Isom(µ_{p^∞}, H_∞) over the missing formal tower. OverconvergentAutomorphicForms:O7 plans Igusa towers only for Hilbert ordinary forms.

items.name: Weight algebra Λ = Z_p[[Z_p^×]] and universal character κ
items.statement: Λ := Z_p[[Z_p^×]] is the completed group algebra of Z_p^×, and κ : Z_p^× → Λ^× is the universal (tautological) character. For n ≥ 1, Λ_n := Z/p^nZ[(Z/p^nZ)^×]. For m ≥ n, κ_{m,n} : (Z/p^mZ)^× → Λ_n^× is the tautological character factoring through (Z/p^nZ)^×. For k ∈ Z, specialisation 'at k' means the character x ↦ x^k (Λ → Z_p, [x] ↦ x^k).
items.note: Λ = Z_p[[Z_p^×]], κ as the tautological map, and the weight-k specialisation (by the universal property for continuous characters) are planned (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1, and completedGroupAlgebra in the Tau Ceti ProfiniteProPGroups layer 9). The finite group rings Λ_n = Z/p^nZ[(Z/p^nZ)^×] and the maps κ_{m,n} are already in Mathlib: Λ_n is MonoidAlgebra (ZMod (p^n)) (ZMod (p^n))ˣ, and κ_{m,n} is the composite of ZMod.unitsMap (p^n ∣ p^m) and MonoidAlgebra.of. Λ itself is in neither library. The introduction (§1, p. 2) already introduces Λ = Z_p[[Z_p^×]] as the one-dimensional Iwasawa algebra and, for each integer k, the map k : Λ → Z_p extending the character z ↦ z^k of Z_p^×. From Theorem 1.1 (p. 3) on, M ⊗^L_{Λ,k} N denotes the derived tensor product along k : Λ → Z_p: for instance M ⊗^L_{Λ,k} Q_p and M ⊗^L_{Λ,k} Q_p/Z_p in Theorem 1.1, and fRΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p), 𝔉^κ ⊗ ω^2(−D)) ⊗^L_{Λ,k} Z_p in Theorem 11.3.1 (3), (4) (p. 71). So §1, p. 2 is a second locator. The derived tensor product is planned at DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:P7.

items.name: The p-adic interpolation sheaf 𝔉^κ over 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p)
items.statement: Let π : 𝔍𝔊(p^∞) → 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p) be the projection. Define 𝔉^κ := (π_* O_{𝔍𝔊(p^∞)} ⊗̂_{Z_p} Λ)^{Z_p^×}, where Z_p^× acts diagonally: on π_*O_{𝔍𝔊(p^∞)} through the torsor structure, and on Λ through κ. The paper states that 𝔉^κ is an invertible sheaf of O_{𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^∞)} ⊗̂_{Z_p} Λ-modules over 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p).

items.name: Remark 9.3.1: working over 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p) or 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^∞) gives the same cohomology
items.statement: The map 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^∞) → 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p) is affine. Hence, for the p-adic sheaves (defined over 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^∞) and viewed over 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p) by pushforward), cohomology over 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^∞) equals cohomology over 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p).
items.note: The general input is standard scheme cohomology (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2): pushforward along an affine morphism preserves the cohomology of quasi-coherent sheaves. What is missing is the pro-affine formal tower and its very large sheaves, to which it is applied.

items.name: Specialisations 𝔉^χ
items.statement: For an adic complete Z_p-algebra R and a continuous character χ : Z_p^× → R^×, 𝔉^χ := 𝔉^κ ⊗̂_{Λ,χ} R. In particular 𝔉^k (k ∈ Z) is the specialisation at χ(x) = x^k.
items.note: Base change of the missing sheaf 𝔉^κ along a continuous character. The character-space side is planned (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L0a/L1); the sheaf is not.

items.name: Truncated sheaves F^κ_{m,n} and F^χ_{m,n}
items.statement: Let π_{m,n} : IG(p^m)_n → X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_n be the projection. For m ≥ n, F^κ_{m,n} := (π_{m,n})_*(O_{IG(p^m)_n} ⊗_{Z_p} Λ_n)[κ_{m,n}], the κ_{m,n}-isotypic part for the diagonal (Z/p^mZ)^×-action. It is a sheaf of O_{X^{≥1}_Kli(p^m)_n} ⊗ Λ_n-modules. For a character χ : (Z/p^nZ)^× → R^× with R a Z/p^nZ-algebra, F^χ_{m,n} is the base change of F^κ_{m,n} along Λ_n → R. For k ∈ Z, F^k_{m,n} denotes the case χ(x) = x^k.
items.note: Isotypic parts of π_*O_{IG(p^m)_n} ⊗ Λ_n on the missing Igusa tower. Λ_n is Mathlib's MonoidAlgebra (see iwasawa-algebra-universal-character); the sheaves are missing.

items.name: Transition maps of the F^κ_{m,n}; F^κ_{∞,n} and 𝔉^κ = lim_n F^κ_{∞,n}
items.statement: Viewing all sheaves over X^{≥1}_Kli(p^m)_n, there is a commutative square. Its vertical maps are the inclusions F^κ_{m−1,n} ↪ F^κ_{m,n} and F^κ_{m−1,n−1} ↪ F^κ_{m,n−1}. Its horizontal maps F^κ_{m,n} → F^κ_{m,n−1} and F^κ_{m−1,n} → F^κ_{m−1,n−1} are reduction modulo the kernel of Λ_n → Λ_{n−1}. Set F^κ_{∞,n} := colim_m F^κ_{m,n}. Then the maps F^κ_{∞,n} → F^κ_{∞,n−1} are surjective and 𝔉^κ = lim_n F^κ_{∞,n}.
items.note: OverconvergentAutomorphicForms:O7 plans the same limit order (colimit in Igusa level m, then limit in n) for Hilbert ordinary Igusa forms: 'construct the direct limit in Igusa level modulo p^m and then the inverse limit in m'. Nothing plans it on the Siegel deep Klingen tower.

items.name: Hodge–Tate isomorphism for the universal multiplicative subgroup H_n
items.statement: Let f_n : X^{≥1}_Kli(p^n)_n → X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_n be the forgetful map and H_n ↪ G the universal subgroup over X^{≥1}_Kli(p^n)_n (étale-locally ≅ µ_{p^n}). Passing to conormal sheaves gives a surjection ω_G → ω_{H_n}, where ω_G is locally free of rank 2 and ω_{H_n} is locally free of rank 1 (over X^{≥1}_Kli(p^n)_n, on which p^n = 0). The Hodge–Tate map HT : H_n^D ⊗_{Z_p} O_{X^{≥1}_Kli(p^n)_n} → ω_{H_n}, x ↦ x^*(dt/t), is an isomorphism.
items.note: The finite-level Hodge–Tate map is planned (HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T0: 'Build the finite-level Hodge–Tate map using Cartier duality and differentials of characters'). The conormal sheaf ω_G of the Siegel abelian scheme belongs to AutomorphicBundles B3–B4. No layer states that HT ⊗ O is an isomorphism for a subgroup étale-locally ≅ µ_{p^n} (étale-locally the dt/t computation), and H_n lives on the missing tower. The introduction's infinite-level form, recorded below, is missing for the same reasons. The introduction (§1, p. 4) states the infinite-level form: the Hodge–Tate period map HT : T_p(H_∞^D) → ω_{H_∞} gives a Z_p^×-reduction of the G_m-torsor ω_{H_∞}, and this is what allows the powers of ω_{H_∞} to be p-adically interpolated into 𝔉^κ. It is the limit over n of the §9.4 isomorphisms HT : H_n^D ⊗_{Z_p} O_{X^{≥1}_Kli(p^n)_n} → ω_{H_n}. The body phrases this reduction through the Igusa tower 𝔍𝔊(p^∞) = Isom(µ_{p^∞}, H_∞), a Z_p^×-torsor over 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^∞) (§9.2, pp. 55–56). So §1, p. 4 is a second locator.

items.name: F^k_{n,n} ≅ ω_{H_n}^{⊗k}
items.statement: For k ∈ Z, the Hodge–Tate isomorphism induces an isomorphism F^k_{n,n} ≅ (ω_{H_n})^{⊗k} of invertible sheaves over X^{≥1}_Kli(p^n)_n.
items.note: Needs the missing sheaves F^k_{n,n} and the Hodge–Tate isomorphism for H_n (missing, T0 route).

items.name: Comparison map Ω^{(k,r)} → F^k_{n,n} ⊗ ω^r and the kernel KΩ^{(k,r)}
items.statement: Notation (§6.2.1): ω = det ω_G and Ω^{(k,r)} = Sym^k ω_G ⊗ det^r ω_G for (k,r) ∈ Z_{≥0} × Z. The surjection ω_G → ω_{H_n} induces a surjection of locally free sheaves Ω^{(k,0)} = Sym^k ω_G → (ω_{H_n})^{⊗k} ≅ F^k_{n,n} on X^{≥1}_Kli(p^n)_n. KΩ^{(k,0)} is its kernel, and KΩ^{(k,r)} := KΩ^{(k,0)} ⊗ ω^r. For all (k,r) ∈ Z_{≥0} × Z this gives an exact sequence of sheaves over X^{≥1}_Kli(p^n)_n: 0 → KΩ^{(k,r)} → Ω^{(k,r)} → F^k_{n,n} ⊗ ω^r → 0.
items.note: Ω^{(k,r)} = Sym^k ω_G ⊗ det^r ω_G is planned (AutomorphicBundles:B4; see automorphic-sheaves-Omega-kr). The surjection Sym^k ω_G → ω_{H_n}^{⊗k} ≅ F^k_{n,n}, its kernel KΩ^{(k,r)} and the exact sequence live on the missing deep Klingen tower and are missing, as is the infinite-level form recorded below. The introduction (§1, p. 4) states the surjection at infinite level: ω_{H_∞}, the dual of the Lie algebra of H_∞, is a line bundle over 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^∞), and over 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^∞) there is a canonical surjection Ω^{(k,0)} → ω_{H_∞}^{⊗k}, described there as an analogue of the projection to highest weight vectors in representation theory. It is the p-adic limit over n of the surjections Ω^{(k,0)} → (ω_{H_n})^{⊗k} of §9.4 and Remark 9.4.1. So §1, p. 4 is a further locator.

items.name: Paramodular variant X^{≥1}_{par,Kli}(p^m)_n
items.statement: Let X_par be the toroidal compactification of paramodular level at p with semi-abelian scheme G' (the polarization is never used in §9), and let Ω^{(k,r)} on X_par be defined from the conormal sheaf of G' → X_par. X^{≥1}_{par,n} ⊂ X_{par,n} is the open subscheme where the p-rank is ≥ 1. X^{≥1}_{par,Kli}(p^m)_n → X^{≥1}_{par,n} is the moduli space of subgroups H'_m ⊂ G'[p^m] étale-locally isomorphic to µ_{p^m}.
items.note: The paramodular integral model X_par and its toroidal compactification are missing (K1/K3: parahoric-level moduli are not planned). PELModuli:M2 requires 'no nontrivial level at p', and K1 routes the Klingen case to PELModuli:M4 with ShimuraCompactifications:C5. The deep paramodular tower over the p-rank ≥ 1 locus is this paper's.

items.name: Lemma 9.5.1: paramodular deep Klingen transition maps are étale and affine
items.statement: For all m ≥ 1 and n ≥ 1, the map X^{≥1}_{par,Kli}(p^m)_n → X^{≥1}_{par,Kli}(p^{m−1})_n is étale and affine.
items.note: Lemma 9.5.1, the paramodular analogue of the missing Lemma 9.1.1.1, on the missing paramodular model.

items.name: Paramodular formal towers and sheaves 𝔉^κ, F^κ_{m,n}
items.statement: 𝔛^{≥1}_{par,Kli}(p^m) is the formal scheme lim_n X^{≥1}_{par,Kli}(p^m)_n, and 𝔛^{≥1}_{par,Kli}(p^∞) the inverse limit over m of 𝔛^{≥1}_{par,Kli}(p^m). As in §9.3 one defines a sheaf 𝔉^κ of O_{𝔛^{≥1}_{par,Kli}(p^∞)} ⊗̂_{Z_p} Λ-modules over 𝔛^{≥1}_{par,Kli}(p), and sheaves F^κ_{m,n} of O_{X^{≥1}_{par,Kli}(p^m)_n} ⊗ Λ_n-modules.
items.note: Paramodular versions of the missing towers and of the sheaves 𝔉^κ and F^κ_{m,n}.

items.name: U corresponds to p^{3−r} U_{Kli(p),1}
items.statement: The operator U (constructed in §10.4 as U_1 ∘ U_2) is a Hecke operator at Klingen level associated with diag(p^2, p, p, 1) ∈ GSp4(Q_p). On cohomology in weight (k,r) it corresponds to p^{3−r} U_{Kli(p),1}, where U_{Kli(p),1} = Kli(p) diag(p^2, p, p, 1) Kli(p) is the Klingen parahoric double coset of §5.1.4.
items.note: Abstract double cosets over rings are planned (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.1: 'construct integral double-coset operators by finite correspondences'). Comparing the coherent operator U with p^{3−r}U_{Kli(p),1} needs the missing correspondence ℭ(p^m) and its normalizations. No layer plans integral Hecke correspondences at p on higher coherent cohomology of the Siegel threefold (as for K1's hecke-operator-U-klingen); this is the paper's own U-operator construction.

items.name: The U-correspondence ℭ_𝔜(p^m) on the abelian locus
items.statement: Let 𝔜^{≥1}_Kli(p^m) ⊂ 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^m) be the open formal subscheme where the semi-abelian scheme is an abelian scheme. ℭ_𝔜(p^m) is the moduli space over 𝔜^{≥1}_Kli(p^m) of triples (G, H_m, L) with these properties: L ⊂ G[p^2] is a totally isotropic subgroup scheme of order p^4, i.e. a Lagrangian for the Weil pairing on G[p^2] (the printed definition omits the order; it is forced by the proof of Lemma 10.1.1, footnote 16 and §13.2.1); L[p] has order p^3; and L ∩ H_m = {0}. The two projections t_1, t_2 : ℭ_𝔜(p^m) → 𝔜^{≥1}_Kli(p^m) are t_1(G, H_m, L) = (G, H_m) and t_2(G, H_m, L) = (G/L, (H_m + L)/L).
items.locator: §10.1, p. 57 (projections p. 58; order p^4: footnote 16, p. 60)
items.note: Moduli of triples (G, H_m, L), with L ⊂ G[p^2] totally isotropic, over the missing deep Klingen tower. No layer plans integral Hecke correspondences at p on higher coherent cohomology of the Siegel threefold (as for K1's hecke-operator-U-klingen); this is the paper's own U-operator construction.

items.name: Fibrewise criterion for truncated Barsotti–Tate groups
items.statement: Let S be a scheme on which p is nilpotent and M → S a finite flat (finite locally free) group scheme. Then M is a truncated Barsotti–Tate group of level n if and only if M is killed by p^n and, for every s ∈ S, the fibre M_s → s is a truncated Barsotti–Tate group of level n.
items.locator: §10.1, proof of Lemma 10.1.1 and footnote 14, p. 57
items.note: No layer defines truncated Barsotti–Tate groups BT_n. An atlas search for 'truncated Barsotti', 'BT_1', 'BT₁' and 'BT_n' finds nothing. FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.1 defines only p-divisible groups ('Define a p-divisible group as compatible finite locally free levels with the exactness and rank conditions'). Neither Mathlib nor Tau Ceti has them. The paper attributes the criterion to Fargues without a reference and proves the case n = 1 using the critère de platitude par fibres. External input: Attributed to L. Fargues (footnote 14: 'We learnt this from Fargues, but we could not find a reference'). The paper proves the case n = 1.

items.name: Critère de platitude par fibres
items.statement: Let S be a scheme, X and Y locally of finite presentation over S, f : X → Y an S-morphism, x ∈ X, y = f(x) and s the image of x in S. If X is flat over S at x and the fibre map f_s : X_s → Y_s is flat at x, then f is flat at x and Y is flat over S at y.
items.note: Neither library has the local flatness criterion or EGA IV_3 11.3.10: searches of the declaration index and of Mathlib/RingTheory/Flat find no fibrewise criterion. Tau Ceti ModularCurves layer 2A consumes 'the local criterion for flatness after noetherian approximation' but does not own the critère. DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3 owns the local commutative algebra ('regular sequences, depth, Cohen–Macaulay rings/modules ... dimension formulas under the local maps actually used'). PAPER-BOCKLE-IYENGAR-PASKUNAS-23 routes its fibrewise flatness criterion there. External input: EGA IV_3, Théorème 11.3.10 (not cited explicitly; the paper says 'By the criterion for flatness by fiber').

items.name: Lemma 10.1.1: structure of the subgroup L of the U-correspondence
items.statement: Let (G, H_m, L) be a point of ℭ_𝔜(p^m) (over a base on which p is nilpotent), let H_1 = H_m[p], and let H_1^⊥ be the orthogonal of H_1 for the Weil pairing on G[p]. Then there is an exact sequence 0 → L ∩ H_1^⊥ → L → L/(L ∩ H_1^⊥) → 0 in which L ∩ H_1^⊥ is a truncated Barsotti–Tate group of level 1, height 2 and dimension 1 (the (p,p)-part of the correspondence) and L/(L ∩ H_1^⊥) is étale-locally isomorphic to Z/p^2Z (the p^2-part).
items.note: Lemma 10.1.1 describes the subgroups L of the missing U-correspondence. It needs the Weil pairing on G[p] (planned: AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A3) and the missing BT_1 criterion.

items.name: The locus 𝔛^{m−et}_par and 𝔛^{m−et}_{par,Kli}(p^m)
items.statement: Fix toroidal compactifications X_Σ, X_Kli(p)_{Σ'}, X_{par,Σ''} for good polyhedral cone decompositions with Σ' refining Σ and Σ''. There are maps p_1 : X_Kli(p)_{Σ'} → X_Σ and p_2 : X_Kli(p)_{Σ'} → X_{par,Σ''}, and over X_Kli(p)_{Σ'} a chain G → G' → G (the first isogeny of degree p^3, the composite multiplication by p), with G the semi-abelian scheme over X_Σ and G' the one over X_{par,Σ''}. Let 𝔛_par be the formal completion of X_par. 𝔛^{m−et}_par ⊂ 𝔛_par is the open formal subscheme where the kernel K(λ') of the polarization λ' : G' → (G')^t contains a multiplicative group; when G' is abelian, K(λ') is then an extension of an étale group by a multiplicative group. 𝔛^{m−et}_par is contained in the p-rank ≥ 1 locus. 𝔛^{m−et}_{par,Kli}(p^m) → 𝔛^{m−et}_par is the moduli space of subgroups H'_m ⊂ G' étale-locally isomorphic to µ_{p^m}.
items.note: The locus of the missing paramodular compactification where K(λ') contains a multiplicative subgroup, and its deep Klingen cover. Planned nowhere.

items.name: The first half ℭ^1(p^m) of the U-correspondence, with q_1, q_2
items.statement: ℭ^1(p^m) is the formal subscheme of 𝔛_Kli(p) ×_𝔛 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^m) where the universal triple (G → G', H_m) satisfies Ker(G → G') ∩ H_m = {0}. The map q_1 : ℭ^1(p^m) → 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^m) sends (G → G', H_m) to (G, H_m). The projection ℭ^1(p^m) → 𝔛_par induced by p_2 factors through 𝔛^{m−et}_par and lifts to q_2 : ℭ^1(p^m) → 𝔛^{m−et}_{par,Kli}(p^m), q_2(G → G', H_m) = (G', H'_m), where H'_m is the image of H_m, onto which G → G' maps H_m isomorphically. The maps q_1 and q_2 are proper (composites of proper maps).
items.note: First half of the missing U-correspondence, inside 𝔛_Kli(p) ×_𝔛 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^m); the Klingen model is missing. No layer plans integral Hecke correspondences at p on higher coherent cohomology of the Siegel threefold (as for K1's hecke-operator-U-klingen); this is the paper's own U-operator construction.

items.name: Lemma 10.2.1: ℭ^1(p^m) is open and closed
items.statement: The formal subscheme ℭ^1(p^m) of 𝔛_Kli(p) ×_𝔛 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^m) is open and closed.
items.note: Lemma 10.2.1 for the missing ℭ^1(p^m). It uses the rigidity of multiplicative groups (missing, R07.1 route).

items.name: Rigidity of groups of multiplicative type
items.statement: Rigidity of homomorphisms out of a group of multiplicative type. Let H be a finite group scheme of multiplicative type (e.g. H_1 = H_m[p], étale-locally ≅ µ_p) and N a finite locally free commutative group scheme over the same base. By Cartier duality, Hom(H, N) = Hom(N^D, H^D) with H^D étale. Such homomorphisms therefore deform uniquely along nilpotent thickenings and are locally constant, so the locus where a given homomorphism H → N vanishes is open and closed. As used in Lemma 10.2.1: since Ker(G → G') ⊂ G[p], Ker(G → G') ∩ H_m = Ker(G → G') ∩ H_1. On geometric fibres this intersection is non-zero iff the composite H_1 ↪ G[p] → G[p]/Ker(G → G') vanishes. Hence the locus where Ker(G → G') ∩ H_m = {0} is closed (as well as open) in 𝔛_Kli(p) ×_𝔛 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^m).
items.note: Tau Ceti has groups of multiplicative type and diagonalizable groups only over a field (TauCeti.multiplicativeTypeCommHopfAlgProperty, TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.*), with no rigidity in families. Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups layer 4 plans diagonalizable groups over a field. SGA 3 IX–X rigidity is planned nowhere. For finite groups it reduces to the étale case by Cartier duality. Tau Ceti already has Cartier duality over an affine base: TauCeti.FiniteLocallyFreeBicommutativeHopfAlgCat.cartierDuality, an anti-equivalence of finite locally free bicommutative Hopf algebras over a commutative ring. R07.1 plans it for schemes ('Develop Cartier duality, connected–étale sequences over the allowed bases'). External input: SGA 3, Exp. IX–X (rigidity of groups of multiplicative type). Not cited explicitly: 'by the rigidity property of multiplicative groups'.

items.name: The second half ℭ^2(p^m) of the U-correspondence, with r_1, r_2
items.statement: ℭ^2(p^m) is the open and closed formal subscheme of 𝔛_Kli(p) ×_{𝔛_par} 𝔛^{m−et}_{par,Kli}(p^m) where, for the universal triple (G' → G, H'_m ⊂ G'), Ker(G' → G) is not a multiplicative group. Since Ker(G' → G) ⊂ K(λ') and K(λ') contains a unique multiplicative subgroup K(λ')^m of order p, the condition is Ker(G' → G) ∩ K(λ')^m = {0}; it is open and closed as in Lemma 10.2.1. Over the interior, Ker(G' → G) is étale. The map r_1 : ℭ^2(p^m) → 𝔛^{m−et}_{par,Kli}(p^m) is r_1(G' → G, H'_m) = (G', H'_m). The projection ℭ^2(p^m) → 𝔛 induced by p_1 factors through 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p) and lifts to r_2 : ℭ^2(p^m) → 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^m), r_2(G' → G, H'_m) = (G, H_m), where H_m is the image of H'_m, onto which G' → G maps H'_m isomorphically. The maps r_1 and r_2 are proper.
items.note: Second half of the missing U-correspondence, over the missing paramodular locus 𝔛^{m−et}_{par,Kli}(p^m). No layer plans integral Hecke correspondences at p on higher coherent cohomology of the Siegel threefold (as for K1's hecke-operator-U-klingen); this is the paper's own U-operator construction.

items.name: Local complete intersection morphism of formal schemes over Spf Z_p
items.statement: A morphism of formal schemes 𝔖 → Spf Z_p is a local complete intersection morphism if it is locally topologically of finite type, flat, and its special fibre S = 𝔖 ×_{Spf Z_p} Spec F_p → Spec F_p is a local complete intersection morphism in the schematic sense (§4.1.3: locally a regular immersion into a smooth scheme).
items.note: Footnote 15 fixes a convention for formal schemes over Spf Z_p. Its schematic input, lci morphisms (§4.1.3, K2's lci-morphism-cotangent-complex-dualizing-sheaf), is in neither library. The atlas plans it only indirectly: DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0 ('Prove the lci amplitude criterion') and SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.5 ('flat/lci pullback'). No layer defines lci morphisms of formal schemes.

items.name: Lemma 10.2.2: ℭ^1(p^m) and ℭ^2(p^m) are lci over Spf Z_p
items.statement: For i ∈ {1, 2}, the structure morphism ℭ^i(p^m) → Spf Z_p is a local complete intersection morphism (in the sense of footnote 15).
items.note: Lemma 10.2.2 for the missing correspondences. It also needs X_Kli(p) to be lci over Z_p (K2/K3: Proposition 6.1.4.1 and Theorem 6.1.5.1(4)), and the Klingen model is missing.

items.name: The composite correspondence ℭ(p^m) and its projections t_1, t_2
items.statement: ℭ(p^m) := ℭ^2(p^m) ×_{r_1, 𝔛^{m−et}_{par,Kli}(p^m), q_2} ℭ^1(p^m), with projections r'_1 : ℭ(p^m) → ℭ^1(p^m) and q'_2 : ℭ(p^m) → ℭ^2(p^m) (a diagram with cartesian centre). Set t_1 := q_1 ∘ r'_1 and t_2 := r_2 ∘ q'_2 : ℭ(p^m) → 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^m).
items.note: Fibre product of the missing ℭ^2 and ℭ^1. No layer plans integral Hecke correspondences at p on higher coherent cohomology of the Siegel threefold (as for K1's hecke-operator-U-klingen); this is the paper's own U-operator construction.

items.name: Proposition 10.2.1: ℭ(p^m) restricted to the abelian locus is ℭ_𝔜(p^m)
items.statement: The restriction of ℭ(p^m) to 𝔜^{≥1}_Kli(p^m) is the correspondence ℭ_𝔜(p^m), compatibly with t_1 and t_2. Precisely, (G, H_m, L) ↦ (G → G/L[p] → G/L, H_m) identifies ℭ_𝔜(p^m) with the locus of ℭ(p^m) where the semi-abelian schemes are abelian.
items.note: Proposition 10.2.1, comparing the missing ℭ(p^m) and ℭ_𝔜(p^m).

items.name: Lemma 10.3.1: t_1 is finite flat on the abelian locus
items.statement: The map t_1 : ℭ_𝔜(p^m) → 𝔜^{≥1}_Kli(p^m) is finite flat.
items.note: Lemma 10.3.1 for the missing correspondence. Its proof uses miracle flatness (missing, R03.3 route) and the lci property of Lemma 10.2.2.

items.name: Miracle flatness
items.statement: Let (A, m) → (B, n) be a local homomorphism of noetherian local rings with A regular, B Cohen–Macaulay and dim B = dim A + dim B/mB. Then B is flat over A (Matsumura, Commutative Ring Theory, Thm 23.1). In particular, let f : X → Y be a quasi-finite morphism, locally of finite type, of locally noetherian schemes (or formal schemes, working with completed local rings) with Y regular and X Cohen–Macaulay. If dim O_{X,x} = dim O_{Y,f(x)} for every x ∈ X, then f is flat.
items.locator: §10.3, proof of Lemma 10.3.1, p. 60 (cited as '[53], chap. 23, thm. 2.3.1')
items.note: Not in Mathlib, which has IsRegularLocalRing but no Cohen–Macaulay rings and no miracle flatness, and not in Tau Ceti. Tau Ceti ModularCurves layer 4D plans only 'miracle flatness for finite morphisms between regular local schemes of equal dimension', which needs a regular source; here the source ℭ_𝔜(p^m) is only Cohen–Macaulay. Precedent: PAPER-BOCKLE-IYENGAR-PASKUNAS-23/121 (the same Matsumura 23.1) is missing and source-routed to R03.3. PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 also marks it missing. The paper uses the same criterion a second time, without citation, in §7.4.2, proof of Proposition 7.4.2.1, p. 46: the map p_1 : Ĉ → B̂ is finite flat 'because B̂ is regular, p_1 is finite (because we removed the p-rank 0 locus) and dominant, and Ĉ is Cohen-Macaulay'. Here B̂ is the completion of Y_1 along its p-rank-one locus (regular) and Ĉ a completion of X_Kli(p) (Cohen–Macaulay), so again the source is only Cohen–Macaulay. External input: H. Matsumura, Commutative Ring Theory, Theorem 23.1 (cited as '[53], chap. 23, thm. 2.3.1').

items.name: Lemma 10.3.2: normalized trace (1/p^3)Tr_{t_1}
items.statement: The trace of the finite flat morphism t_1 : ℭ_𝔜(p^m) → 𝔜^{≥1}_Kli(p^m) is divisible by p^3. Hence there is a normalized trace map (1/p^3)Tr_{t_1} : (t_1)_* O_{ℭ_𝔜(p^m)} → O_{𝔜^{≥1}_Kli(p^m)}.
items.note: Lemma 10.3.2 for the missing correspondence. It uses the missing Serre–Tate coordinates. Mathlib has the trace of finite locally free algebras (Algebra.trace), but not the integrality of (1/p^3)Tr_{t_1}.

items.name: Algebraization of formal projective schemes (Grothendieck existence)
items.statement: If A is a noetherian ring complete for an ideal-adic topology and 𝔓 → Spf A is a projective formal scheme, then 𝔓 is the formal completion of a projective scheme over Spec A.
items.locator: §10.3, proof of Lemma 10.3.3, p. 61 (the alternative definition suggested by the referee)
items.note: Grothendieck's existence theorem and the algebraization of formal projective schemes by an ample line bundle (EGA III_1 5.4.5) are planned. Mathlib has no formal schemes. External input: EGA III_1, Théorème 5.4.5 (not cited in the paper).

items.name: The dualizing sheaf q_1^! O_{𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^m)} for the formal projective map q_1
items.statement: For each n, q_1 : C^1(p^m)_n → X^{≥1}_Kli(p^m)_n is a projective morphism between local complete intersections over Spec Z/p^nZ, so q_1^! O_{X^{≥1}_Kli(p^m)_n} is an invertible sheaf. There are canonical isomorphisms q_1^! O_{X^{≥1}_Kli(p^m)_n} ⊗_{Z_p} Z/p^{n−1}Z = q_1^! O_{X^{≥1}_Kli(p^m)_{n−1}}, and one defines q_1^! O_{𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^m)} := lim_n q_1^! O_{X^{≥1}_Kli(p^m)_n}. Equivalently, over each open affine Spf A ⊂ 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^m), ℭ^1(p^m) ×_{𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^m)} Spf A algebraizes to a projective scheme over Spec A, and q_1^! is taken there (the definition is local on the base).
items.note:
Needs:
- Grothendieck duality f^! for projective lci morphisms over Z/p^n (K2's upper-shriek items). Coherent duality in relative dimension > 1 is planned nowhere, and PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18/verdier-serre-duality was routed to AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:A0-extension.
- algebraization, which is planned (AdicSpacesPartII:F0);
- the missing map q_1.

items.name: Lemma 10.3.3: normalized trace (1/p^2)Tr_{q_1}
items.statement: There is a fundamental class Θ : q_1^* O_{𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^m)} → q_1^! O_{𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^m)} which, over the complement of the boundary, is the trace of the finite flat morphism q_1 : ℭ^1(p^m)|_{𝔜^{≥1}_Kli(p^m)} → 𝔜^{≥1}_Kli(p^m) (§4.2.2). Θ is divisible by p^2. By adjunction, (1/p^2)Θ gives a normalized trace map (1/p^2)Tr_{q_1} : R(q_1)_* O_{ℭ^1(p^m)} → O_{𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^m)}.
items.note: Lemma 10.3.3: the fundamental class of the missing q_1 (§4.2, K2's fundamental-class items) and its divisibility by p^2.

items.name: Remark 10.3.1: R^i(q_1)_* O_{ℭ^1(p^m)} = 0 for i > 0
items.statement: R^i(q_1)_* O_{ℭ^1(p^m)} = 0 for all i > 0.
items.note: Remark 10.3.1, stated without proof, for the missing q_1.

items.name: Lemma 10.3.4: normalized trace (1/p)Tr_{r_1}
items.statement: There is a normalized trace map (1/p)Tr_{r_1} : R(r_1)_* O_{ℭ^2(p^m)} → O_{𝔛^{m−et}_{par,Kli}(p^m)}.
items.note: Lemma 10.3.4 ('left to the reader'), for the missing r_1.

items.name: Local form (10.4.A) of the differential of G → G' over ℭ^1
items.statement: Over ℭ^1(p^∞) := lim_m ℭ^1(p^m), or over C^1(p^m)_n := ℭ^1(p^m) mod p^n with m ≥ n, the universal isogeny G → G' maps H_m isomorphically onto H'_m. This gives a commutative diagram of conormal sheaves with exact rows ω_{G'} → ω_{H'_m} → 0 and ω_G → ω_{H_m} → 0, whose vertical maps are the differentials (the right-hand one an isomorphism). There is a Zariski covering by affine opens Spf R (resp. Spec R) over which this diagram is isomorphic to: rows R ⊕ R → R, (a,b) ↦ b; left vertical map diag(p, 1); right vertical map id_R.
items.note: Local form (10.4.A) of the differential of G → G' over the missing ℭ^1.

items.name: Normalized map q_2^*Ω^{(k,r)} → q_1^*Ω^{(k,r)}
items.statement: For all m ≥ 1 (the hypothesis m ≥ n of (10.4.A) is dropped) and (k,r) ∈ Z_{≥0} × Z, there is a normalized morphism q_2^⋆Ω^{(k,r)} → q_1^⋆Ω^{(k,r)} over ℭ^1(p^m). It is the tensor product of two maps. The first is the natural map q_2^⋆Ω^k → q_1^⋆Ω^k, where Ω^k = Ω^{(k,0)} = Sym^k ω_G, induced by the differential ω_{G'} → ω_G of the universal isogeny G → G'. The second is the normalized map (1/p^r) q_2^⋆ω^r → q_1^⋆ω^r, where ω = det ω_G and ω^r = Ω^{(0,r)}; the determinant of the differential is divisible by p, by (10.4.A).
items.note: The normalized map q_2^*Ω^{(k,r)} → q_1^*Ω^{(k,r)} over the missing ℭ^1. The bundles Ω^{(k,r)} are planned (AutomorphicBundles:B4); the map is not.

items.name: The operator U_1
items.statement: Composing the normalized map q_2^*Ω^{(k,r)} → q_1^*Ω^{(k,r)} with the normalized trace of Lemma 10.3.3 (and the projection formula) gives R(q_1)_* q_2^* Ω^{(k,r)} → Ω^{(k,r)}. This yields U_1 ∈ Hom(RΓ(𝔛^{m−et}_{par,Kli}(p^m), Ω^{(k,r)}), RΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^m), Ω^{(k,r)})), independent of the choices of good polyhedral decompositions.
items.note: Cohomological correspondence along the missing ℭ^1. No layer plans integral Hecke correspondences at p on higher coherent cohomology of the Siegel threefold (as for K1's hecke-operator-U-klingen); this is the paper's own U-operator construction.

items.name: The operator U_2
items.statement: Over ℭ^2(p^m) the tautological isogeny G' → G is étale and induces an isomorphism on differentials. This gives a canonical isomorphism r_2^* Ω^{(k,r)} → r_1^* Ω^{(k,r)} with no normalization. With the trace of Lemma 10.3.4 it gives a cohomological correspondence R(r_1)_* r_2^* Ω^{(k,r)} → Ω^{(k,r)} and an operator U_2 ∈ Hom(RΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^m), Ω^{(k,r)}), RΓ(𝔛^{m−et}_{par,Kli}(p^m), Ω^{(k,r)})).
items.note: Cohomological correspondence along the missing ℭ^2. No layer plans integral Hecke correspondences at p on higher coherent cohomology of the Siegel threefold (as for K1's hecke-operator-U-klingen); this is the paper's own U-operator construction.

items.name: The U-operator U = U_1 ∘ U_2
items.statement: U := U_1 ∘ U_2 ∈ End(RΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^m), Ω^{(k,r)})) for (k,r) ∈ Z_{≥0} × Z and m ≥ 1.
items.note: U = U_1 ∘ U_2, the paper's Klingen-level operator (missing). No layer plans integral Hecke correspondences at p on higher coherent cohomology of the Siegel threefold; this is the paper's own U-operator construction. The introduction (§1, p. 2) attaches U to the double coset Kli(p)diag(p²,p,p,1)Kli(p), acting on the cohomology of X_Kli(p)K. On p. 4 it explains that the correspondence is defined integrally by factoring diag(p²,p,p,1) = diag(p,p,p,1)·diag(p,1,1,1), which splits it into the two correspondences U_1 and U_2, and that the trace maps come from Grothendieck–Serre duality. §10 (p. 57) says U corresponds to p^{3−r}U_{Kli(p),1} of §5.1.4 in weight (k,r). The analytic version on classical coherent cohomology is normalized-U-n-on-classical-coherent-cohomology (§14.4.2), and the overconvergent one is U-operator-on-overconvergent-cohomology (§13.2.3). The comparison with the classical double coset operator, the correspondence on the abelian locus, the composite correspondence through paramodular level and the trace maps are recorded in U-operator-vs-classical-klingen-hecke-operator, correspondence-C-Y-on-abelian-locus, composite-correspondence-C and the §10.3 trace lemmas (normalized-trace-t1, normalized-trace-q1, normalized-trace-r1).

items.name: U_1, U_2 and U in characteristic p (m = 1)
items.statement: Take m = 1 and reduce modulo p. This gives C(p)_1 = C^2(p)_1 ×_{X^{m−et}_{par,Kli}(p)_1} C^1(p)_1 over X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1 and X^{m−et}_{par,Kli}(p)_1. By reduction modulo p and Prop. 4.1.2.1 one gets cohomological correspondences q_2^*Ω^{(k,r)}|_{X^{m−et}_{par,Kli}(p)_1} → q_1^!Ω^{(k,r)}|_{X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1} on C^1(p)_1 and r_2^*Ω^{(k,r)}|_{X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1} → r_1^!Ω^{(k,r)}|_{X^{m−et}_{par,Kli}(p)_1} on C^2(p)_1. They induce U_1 ∈ Hom(RΓ(X^{m−et}_{par,Kli}(p)_1, Ω^{(k,r)}), RΓ(X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1, Ω^{(k,r)})) and U_2 ∈ Hom(RΓ(X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1, Ω^{(k,r)}), RΓ(X^{m−et}_{par,Kli}(p)_1, Ω^{(k,r)})). Set U := U_1 ∘ U_2.
items.note: Characteristic-p versions of U_1, U_2 and U. They use Proposition 4.1.2.1 (K2's upper-shriek-projection-formula) and the missing correspondences.

items.name: Lemma 10.5.2.1 (1)–(2): the Hasse invariant pulls back compatibly along C^1(p)_1 and C^2(p)_1
items.statement: (1) On C^1(p)_1, under the canonical isomorphism q_2^*ω^{p−1} ≅ q_1^*ω^{p−1} (the canonical map of Lemma 6.3.4.2, which is the normalized map of §10.4), q_2^*Ha = q_1^*Ha. (2) On C^2(p)_1, under the isomorphism r_2^*ω^{p−1} ≅ r_1^*ω^{p−1} induced by the étale isogeny, r_2^*Ha = r_1^*Ha. No restriction on the weight.
items.note: The genus-two Hasse invariant is planned nowhere (PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20/hasse-invariant-h-and-lift-A is missing and routed to the proposed SiegelModularFormsModPn, which is not in the atlas). The compatibility along ℭ^1(p)_1 and ℭ^2(p)_1 uses Lemma 6.3.4.2 (K3) and the missing correspondences.

items.name: Lemma 10.5.2.1 (3): U_1 and U_2 commute with multiplication by Ha
items.statement: For all (k,r), the following squares commute: U_1 : q_2^*Ω^{(k,r)} → q_1^!Ω^{(k,r)} followed by Ha equals Ha followed by U_1 : q_2^*Ω^{(k,r+(p−1))} → q_1^!Ω^{(k,r+(p−1))}. Likewise, U_2 : r_2^*Ω^{(k,r)} → r_1^!Ω^{(k,r)} commutes with Ha : Ω^{(k,r)} → Ω^{(k,r+(p−1))}.
items.note: Commutation of the missing U_1 and U_2 with Ha. The genus-two Hasse invariant is planned nowhere (PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20/hasse-invariant-h-and-lift-A is missing and routed to the proposed SiegelModularFormsModPn, which is not in the atlas).

items.name: Lemma 10.5.2.2: Ha is a non-zero-divisor on C^1(p)_1 and C^2(p)_1
items.statement: The Hasse invariant is not a zero divisor on C^1(p)_1 or on C^2(p)_1.
items.note: Lemma 10.5.2.2 on the missing ℭ^1(p)_1 and ℭ^2(p)_1. The genus-two Hasse invariant is planned nowhere (PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20/hasse-invariant-h-and-lift-A is missing and routed to the proposed SiegelModularFormsModPn, which is not in the atlas).

items.name: X^{=1}_Kli(p)_1 and its identification with X_1^{=1}
items.statement: X^{=1}_Kli(p)_1 ⊂ X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1 is the vanishing locus of Ha. The projection p_1 induces a canonical isomorphism X^{=1}_Kli(p)_1 ≅ X_1^{=1}. Taking non-ordinary loci everywhere gives C^{=1}(p)_1, C^{i,=1}(p)_1 and X^{m−et,=1}_{par,Kli}(p)_1.
items.note: The vanishing locus of Ha on the missing X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1, and its identification with X_1^{=1}. The p-rank strata are planned nowhere (K3 special-fibres-and-p-rank-strata).

items.name: U on the p-rank one locus X_1^{=1}
items.statement: Lemma 10.5.2.1 (3) and Prop. 4.1.2.1 give cohomological correspondences R(q_1)_*(q_2)^*Ω^{(k,r)}|_{X^{m−et,=1}_{par,Kli}(p)_1} → Ω^{(k,r)}|_{X_1^{=1}} and R(r_1)_*(r_2)^*Ω^{(k,r)}|_{X_1^{=1}} → Ω^{(k,r)}|_{X^{m−et,=1}_{par,Kli}(p)_1}. They induce U_1 ∈ Hom(RΓ(X^{m−et,=1}_{par,Kli}(p)_1, Ω^{(k,r)}), RΓ(X_1^{=1}, Ω^{(k,r)})), U_2 ∈ Hom(RΓ(X_1^{=1}, Ω^{(k,r)}), RΓ(X^{m−et,=1}_{par,Kli}(p)_1, Ω^{(k,r)})), and U := U_1 ∘ U_2.
items.note: U on the p-rank-one locus, from the missing correspondences restricted to the non-ordinary loci.

items.name: U acts equivariantly on the Ha long exact sequence
