items.statement: By Lemma 10.5.2.2 there is a map of exact triangles from R(q_1)_*q_2^*Ω^{(k,r)} →^{Ha} R(q_1)_*q_2^*Ω^{(k,r+(p−1))} → R(q_1)_*(q_2)^*Ω^{(k,r+(p−1))}|_{X^{m−et,=1}_{par,Kli}(p)_1} →^{+1} to Ω^{(k,r)} →^{Ha} Ω^{(k,r+(p−1))} → Ω^{(k,r+(p−1))}|_{X_1^{=1}} →^{+1}, and similarly for C^2. Consequently U acts equivariantly on the long exact sequence ⋯ → H^*(X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1, Ω^{(k,r)}) →^{Ha} H^*(X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1, Ω^{(k,r+(p−1))}) → H^*(X^{=1}_Kli(p)_1, Ω^{(k,r+(p−1))}) → ⋯ .
items.note: Map of triangles for the missing U and Ha.

items.name: Lemma 10.5.3.1 (1)–(2): compatibility with the second Hasse invariant Ha'
items.statement: Let Ha' ∈ H^0(X_1^{≤1}, ω^{p^2−1}) be the second Hasse invariant (§6.3). (1) Under the isomorphism (q_2)^*ω^{p^2−1} = (q_1)^*ω^{p^2−1}, (q_2)^*Ha' = (q_1)^*Ha'. (2) Under the isomorphism (r_2)^*ω^{p^2−1} = (r_1)^*ω^{p^2−1}, (r_2)^*Ha' = (r_1)^*Ha'.
items.note: The second Hasse invariant Ha' is planned nowhere (PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20/secondary-hasse-invariant is missing; K3 second-hasse-invariant). Its compatibility with the missing correspondences is this paper's.

items.name: Lemma 10.5.3.1 (3): U commutes with multiplication by Ha' on H^0(X_1^{=1})
items.statement: The square with U : H^0(X_1^{=1}, Ω^{(k,r)}) → H^0(X_1^{=1}, Ω^{(k,r)}) on top, U : H^0(X_1^{=1}, Ω^{(k,r+p^2−1)}) → H^0(X_1^{=1}, Ω^{(k,r+p^2−1)}) at the bottom, and both vertical maps multiplication by Ha', commutes.
items.note: Lemma 10.5.3.1 (3), for the missing U and Ha'.

items.name: Action of U on the p-adic sheaves F^κ_{m,n} and 𝔉^κ
items.statement: Over ℭ^1(p^∞) or C^1(p^m)_n, the universal isogeny induces an isomorphism q_1^*H_m ≅ q_2^*H'_m. This gives maps q_2^*F^κ_{m,n} → q_1^*F^κ_{m,n} for m ≥ n, and q_2^*𝔉^κ → q_1^*𝔉^κ. These (tensored with the normalized map on ω^r) define U_1, U_2 is defined similarly, and U = U_1 ∘ U_2 acts on RΓ(X^{≥1}_Kli(p^m)_n, F^κ_{m,n} ⊗ ω^r) and on RΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p^∞), 𝔉^κ ⊗ ω^r).
items.note: Action of the missing U on the missing sheaves F^κ_{m,n} and 𝔉^κ.

items.name: Lemma 10.7.1: U is divisible by p on KΩ^{(k,r)}
items.statement: For all (k,r) ∈ Z_{≥0} × Z and n ≥ 1, U preserves KΩ^{(k,r)} ⊂ Ω^{(k,r)} over X^{≥1}_Kli(p^n)_n and U ∈ p·End(RΓ(X^{≥1}_Kli(p^n)_n, KΩ^{(k,r)})). In particular U acts by 0 on RΓ(X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1, KΩ^{(k,r)}).
items.note: Lemma 10.7.1, about the missing U and the missing kernel KΩ^{(k,r)}.

items.name: Koecher principle
items.statement: For the Siegel threefold, sections of the automorphic vector bundles Ω^{(k,r)} over the complement of the boundary (also over the ordinary locus) extend uniquely over the boundary of the toroidal compactification: H^0(Y^{ord}_1, Ω^{(k,r)}) = H^0(X^{ord}_1, Ω^{(k,r)}), and the Hecke operators considered preserve cuspidality.
items.note: The Siegel Koecher principle with torsion coefficients is planned nowhere. ShimuraCompactifications:C6 plans only 'the precise Koecher extension theorem needed for Hilbert sections', and ShimuraVarieties:V2 only asks that any use of Koecher prove its hypothesis. The gap and route are the same as for PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20/koecher-principle. Here it is used mod p over the ordinary locus, H^0(Y^{ord}_1) = H^0(X^{ord}_1), and the Hecke operators preserve cuspidality. External input: Koecher's principle (not cited at this point; cf. K.-W. Lan, Higher Koecher principles, Math. Res. Lett. 23 (2016), [51] in the paper).

items.name: Decomposition T_i = T_i^{et} + T_i^m over the ordinary locus
items.statement: Let T_1 : H^0(X^{=2}_{par,1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) → H^0(X_1^{=2}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) and T_2 : H^0(X_1^{=2}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) → H^0(X^{=2}_{par,1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) be the operators of §7 restricted to the ordinary loci (T = T_1 ∘ T_2). They decompose as T_1 = T_1^{et} + T_1^m and T_2 = T_2^{et} + T_2^m. Here T_1^{et} (resp. T_1^m) is the contribution of the isogenies G → G' whose kernel has étale rank 2 and multiplicative rank 1 (resp. multiplicative rank 2 and étale rank 1), and T_2^{et} (resp. T_2^m) is the contribution of the isogenies G' → G with étale (resp. multiplicative) kernel.
items.note: Decomposition of the spherical operators T_1 and T_2 of §7 (K1 hecke-operator-T-spherical, missing) by the étale or multiplicative type of the kernel.

items.name: Lemma 11.1.1.1: T_1^m = T_2^m = 0 on the ordinary locus
items.statement: For all r ≥ 2 and k ≥ 1, the operators T_2^m : H^0(X_1^{ord}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) → H^0(X^{ord}_{par,1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) and T_1^m : H^0(X^{ord}_{par,1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) → H^0(X_1^{ord}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) are 0.
items.note: Lemma 11.1.1.1, for the missing operators T_i^m.

items.name: The correspondence 𝔇 and the operator T'
items.statement: Let 𝔜 ⊂ 𝔛 be the open formal subscheme where G is abelian and 𝔜^{ord} its ordinary locus. 𝔇 → 𝔜^{ord} parametrizes pairs (G, L) with L ⊂ G[p^2] a totally isotropic subgroup scheme that is an extension of an étale group scheme étale-locally ≅ Z/pZ ⊕ Z/p^2Z by a multiplicative group scheme étale-locally ≅ µ_p (type (1, p, p, p^2)). The projections g_1(G, L) = G and g_2(G, L) = G/L are finite flat. T' is the associated Hecke operator, normalized by p^{−3−r}. Moreover g_2 lifts to g_2 : 𝔇 → 𝔜^{ord}_Kli(p), (G, L) ↦ (G/L, image of G[p] in G/L).
items.note: The correspondence 𝔇 of subgroups of type (1, p, p, p^2) and its operator T'. No layer plans integral Hecke correspondences at p on higher coherent cohomology of the Siegel threefold (as for K1's hecke-operator-U-klingen); this is the paper's own U-operator construction.

items.name: T' = T_1^{et} ∘ T_2^{et} = T on H^0(X_1^{ord}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D))
items.statement: On H^0(X_1^{ord}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)), T' = T_1^{et} ∘ T_2^{et}. If r ≥ 2 and k ≥ 1, this equals T = T_1 ∘ T_2 by Lemma 11.1.1.1.
items.note: Identity of the missing operators T' and T.

items.name: The operators T'' and T''' on H^0(X^{ord}_Kli(p)_1)
items.statement: Since g_2 lifts to 𝔜^{ord}_Kli(p), T' ∈ End H^0(X_1^{ord}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) factors as H^0(X_1^{ord}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) →^{i} H^0(X^{ord}_Kli(p)_1, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) →^{T''} H^0(X_1^{ord}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)), where i is the canonical inclusion (pull-back). Define T''' := i ∘ T'' ∈ End H^0(X^{ord}_Kli(p)_1, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)). T''' is the operator of the correspondence of triples (G, H, L), with H ⊂ G[p] multiplicative of order p and L as in 𝔇 (no condition on L ∩ H), and projections (G, H, L) ↦ (G, H) and (G, H, L) ↦ (G/L, image of G[p]). Since L does not depend on H, for r ≥ 2 and k ≥ 1: T = T' = T'' ∘ i and T''' ∘ i = i ∘ T.
items.note: The factorizations T'' and T''' of the missing T' through the Klingen ordinary locus.

items.name: Lemma 11.1.1.2: T''' is locally finite
items.statement: If r ≥ 2 and k ≥ 1, T''' acts locally finitely on the F_p-vector space H^0(X^{ord}_Kli(p)_1, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)): every vector lies in a finite-dimensional T'''-stable subspace.
items.note: Lemma 11.1.1.2, for the missing T'''.

items.name: Lemma 11.1.1.3: U ∘ T''' = U ∘ U
items.statement: For r ≥ 2 and k ≥ 1, U ∘ T''' = U ∘ U on H^0(X^{ord}_Kli(p)_1, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)).
items.note: Lemma 11.1.1.3, for the missing U and T'''.

items.name: Corollary 11.1.1.1: U is locally finite on H^0(X^{ord}_Kli(p)_1); the projector f
items.statement: For all r ≥ 2 and k ≥ 1, U acts locally finitely on H^0(X^{ord}_Kli(p)_1, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)). f denotes the associated ordinary projector (Lemma 2.1.3: f = lim U^{N!}).
items.note: Local finiteness of the missing U. The projector f = lim U^{N!} is Lemma 2.1.3, and PadicFamilies:L0a does not plan its locally finite, non-finite generality (K1 lemma-2-1-3-ordinary-projector, missing).

items.name: 𝔛^{ord}_Kli(p) → 𝔛^{ord} is finite étale of degree p + 1; its trace
items.statement: The morphism 𝔛^{ord}_Kli(p) → 𝔛^{ord} (the ordinary part of 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p) → 𝔛^{≥1}) is finite étale of rank p + 1. Tr : H^0(𝔛^{ord}_Kli(p), Ω^{(k,r)}) → H^0(𝔛^{ord}, Ω^{(k,r)}) denotes its trace and i the pull-back, so that Tr ∘ i = (p + 1)·id.
items.note: The finite étale map 𝔛^{ord}_Kli(p) → 𝔛^{ord} of degree p+1 lives on the missing Klingen model. The algebraic identity Tr ∘ i = rank · id is Mathlib's Algebra.trace_algebraMap for free algebras (read in Mathlib/RingTheory/Trace/Defs.lean), and AdicSpacesPartII:R3 plans traces for finite locally free algebras. Neither gives this map.

items.name: Lemma 11.1.1.4: Tr ∘ U^n ∘ i ≡ p T^n mod p^k
items.statement: For all n ≥ 1 [printed n ≥ 0, which is false for n = 0, where Tr ∘ i = (p+1)·Id; sourceIssues E85], Tr ∘ U^n ∘ i ≡ p·T^n mod p^k as endomorphisms of H^0(𝔛^{ord}, Ω^{(k,r)}) (standing assumptions r ≥ 2, k ≥ 1).
items.note: Lemma 11.1.1.4, for the missing U and T. It is printed with 'n ≥ 0', which is false for n = 0 (sourceIssues E85). The proof's claim that every isogeny in T^{n,m} factors through multiplication by p is also wrong as stated (sourceIssues E84).

items.name: Corollary 11.1.1.2: T-ordinary equals U-ordinary for H^0 on the ordinary locus
items.statement: Assume r ≥ 2 and k ≥ 2. Then the canonical map f ∘ i : eH^0(X_1^{ord}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) → fH^0(X^{ord}_Kli(p)_1, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) is bijective, where e is the ordinary projector for T and f the ordinary projector for U.
items.note: Corollary 11.1.1.2, comparing the missing projectors e and f.

items.name: Lemma 11.1.2.1: U = T on H^0(X_1^{=1})
items.note: Lemma 11.1.2.1, for the missing U and T.

items.name: Corollary 11.1.3.1 (1): U is locally finite on RΓ(X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D))
items.statement: For all r ≥ 2 and k > p + 1, the action of U on RΓ(X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) is locally finite; f denotes the corresponding projector.
items.note: Corollary 11.1.3.1 (1), for the missing U.

items.name: Corollary 11.1.3.1 (2): eRΓ(X_1^{≥1}) ≅ fRΓ(X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1)
items.statement: For all r ≥ 2 and k > p + 1, the pull-back map eRΓ(X_1^{≥1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) → fRΓ(X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) is a quasi-isomorphism.
items.note: Corollary 11.1.3.1 (2), for the missing e and f.

items.name: Corollary 11.1.3.1 (3): classical T-ordinary mod p equals U-ordinary over X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1 for r ≥ 3
items.statement: There is a constant C, independent of the prime-to-p level K^p, such that for all k ≥ C and r ≥ 3 the map eRΓ(X_1, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) → fRΓ(X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) is a quasi-isomorphism.
items.note: Corollary 11.1.3.1 (3). It uses the paper's Proposition 8.2.1 (missing).

items.name: Corollary 11.1.3.1 (4): weight (k,2), degrees 0 and 1, mod p
items.statement: For k ≥ C, the map eH^i(X_1, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) → fH^i(X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) is bijective for i = 0 and injective for i = 1.
items.note: Corollary 11.1.3.1 (4), in weight (k,2).

items.name: Corollary 11.1.3.1 (5): fRΓ(X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1) is perfect of amplitude [0,1]
items.statement: For r ≥ 2 and k ≥ C, fRΓ(X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) is a perfect complex of F_p-vector spaces of amplitude [0, 1] (finite-dimensional cohomology in degrees 0 and 1 only).
items.note: Corollary 11.1.3.1 (5): perfectness over F_p of the missing fRΓ.

items.name: Ha^{p^{n−1}} lifts canonically modulo p^n
items.statement: For n ≥ 1, the section Ha^{p^{n−1}} ∈ H^0(X_1, ω^{p^{n−1}(p−1)}) lifts to a section of H^0(X_n, ω^{p^{n−1}(p−1)}): the p^{n−1}-th power of a local lift of Ha to X_n does not depend on the lift, so these glue. The same holds on X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_n.
items.note: The local computation is in Mathlib: dvd_sub_pow_of_dvd_sub, '(h : (p : R) ∣ a − b) (k : ℕ) : (p ^ (k + 1) : R) ∣ a ^ p ^ k − b ^ p ^ k' (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Basic.lean), shows that the p^{n−1}-th powers of any two local lifts agree mod p^n. The global section of ω^{p^{n−1}(p−1)} on X_n needs the missing Siegel Hasse invariant (PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20/hasse-invariant-h-and-lift-A). CG20's SiegelModularFormsModPn brief (proposed, not in the atlas) already lists this fact: 'A^{p^{m−1}} mod ϖ^m depends only on h^r (Goldring 2014, Thm 6.2.1)'. External input: Standard fact, asserted without proof or citation in the paper.

items.name: Acyclic resolution by the ordinary locus and the complexes M^•, N^•
items.statement: Over X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_n or X_n^{≥1} there is an exact sequence 0 → Ω^{(k,r)}(−D) → colim_l Ω^{(k, r+lp^{n−1}(p−1))}(−D) → colim_l Ω^{(k, r+lp^{n−1}(p−1))}(−D)/Ha^{lp^{n−1}} → 0, with colimits along multiplication by the lift of Ha^{p^{n−1}}. The middle sheaf is the restriction of Ω^{(k,r)}(−D) to the ordinary locus. This is an acyclic resolution by flat Z/p^nZ-sheaves: all sheaves are acyclic relative to the minimal compactification, and the middle and right sheaves are supported over affine subschemes of the minimal compactification. Passing to the limit over n gives an acyclic resolution of Ω^{(k,r)}(−D) over 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p) or 𝔛^{≥1} by flat, p-adically complete and separated sheaves of Z_p-modules. M^• and N^• are the resulting complexes, concentrated in degrees [0, 1], computing RΓ(𝔛^{≥1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) and RΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p), Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)). They are objects of C^{flat}(Z_p).
items.note: Resolution by colimits over the lifted Hasse powers on the missing X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_n and X_n^{≥1}. It needs Lan's relative vanishing (missing) and the affineness of the ordinary locus in the minimal compactification (missing). C^{flat}(Z_p) is planned (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:P7, per K1's complexes-C-comp-C-flat-C-perf).

items.name: Theorem 11.2.1 (1): U is locally finite on RΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p), Ω^{(k,r)}(−D))
items.statement: For k > p + 1 and r ≥ 2, the Hecke operator U acts locally finitely on RΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p), Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) (in the sense of Def. 2.3.2, via the representative N^•).
items.note: Theorem 11.2.1 (1), for the missing U.

items.name: Theorem 11.2.1 (2): T is locally finite on RΓ(𝔛^{≥1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D))
items.statement: For k > p + 1 and r ≥ 2, the Hecke operator T acts locally finitely on RΓ(𝔛^{≥1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)).
items.note: Theorem 11.2.1 (2), for the missing T.

items.name: Theorem 11.2.1 (3): cohomology only in degrees 0 and 1
items.statement: For k > p + 1 and r ≥ 2, the complexes RΓ(𝔛^{≥1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) and RΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p), Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) only have cohomology in degrees 0 and 1.
items.note: Theorem 11.2.1 (3), from the missing two-term resolution.

items.name: Theorem 11.2.1 (4): eRΓ(𝔛^{≥1}) ≅ fRΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p))
items.statement: For k > p + 1 and r ≥ 2, with f the ordinary projector of U and e that of T, the natural map eRΓ(𝔛^{≥1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) → fRΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p), Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) is a quasi-isomorphism.
items.note: Theorem 11.2.1 (4), for the missing e and f.

items.name: Theorem 11.2.1 (5): eRΓ(𝔛) ≅ eRΓ(𝔛^{≥1}) for r ≥ 3
items.statement: There is a constant C, independent of the level K^p, such that for k ≥ C and r ≥ 3 (within k > p + 1) the map eRΓ(𝔛, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) → eRΓ(𝔛^{≥1}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) is a quasi-isomorphism.
items.note: Theorem 11.2.1 (5).

items.name: Theorem 11.2.1 (6): weight (k,2), degrees 0 and 1
items.statement: For all k ≥ C, the map eH^i(𝔛, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) → eH^i(𝔛^{≥1}, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) is bijective for i = 0 and injective for i = 1. [Printed with Ω^{(k,r)} in the target; sourceIssues E87.]
items.note: Theorem 11.2.1 (6). The printed statement has Ω^{(k,r)} for Ω^{(k,2)} in the target (sourceIssues E87).

items.name: Theorem 11.2.1 (7): fRΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p)) is perfect of amplitude [0,1] over Z_p
items.statement: For all k ≥ C and r ≥ 2 (within k > p + 1), fRΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p), Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) is a perfect complex of Z_p-modules of amplitude [0, 1].
items.note: Theorem 11.2.1 (7): perfectness over Z_p of the missing fRΓ. The perfectness criterion (Proposition 2.2.2) is planned at DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:P7 (K1); the complex is not.

items.name: Corollary 11.2.1: H^0 with Q_p/Z_p coefficients
items.statement: For k > p + 1, the natural map eH^0(𝔛, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D) ⊗ Q_p/Z_p) → fH^0(𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p), Ω^{(k,2)}(−D) ⊗ Q_p/Z_p) is an isomorphism (printed: 'quasi-isomorphism').
items.note: Corollary 11.2.1 (printed as a 'quasi-isomorphism'), deduced from Theorem 11.2.1 (4) and extension across codimension 2.

items.name: Acyclic resolution of F^κ_{m,n} ⊗ ω^2(−D)
items.statement: For all m ≥ n, over X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_n, 0 → F^κ_{m,n} ⊗ ω^2(−D) → colim_l F^κ_{m,n} ⊗ ω^{2+lp^{n−1}(p−1)}(−D) → colim_l F^κ_{m,n} ⊗ ω^{2+lp^{n−1}(p−1)}(−D)/Ha^{lp^{n−1}} → 0 is an acyclic resolution. All terms are acyclic relative to the minimal compactification, and the middle and right terms have affine support in the minimal compactification. (The printed version carries the twist (−D) twice.)
items.note: Resolution of the missing F^κ_{m,n} ⊗ ω^2(−D). The item records the printed double twist (−D).

items.name: fRΓ(X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) ≅ fRΓ(X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1, F^k_{1,1} ⊗ ω^2(−D))
items.statement: For every k ∈ Z_{≥0} there is an exact sequence 0 → KΩ^{(k,2)}(−D) → Ω^{(k,2)}(−D) → F^k_{1,1} ⊗ ω^2(−D) → 0 over X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1. For k > p + 1, U is locally finite on all terms of the resulting diagram of two-term complexes and acts by 0 on the KΩ complex. Applying f gives a quasi-isomorphism fRΓ(X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) → fRΓ(X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1, F^k_{1,1} ⊗ ω^2(−D)).
items.note: Comparison through the missing KΩ sequence and the missing U.

items.name: The correspondence C_m of U^m and the factorization (U^m)'
items.statement: For m ≥ 1, U^m on X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1 arises from the correspondence C_m of triples (G, H_1, G_m) with (G, H_1) ∈ X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1 and G → G_m an isogeny with kernel L_m such that L_m ∩ H_1 = {0} and, if G is abelian, L_m is an extension of an étale group scheme étale-locally ≅ Z/p^{2m}Z by a truncated BT group of level m, height 2 and dimension 1. The projections are z_1(G, H_1, G_m) = (G, H_1) and z_2(G, H_1, G_m) = (G_m, Im H_1), and z_2 lifts to z_2 : C_m → X^{≥1}_Kli(p^m)_1, (G_m, H'_m) with H'_m the image of G[p^m] in G_m. Consequently there is a map (U^m)' : RΓ(X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1, F^k_{m,1} ⊗ ω^2(−D)) → RΓ(X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1, F^k_{1,1} ⊗ ω^2(−D)) with ι ∘ (U^m)' = U^m on the F^k_{m,1}-term and (U^m)' ∘ ι = U^m on the F^k_{1,1}-term, where ι is induced by F^k_{1,1} ↪ F^k_{m,1}.
items.note: The correspondence C_m of U^m, lifted to the deep Klingen tower, and the factorization (U^m)'. Two misprints on p. 72, checked on the page image: the lower-right corner of the displayed diagram has F^κ_{1,1} for F^k_{1,1} (sourceIssues E95), and z_2 is written C → X instead of C_m → X (sourceIssues E94).

items.name: f colim_m RΓ(F^k_{m,1} ⊗ ω^2(−D)) ≅ fRΓ(Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) mod p
items.statement: U is locally finite on colim_m RΓ(X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1, F^k_{m,1} ⊗ ω^2(−D)), and f colim_m RΓ(X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1, F^k_{m,1} ⊗ ω^2(−D)) ≅ fRΓ(X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1, F^k_{1,1} ⊗ ω^2(−D)) ≅ fRΓ(X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)). This holds first for k > p + 1 and then (p. 73) for all k ≥ 0.
items.note: Ordinary comparison of the missing colim_m RΓ(F^k_{m,1} ⊗ ω^2(−D)) with fRΓ(Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)). Pages 72–73 print Ω^{(k,r)} for Ω^{(k,2)}.

items.name: Theorem 11.3.1 (1): U is locally finite on the Λ-adic complex
items.statement: The action of U on RΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p), 𝔉^κ ⊗ ω^2(−D)) is locally finite. Call f the associated projector.
items.note: Theorem 11.3.1 (1), the paper's main Λ-adic finiteness statement (K1 thm-1-1-perfect-complex-M, missing).

items.name: Theorem 11.3.1 (2): the ordinary family is a perfect Λ-complex in degrees [0,1]
items.statement: fRΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p), 𝔉^κ ⊗ ω^2(−D)) is a perfect complex of Λ-modules concentrated in degrees [0, 1].
items.note: Theorem 11.3.1 (2). Perfect complexes over Λ and the §2 criterion are planned (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:P7); the complex fRΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p), 𝔉^κ ⊗ ω^2(−D)) is not.

items.name: Theorem 11.3.1 (3): control theorem in every weight k ≥ 0
items.statement: For all k ≥ 0, U is locally finite on RΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p), Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)), and there is a quasi-isomorphism fRΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p), Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) → fRΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p), 𝔉^κ ⊗ ω^2(−D)) ⊗^L_{Λ,k} Z_p, where Λ → Z_p is [x] ↦ x^k.
items.note: Theorem 11.3.1 (3), the control theorem. The derived tensor product ⊗^L_{Λ,k} is P7's; the complexes are missing.

items.name: Theorem 11.3.1 (4): classical comparison in large weight
items.statement: There is a constant C, independent of the level K^p, such that for all k ≥ C the canonical map eH^i(𝔛, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) → H^i(fRΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p), 𝔉^κ ⊗ ω^2(−D)) ⊗^L_{Λ,k} Z_p) is bijective for i = 0 and injective for i = 1.
items.note: Theorem 11.3.1 (4), comparison with classical eH^i in large weight. The introduction (§1, p. 4) states the i = 0 case as an integral control theorem for k ≫ 0: H^0(M ⊗^L_{Λ,k} Z_p) = H^0(X_K, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D))^{T−ord}, where M = fRΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p), 𝔉^κ ⊗ ω^2(−D)). Here e is the ordinary projector for T (Theorem 11.2.1 (4)), and formal GAGA identifies H^0(𝔛, ·) with H^0(X_K, ·). The introduction's accompanying claim that M is a perfect complex is Theorem 11.3.1 (2), recorded as higher-hida-family-perfect-complex-over-Lambda. The introduction adds that an integral control theorem for all k ≥ 0 seems very hard. So §1, p. 4 is a second locator.

items.name: Part III conventions: base ring O_{C_p}, p^w, M_w, Adm, NAdm
items.statement: Throughout Part III the base ring is O := O_{C_p}, the ring of integers of C_p (not Z_p), with the valuation normalized by v(p) = 1. For a rational number w, p^w ∈ O denotes an element of valuation w; for an O-module M, M_w := M/p^w M. Adm is the category of admissible O-algebras: flat O-algebras which are quotients of a convergent power series ring O⟨X_1,…,X_s⟩ by a finitely generated ideal. NAdm (printed 'Nadm' on p. 76) is the category of normal admissible O-algebras.
items.note: O_{C_p}, C_p and O⟨X_1,…,X_s⟩ are in the libraries. Admissible O-algebras (flat and topologically finitely presented) and the p^w bounds are planned in R2. Two conventions need care. (1) Mathlib's valuation on ℂ_[p] is multiplicative and ℝ≥0-valued, with v(p) = 1/p (PadicComplex.valuation_p, Complex.lean:162); the paper's additive v(p) = 1 is −log_p of it. (2) O_{C_p} is not noetherian, so R2 needs Bosch–Lütkebohmert admissibility over a rank-one valuation ring, not F0's noetherian Spf. NAdm only adds normality. Elements p^w exist for every rational w because C_p is algebraically closed (Mathlib: PadicComplex.isAlgClosed). O is Mathlib's PadicComplexInt (notation 𝓞_ℂ_[p]). M_w = M/p^w M and the category NAdm are only notation.

items.name: Formal and analytic Siegel threefolds of full level p^n and the Hodge–Tate map HT
items.statement: Fix a Γ-admissible polyhedral cone decomposition Σ and let X → Spec O be the associated toroidal compactification of the Siegel threefold with spherical level at p and tame level K^p (as in [63] §1.2). 𝒳 is the associated analytic adic space over Spa(C_p,O), 𝔛 the p-adic formal completion of X, 𝒳(p^n) → 𝒳 the adic Siegel threefold with full level p^n structure, and 𝔛(p^n) the normalization of 𝔛 in 𝒳(p^n). 𝔜 ⊂ 𝔛 and 𝔜(p^n) ⊂ 𝔛(p^n) are the complements of the boundary. Over 𝔜(p^n) there is a universal homomorphism of group schemes (Z/p^nZ)^4 → G[p^n] (G the universal abelian surface) which is a symplectic isomorphism up to a similitude factor on the analytic generic fibre, and a Hodge–Tate period map G[p^n] → ω_G/p^n ω_G (ω_G and ω_{G^t} identified via the polarization). HT : (Z/p^nZ)^4 → ω_G/p^n ω_G denotes the composite.
items.note: This follows CG20, which marked siegel-threefold-Y-K planned at M1/M2/M5 and toroidal-compactification-hodge-bundle planned at C5/C3. Two small steps are named nowhere. First, the universal level map (Z/p^n)^4 → G[p^n] must be extended from the generic fibre to the normalization 𝔜(p^n): a section of the finite flat G[p^n] over a normal, O-flat base extends. M4 warns against asserting 'a fine moduli interpretation ... on such a normalization without a separate theorem'. Second, that map is a symplectic similitude on the generic fibre. The extension of HT over the boundary is a separate item (missing). Source: Pilloni–Stroh [63] §1.2. The objects of this setup are planned: the integral toroidal Siegel threefold at spherical level (PELModuli:M5, ShimuraCompactifications:C5); the generic-fibre toroidal compactifications at full level p^n (ShimuraCompactifications:C2), with their analytification and formal completion (AdicSpacesPartII:R1, R2); the normalization 𝔛(p^n) of 𝔛 in 𝒳(p^n) (PELModuli:M4, ShimuraCompactifications:C5); the p-level tower (PerfectoidShimuraVarieties:S0); and the finite-level Hodge–Tate map (HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T0).

items.name: Extension of HT over the toroidal compactification (Pilloni–Stroh Prop. 1.2)
items.statement: The Hodge–Tate period map extends over 𝔛(p^n) (boundary included) to a morphism HT : (Z/p^nZ)^4 → ω_G/p^n.
items.note: T0 plans the finite-level HT map ('Build the finite-level Hodge–Tate map using Cartier duality and differentials of characters'). What it extends 'to semi-abelian degeneration charts' is only 'the local construction' (the Hodge ideal). No layer extends HT : (Z/p^n)^4 → ω_G/p^n over the boundary of the normalized toroidal model 𝔛(p^n). T6's toroidal statement is a different map: the flag-valued period map on the infinite-level diamond (Boxer–Pilloni 4.4.40), not this integral finite-level map. External input: [63] V. Pilloni, B. Stroh, Cohomologie cohérente et représentations galoisiennes, Ann. Math. Québec 40 (2016), Prop. 1.2

items.name: The modification 𝔛(p^n)^mod and the locally free sheaf ω_G^mod (Pilloni–Stroh Prop. 1.10)
items.statement: There is a formal scheme 𝔛(p^n)^mod → 𝔛(p^n), the normalization of a blow-up, carrying a locally free rank-2 modification ω_G^mod ↪ ω_G such that (1) p^{1/(p−1)} ω_G ⊂ ω_G^mod ⊂ ω_G, and (2) the Hodge–Tate map factors through ω_G^mod/p^n ω_G and induces a surjective homomorphism (Z/p^nZ)^4 ⊗_Z O_{𝔛(p^n)^mod} → ω_G^mod/p^{n−1/(p−1)} ω_G^mod.
items.note: The Hilbert analogue is planned: T5 'Construct the integral differential lattice ω^int used in BHW §7 by its finite-level Hodge–Tate image and inverse-image description. Prove ... local freeness ... and the cokernel estimates'. No layer builds the Siegel modification 𝔛(p^n)^mod, the normalization of a blow-up. Its properties are also unplanned: p^{1/(p−1)}ω_G ⊂ ω_G^mod ⊂ ω_G, and the surjection (Z/p^n)^4 ⊗ O → ω^mod/p^{n−1/(p−1)}ω^mod. Admissible blow-ups come from AdicSpacesPartII:R2. External input: [63] Pilloni–Stroh, Ann. Math. Québec 40 (2016), Prop. 1.10

items.name: The formal neighbourhood 𝔛(p^n,ε) where HT(e_1) ≡ 0 mod p^ε
items.statement: Equip (Z/p^nZ)^4 with its canonical basis (e_1,e_2,e_3,e_4) and the standard symplectic form of matrix J (§5.1; J pairs e_1 with e_4 and e_2 with e_3). For ε ∈ [0, n − 1/(p−1)] ∩ Q, 𝔛(p^n,ε) → 𝔛(p^n)^mod is the formal scheme where HT(e_1) = 0 in ω_G^mod/p^ε ω_G^mod. It is an open formal subscheme of an admissible blow-up of 𝔛(p^n)^mod.
items.note: The locus where HT(e_1) ≡ 0 mod p^ε ω^mod, i.e. where the Klingen subgroup ⟨e_1⟩ is close to multiplicative, is planned nowhere. T4 defines 'canonical and anticanonical loci by subgroup conditions' only for the BHW Hilbert tower. R2 supplies only the generic mechanism: 'rational subdomains cut out by a section of a line bundle and a valuation bound ... Apply this to a Hasse ideal and its blow-ups'.

items.name: Canonical filtration Fil^can_ε
items.statement: Over 𝔛(p^n,ε), Fil^can_ε ⊂ (ω_G^mod)_ε = ω_G^mod/p^ε ω_G^mod is the coherent subsheaf generated by HT(e_2) and HT(e_3).
items.note: Defined only on the missing 𝔛(p^n,ε), from the missing ω^mod. No layer plans it.

items.name: Lemma 12.2.2.1: Fil^can_ε is locally free of rank one and locally a direct summand
items.statement: For ε ∈ [0, n − 1/(p−1)] ∩ Q, the sheaf Fil^can_ε is a locally free sheaf of rank one of O_{𝔛(p^n,ε)}/p^ε-modules and is locally a direct summand of (ω_G^mod)_ε.
items.note: Depends on the missing 𝔛(p^n,ε) and Fil^can_ε. The proof misprints the generator: when c is a unit it is HT(e_3). The print says HT(e_2) (sourceIssues E96).

items.name: The open cover 𝔛(p^n,ε) = 𝔛(p^n,ε,e_2) ∪ 𝔛(p^n,ε,e_3)
items.statement: 𝔛(p^n,ε,e_2) and 𝔛(p^n,ε,e_3) are the open formal subschemes of 𝔛(p^n,ε) where HT(e_2), respectively HT(e_3), generates Fil^can_ε; they cover 𝔛(p^n,ε). Over 𝔛(p^n,ε,e_i) (i ∈ {2,3}) the vectors HT(e_i), HT(e_4) form a basis of (ω_G^mod)_ε.
items.note: Specific to 𝔛(p^n,ε). Nothing plans it.

items.name: Canonical quotient Gr^can_ε and the isomorphism HT_4 ⊗ 1
items.statement: Gr^can_ε := coker(Fil^can_ε → (ω_G^mod)_ε). Passing to the quotient, HT induces a canonical map HT_4 : (Z/p^nZ)^4/⟨e_1,e_2,e_3⟩ ≅ Z/p^nZ → Gr^can_ε, and HT_4 ⊗ 1 : Z/p^nZ ⊗ (O_{𝔛(p^n,ε)})_ε → Gr^can_ε is an isomorphism.
items.note: Depends on the missing Fil^can_ε and on the extension of HT over 𝔛(p^n). Nothing plans it.

items.name: Formal flag varieties 𝔉𝔏_n, 𝔉𝔏_{n,ε,w} and 𝔉𝔏^+_{n,ε,w,w'}
items.statement: 𝔉𝔏_n → 𝔛(p^n)^mod is the flag variety (a P^1-bundle) parametrizing locally free direct summands of rank one Filω_G^mod ⊂ ω_G^mod. For rationals 0 ≤ w ≤ ε, 𝔉𝔏_{n,ε,w} → 𝔉𝔏_n ×_{𝔛(p^n)^mod} 𝔛(p^n,ε) → 𝔛(p^n,ε) is the admissible formal scheme parametrizing such Filω_G^mod with (Filω_G^mod)_w = Fil^can_w (the reduction of Fil^can_ε mod p^w). For positive rationals w' ≤ w, 𝔉𝔏^+_{n,ε,w,w'} → 𝔉𝔏_{n,ε,w} is the normal admissible formal scheme parametrizing bases ρ : O_{𝔉𝔏^+} ≅ ω_G^mod/Filω_G^mod such that ρ_{w'} = HT_4 ⊗ 1 mod p^{w'}.
items.note: Only 𝔉𝔏_n is planned: AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.1 'Construct projective bundles, Grassmannians and flag schemes with their quotient/subbundle universal properties', with formal completion from AdicSpacesPartII:R2. Mathlib's Module.Grassmannian (RingTheory/Grassmannian.lean:68) is only the functor of points; its representability is listed as a TODO there. The other two spaces depend on the missing Fil^can and HT_4. 𝔉𝔏_{n,ε,w} consists of the flags with (Filω^mod)_w = Fil^can_w. 𝔉𝔏^+ consists of the trivializations ρ with ρ ≡ HT_4 ⊗ 1 mod p^{w'}.

items.name: Klingen parabolic, group action and the formal quotient 𝔛_Kli(p^n,ε)
items.statement: 𝔊𝔖𝔭_4 is the formal p-adic completion of GSp_4 and 𝔎𝔩𝔦 ⊂ 𝔊𝔖𝔭_4 the Klingen parabolic of block upper triangular matrices with blocks of sizes 1×1, 2×2, 1×1. The action of GSp_4(Z/p^nZ) on 𝒳(p^n) (trivial over 𝒳) extends by normality to 𝔛(p^n) and to 𝔛(p^n)^mod (obtained by blowing up invariant ideals and normalizing); Kli(Z/p^nZ) acts on 𝔛(p^n,ε), and 𝔛_Kli(p^n,ε) := 𝔛(p^n,ε)/Kli(Z/p^nZ).
items.note: Some inputs are planned. The Klingen parabolic is planned as in CG20 (def-klingen-parabolic-and-levi: tauceti ReductiveGroups layer 7, ShimuraCompactifications:C1). The GSp4(Z/p^n)-action on the level-p^n tower is PerfectoidShimuraVarieties:S0 ('construct their right group actions with the correct level changes'). Not planned: the extension of the action to 𝔛(p^n)^mod and 𝔛(p^n,ε), and the formal quotient 𝔛_Kli(p^n,ε).

items.name: The formal groups 𝔗_{w'} ⊃ 𝔗^0_{w'} and the torsor 𝔉𝔏^+ → 𝔉𝔏
items.statement: For rational w' > 0 (printed w' ≥ 0), 𝔗_{w'} is the formal group scheme with 𝔗_{w'}(R) = Z_p^×(1 + p^{w'}R) for R ∈ Adm, and 𝔗^0_{w'} is its identity component, 𝔗^0_{w'}(R) = 1 + p^{w'}R. The group 𝔗^0_{w'} acts on 𝔉𝔏^+_{n,ε,w,w'} (through ρ) and 𝔉𝔏^+_{n,ε,w,w'} → 𝔉𝔏_{n,ε,w} is a 𝔗^0_{w'}-torsor.
items.note: The groups Z_p^×(1+p^{w'}R) are the domains of analyticity planned with the weights (OverconvergentAutomorphicForms:O0, PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L0a; see w-prime-analytic-character). The torsor statement for 𝔉𝔏^+ → 𝔉𝔏_{n,ε,w} under 𝔗^0_{w'} is Siegel-specific and unplanned. The printed 'w' ≥ 0' should read 'w' > 0'; this is already recorded.

items.name: The group 𝔗_{w',n} and its action on 𝔉𝔏^+_{n,ε,w,w'}
items.statement: For integers n ≥ w', 𝔗_{w',n} := 𝔗_{w'} ×_{𝔗_{w'}/𝔗^0_{w'}} Kli(Z/p^nZ), where Kli(Z/p^nZ) → 𝔗_{w'}/𝔗^0_{w'} is the composite of Kli(Z/p^nZ) → (Z/p^nZ)^× (last diagonal entry) with the natural projection (Z/p^nZ)^× → 𝔗_{w'}/𝔗^0_{w'} (defined since w' ≤ n). 𝔗^0_{w'} is naturally a subgroup of 𝔗_{w',n}, and the action of 𝔗^0_{w'} on 𝔉𝔏^+_{n,ε,w,w'} extends to an action of 𝔗_{w',n} which induces the action of Kli(Z/p^nZ) on 𝔛(p^n,ε).
items.note: Built from the missing Klingen action and torsor. No layer plans it.

items.name: Local description of 𝔉𝔏^+_{n,ε,w,w'}
items.statement: Let Spf R ↪ 𝔛(p^n,ε) be a Zariski open with ω_G^mod|_{Spf R} = Rω_1 ⊕ Rω_2, where ω_1 lifts a basis of Fil^can and ω_2 lifts HT(e_4). Over Spf R, 𝔉𝔏^+_{n,ε,w,w'} is identified with (1 0; p^w 𝔅(0,1)_R 1) × (1 + p^{w'} 𝔅(0,1)_R), 𝔅(0,1)_R = Spf R⟨X⟩: the universal matrix (1 0; p^w X 1) × (1 + p^{w'}X') corresponds to the flag Filω_G^mod = ⟨ω_1 + p^w X ω_2⟩ and the trivialization ρ of Grω_G^mod given by ρ(1) = (1 + p^{w'}X')·ω_2.
items.note: A chart computation on the missing 𝔉𝔏^+. The closed discs Spf R⟨X⟩ are Tau Ceti's restricted power series (restrictedMvPowerSeriesSubring), but the identification itself is not planned.

items.name: Formal Banach sheaf (AIP Def. A.1.1.1)
items.statement: Let 𝔖 be an admissible formal scheme. A formal Banach sheaf over 𝔖 is a family (𝔉_n)_{n≥0} of quasi-coherent sheaves such that (1) 𝔉_n is a sheaf of O_𝔖/p^n-modules, (2) 𝔉_n is flat over O/p^n, (3) for all 0 ≤ m ≤ n there are compatible isomorphisms 𝔉_n ⊗_O O/p^m ≅ 𝔉_m. It is identified with the sheaf 𝔉 = lim_n 𝔉_n. It is flat if each 𝔉_n is a flat O_𝔖/p^n-module.
items.note: No layer defines formal Banach sheaves, i.e. compatible systems of O/p^n-flat quasi-coherent sheaves on an admissible formal scheme. OverconvergentAutomorphicForms:O5 constructs the 'integral and rational versions' of the Hilbert AIP sheaf, which needs this formalism, but does not name it. AdicSpacesPartII:R3 treats coherent sheaves only. Neither library has anything. External input: [3] F. Andreatta, A. Iovita, V. Pilloni, p-adic families of Siegel modular cuspforms, Ann. of Math. 181 (2015), Def. A.1.1.1

items.name: w'-analytic character κ_A
items.statement: Let n ≥ 1, ε ∈ ]0, n − 1/(p−1)] ∩ Q and rationals 0 < w' ≤ w ≤ ε. Let A ∈ NAdm. A continuous character κ_A : Z_p^× → A^× is w'-analytic if it extends to a pairing κ_A : 𝔗_{w'} × Spf A → G_m.
items.note: The paper's version is integral: κ_A over A ∈ NAdm must extend to a morphism of formal schemes 𝔗_{w'} × Spf A → G_m, as in AIP. The L0a/O0 blueprint should state this formal-model form beside the rigid one. The library audit finds no rigid character space in either library.

items.name: The invertible sheaf 𝔏^{κ_A} on 𝔉𝔏_{n,ε,w} × Spf A
items.statement: Let π_1 : 𝔉𝔏^+_{n,ε,w,w'} → 𝔉𝔏_{n,ε,w} (a 𝔗^0_{w'}-torsor). Define 𝔏^{κ_A} := ((π_1)_⋆ O_{𝔉𝔏^+_{n,ε,w,w'}} ⊗̂_O A)^{𝔗^0_{w'}}, the invariants for the diagonal action of 𝔗^0_{w'} (geometric action on 𝔉𝔏^+, action via κ_A on A); it is an invertible sheaf on 𝔉𝔏_{n,ε,w} × Spf A.
items.note: The generic step is planned in OverconvergentAutomorphicForms:O1: 'Given an actual torsor/group action and an analytic automorphy cocycle, construct the equivariant coefficient sheaf as an equalizer'. The torsor 𝔉𝔏^+ → 𝔉𝔏_{n,ε,w} and the formal ⊗̂_O A version are specific to this paper. O8 instantiates coefficients on Siegel varieties only 'on the proven anticanonical domains', not on the Klingen neighbourhoods 𝔛(p^n,ε).

items.name: Remark 12.6.2.1: 𝔏^{κ_A} does not depend on w'
items.statement: For w'' ∈ [w', w], viewing κ_A as a character of 𝔗^0_{w''} and performing the same construction with 𝔉𝔏^+_{n,ε,w,w''} gives an invertible sheaf canonically isomorphic to 𝔏^{κ_A}; the isomorphism comes from the natural map 𝔉𝔏^+_{n,ε,w,w''} → 𝔉𝔏^+_{n,ε,w,w'}, equivariant for 𝔗^0_{w''} → 𝔗^0_{w'}.
items.note: A property of the missing 𝔏^{κ_A}.

items.name: The formal Banach sheaf 𝔊^{κ_A,w} on 𝔛(p^n,ε) × Spf A
items.statement: Let π_2 : 𝔉𝔏_{n,ε,w} → 𝔛(p^n,ε). Define the formal Banach sheaf 𝔊^{κ_A,w} := (π_2)_⋆ 𝔏^{κ_A} over 𝔛(p^n,ε) × Spf A.
items.note: The pushforward of the missing 𝔏^{κ_A}. The formal Banach sheaf notion is itself missing (see formal-banach-sheaf).

items.name: Lemma 12.6.2.1: 𝔊^{κ_A,w} is flat
items.statement: The formal Banach sheaf 𝔊^{κ_A,w} is flat; more precisely, for Spf R ⊂ 𝔛(p^n,ε) as in §12.5, 𝔊^{κ_A,w}(Spf R × Spf A) ≅ R ⊗̂ A⟨X⟩.
items.note: Depends on the missing chart description and sheaf. The proof misprints 𝔗^0_w for 𝔗^0_{w'} (sourceIssues E98).

items.name: Lemma 12.6.2.2: 𝔊^{κ_A,w}/p^w is an inductive limit of extensions of O/p^w
items.statement: For i ∈ {2,3}, the restriction of the quasi-coherent sheaf 𝔊^{κ_A,w}/p^w to 𝔛(p^n,ε,e_i) is an inductive limit of coherent sheaves which are extensions of the sheaf O_{𝔛(p^n,ε,e_i)}/p^w.
items.note: The proof rests on AIP [3] Cor. 8.1.5.4 and 8.1.6.4 for Siegel varieties, which no layer plans; O5 plans the Hilbert AIP construction only. External input: [3] AIP, Ann. of Math. 181 (2015), main construction §4.5 and Cor. 8.1.5.4, Cor. 8.1.6.4

items.name: The formal Banach sheaf 𝔉^{κ_A,w} on 𝔛_Kli(p^n,ε) × Spf A
items.statement: Let π_3 : 𝔛(p^n,ε) → 𝔛_Kli(p^n,ε) be the finite projection. The sheaf (π_3)_⋆𝔊^{κ_A,w} is 𝔗_{w',n}-equivariant, and 𝔉^{κ_A,w} := ((π_3)_⋆𝔊^{κ_A,w})^{𝔗_{w',n}} = (π_⋆ O_{𝔉𝔏^+_{n,ε,w,w'}} ⊗̂ A)^{𝔗_{w',n}} over 𝔛_Kli(p^n,ε) × Spf A (π : 𝔉𝔏^+_{n,ε,w,w'} → 𝔛_Kli(p^n,ε)).
items.note: Depends on the missing 𝔊^{κ_A,w} and 𝔗_{w',n}. The printed 𝔗_{w,n} should read 𝔗_{w',n}; this is already recorded.

items.name: Analytic spaces 𝒳_Kli(p^n), 𝒳_Kli(p^n)^+, 𝒳(p^n,ε), 𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), 𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε)^+
items.statement: 𝒳_Kli(p^n) := 𝒳(p^n)/Kli(Z/p^nZ), Kli(Z/p^nZ) ⊂ GSp_4(Z/p^nZ) the block upper triangular matrices (blocks 1,2,1). Kli(Z/p^nZ)^+ ⊂ Kli(Z/p^nZ) is the normal subgroup of elements with trivial last diagonal entry, Kli(Z/p^nZ)/Kli(Z/p^nZ)^+ ≅ (Z/p^nZ)^×, and 𝒳_Kli(p^n)^+ := 𝒳(p^n)/Kli(Z/p^nZ)^+. For ε ∈ [0, n − 1/(p−1)] ∩ Q, 𝒳(p^n,ε) is the analytic space associated to 𝔛(p^n,ε), an open subset of 𝒳(p^n) stable under Kli(Z/p^nZ); 𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε) := 𝒳(p^n,ε)/Kli(Z/p^nZ) ⊂ 𝒳_Kli(p^n) and 𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε)^+ := 𝒳(p^n,ε)/Kli(Z/p^nZ)^+ ⊂ 𝒳_Kli(p^n)^+. For n ≥ 1 there are commutative squares 𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε) → 𝒳_Kli(p^n) over 𝒳_Kli(p^{n−1},ε) → 𝒳_Kli(p^{n−1}) and similarly with +.
items.note: The Klingen-level threefolds 𝒳_Kli(p^n) and 𝒳_Kli(p^n)^+ are Shimura varieties at level K^p·Kli(p^n) (resp. Kli(p^n)^+), so they are planned: ShimuraCompactifications:C2/C3 in characteristic 0 and AdicSpacesPartII:R1 for the analytification. The neighbourhoods 𝒳(p^n,ε), 𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε) and 𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε)^+ are not.

items.name: The étale sheaf ω_G^{mod,+} (with Remark 12.7.1.1)
items.statement: Over 𝒳, ω_G^{mod,+} is the sheaf of O_𝒳^+-modules for the étale topology defined as the subsheaf of the sheaf ω_G^+ of integral differential forms at the origin of G generated by the image of the Hodge–Tate period map. (Remark 12.7.1.1) It does not come from the analytic site, but its pullback to 𝒳(p^n) for n ≥ 1 (n ≥ 2 if p = 2) comes from a sheaf on the Zariski site.
items.note: This is an étale-site sheaf generated by the image of HT, for which T5's ω^int ('by its finite-level Hodge–Tate image') is the Hilbert analogue. No layer plans the Siegel version or Remark 12.7.1.1: after pullback to 𝒳(p^n), n ≥ 1 (n ≥ 2 if p = 2), it comes from the Zariski site. The étale sites are AdicEtaleGeometry:A1 and AdicSpacesPartII:R4.

items.name: Modular interpretation of 𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε)
items.statement: 𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε) parametrizes pairs (x, H_n) where x is a point of 𝒳 and H_n ⊂ G_x[p^n] is a finite flat group scheme locally isomorphic to Z/p^nZ which, locally for the étale topology, is generated by an element e_1 with HT(e_1) = 0 in ω_{G_x}^{mod,+}/p^ε ω_{G_x}^{mod,+}.
items.note: A moduli description of the missing 𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), through subgroups H_n ≅ Z/p^n with HT(e_1) ≡ 0 mod p^ε. No layer plans it.

items.name: Étale sheaves Fil^can_ε, Gr^can_ε on 𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε) and HT_4 ⊗ 1 over 𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε)^+
items.statement: Define étale sheaves Fil^can_ε := Im(HT ⊗ 1 : H_n^⊥ ⊗ O^+_{𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε)} → (ω_G^{mod,+})_ε) and Gr^can_ε := coker(HT ⊗ 1 : H_n^⊥ ⊗ O^+_{𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε)} → (ω_G^{mod,+})_ε); they are locally free sheaves of O^+_{𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε)}/p^ε-modules. 𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε)^+ → 𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε) is the torsor of trivializations of H_n^D, with universal trivialization ψ : Z/p^nZ → H_n^D. Over 𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε)^+, ψ and the Hodge–Tate map of G[p^n] give a canonical isomorphism HT_4 ⊗ 1 : Z/p^nZ ⊗ (O^+_{𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε)})_ε → Gr^can_ε.
items.note: The analytic analogue of the missing formal Fil^can/Gr^can, at Klingen level. No layer plans it.

items.name: Analytic flag spaces ℱℒ_{n,ε,w} and ℱℒ^+_{n,ε,w,w'}
items.statement: ℱℒ^+_{n,ε,w,w'} → ℱℒ_{n,ε,w} → 𝒳(p^n,ε) are the analytic spaces associated to 𝔉𝔏^+_{n,ε,w,w'} and 𝔉𝔏_{n,ε,w}.
items.note: The generic fibres of the missing formal flag spaces. The generic-fibre functor itself is planned in AdicSpacesPartII:R2.

items.name: Lemma 12.7.2.1: ℱℒ_{n,ε,w} descends to ℱℒ_{Kli,n,ε,w} ⊂ ℱℒ over 𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε)
items.statement: ℱℒ_{n,ε,w} descends to an open subspace ℱℒ_{Kli,n,ε,w} of the flag variety ℱℒ → 𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε) of ω_G (a P^1-bundle); ℱℒ_{Kli,n,ε,w} is the space of flags Filω_G ⊂ ω_G such that, locally for the étale topology, (Filω_G ∩ ω_G^{mod,+})_w = Fil^can_w.
items.note: The ambient P^1-bundle ℱℒ of ω_G is planned (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.1, analytified by AdicSpacesPartII:R1). The open ℱℒ_{Kli,n,ε,w} and its descent through Conrad's lemma are not.

items.name: The space ℱℒ^+ → 𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε)^+
items.statement: ℱℒ^+ → 𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε)^+ is the moduli space of flags Filω_G ⊂ ω_G (locally direct summands of rank 1) together with a trivialization ρ of Grω_G = ω_G/Filω_G (a nowhere vanishing section of the line bundle Gr(ω_G)).
items.note: A generic construction. Over the P^1-bundle of rank-one direct summands of ω_G, take the G_m-torsor of trivializations of the universal quotient line bundle, analytify it, and restrict it to 𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε)^+. That base is itself missing (see analytic-klingen-level-spaces-X-Kli-pn-eps). The base is printed 𝒳_Kli(p^n, e_1)^+, a misprint for 𝒳_Kli(p^n, ε)^+ (sourceIssues E100).

items.name: Lemma 12.7.2.2: ℱℒ^+_{n,ε,w,w'} descends to ℱℒ^+_{Kli,n,ε,w,w'}
items.statement: ℱℒ^+_{n,ε,w,w'} descends to an open subspace ℱℒ^+_{Kli,n,ε,w,w'} of ℱℒ^+ → 𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε)^+: the space of pairs (Filω_G ⊂ ω_G, ρ ∈ Gr ω_G) such that (Filω_G ∩ ω_G^{mod,+})_w = Fil^can_w, and ρ belongs to ω_G^{mod,+}/(Filω_G ∩ ω_G^{mod,+}) and reduces to the element HT_4(1) of Gr^can_{w'}.
items.note: Descends the missing ℱℒ^+_{n,ε,w,w'} through Conrad's lemma. No layer plans it.

items.name: Descent of admissible opens along finite flat maps (Conrad)
items.statement: Descent of admissible opens ([16] Lem. 4.2.4), as used in the proofs of Lemmas 12.7.2.1–12.7.2.2. The map q : 𝒳(p^n,ε) ×_{𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε)} ℱℒ → ℱℒ (resp. 𝒳(p^n,ε) ×_{𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε)^+} ℱℒ^+ → ℱℒ^+) is finite flat, and ℱℒ_{n,ε,w} (resp. ℱℒ^+_{n,ε,w,w'}) is an admissible open of its source. The paper deduces from [16] Lem. 4.2.4 that this open descends to an admissible open ℱℒ_{Kli,n,ε,w} ⊂ ℱℒ (resp. ℱℒ^+_{Kli,n,ε,w,w'} ⊂ ℱℒ^+). For this the open must be the full preimage of a subset of the target, i.e. stable under Kli(Z/p^nZ) (resp. Kli(Z/p^nZ)^+). That holds because the defining conditions involve only Fil^can, Gr^can and HT_4, which are built from H_n^⊥ and ψ. The paper checks neither this stability nor the precise hypotheses of [16] Lem. 4.2.4.
items.note: No layer plans descent of admissible opens along finite flat maps of rigid or adic spaces. The nearest owner is AdicSpacesPartII:R0: 'Construct open and closed immersions, separatedness, finite maps, smooth maps, and étale maps using local presentations'. The paper does not quote the exact hypotheses of [16] Lem. 4.2.4. External input: [16] B. Conrad, Relative ampleness in rigid geometry, Ann. Inst. Fourier 56 (2006), Lem. 4.2.4

items.name: Analytic sheaves ℒ^{κ_A}, 𝒢^{κ_A,w}, ℱ^{κ_A,w}
items.statement: 𝒯_{w'}, 𝒯^0_{w'}, 𝒯_{w',n} are the analytic fibres of 𝔗_{w'}, 𝔗^0_{w'}, 𝔗_{w',n}. ℒ^{κ_A} is the invertible sheaf on ℱℒ_{n,ε,w} × Spa(A[1/p],A) associated to 𝔏^{κ_A}; 𝒢^{κ_A,w} is the Banach sheaf generic fibre of 𝔊^{κ_A,w} over 𝒳(p^n,ε) × Spa(A[1/p],A); ℱ^{κ_A,w} is the Banach sheaf associated to 𝔉^{κ_A,w} over 𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε) × Spa(A[1/p],A). Directly, ℱ^{κ_A,w} = (π_⋆ O_{ℱℒ^+_{Kli,n,ε,w,w'}} ⊗̂ A)^{𝒯_{w',n}}, π : ℱℒ^+_{Kli,n,ε,w,w'} → 𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε).
items.note: The generic-fibre functor for formal Banach sheaves (AIP Def. A.2.1.2, Prop. A.2.2.3) belongs with formal-banach-sheaf in AdicSpacesPartII:R3. The three Siegel sheaves ℒ^{κ_A}, 𝒢^{κ_A,w} and ℱ^{κ_A,w} are specific to this paper. External input: [3] AIP, Def. A.2.1.2 and Prop. A.2.2.3 (generic fibre of a formal Banach sheaf)

items.name: (n,ε)-overconvergent, w-analytic cohomology C(n,ε,w,κ_A,r) and C_cusp
items.statement: For r ∈ Z, C(n,ε,w,κ_A,r) := RΓ(𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), ℱ^{κ_A,w} ⊗ ω^r) and C_cusp(n,ε,w,κ_A,r) := RΓ(𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), ℱ^{κ_A,w} ⊗ ω^r(−D)), where ω = det ω_G and D is the boundary divisor. There are restriction maps C(n,ε,w,κ,r) → C(n_1,ε_1,w_1,κ,r) for n_1 ≥ n, ε_1 ≥ ε, w_1 ≥ w (with w ≤ ε, w_1 ≤ ε_1, ε ≤ n − 1/(p−1), ε_1 ≤ n_1 − 1/(p−1)), and likewise for C_cusp.
items.note: No layer plans overconvergent coherent cohomology in any degree. OverconvergentAutomorphicForms:O3 plans only Hilbert sections: 'Construct the space of sections at a fixed radius and the direct system under restriction to smaller neighbourhoods of the ordinary locus'.

items.name: Overconvergent locally analytic cohomology H^i(†,κ_A,r) and H^i_cusp(†,κ_A,r)
items.statement: H^i(†,κ_A,r) := colim_{n,ε,w→∞} H^i(𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), ℱ^{κ_A,w} ⊗ ω^r) and H^i_cusp(†,κ_A,r) := colim_{n,ε,w→∞} H^i(𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), ℱ^{κ_A,w} ⊗ ω^r(−D)), the colimits along the restriction maps of §12.8.1.
items.note: The Hilbert degree-0 analogue is O3: 'Define the overconvergent space as its colimit over positive permitted radii'. Higher-degree colimits are planned nowhere.

items.name: §12.8.2: cohomology of ℱ^{κ_A,w} as cohomology of ℒ^{κ_A} on ℱℒ_{n,ε,w}
items.statement: ℱℒ_{n,ε,w} → 𝒳(p^n,ε) is locally affine: 𝒳(p^n,ε) has a covering by affinoids whose preimages in ℱℒ_{n,ε,w} are affinoid (this does not imply that the preimage of every affinoid is affinoid). 𝒢^{κ_A,w} = (π_2)_⋆ ℒ^{κ_A} and R^i(π_2)_⋆ ℒ^{κ_A} = 0 for i > 0; hence RΓ(𝒳(p^n,ε), 𝒢^{κ_A,w} ⊗ ω^r) = RΓ(ℱℒ_{n,ε,w}, ℒ^{κ_A} ⊗ ω^r) and RΓ(𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), ℱ^{κ_A,w} ⊗ ω^r) = RΓ(Kli(Z/p^nZ), RΓ(ℱℒ_{n,ε,w}, ℒ^{κ_A} ⊗ ω^r)); similarly for cuspidal cohomology.
items.note: Built on the missing flag spaces and sheaves. Footnote 19 is a caveat: local affineness of ℱℒ_{n,ε,w} does not make the preimage of every affinoid affinoid.

items.name: Proposition 12.8.2.1: C and C_cusp are bounded complexes of projective Banach A[1/p]-modules
items.statement: For A ∈ NAdm, κ_A w'-analytic, 0 < w' ≤ w ≤ ε ≤ n − 1/(p−1) and r ∈ Z, the complexes C(n,ε,w,κ_A,r) and C_cusp(n,ε,w,κ_A,r) are represented by bounded complexes of projective Banach A[1/p]-modules.
items.note: Projective Banach modules are planned in LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L4, reviewed node L4/projective-banach-modules: 'Define property (Pr) by the existence of a Banach complement making P⊕Q potentially orthonormalizable'. The Čech complexes of the missing sheaves are not. In the Čech sentence of the proof, 𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε) should read 𝒳(p^n,ε); this is already recorded.

items.name: Proposition 12.9.1: H^i_cusp(†,κ_A,r) = 0 for i > 1
items.statement: For A ∈ NAdm, a w'-analytic character κ_A and r ∈ Z, the cuspidal overconvergent locally analytic cohomology H^i_cusp(†,κ_A,r) vanishes for all i > 1.
items.note: The main result of §12. No layer plans overconvergent coherent cohomology or its vanishing. The introduction (§1, p. 6) restates this as the delicate step of Part III: 'proving that the cuspidal cohomology is concentrated in degree 0 and 1'. The same paragraph says that U is compact on the overconvergent cohomology, so that the finiteness of the finite slope cohomology follows easily; compactness of U is cor-13-2-4-1-U-is-compact (Corollary 13.2.4.1, p. 87). The opening of §12 (p. 73) also calls Proposition 12.9.1 the most delicate result of the section. So §1, p. 6 is a second locator.

items.name: Minimal compactification 𝔛^⋆, its Stein factorization 𝔛(p^n)^⋆, and descent of Λ^2 HT
items.statement: 𝔛^⋆ is the minimal compactification of 𝔜; 𝔛(p^n)^⋆ is the Stein factorization of the natural map 𝔛(p^n) → 𝔛^⋆. The determinant of the Hodge–Tate map Λ^2 HT : Λ^2((Z/p^nZ)^4) → det ω_G/p^n descends from 𝔛(p^n) to 𝔛(p^n)^⋆.
items.note: 𝔛^⋆ is planned (ShimuraCompactifications:C5, 'the integral minimal compactification'). 𝔛(p^n)^⋆, as the normalization at level p^n, is covered by C5 ('For higher p-level normalizations ...') and PerfectoidShimuraVarieties:S1 ('Extend the construction to the minimal compactification using the boundary/normalization construction of the source'). The descent of Λ²HT to 𝔛(p^n)^⋆ (Pilloni–Stroh) is planned nowhere. External input: [63] Pilloni–Stroh, Ann. Math. Québec 40 (2016) (descent of Λ^2 HT to the minimal compactification)

items.name: 𝔛(p^n)^{⋆−mod} and det ω_G^mod (Pilloni–Stroh §1.8)
items.statement: There is a formal scheme 𝔛(p^n)^{⋆−mod} → 𝔛(p^n)^⋆, the normalization of a blow-up, carrying a locally free modification det ω_G^mod ⊂ det ω_G with (1) p^{2/(p−1)} det ω_G ⊂ det ω_G^mod ⊂ det ω_G and (2) a surjective map Λ^2 HT : Λ^2((Z/p^nZ)^4) ⊗ O_{𝔛(p^n)^{⋆−mod}} → det ω_G^mod/p^{n−2/(p−1)}. By the universal property of blow-up and normalization there is a map 𝔛(p^n)^mod → 𝔛(p^n)^{⋆−mod} pulling det ω_G^mod back to det of ω_G^mod and Λ^2 HT back to Λ^2 of HT : (Z/p^nZ)^4 → ω_G^mod/p^{n−2/(p−1)}.
items.note: The minimal-compactification counterpart of ω^mod: 𝔛(p^n)^{⋆−mod}, with p^{2/(p−1)} det ω_G ⊂ det ω_G^mod ⊂ det ω_G and a surjective Λ²HT. No layer plans it. External input: [63] Pilloni–Stroh, Ann. Math. Québec 40 (2016), §1.8

items.name: The neighbourhood 𝔛(p^n,ε)^⋆ in the minimal compactification
items.statement: For ε ∈ [0, n − 2/(p−1)] ∩ Q, 𝔛(p^n,ε)^⋆ is the formal scheme (over 𝔛(p^n)^{⋆−mod}) where HT(e_1)∧HT(e_2) = HT(e_1)∧HT(e_3) = HT(e_1)∧HT(e_4) = 0 mod p^ε.
items.note: Specific to this paper, and depends on the missing 𝔛(p^n)^{⋆−mod}.

items.name: Lemma 12.9.1.1: 𝔛(p^n,ε) = 𝔛(p^n)^mod ×_{𝔛(p^n)^{⋆−mod}} 𝔛(p^n,ε)^⋆
items.statement: For ε ∈ [0, n − 2/(p−1)] ∩ Q, the square with 𝔛(p^n,ε) → 𝔛(p^n)^mod over 𝔛(p^n,ε)^⋆ → 𝔛(p^n)^{⋆−mod} is cartesian.
items.note: Relates the missing 𝔛(p^n,ε) and 𝔛(p^n,ε)^⋆.

items.name: The opens 𝔛(p^n,ε,e_2)^⋆, 𝔛(p^n,ε,e_3)^⋆
items.statement: 𝔛(p^n,ε,e_2)^⋆ and 𝔛(p^n,ε,e_3)^⋆ are the open formal subschemes of 𝔛(p^n,ε)^⋆ where (det ω_G^mod)_ε is generated by HT(e_4)∧HT(e_2), respectively HT(e_4)∧HT(e_3).
items.note: Specific to this paper.

items.name: Lemma 12.9.1.2: 𝔛(p^n,ε,e_i) = 𝔛(p^n)^mod ×_{𝔛(p^n)^{⋆−mod}} 𝔛(p^n,ε,e_i)^⋆
items.statement: For i ∈ {2,3}, the square with 𝔛(p^n,ε,e_i) → 𝔛(p^n)^mod over 𝔛(p^n,ε,e_i)^⋆ → 𝔛(p^n)^{⋆−mod} is cartesian.
items.note: Specific to this paper.

items.name: The model 𝔛(p^n)^{⋆−HT} with ample det ω^mod and sections s_{i,j} (Scholze)
items.statement: There is an integer N such that for all n ≥ N there are a formal scheme 𝔛(p^n)^{⋆−HT} and a projective map 𝔛(p^n)^{⋆−mod} → 𝔛(p^n)^{⋆−HT} such that: (1) 𝔛(p^n)^{⋆−HT} is a normal admissible formal scheme with generic analytic adic fibre 𝒳(p^n)^⋆; (2) det ω_G^mod descends to an ample invertible sheaf det ω_G^mod on 𝔛(p^n)^{⋆−HT}; (3) for every ε > 0 there is n(ε) ≥ N such that for all n ≥ n(ε) there are sections s_{i,j} ∈ H^0(𝔛(p^n)^{⋆−HT}, det ω_G^mod), 1 ≤ i,j ≤ 4, with s_{i,j} = HT(e_i)∧HT(e_j) in det ω_G^mod/p^ε.
items.note: Scholze's construction of the Hodge–Tate period map on the minimal compactification is planned (PerfectoidShimuraVarieties:S1, and S3: 'Construct the extension to the compactification in the precise Hodge-type form provided by the source'), and this finite-level approximation is a step of that proof. As stated here, though, it uses Pilloni–Stroh's 𝔛(p^n)^{⋆−mod} and det ω^mod. Those are missing (modified-det-omega-on-minimal-compactification), so the item is marked missing. External input: [71] P. Scholze, On torsion in the cohomology of locally symmetric varieties, Ann. of Math. 182 (2015), p. 72; see also [63] Pilloni–Stroh, Thm. 1.16

items.name: The formal schemes 𝔛(p^n,ε,e_i)^{⋆−HT}
items.statement: For ε > 0, n ≥ n(ε) and i ∈ {2,3}, 𝔛(p^n,ε,e_i)^{⋆−HT} → 𝔛(p^n)^{⋆−HT} is defined by the conditions s_{i,4} ≠ 0 (s_{i,4} generates det ω_G^mod) and s_{1,j} ∈ p^ε det ω_G^mod for all 1 ≤ j ≤ 4.
items.note: Specific to this paper, and depends on the missing Scholze-model item.

items.name: Lemma 12.9.1.3: 𝔛(p^n,ε,e_i)^{⋆−HT} is affine and 𝔛(p^n,ε,e_i)^⋆ → 𝔛(p^n,ε,e_i)^{⋆−HT} is projective, an isomorphism on generic fibres
items.statement: Let ε > 0, n ≥ n(ε) (and ε ≤ n − 2/(p−1)), i ∈ {2,3}. The formal scheme 𝔛(p^n,ε,e_i)^{⋆−HT} is affine, and the map 𝔛(p^n,ε,e_i)^⋆ → 𝔛(p^n,ε,e_i)^{⋆−HT} [printed with source 𝔛(p^n,ε,e_i)^{⋆−mod}; sourceIssues E102] is projective and an isomorphism on the generic fibre.
items.note: Specific to this paper. Its source is misprinted ^{⋆−mod}, in the statement and in the last line of the proof (sourceIssues E102).

items.name: Small formal Banach sheaf
items.statement: A formal Banach sheaf 𝔉 over an admissible formal scheme 𝔖 is small if 𝔉_1 can be written as an inductive limit colim_{j∈N} 𝔉_{1,j} of coherent sheaves with injective transition maps, and there is a coherent sheaf 𝒢 over 𝔖 such that each quotient 𝔉_{1,j+1}/𝔉_{1,j} is a direct summand of 𝒢.
items.note: Part of AIP [3] Appendix A. No layer plans it; see formal-banach-sheaf. External input: [3] AIP, Ann. of Math. 181 (2015), Appendix A

items.name: Theorem 12.9.2.1 (AIP Thm. A.1.2.2): Čech acyclicity of small Banach sheaves after inverting p
items.statement: Let 𝔖 be an admissible formal scheme admitting a projective map 𝔖 → 𝔖' to an affine admissible formal scheme which is an isomorphism of the associated analytic adic spaces over Spa(C_p,O). Let 𝔉 be a small Banach sheaf over 𝔖 and 𝔘 an affine cover of 𝔖. Then the Čech complex Čech(𝔘,𝔉) ⊗_O C_p is acyclic in positive degrees.
items.note: AdicSpacesPartII:R3 plans 'the affinoid coherent-sheaf equivalence, acyclicity and the comparison needed for finite affinoid covers', but for coherent sheaves only. Nothing covers small Banach sheaves on a formal scheme projective over an affine one with isomorphic generic fibres. External input: [3] AIP, Ann. of Math. 181 (2015), Thm. A.1.2.2

items.name: Proposition 12.9.2.1: R^iπ_⋆ O_{𝔛(p^n,ε)}(−D) = 0 for i ≥ 1
items.statement: Let π : 𝔛(p^n,ε) → 𝔛(p^n,ε)^⋆ be the projection (ε ∈ [0, n − 2/(p−1)] ∩ Q). Then R^iπ_⋆ O_{𝔛(p^n,ε)}(−D) = 0 for all i ≥ 1.
items.note: The analogue of AIP Prop. 8.2.2.4 and Lan's §4. ShimuraCompactifications:C3 leaves higher direct images to 'a separate theorem with the relevant coefficient hypotheses'. CG20 routed its related integral vanishing (ext-pilloni-vanishing-large-parallel-weight) to IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes, a different setting. Here the proof is given only by reference ('One can conclude by repeating the arguments of these papers'); this gap is already recorded.

items.name: Boundary stratification of 𝔛(p^n,ε) and local structure along strata
items.statement: 𝔛(p^n,ε) is stratified by (a subset of) the totally isotropic locally direct factors W of V = Z^4 (printed 'Lagrangian'), based on [63] Prop. 4.9. W = 0: the open dense stratum (complement of D), mapping isomorphically to its image in 𝔛(p^n,ε)^⋆. dim W = 1: from the formal affine modular curve 𝔛_W (prime-to-p level determined by W and K^p) one builds 𝔛_W(p^n) (normal, finite over 𝔛_W, full level p^n), 𝔛_W(p^n)^mod (blow-up and normalization, carrying a locally free modification of the conormal sheaf of the universal elliptic curve) and the one-dimensional affine formal scheme 𝔛_W(p^n,ε) (an open in a blow-up of 𝔛_W(p^n)^mod defined by a Hodge–Tate condition). Over 𝔛_W(p^n,ε) there are an elliptic curve 𝔅_W(p^n,ε) isogenous to the universal one, a G_m-torsor 𝔐_W(p^n,ε) → 𝔅_W(p^n,ε) isogenous to the torsor of trivializations of O(−2O), and a relative toroidal embedding 𝔐_W ↪ 𝔐̄_W (adjoining 0) whose complement maps isomorphically to 𝔅_W. The W-stratum is 𝔅_W(p^n,ε); the completion of 𝔛(p^n,ε) along it is isomorphic to the completion of 𝔐̄_W(p^n,ε) along 𝔅_W(p^n,ε); and π|_{𝔅_W} factors through 𝔅_W → 𝔛_W(p^n,ε) → 𝔛(p^n,ε)^⋆, the last map finite ([63] Lem. 4.4, Thm. 4.7). dim W = 2: the boundary component lies in the ordinary locus, where 𝔛(p^n,ε) → 𝔛(p^n)^mod → 𝔛(p^n) restrict to an open immersion and an isomorphism. By [63] Thm. 4.1 there are a formal torus T_W isogenous to the p-adic completion of Hom(Sym^2(V/W^⊥), G_m), a T_W-torsor 𝔐_W(p^n,ε), a relative toroidal embedding 𝔐_W ↪ 𝔐̄_W, a closed codimension-1 formal subscheme 𝔷_W(p^n,ε) ⊂ 𝔐̄_W ∖ 𝔐_W and an arithmetic subgroup Γ_W ⊂ GL(W). The closed W-stratum is ≅ 𝔷_W/Γ_W, the completion of 𝔛(p^n,ε) along it is ≅ the completion of 𝔐̄_W/Γ_W along 𝔷_W/Γ_W, and the image of 𝔷_W/Γ_W in 𝔛(p^n,ε)^⋆ is a closed formal subscheme finite over Spf O.
items.note: C4 plans 'the formal local description of the universal degeneration' and C5 'their formal completion descriptions', both at good level. Not planned: the strata at level p^n on the ω^mod-modified ε-neighbourhoods (Pilloni–Stroh Prop. 4.9, Thm. 4.1, 4.7). External input: [63] Pilloni–Stroh, Prop. 4.9 (stratification of 𝔛(p^n)^mod), Thm. 4.1 (dim W = 2), Lem. 4.4 and Thm. 4.7 (dim W = 1)

items.name: AIP Prop. A.1.3.1 (as invoked): pushforward of the Banach sheaf to the minimal compactification is small with vanishing higher direct images
items.statement: As invoked in the proof of Lemma 12.9.2.1: combined with Lemma 12.6.2.2 (𝔊^{κ_A,w}/p^w is an inductive limit of extensions of O/p^w on 𝔛(p^n,ε,e_i)) and Prop. 12.9.2.1 (R^iπ_⋆O(−D) = 0, i ≥ 1), [3] Prop. A.1.3.1 gives that π_⋆(𝔊^{κ_A,w} ⊗ ω^r(−D)) is a small formal Banach sheaf over 𝔛(p^n,ε)^⋆ (over the opens 𝔛(p^n,ε,e_i)^⋆) and R^iπ_⋆(𝔊^{κ_A,w} ⊗ ω^r(−D)) = 0 for all i > 0.
items.note: The general proposition, AIP [3] Prop. A.1.3.1, is planned nowhere. Its use here, for π_⋆(𝔊^{κ_A,w} ⊗ ω^r(−D)), depends on the missing Lemma 12.6.2.2 and Prop. 12.9.2.1. External input: [3] AIP, Ann. of Math. 181 (2015), Prop. A.1.3.1

items.name: Lemma 12.9.2.1: RΓ(𝒳(p^n,ε), 𝒢^{κ_A,w} ⊗ ω^r(−D)) is concentrated in degrees 0 and 1
items.statement: Let ε > 0. There exists n(ε) such that for all n ≥ n(ε) (and all w ≤ ε, A ∈ NAdm, κ_A w'-analytic, r ∈ Z), RΓ(𝒳(p^n,ε), 𝒢^{κ_A,w} ⊗ ω^r(−D)) is concentrated in degrees 0 and 1.
items.note: Specific to this paper. A recorded gap: acyclicity on the intersection of the two opens is also needed.

items.name: Corollary 12.9.2.1: C_cusp(n,ε,w,κ_A,r) is concentrated in degrees 0 and 1 for n ≥ n(ε)
items.statement: Let ε > 0. There exists n(ε) such that for all n ≥ n(ε), RΓ(𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), ℱ^{κ_A,w} ⊗ ω^r(−D)) is concentrated in degrees 0 and 1.
items.note: Taking Kli(Z/p^n)-invariants in characteristic 0. Specific to this paper.

items.name: h-slope decomposition (corrected)
items.statement: Let k be a complete non-archimedean extension of Q_p (v(p) = 1), M a k-vector space, U ∈ End_k(M) and h ∈ Q. An h-slope decomposition of M with respect to U is a decomposition M = M^{≤h} ⊕ M^{>h} of k-vector spaces such that: (1) M^{≤h} and M^{>h} are U-stable; (2) M^{≤h} is finite dimensional; (3) all eigenvalues of U on M^{≤h} (in an algebraic closure of k) have valuation ≤ h; (4) for every polynomial Q ∈ k[X] with Q(0) ≠ 0 all of whose roots have valuation ≥ −h (equivalently, whose reciprocal Q^⋆(X) = X^{deg Q} Q(1/X) has all roots of valuation ≤ h), Q^⋆(U) restricted to M^{>h} is invertible. [Printed (4): 'For any polynomial Q with roots of valuation strictly greater than h, the restriction of Q^⋆(U) to M^{>h} is an invertible endomorphism', which is wrong; sourceIssues E107.]
items.note: L4's reviewed decomposition splits a compact operator on a (Pr) module along a factor Q of its Fredholm series. Urban's h-slope decomposition, for an arbitrary endomorphism of a k-vector space, is needed for cohomology groups, which are not Banach; L4 must state it too. The L4 library audit: 'Slope decompositions ... absent'. Condition (4) is printed wrongly (sourceIssues E107); the item uses the corrected form.

items.name: Uniqueness of slope decompositions (Urban Cor. 2.3.3)
items.statement: If an h-slope decomposition of M with respect to U exists, it is unique.
items.note: Uniqueness for arbitrary modules is Urban Cor. 2.3.3. L4 should prove it for the general definition, not only for Buzzard's compact-operator splitting. External input: [81] E. Urban, Eigenvarieties for reductive groups, Ann. of Math. 174 (2011), Cor. 2.3.3

items.name: Slope decomposition for all h; the parts M^{=h}, M^{<h}
items.statement: M has slope decomposition (w.r.t. U) if it has an h-slope decomposition for every h ∈ Q; then the submodules M^{=h} (slope exactly h) and M^{<h} are defined for all h ∈ Q (e.g. M^{=h} = M^{≤h} ∩ M^{>h'} for h' < h close to h, M^{<h} = ∪_{h'<h} M^{≤h'}).
items.note: Derived notions of the h-slope decompositions, with no further mathematics; they belong to L4's slope API.

items.name: Ban(A), projective Banach modules, K^proj(A), compact endomorphisms
items.statement: Let A be a Tate (affinoid) algebra over k. Ban(A) is the category of Banach A-modules; a Banach module is projective if it is a direct factor of an orthonormalizable Banach module. K^proj(A) is the category whose objects are bounded complexes of projective Banach A-modules and whose morphisms are homotopy classes of morphisms of complexes. For M^• ∈ K^proj(A), U ∈ End_{K^proj(A)}(M^•) is compact if it has a representative Ũ ∈ End_A(M^•) whose restriction to each M^k is compact (completely continuous).
items.note: Projective Banach modules and compact maps are planned: L4/projective-banach-modules ('Define property (Pr) by the existence of a Banach complement making P⊕Q potentially orthonormalizable') and L4/compact-matrix-criterion ('compactness in the sense of operator-norm limits of finite-rank maps'). K^proj(A), the bounded complexes up to homotopy, and compactness of a homotopy class are planned nowhere. Mathlib's HomotopyCategory (Algebra/Homology/HomotopyCategory.lean:46) is generic, and Ban(A) is absent. Mathlib's IsCompactOperator (Analysis/Normed/Operator/Compact/Basic.lean:71: some neighbourhood of 0 has relatively compact image) is a different notion. Over C_p any continuous linear map with that property is 0, because O_{C_p}·y is closed and not compact for y ≠ 0.

items.name: Characteristic series P̃(X) = det(1 − XŨ | M^•)
items.statement: For a compact representative Ũ of U on M^• ∈ K^proj(A), the characteristic series P̃(X) := det(1 − XŨ | M^•) := ∏_k det(1 − XŨ | M^k) (product of Fredholm determinants, not alternating) is entire: it defines a function on A^1 × Spa(A,A^+).
items.note: P̃ = ∏_k det(1−XŨ|M^k) equals det(1−X⊕_kŨ^k | ⊕_kM^k) by multiplicativity on direct sums, so it is L4's determinant of a single compact operator. Only the complex framework is missing (projective-banach-modules-Kproj-compact-endomorphism). Mathlib has only the finite-dimensional det(1 − X·M), Matrix.charpolyRev (LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Charpoly/Coeff.lean:291). The L4 audit: 'Neither library has p-adic Fredholm determinants'. External input: [14] R. Coleman, p-adic Banach spaces and families of modular forms, Invent. Math. 127 (1997), Part A; [9] K. Buzzard, Eigenvarieties (2007)

items.name: The spectral variety Z̃ of Ũ and the universal eigenspace complex 𝓜^•
items.statement: Z̃ ↪ A^1 × Spa(A,A^+) is the closed subspace defined by P̃(X); it depends on Ũ. Over Z̃ there is a complex of coherent sheaves 𝓜^•, the universal eigenspace of M^• for Ũ; Z̃ has a covering by opens 𝒰 which are finite over their image 𝒱 in Spa(A,A^+) and such that 𝓜^•|_𝒰 is a perfect complex of O_𝒱-modules.
items.note: Z̃ is L2a's Fredholm hypersurface for ⊕_kŨ^k (node L2a/spectral-hypersurface: 'form Z_φ=V(det(1−Tφ)) inside Sp(R)×A¹_an'). The slope summands are finite projective (L2a/slope-polynomials). Two things are not stated anywhere: the universal eigenspace complex 𝓜^• with its differentials, and its perfectness locally over 𝒱. L2a works with a single module, and its 'coherent eigenmodule sheaf' is still listed as remaining in the reviewed decomposition. External input: [14] Coleman, Part A; [9] Buzzard, Eigenvarieties (Riesz theory and slope factorizations)

items.name: The spectral variety Z = V(ℐ) of (U, M^•)
items.statement: The cohomology groups H^•(𝓜^•) are coherent sheaves on Z̃. Let ℐ ⊂ O_{Z̃} be the annihilator of the graded module H^•(𝓜^•) and Z := V(ℐ) ⊂ Z̃. Z is the spectral variety associated to U and M^•; it does not depend on the choice of Ũ and carries the graded coherent sheaf H^•(𝓜^•).
items.note: The annihilator of H^•(𝓜^•), and the independence of Z from the choice of Ũ, are planned nowhere. This is the complex-level spectral variety.

items.name: Slope decomposition of the fibre cohomology at rank-one points (Serre)
items.statement: Let M^• ∈ K^proj(A) with compact U and x : Spa(K,O_K) → Spa(A,A^+) a rank one point (valuation v_x with v_x(p) = 1). Then each H^i(M^•_x), M^•_x := M^• ⊗̂_A K, has a slope decomposition with respect to U.
items.note: Each M_x^k = M^k ⊗̂_A K is a (Pr) Banach space with compact Ũ, so it has slope decompositions. Since these are unique and functorial, the differentials respect them, and H^i(M_x^•) inherits one. That last step is a one-line corollary that L4 does not state; it belongs next to the complex framework. External input: [72] J-P. Serre, Endomorphismes complètement continus des espaces de Banach p-adiques, Publ. IHES 12 (1962)

items.name: Proposition 13.1.3.1: local constancy of the slope-h Euler characteristic
items.statement: Let M^• ∈ K^proj(A) with compact U. For every h ∈ Q the function x ↦ Σ_i (−1)^i dim_K H^i(M^•_x)^{=h} on rank one points x of Spa(A,A^+) is locally constant: for every rank one point x there is a neighbourhood 𝒰_x of x in Spa(A,A^+) such that for every rank one point y ∈ 𝒰_x, Σ_i (−1)^i dim H^i(M^•_x)^{=h} = Σ_i (−1)^i dim H^i(M^•_y)^{=h}. (The 𝒰_x need not cover Spa(A,A^+).)
items.note: The proof needs two things. (1) Local constancy of dim(M_x^i)^{=h} near a rank-one point (Coleman Part A). L4's 'compatibility with specialization on slope-adapted affinoids' and L2a's slope-adapted affinoids give dim^{≤h}; =h also needs continuity of the roots. (2) Σ(−1)^i dim H^i = Σ(−1)^i dim of the terms, for the finite complex (M_x^•)^{=h}. The Euler-characteristic statement is planned nowhere. Footnote 20: the neighbourhoods 𝒰_x need not cover Spa(A,A^+).

items.name: The Hecke correspondence C at Klingen level p^n (U-operator correspondence)
items.statement: 𝒴_Kli(p^n) ⊂ 𝒳_Kli(p^n) is the open where the semi-abelian scheme is abelian. C|_{𝒴_Kli(p^n)} is the moduli space of triples (G, H_n, L) with (G,H_n) a point of 𝒴_Kli(p^n) and L ⊂ G[p^2] a totally isotropic subgroup, étale locally isomorphic to (Z/pZ)^2 ⊕ Z/p^2Z, with L ∩ H_n = {0}. t_1 : C|_{𝒴_Kli(p^n)} → 𝒴_Kli(p^n), (G,H_n,L) ↦ (G,H_n); t_2 : C|_{𝒴_Kli(p^n)} → 𝒴_Kli(p^{n+1}), (G,H_n,L) ↦ (G/L, ([p]^{-1}(H_n) + L)/L).
items.note: ShimuraVarieties:V1 plans the adelic correspondence ('Construct the Hecke correspondence through K∩gKg⁻¹, with both maps'). The moduli description at Klingen level p^n is not planned: L ⊂ G[p²] totally isotropic, ≅ (Z/p)² ⊕ Z/p², with L ∩ H_n = 0, and t_2(G,H_n,L) = (G/L, ([p]^{-1}H_n + L)/L). CG20's Klingen operators U_{x,i} were also missing. The printed t_1 and t_2 contain misprints (sourceIssues E109).

items.name: Toroidal compactification C_{Σ'} of the correspondence and (t_1)_⋆O_C ≅ R(t_1)_⋆O_C
items.statement: There exist a polyhedral cone decomposition Σ' and a toroidal compactification C = C_{Σ'} of C|_{𝒴_Kli(p^n)} with maps t_1 : C_{Σ'} → 𝒳_Kli(p^n)_Σ and t_2 : C_{Σ'} → 𝒳_Kli(p^{n+1})_Σ extending t_1, t_2. Moreover (t_1)_⋆O_C → R(t_1)_⋆O_C is a quasi-isomorphism.
items.note: The compactification is planned: C3 'For a morphism of data or a Hecke translation, choose compatible source and target fans and construct the extension'. The quasi-isomorphism (t_1)_⋆O_C → R(t_1)_⋆O_C is not. C3 says 'Where higher direct images are required, make their vanishing a separate theorem with the relevant coefficient hypotheses', and names no such theorem. External input: [48] K.-W. Lan, Arithmetic compactifications of PEL-type Shimura varieties, LMS Monographs 36 (2013)

items.name: Lemma 13.2.1.1: C_ε is a correspondence 𝒳_Kli(p^{n+1},ε+1) ← C_ε → 𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε)
items.statement: Let ε ∈ [0, n − 1/(p−1)] ∩ Q and C_ε := C ×_{t_1, 𝒳_Kli(p^n)} 𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε). Then t_2|_{C_ε} factors through 𝒳_Kli(p^{n+1}, ε+1), so C_ε is a correspondence with t_2 : C_ε → 𝒳_Kli(p^{n+1},ε+1) and t_1 : C_ε → 𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε).
items.note: Specific to this paper: the correspondence moves the radius from ε to ε+1.

items.name: The map t_1^⋆ℱℒ → t_2^⋆ℱℒ, Filω_G ↦ (ξ^⋆)^{-1}Filω_G
items.statement: For rational 0 < w ≤ ε: over C_ε, the universal isogeny ξ : G → G_1 has differential ξ^⋆ : ω_{G_1} → ω_G (an isomorphism on the generic fibre), which gives a map t_1^⋆ℱℒ → t_2^⋆ℱℒ, Filω_G ↦ (ξ^⋆)^{-1}Filω_G.
items.note: Uses the ξ^⋆ of the universal isogeny over the missing C_ε. No layer plans it.

items.name: Lemma 13.2.2.1: t_1^⋆ℱℒ_{Kli,n,ε,w} → t_2^⋆ℱℒ_{Kli,n+1,ε+1,w+1}
items.statement: For rational 0 < w ≤ ε, the map t_1^⋆ℱℒ → t_2^⋆ℱℒ restricts to a map t_1^⋆ℱℒ_{Kli,n,ε,w} → t_2^⋆ℱℒ_{Kli,n+1,ε+1,w+1}.
items.note: Specific to this paper. The printed ω-subscripts should be w; this is already recorded.

items.name: Corollary 13.2.2.1: ξ^⋆ : t_2^⋆ℱ^{κ_A,w+1} → t_1^⋆ℱ^{κ_A,w}
items.statement: For rational 0 < w' ≤ w ≤ ε there is a map ξ^⋆ : t_2^⋆ℱ^{κ_A,w+1} → t_1^⋆ℱ^{κ_A,w} over C_ε: for a point Spa(R,R^+) → C_ε with isogeny ξ : G → G_1, (Filω_G, ρ_G : R ≅ Gr(ω_G)) ∈ ℱℒ^+_{Kli,n,ε,w,w'} is sent to ((ξ^⋆)^{-1}Filω_G, (ξ^⋆)^{-1}ρ_G : R ≅ Gr(ω_G) ≅ Gr(ω_{G_1})) ∈ ℱℒ^+_{Kli,n+1,ε+1,w+1,w'}, and for s ∈ t_2^⋆ℱ^{κ_A,w+1}, (ξ^⋆s)(Filω_G, ρ_G) := s((ξ^⋆)^{-1}Filω_G, (ξ^⋆)^{-1}ρ_G).
items.note: Specific to this paper.

items.name: The operator U on C(n,ε,w,κ_A,r) (normalized)
items.statement: U : RΓ(𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), ℱ^{κ_A,w} ⊗ ω^r) → RΓ(𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), ℱ^{κ_A,w} ⊗ ω^r) is the composite of: restriction to RΓ(𝒳_Kli(p^{n+1},ε+1), ℱ^{κ_A,w+1} ⊗ ω^r); pullback by t_2 to RΓ(C_ε, t_2^⋆ℱ^{κ_A,w+1} ⊗ ω^r); (1/p^r)ξ^⋆ to RΓ(C_ε, t_1^⋆ℱ^{κ_A,w} ⊗ ω^r), where ξ^⋆ is the tensor product of the map of Cor. 13.2.2.1 with the natural map t_2^⋆ω^r → t_1^⋆ω^r; the identification with RΓ(𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), (t_1)_⋆t_1^⋆ℱ^{κ_A,w} ⊗ ω^r); and (1/p^3)Tr to RΓ(𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), ℱ^{κ_A,w} ⊗ ω^r). Similarly on cuspidal cohomology.
items.note: Trace along the finite flat t_1 and pull–identify–trace are planned in general (AdicSpacesPartII:R3: 'Construct pull–identify–trace on coefficient sheaves along correspondences'). The normalized U on overconvergent cohomology, with (1/p^r)ξ^⋆ and (1/p^3)Tr, is not.

items.name: Lemma 13.2.4.1: the restriction C(n,ε,w) → C(n+1,ε+1,w+1) is compact
items.statement: The natural map RΓ(𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), ℱ^{κ_A,w} ⊗ ω^r) → RΓ(𝒳_Kli(p^{n+1},ε+1), ℱ^{κ_A,w+1} ⊗ ω^r) is compact (represented by a compact map of Čech complexes); similarly for cuspidal cohomology.
items.note: OverconvergentAutomorphicForms:O6 plans the Hilbert analogue: 'prove the compact restriction theorem for the relevant nested affinoid neighbourhoods, and deduce complete continuity of the controlling operator'. The general principle is named nowhere: restriction along an inclusion of affinoids whose closure lies inside is completely continuous. The proof misprints 𝒳_Kli for 𝒳 in the fibre product and 𝔎𝔩𝔦(Z/p^nZ) for 𝔎𝔩𝔦(Z/p^{n+1}Z) (sourceIssues E111).

items.name: Relatively compact affinoid neighbourhoods (Lütkebohmert Thm. 5.1)
items.statement: As used in the proof of Lemma 13.2.4.1 ([52] = Lütkebohmert, Formal-algebraic and rigid-analytic geometry, Thm. 5.1). All spaces involved are opens of the proper flag variety ℱℒ over 𝒳(p^{n+1}). The closure of ℱℒ_{n+1,ε+1,w+1} lies in 𝒳(p^{n+1}) ×_{𝒳(p^n)} ℱℒ_{n,ε,w}. For each affinoid 𝒰_i of a Kli(Z/p^{n+1}Z)-stable affinoid covering of ℱℒ_{n+1,ε+1,w+1}, [52] Thm. 5.1 gives an affinoid open 𝒰'_i ⊂ 𝒳(p^{n+1}) ×_{𝒳(p^n)} ℱℒ_{n,ε,w} with \bar{𝒰_i} ⊂ 𝒰'_i. Restriction O(𝒰'_i) → O(𝒰_i) is then completely continuous, so the Čech restriction map is compact. The paper does not state the general hypotheses of [52] Thm. 5.1.
items.note: AdicSpacesPartII:R3 plans 'Kiehl-type proper finiteness/coherence', whose proof uses relatively compact affinoid inclusions, but the statement itself is not named. The paper does not reproduce the exact form of [52] Thm. 5.1. External input: [52] W. Lütkebohmert, Formal-algebraic and rigid-analytic geometry, Math. Ann. 286, Thm. 5.1

items.name: Corollary 13.2.4.1: U is compact
items.statement: The operator U on C(n,ε,w,κ_A,r) (and on C_cusp(n,ε,w,κ_A,r)) is compact, i.e. it has a representative on a bounded complex of projective Banach A[1/p]-modules which is compact in each degree.
items.note: Specific to this paper. 'Compact' means completely continuous (L4/compact-matrix-criterion). Mathlib's IsCompactOperator cannot be used over C_p (see projective-banach-modules-Kproj-compact-endomorphism).

items.name: Finite slope classes
items.statement: A class f ∈ H^i(C(n,ε,w,κ_A,r)) is of finite slope for U if, locally on A, there is a polynomial P(X) ∈ A[X] with P(0) = 0 such that f = P(U)f (equivalently (1 − P(U))f = 0 with 1 − P(X) of constant term 1). H^i(…)^{fs} denotes the finite slope classes.
items.note: The general notion is stated nowhere: an element annihilated, locally on A, by a polynomial with constant term 1 in the operator. L4 owns slope theory. The paper's definition is made on H^i of the missing complexes. The printed extension P(Ũ)f should be Ũ(Q(U)f), where P = X·Q (sourceIssues E112).

items.name: Corollary 13.2.4.2: restriction is an isomorphism on finite slope parts
items.statement: For n' ≥ n, ε' ≥ ε, w' ≥ w (all admissible), the restriction map C(n,ε,w,κ_A,r) → C(n',ε',w',κ_A,r) induces an isomorphism on the finite slope parts H^i(…)^{fs} for U; the same holds for cuspidal cohomology. Consequently (Remark 13.2.4.1) finite slope classes in H^i(†,κ_A,r) are identified with classes of any prescribed radius of convergence and analyticity.
items.note: Specific to this paper. PadicFamilies:L2a/linked-banach-families ('A primitive link α:M′→M with compact Hecke-equivariant c ... induces an isomorphism of eigenvarieties') is the module-level analogue.

items.name: Remark 13.2.4.2: U acts compactly on RΓ(𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), Ω^{(k,r)}) and its cuspidal version
items.statement: U acts compactly on RΓ(𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), Ω^{(k,r)}) and on RΓ(𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)), where Ω^{(k,r)} = Sym^k ω_G ⊗ det^r ω_G.
items.note: Specific to this paper: U on (n,ε)-overconvergent cohomology of Ω^{(k,r)}.

items.name: Integral structure ℱ^{κ,w,++}
items.statement: ℱ^{κ,w} is a subsheaf of π_⋆O_{ℱℒ^+_{Kli,n,ε,w,w'}} (printed O_{ℱℒ_{Kli,n,ε,w,w'}}), π : ℱℒ^+_{Kli,n,ε,w,w'} → 𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε). Set ℱ^{κ,w,++} := ℱ^{κ,w} ∩ π_⋆O^{++}_{ℱℒ^+_{Kli,n,ε,w,w'}}, where ++ means topologically nilpotent sections (O^{++}(U) = {f : |f|_x < 1 for all x ∈ U}, §3.1). The proof also uses a lattice ω^{++} ⊂ ω = det ω_G that the paper does not define. Presumably ω^{++} = ω^+ ⊗_{O^+} O^{++}, with ω^+ = det ω_G^+ from integral differentials.
items.note: Specific to this paper. The printed O_{ℱℒ_{Kli,n,ε,w,w'}} should read π_⋆O_{ℱℒ^+_{Kli,n,ε,w,w'}}; this is already recorded.

items.name: Proposition 13.3.1.1 (first part): U has slopes ≥ −3 in all degrees
items.statement: Let κ : Z_p^× → O^× be a w-analytic character and r ∈ Z. On H^i(†,κ,r) and H^i_cusp(†,κ,r), for every i, every slope of U is ≥ −3 (every eigenvalue α of U on a finite slope part has v(α) ≥ −3); the same holds at any finite level H^i(𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), ℱ^{κ,w} ⊗ ω^r) (cuspidal or not).
items.note: Specific to this paper. It uses Lemma 14.3.1(2) and Prop. 14.4.1.1, which are forward references, and Lemma 3.2.2. The gaps in these uses are already recorded.

items.name: Proposition 13.3.1.1 (second part): on degree 0 cohomology U has slopes ≥ 0
items.statement: Let κ : Z_p^× → O^× be a w-analytic character. On H^0(†,κ,r) and H^0_cusp(†,κ,r) every slope of U is ≥ 0.
items.note: Specific to this paper. It depends on the missing p-adic Siegel modular forms (padic-siegel-modular-forms-and-q-expansion-integrality).

items.name: p-adic Siegel modular forms, embedding of H^0(†) and integrality of U on q-expansions
items.statement: As used: H^0(†,κ,r) embeds (by construction, restriction to the ordinary locus) into the module of p-adic modular forms of weight (κ,r) of [60] Def. 4.3 tensored with C_p; p-adic modular forms have a q-expansion map, and the U-operator preserves integrality of q-expansions.
items.note: p-adic modular forms and q-expansions are planned only for modular curves (PadicFamilies:L0: 'Construct p-adic modular forms from the ordinary tower and the corresponding spaces of q-expansions, including the q-expansion principle') and for Hilbert Igusa forms (OverconvergentAutomorphicForms:O7). CG20 proposes Siegel q-expansions and operators at p modulo p^n as SiegelModularFormsModPn. That proposal is not in atlas.json, so it cannot be a planned target. External input: [60] V. Pilloni, Sur la théorie de Hida pour GSp_2g, Bull. SMF 140 (2012), Def. 4.3; [34] H. Hida, Control theorems for coherent sheaves on Shimura varieties of PEL type, J. Inst. Math. Jussieu 1 (2002)

items.name: Lemma 13.3.2.1: canonical map Ω^{(k,r)} → ℱ^{k,w} ⊗ ω^r (classical to overconvergent)
items.statement: For (k,r) ∈ Z_{≥0} × Z there is a canonical (injective) map of sheaves Ω^{(k,r)} → ℱ^{k,w} ⊗ ω^r over 𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), where k denotes the character t ↦ t^k. It induces the natural map RΓ(𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), Ω^{(k,r)}) → RΓ(𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), ℱ^{k,w} ⊗ ω^r) (and its cuspidal version) from (n,ε)-overconvergent cohomology of the classical sheaf to (n,ε)-overconvergent w-analytic cohomology.
items.note: The bundles Ω^{(k,r)} are planned in characteristic 0: AutomorphicBundles:B4 'For Siegel data, identify the Hodge vector bundle, its determinant, and Schur-functor weights'. Their description as the −k-part of functions on ℱℒ^+, and the map into ℱ^{k,w}, are not planned. The proof misprints the source of i as ℱℒ^+_{n,ε,w,w'} instead of ℱℒ^+_{Kli,n,ε,w,w'} [sourceIssues E118].

items.name: ℱ^{k,w^-} and C(n,ε,w^-,k,r)
items.statement: ℱ^{k,w^-} := colim_{w'<w} ℱ^{k,w'} and C(n,ε,w^-,k,r) := colim_{w'<w} C(n,ε,w',k,r).
items.note: A colimit of the missing sheaves and complexes.

items.name: Proposition 13.3.2.1: relative locally analytic BGG exact sequence
items.statement: Let (k,r) be an algebraic weight ((k,r) ∈ Z_{≥0} × Z). Over 𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε) there is an exact sequence 0 → Ω^{(k,r)} →^{d_0} ℱ^{k,w^-} ⊗ ω^r →^{d_1} ℱ^{−2−k,w^-} ⊗ ω^{k+r+1} → 0, with d_0 induced by Lemma 13.3.2.1.
items.note: No layer plans a locally analytic BGG sequence. Tau Ceti LieHighestWeight layer 6 explicitly says 'Do not invoke a full BGG resolution'. The author notes that [3] Prop. 7.2.1 is stated for a fixed w and that the colimit over w' < w is needed. External input: [3] AIP, Ann. of Math. 181 (2015), Prop. 7.2.1 (corrected: [3] states it for a fixed w without the colimit over w' < w, which the author calls a minor error)

items.name: Corollary 13.3.2.1: BGG exact triangle
items.statement: There is an exact triangle RΓ(𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), Ω^{(k,r)}) → C(n,ε,w^-,k,r) → C(n,ε,w^-,−2−k,k+r+1) →^{+1}; similarly for cuspidal cohomology.
items.note: Follows from the missing BGG sequence.

items.name: Proposition 13.3.3.1: equivariance of d_1 for U (corrected factor p^{k+1})
items.statement: With U the normalized operators on RΓ(𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), ℱ^{k,w^-} ⊗ ω^r) and on RΓ(𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), ℱ^{−2−k,w^-} ⊗ ω^{k+r+1}), one has d_1 ∘ U = p^{k+1} U ∘ d_1, i.e. the square with horizontal arrows U (top) and p^{k+1}U (bottom) and vertical arrows d_1 commutes. [Printed bottom arrow: p^{−k−1}U; sourceIssues E119.]
items.note: Checked on the p. 90 image: the bottom arrow is printed p^{−k−1}U. The corrected factor p^{k+1} is recorded as E119, a sign misprint in the exponent.
