The printed square is false, but nothing downstream uses the wrong sign. The correction is consistent with Cor. 13.3.3.1: a slope-a class has d_1-image of slope a−k−1, which is < −3 exactly when a < k−2, and < 0 when a < k+1. External input: [3] AIP, Ann. of Math. 181 (2015), Prop. 7.2.3

items.name: Corollary 13.3.3.1(1): classicality for slope < k − 2 in all degrees
items.statement: For (k,r) ∈ Z_{≥0} × Z and all i, the maps H^i(𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), Ω^{(k,r)})^{<k−2} → H^i(𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), ℱ^{k,w} ⊗ ω^r)^{<k−2} and H^i(𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), Ω^{(k,r)}(−D))^{<k−2} → H^i(𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), ℱ^{k,w} ⊗ ω^r(−D))^{<k−2} (slope parts for U) are isomorphisms.
items.note: Classicality in coherent cohomology is planned nowhere. PadicFamilies:L2 and ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L2 treat modular symbols and modular curves.

items.name: Corollary 13.3.3.1(2): H^0 classicality for slope < k + 1
items.statement: The maps H^0(𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), Ω^{(k,r)})^{<k+1} → H^0(𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), ℱ^{k,w} ⊗ ω^r)^{<k+1} and H^0(𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), Ω^{(k,r)}(−D))^{<k+1} → H^0(𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), ℱ^{k,w} ⊗ ω^r(−D))^{<k+1} are isomorphisms.
items.note: Specific to this paper.

items.name: Corollary 13.3.3.1(3): H^1 injectivity for slope < k + 1
items.statement: The maps H^1(𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), Ω^{(k,r)})^{<k+1} → H^1(𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), ℱ^{k,w} ⊗ ω^r)^{<k+1} and H^1(𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), Ω^{(k,r)}(−D))^{<k+1} → H^1(𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), ℱ^{k,w} ⊗ ω^r(−D))^{<k+1} are injective.
items.note: Specific to this paper.

items.name: Analytic weight space 𝒲, affinoids Spa(A_l[1/p],A_l), universal characters κ_{A_l}
items.statement: 𝒲 := Spa(Λ,Λ) × Spa(C_p,O), Λ = Z_p[[Z_p^×]] the one-dimensional Iwasawa algebra, is the analytic weight space in characteristic zero. 𝒲 is an increasing union of affinoids Spa(A_l[1/p], A_l), and κ_{A_l} : Z_p^× → A_l^× is the universal character. Z_{≥0} ↪ 𝒲 via k ↦ (t ↦ t^k), with the subspace topology (the p-adic topology on each residue class mod p − 1, or mod 2 if p = 2).
items.note: The library audit for L0a finds no rigid weight space in either library, and AUDIT-26 finds no completed group ring. The embedding Z_{≥0} ↪ 𝒲 and its subspace topology (footnote 23) follow from L3's component description.

items.name: The finite slope cuspidal complex C_cusp(A_l) over Spa(A_l[1/p],A_l) × G_m
items.statement: Applying §13.1.2 to C_cusp(n,ε,w,κ_{A_l},2) (n,ε,w large enough) with the compact operator U gives a complex C_cusp(A_l) over Spa(A_l[1/p],A_l) × G_m of finite slope cuspidal overconvergent cohomology of weight (κ_{A_l},2), with cohomology concentrated in degrees 0 and 1; C_cusp(A_l) is independent of (n,ε,w) because U improves convergence and analyticity (Cor. 13.2.4.2, Remark 13.2.4.1).
items.note: The complex version of L2a's machine (missing, source route) applied to the missing Siegel complexes. The input is C_cusp(n,ε,w,κ_{A_l},2) := RΓ(𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), ℱ^{κ_{A_l},w} ⊗ ω²(−D)) (§12.8.1, p. 79). Proposition 12.8.2.1 (p. 79) represents it by a bounded complex of projective Banach A_l[1/p]-modules, which is what the formalism of §13.1.2 requires.

items.name: Fibres of C_cusp(A_l) and eigenspaces of U
items.statement: For κ : Spa(C_p,O) → Spa(A_l[1/p],A_l) and α ∈ C_p^× giving (κ,α^{-1}) : Spa(C_p,O) → Spa(A_l[1/p],A_l) × G_m, the paper asserts H^i((κ,α^{-1})^⋆C_cusp(A_l)) = H^i_cusp(†,κ,2)[U = α] (printed with H^i_cusp(κ,r)).
items.note: Specific to this paper. The printed identity is imprecise and is recorded as a gap. The correct statement uses generalized eigenspaces, and the derived fibre adds Tor terms. Only Euler characteristics are used later.

items.name: The cuspidal spectral variety 𝒵 → 𝒲 and the universal module H^•(C_cusp)
items.statement: The annihilator of H^•(C_cusp(A_l)) is a coherent ideal ℐ_l ⊂ O_{Spa(A_l[1/p],A_l) × G_m}; the associated closed subspace is the spectral variety 𝒵_l, and 𝒵_l → Spa(A_l[1/p],A_l) is quasi-finite and locally finite. For varying l the 𝒵_l glue to 𝒵 → 𝒲, which carries a universal graded coherent module H^•(C_cusp) supported in degrees 0 and 1.
items.note: For modules, gluing over the weight space is planned: L2a 'independence of admissible coverings' and node L2a/global-weight-gluing. For complexes, and for this Siegel instance, it is not.

items.name: Proposition 13.4.1: k ↦ dim H^1_cusp(†,k,2)^{=0} − dim H^0_cusp(†,k,2)^{=0} is locally constant
items.statement: The function on Z_{≥0} ⊂ 𝒲 (subspace topology: p-adic on each residue class mod p − 1, mod 2 if p = 2) given by k ↦ dim_{C_p} H^1_cusp(†,k,2)^{=0} − dim_{C_p} H^0_cusp(†,k,2)^{=0} is locally constant. [Printed dim_ℂ; sourceIssues E117.]
items.note: Follows from the missing spectral variety of the Siegel complexes and the missing Prop. 13.1.3.1. This is the input to the control theorem 14.8.1.

items.name: Klingen analytic Siegel threefold, universal chain G → G′ → G, subgroup H and section δ_H
items.statement:
Notation:
- 𝒳_Kli(p) is the analytic Siegel threefold of Klingen level at p: the analytic adic space over Spa(C, O) of a toroidal compactification (cone decomposition Σ suppressed).
- There is a universal chain of isogenies of semi-abelian schemes G → G′ → G, with G → G′ of degree p^3 and composite multiplication by p.
- H := Ker(G → G′)^⊥, the orthogonal for the Weil pairing. Where G is abelian, H is finite flat of order p.
- G″ := G/H = (G′)^t.
- ω^+_G is the locally free O^+_{𝒳_Kli(p)}-module (of rank 2) of integral differentials at the unit section; similarly ω^+_{G″}.
- δ_H ∈ det ω^+_G ⊗ det^{−1} ω^+_{G″} is the determinant of the map ω^+_{G″} → ω^+_G induced by G → G″.

For a rank-one point x: Spa(K, O_K) → 𝒳_Kli(p) with v_x(p) = 1: if the schematic closure of H_x is a finite flat subgroup scheme of G over Spf O_K (e.g. G has good reduction at x), then v_x(δ_H) = deg H_x ∈ [0, 1] (Fargues degree).

items.name: Neighbourhoods 𝒳_Kli(p)_ε of the locus where H is multiplicative
items.statement:
- For ε ∈ R (in practice ε ∈ [0, 1] ∩ Q), 𝒳_Kli(p)_ε ⊂ 𝒳_Kli(p) is the locus where |δ_H| ≤ |p^ε|. At rank-one points where deg H is defined, this means deg H_x ≥ ε.
- 𝒳_Kli(p)_{ε′} ⊂ 𝒳_Kli(p)_ε when ε′ ≥ ε, and 𝒳_Kli(p)_0 = 𝒳_Kli(p).
- 𝒳_Kli(p)_1 = 𝒳^{≥1}_Kli(p) is the adic space over Spa(C, O) attached to the formal scheme 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p) (p-rank ≥ 1 and H multiplicative).
- This is used as a measure of distance to the p-rank-one locus.
items.locator: §14.1, p. 92; identification with 𝒳^{≥1}_Kli(p) on p. 100 (§14.8)
items.note: AdicSpacesPartII:R2 plans the general mechanism: 'Construct rational subdomains cut out by a section of a line bundle and a valuation bound ... Define fractional p-valuation bounds by valuation ideals'. That gives 𝒳_Kli(p)_ε once δ_H exists. Three things are not planned: the loci themselves, their monotonicity in ε, and the identification 𝒳_Kli(p)_1 = generic fibre of 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p). The last needs the Klingen-level integral model, which no layer plans.

items.name: Lemma 14.1.1 (comparison of 𝒳_Kli(p^n, ε) with 𝒳_Kli(p)_ε)
items.statement:
Setup:
- Let n ≥ 1 and ε ∈ [0, n − 1/(p−1)] ∩ Q.
- 𝒳_Kli(p^n, ε) (§12.7.1) parametrizes pairs (x, H_n), where H_n ⊂ G_x[p^n] is finite flat, étale-locally isomorphic to Z/p^n Z and étale-locally generated by e_1, with HT(e_1) = 0 in ω^{mod,+}_{G_x}/p^ε.

Claim: the natural map 𝒳_Kli(p^n, ε) → 𝒳_Kli(p), (x, H_n) ↦ (x, H_n[p]), factors through
  𝒳_Kli(p)_{max{0, 1 − (2/n)(n − ε + 1/(p−1))}}.

Remark 14.1.1: for ε = n − 1/(p−1) and n → ∞, the index 1 − (2/n)(n − ε + 1/(p−1)) tends to 1.
items.note: The proof uses 𝒳_Kli(p^n, ε) from §12.7.1 (another cluster) and three Fargues inputs: the Hodge–Tate cokernel bound, degree monotonicity and degree duality (the external-fargues-* items, all missing). No layer compares these neighbourhoods.

items.name: Lemma 14.1.2
items.statement: For all ε ≥ 1 − 1/p, 𝒳_Kli(p)_ε ⊂ 𝒳_Kli(p, 1 − 1/(p−1)) as open subspaces of 𝒳_Kli(p) = 𝒳_Kli(p^1). Here 𝒳_Kli(p, ε′) is the level-p space of §12.7.1 with ε′ ∈ [0, 1 − 1/(p−1)].
items.note: The proof is an Oort–Tate computation (external-oort-tate-classification, missing). No layer plans the comparison. External input: Proof by an 'easy computation using Oort–Tate theory' ([58] F. Oort, J. Tate, Group schemes of prime order, Ann. Sci. ENS 3 (1970)).

items.name: Hecke correspondences t_{n,1}, t_{n,2}: C_n → 𝒳_Kli(p)
items.note: ShimuraCompactifications:C3 supplies the toroidal extension: 'For a morphism of data or a Hecke translation, choose compatible source and target fans and construct the extension ... Do not assert that one fixed fan admits every Hecke correspondence' (characteristic 0). Not planned: the moduli description of C_n (L_n totally isotropic, étale-locally (Z/p^n)^2 ⊕ Z/p^{2n}, L_n ∩ H = 0), the maps t_{n,1}, t_{n,2}, and C_n = C_1^{∘n}.

items.name: Section δ_{L_n} and degree deg L_n on C_n
items.statement:
- Over C_n there is an isogeny G → G_n with kernel L_n. Its differential gives (Ω^1_{G_n/C_n})^+ → (Ω^1_{G/C_n})^+, where (·)^+ is the locally free O^+_{C_n}-module of integral differentials.
- δ_{L_n} ∈ det(Ω^1_{G/C_n})^+ ⊗ det^{−1}(Ω^1_{G_n/C_n})^+ is its determinant.
- For a rank-one point x: Spa(K, O_K) → C_n with v_x(p) = 1, set deg L_n|_x := v_x(δ_{L_n}), computed in any local trivialization.
- If G|_x extends to an abelian scheme 𝔊 over Spf O_K, this equals the Fargues degree of the schematic closure of L_n|_x in 𝔊.
- In general G|_x = G^0/(lattice) with G^0 semi-abelian extending to 𝔊^0 over Spf O_K, and deg L_n|_x = deg(L_n|_x ∩ G^0).
items.note: δ_{L_n} is the determinant of the differential of G → G_n on O^+-lattices. The paper compares it with Fargues' degree (missing), including the Raynaud-uniformised boundary case, which uses the ShimuraCompactifications:C4 degeneration data. Neither the definition nor the comparison is planned.

items.name: Lemma 14.3.1(1)
items.statement:
Let x: Spa(K, O_K) → C_1 be a rank-one point corresponding to (G, H, L = L_1). Then
  deg H + deg L[p] ≤ 2.
items.note: The proof uses the generic isomorphism H × L[p] → G[p] and Fargues coro. 3 (external-fargues-degree-monotone-under-generic-isomorphism, missing). No layer plans degree estimates on Hecke correspondences.

items.name: Lemma 14.3.1(2)
items.statement:
In the setting of Lemma 14.3.1 (rank-one point (G, H, L) of C_1):
  deg(L[p]/pL) = 1.
items.note: The proof uses the Weil-pairing self-duality of L[p]/pL, which rests on Lemma 14.3.2 (missing), and deg 𝒢 + deg 𝒢^D = height (missing). Unplanned.

items.name: Lemma 14.3.1(3)
items.statement:
In the setting of Lemma 14.3.1:
  deg(L/L[p]) ≤ deg(pL).
items.note: The proof applies Fargues coro. 3 (missing) to the generic isomorphism p: L/L[p] → pL. Unplanned.

items.name: Lemma 14.3.1(4)
items.statement:
In the setting of Lemma 14.3.1:
  deg((G[p] + L)/L) = 1 − deg(L/L[p]).
items.note: The proof uses the pairing between (G[p]+L)/L and L/L[p] induced by the Weil pairing on G[p^2], together with the degree duality formula (missing). Unplanned.

items.name: Lemma 14.3.1(5)
items.statement:
In the setting of Lemma 14.3.1:
- deg((G[p] + L)/L) ≥ deg H.
- In case of equality, H is of multiplicative or of étale type.
items.note: The proof uses degree monotonicity (missing) and the fact that an order-p direct factor of a truncated BT_1 is étale or multiplicative. FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1–R07.2 do not state that fact. Unplanned.

items.name: Lemma 14.3.2
items.statement:
Let J be a finite flat group scheme over O_K.
- Let M_K ⊂ J_K be a subgroup, with schematic closure M.
- Let M_K^⊥ ⊂ J_K^D be its orthogonal, with schematic closure M^⊥.
Then J^D/M^⊥ = M^D.
items.note: FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.1 plans 'Cartier duality ... finite-flat subgroup and quotient constructions' and states 'Finite-flat closure of a generic subgroup requires a proof under the correct base hypotheses'. It does not plan the compatibility J^D/M^⊥ = M^D of schematic closure with orthogonals. Tau Ceti has Cartier duality over an affine base (tauceti:TauCeti.FiniteLocallyFreeCommAffineGroupSchemeCat.cartierDual, TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AffineGroupScheme/CartierDuality/FiniteLocallyFree.lean:275) but no schematic closures and no orthogonal subgroups.

items.name: Corollary 14.3.1
items.statement:
Let n ≥ 1 and let x: Spa(K, O_K) → C_n be a rank-one point corresponding to (G, H, L_n). Let ε ∈ R and assume deg L_n ≤ n(3 − 2ε). Then
  deg((G[p] + L_n)/L_n) ≥ ε.
items.note: Follows from Lemma 14.3.1 (missing) and additivity of degree along the filtration L_1 ⊂ … ⊂ L_n (missing). Unplanned.

items.name: Corollary 14.3.2 (dynamics of C_1)
items.statement:
Let [a, b] ⊂ ]0, 1[. There exists r(a, b) > 0 such that for all ε ∈ [a, b],
  t_{1,2}(t_{1,1}^{−1}(𝒳_Kli(p)_ε)) ⊂ 𝒳_Kli(p)_{ε + r(a,b)}.
items.note: The proof cites [62] (Pilloni, Duke 157 (2011), Prop. 2.3.6): Lemma 14.3.1(5) plus the maximum principle on quasi-compact subsets of C_1. Neither is planned; the maximum principle on adic spaces is not stated in AdicSpacesPartII. The paper does not prove this result itself. It imports it from [62] (V. Pilloni, Prolongement analytique sur les variétés de Siegel, Duke Math. J. 157 (2011)), Prop. 2.3.6, and adds only the sketch described above. External input: [62] V. Pilloni, Prolongement analytique sur les variétés de Siegel, Duke Math. J. 157 (2011), Prop. 2.3.6.

items.name: Proposition 14.4.1.1(1) (acyclicity under change of cone decomposition)
items.statement:
Let Σ and Σ′ be smooth polyhedral cone decompositions, with Σ′ refining Σ (implicit), and let π_{Σ′,Σ}: 𝒳_Kli(p)_{Σ′} → 𝒳_Kli(p)_Σ. Then:
- R(π_{Σ′,Σ})_* O_{𝒳_Kli(p)_{Σ′}} = O_{𝒳_Kli(p)_Σ};
- R(π_{Σ′,Σ})_* O^{++}_{𝒳_Kli(p)_{Σ′}} = O^{++}_{𝒳_Kli(p)_Σ}.
Here O^{++} is the sheaf of topologically nilpotent functions (§3.1).
items.note: ShimuraCompactifications:C3 plans 'Prove the structure-sheaf pushforward and the normality statements used to compare sections under refinements. Where higher direct images are required, make their vanishing a separate theorem with the relevant coefficient hypotheses.' That is algebraic and in characteristic 0. With GAGA (AdicSpacesPartII:R1) it would give the O-statement on analytifications. The O^{++} statement on the analytic toroidal compactifications is not planned; it goes through the paper's §3 toric computations (Props. 3.3.1, 3.4.1). PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20 likewise marked Rf_*O = O for refinements missing.

items.name: Proposition 14.4.1.1(2) (acyclicity of t_{n,1})
items.note: The proof factors t_{n,1} through a non-smooth toroidal model C_{n,Σ}, followed by a finite map, and handles the O^{++} version as in part (1). ShimuraCompactifications:C3 plans Hecke extensions for compatible fans but not this acyclicity.

items.name: Classical sheaves F = Ω^{(k,r)}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D) and their integral structures F^+, F^{++}
items.statement:
- F denotes either Ω^{(k,r)} = Sym^k ω_G ⊗ det^r ω_G or its cuspidal twist Ω^{(k,r)}(−D) on 𝒳_Kli(p), with (k, r) ∈ Z_{≥0} × Z_{≥0}.
- F^+ is the integral structure Sym^k ω^+_G ⊗ det^r ω^+_G (twisted by the ideal of D in the cuspidal case), a locally free O^+-module with F = F^+ ⊗_{O^+} O.
- F^{++} = F^+ ⊗_{O^+} O^{++}, the topologically nilpotent sections.
- Since pF^+ ⊂ F^{++} ⊂ F^+, the pro-systems (F/p^n F^+)_n and (F/p^n F^{++})_n are isomorphic.
items.note: The algebraic bundles are planned: AutomorphicBundles:B4 ('For Siegel data, identify the Hodge vector bundle, its determinant, and Schur-functor weights') and B3 (subcanonical extension 𝒱^can(−D)), with analytification in AdicSpacesPartII:R1. The O^+-lattices F^+ on the analytic Klingen-level space, F^{++} = F^+ ⊗ O^{++}, and the pro-system comparison are not planned.

items.name: Normalized cohomological correspondence U^n on F and F^{++}
items.statement:
Let F ∈ {Ω^{(k,r)}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)}.
- The analytification of the algebraic cohomological correspondence gives an unnormalized map (t_{n,1})_* t_{n,2}^* F → F.
- U^n is this map divided by p^{n(3+r)}, consistent with §10.4.
- Restricted to F^{++}, U^n gives (t_{n,1})_* t_{n,2}^* F^{++} → p^{−3n} F^{++}. The factor p^{−3n} instead of p^{−3n−nr} comes from deg L_n ≥ n: each of the n steps has degree ≥ 1 by Lemma 14.3.1(2); the paper prints 'at least one'.
- On cohomology this gives U^n: RΓ(𝒳_Kli(p), F) → RΓ(𝒳_Kli(p), F) and U^n: RΓ(𝒳_Kli(p), F^{++}) → RΓ(𝒳_Kli(p), p^{−3n} F^{++}), using Prop. 14.4.1.1(2).
- U^n is the n-th iterate of U = U^1.
items.note: Related plans exist. AdicSpacesPartII:R3: 'Construct pull–identify–trace on coefficient sheaves along correspondences'. AutomorphicBundles:B5 plans Hecke traces on sections with 'all scalar normalizations'. Not planned: the analytic correspondence on C_n, the normalisation p^{−n(3+r)}, the integrality U^n(F^{++}) ⊂ p^{−3n}F^{++}, and the action on RΓ.

items.name: Maps U^n_{ε,ε′} and res_{ε,ε′}
items.statement:
- If t_{n,2} t_{n,1}^{−1}(𝒳_Kli(p)_{ε′}) ⊂ 𝒳_Kli(p)_ε, the correspondence defines
  U^n_{ε,ε′}: RΓ(𝒳_Kli(p)_ε, F) → RΓ(𝒳_Kli(p)_{ε′}, F).
- If ε′ ≥ ε, restriction along 𝒳_Kli(p)_{ε′} ⊂ 𝒳_Kli(p)_ε gives res_{ε,ε′}: RΓ(𝒳_Kli(p)_ε, F) → RΓ(𝒳_Kli(p)_{ε′}, F).
- Whenever defined: U^n_{ε,ε′} ∘ res_{ε″,ε} = U^n_{ε″,ε′} and res_{ε′,ε″} ∘ U^n_{ε,ε′} = U^n_{ε,ε″}.
- By Lemma 14.3.1(5), U = U^1_{ε,ε} is an endomorphism of RΓ(𝒳_Kli(p)_ε, F).
items.note: Unplanned. OverconvergentAutomorphicForms:O6 plans 'the domain/radius changes and all normalizing factors' only for Hilbert U_p on sections, not for Siegel coherent cohomology.

items.name: Proposition 14.5.1 (analytic continuation of eigenclasses)
items.note: Analytic continuation of U-eigenclasses in higher coherent cohomology of Siegel threefolds is planned nowhere. The proof uses Cor. 14.3.2 (missing).

items.name: Proposition 14.5.2 (analytic continuation of finite-slope classes)
items.note: Unplanned. This is a direct refinement of Prop. 14.5.1 (missing).

items.name: Remark 14.5.1 (finite-slope classes on 𝒳_Kli(p^n, ε) vs 𝒳_Kli(p)_{ε′})
items.statement: Let n ≥ 1, ε ∈ ]0, n − 1/(p−1)] ∩ Q and ε′ ∈ ]0,1[, and let F ∈ {Ω^{(k,r)}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)}. By Lemmas 14.1.1 and 14.1.2, Cor. 13.2.4.2 and Prop. 14.5.2, finite-slope classes in H^i(𝒳_Kli(p^n, ε), F) are identified with finite-slope classes in H^i(𝒳_Kli(p)_{ε′}, F). This covers the cuspidal case F = Ω^{(k,r)}(−D). (Printed: 'for any ε′ > 0'. The restriction ε′ < 1 is needed.)
items.note: Combines Lemmas 14.1.1–14.1.2, Cor. 13.2.4.2 (another cluster) and Prop. 14.5.2, all unplanned.

items.name: Notation 𝒢|_{𝒳_Kli(p)_ε} := j_* j^* 𝒢
items.statement: Let j: 𝒳_Kli(p)_ε ↪ 𝒳_Kli(p) be the open inclusion. In §14.6, for a sheaf 𝒢 on 𝒳_Kli(p), 𝒢|_{𝒳_Kli(p)_ε} denotes j_* j^* 𝒢.
items.note: Only the notation is library. The spaces 𝒳_Kli(p)_ε ⊂ 𝒳_Kli(p) are the missing items above.

items.name: Lemma 14.6.1 (divisibility of the differential of G → G/L_n)
items.note: The statement is about the differential of G → G/L_n at a point of C_n, via a diagonalised map of rank-2 O_K-lattices. Unplanned.

items.name: Proposition 14.6.1 (U^n_{ε,0} with torsion coefficients)
items.note: Unplanned. The proof uses Lemma 14.6.1, Cor. 14.3.1 and the finiteness of t_{n,1} away from the boundary, all specific to this paper.

items.name: Remark 14.6.1 (U on lim_n H^i(𝒳_Kli(p), F/p^n F^{++}))
items.statement:
- U = U^1 maps F^{++} into p^{−3} F^{++}, so it induces maps H^i(𝒳_Kli(p), F/p^n F^{++}) → H^i(𝒳_Kli(p), F/p^{n−3} F^{++}).
- Hence U acts on lim_n H^i(𝒳_Kli(p), F/p^n F^{++}).
items.note: Unplanned. It needs normalized U^n on F^{++} (missing).

items.name: Corollary 14.6.1
items.note: Unplanned. The proof also uses that 𝒳_Kli(p)_ε ↪ 𝒳_Kli(p) is an affine morphism, which no layer states.

items.name: Corollary 14.6.2
items.note: Unplanned. This is a polynomial variant of Cor. 14.6.1 (missing).

items.name: Lemma 14.7.1
items.statement:
Let ε ∈ ]0, 1[ (implicit), F ∈ {Ω^{(k,r)}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)} with integral structure F^+, i ≥ 0 and h ∈ Q.
- U = U_{ε′,ε} ∘ res_{ε,ε′} (for suitable ε′ > ε) is compact on RΓ(𝒳_Kli(p)_ε, F), so H^i(𝒳_Kli(p)_ε, F) has an h-slope decomposition.
- The natural map H^i(𝒳_Kli(p)_ε, F)^{≤h} → lim_n H^i(𝒳_Kli(p)_ε, F/p^n F^+) is injective.
items.note: LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L4 plans slope decompositions for compact operators ('slope decompositions'; nodes L4/riesz-root-projectors and L4/finite-slope-summands), but only on (Pr) Banach modules. Not planned: the Čech-complex slope decomposition on 𝒳_Kli(p)_ε and the boundedness argument, which uses the paper's Lemma 3.2.2 (another cluster).

items.name: Theorem 14.7.1 (small-slope classes on 𝒳_Kli(p)_ε are classical)
Corollary 14.7.1(1)
items.statement:
Let (k, r) ∈ Z_{≥0} × Z_{≥0} and i ≥ 0. The natural map
  H^i(𝒳_Kli(p), Ω^{(k,r)})^{<min{k+2r−3, k−2}} → H^i(†, k, r)^{<min{k+2r−3, k−2}}
is an isomorphism, and likewise H^i(𝒳_Kli(p), Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) → H^i_cusp(†, k, r) on the same slope range.

The map is restriction to 𝒳_Kli(p^n, ε) followed by Ω^{(k,r)} → F^{k,w} ⊗ ω^r (Lemma 13.3.2.1). Here H^i(†, k, r) = colim_{n,ε,w} H^i(𝒳_Kli(p^n, ε), F^{k,w} ⊗ ω^r).
items.note: Combines Thm 14.7.1 with Cor. 13.3.3.1 and the map Ω^{(k,r)} → F^{k,w} ⊗ ω^r of Lemma 13.3.2.1 (both in another cluster). Unplanned.

items.name: Corollary 14.7.1(2)
items.note: Unplanned; it has the same inputs as part (1).

items.name: Corollary 14.7.1(3)
items.note: Unplanned; it has the same inputs as part (1).

items.name: Ordinary projector f for U; the spaces X_Kli(p), 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p), 𝒳^{≥1}_Kli(p)
items.statement:
- X_Kli(p) is the toroidal compactification over Z_p of the Siegel threefold of Klingen level at p (tame level K^p), with boundary divisor D.
- 𝔛_Kli(p) is its p-adic formal completion. 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p) ⊂ 𝔛_Kli(p) is the open formal subscheme where the p-rank is ≥ 1 and the universal order-p subgroup H is multiplicative: the non-vanishing locus of det ω_G → det ω_{G′}.
- 𝒳^{≥1}_Kli(p) is the adic space over Spa(C, O) attached to 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p); it equals 𝒳_Kli(p)_1.
- f is the ordinary projector attached to U: U is locally finite (Theorem 11.3.1), and f is defined as in §2.3.
items.note:
PadicFamilies:L0a plans the group-independent projector ('Apply the result degreewise to finite perfect/cohomological complexes with commuting U and differential'). f itself is 'defined as in §2.3' (another cluster). Not planned:
- the Klingen-level integral toroidal model X_Kli(p) over Z_p. ShimuraCompactifications:C5 works at good primes only, and PELModuli:M4 plans only normalizations 'At arbitrary higher p-level'.
- 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p), as the non-vanishing locus of det ω_G → det ω_{G′};
- local finiteness of U (Theorem 11.3.1).

items.name: Theorem 14.8.1 (classicality of ordinary cohomology)
items.statement:
For all k ≥ 0, the natural (restriction) map
  f RΓ(X_Kli(p), Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) ⊗^L_{Z_p} Q_p → f RΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p), Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) ⊗^L_{Z_p} Q_p
is an isomorphism.
items.note: This is a main result of §14 (classicality of ordinary higher Hida cohomology in weight (k,2)). No layer plans it.

items.name: Lemma 14.8.1(1)
items.statement: f RΓ(X_Kli(p), Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) ⊗^L_{Z_p} C ≃ f RΓ(𝒳_Kli(p), Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)), where 𝒳_Kli(p) is the analytic adic space over Spa(C, O).
items.note: GAGA is planned (AdicSpacesPartII:R1; see external-scholze-comparison-GAGA). Not planned: flat base change Z_p → C for RΓ(X_Kli(p), ·), compatibility of U with analytification, and passage to f. External input: The GAGA theorem 'stated in [69], thm. 9.1' (Scholze). The same comparison is cited as [70], thm. 9.1 in §3.4 (see mistakes).

items.name: Lemma 14.8.1(2)
items.note: The generic-fibre functor is planned (AdicSpacesPartII:R2 'the adic generic-fibre functor'; reviewed node R2/generic-fibre-functor-d). The comparison of the cohomology of the formal scheme 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p), after ⊗^L C and f, with that of its generic fibre is not planned.

items.name: Remark 14.8.1 (0-slope decomposition on 𝒳^{≥1}_Kli(p))
items.note: Unplanned. It uses the §13.1.1 0-slope decomposition (another cluster) and f (missing).

items.name: Two-affine covering of the p-rank ≥ 1 locus; Čech complex and its overconvergent subcomplex
items.statement:
Covering of the minimal compactification:
- X^⋆ → Spec Z_p is the minimal compactification with spherical level at p, and X^⋆_Kli(p) the one with Klingen level. 𝔛^⋆ and 𝔛^⋆_Kli(p) are their formal completions.
- For n large, Ha(G)^{n(p+1)} (first Hasse invariant, defined on V(p)) and Ha′(G)^n (second Hasse invariant, defined on V(p, Ha(G))) lift non-canonically to sections s_1, s_2 of the ample sheaf (det ω_G)^{n(p²−1)} over 𝔛^⋆. Their non-vanishing locus is 𝔛^{⋆,≥1}, so 𝔛^{⋆,≥1} = D(s_1) ∪ D(s_2) is a union of two affines.
- 𝔛^⋆_Kli(p) ×_{𝔛^⋆} 𝔛^{⋆,≥1} → 𝔛^{⋆,≥1} is proper and quasi-finite, hence affine.
- det ω_G → det ω_{G′} descends to 𝔛^⋆_Kli(p). Its non-vanishing locus 𝔛^{⋆,≥1}_Kli(p) has inverse image 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p) in 𝔛_Kli(p). The open immersion 𝔛^{⋆,≥1}_Kli(p) ↪ 𝔛^⋆_Kli(p) is affine and factors through 𝔛^⋆_Kli(p) ×_{𝔛^⋆} 𝔛^{⋆,≥1}. Hence 𝔛^{⋆,≥1}_Kli(p) = 𝔙_1 ∪ 𝔙_2 with 𝔙_i affine.

Analytic Čech complex:
- 𝒳^⋆_Kli(p) is the adic space over Spa(C,O) attached to 𝔛^⋆_Kli(p). V_i ⊂ 𝒳^⋆_Kli(p) are the inverse images of 𝔙_i, and 𝒳^{⋆,≥1}_Kli(p) := V_1 ∪ V_2. π: 𝒳_Kli(p) → 𝒳^⋆_Kli(p) is the projection, U_i = π^{−1}V_i, and 𝒳^{≥1}_Kli(p) = π^{−1}(𝒳^{⋆,≥1}_Kli(p)) = U_1 ∪ U_2.
- Rπ_*Ω^{(k,2)}(−D) = π_*Ω^{(k,2)}(−D) ([50], thm. 8.9). So RΓ(𝒳^{≥1}_Kli(p), Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) is represented by H^0(U_1,·) ⊕ H^0(U_2,·) → H^0(U_1 ∩ U_2,·), and fRΓ(𝒳^{≥1}_Kli(p), ·) is concentrated in degrees 0 and 1.
- The subcomplex H^0(U_1, Ω^{(k,2),†}(−D)) ⊕ H^0(U_2, Ω^{(k,2),†}(−D)) → H^0(U_1 ∩ U_2, Ω^{(k,2),†}(−D)) of overconvergent sections computes colim_{ε<1} H^i(𝒳_Kli(p)_ε, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)). (The paper does not define Ω^{(k,2),†} formally. As its phrase 'overconvergent sections' indicates, H^0(W, Ω^{(k,2),†}(−D)) is the colimit of H^0(W′, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) over strict neighbourhoods W′ of W, which can be taken inside 𝒳_Kli(p)_ε with ε → 1. With this reading the claim follows by a routine colimit argument.)
- H^1(𝒳^{≥1}_Kli(p), ·) carries the quotient topology from H^0(U_1 ∩ U_2, ·). An open bounded submodule is the image of H^i(𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p), Ω^{(k,2)}(−D) ⊗̂_{Z_p} O) with its p-adic topology; this module is p-adically complete but not necessarily separated (footnote 25).

items.name: Lemma 14.8.2(a)
items.statement: For every k ≥ 0 and ε ∈ ]0, 1[ ∩ Q, the complexes f RΓ(𝒳_Kli(p)_ε, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) and f RΓ(𝒳^{≥1}_Kli(p), Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) have cohomology only in degrees 0 and 1.
items.note: Unplanned. Footnote 24 notes an alternative proof via Thm 11.3.1(2) and Prop. 12.9.1 (both in another cluster).

items.name: Lemma 14.8.2(b)
items.note: Unplanned. The proof uses density of the overconvergent subcomplex and finite-dimensionality of the ordinary part.

items.name: Dimension functions d_i(k), d_i^†(k), d_i^{†,′}(k)
items.locator: §14.8, p. 102 (d_i^{†,′} in the proof of Lemma 14.8.4)
items.note: These are definitions on top of the missing ordinary and overconvergent cohomology. They are well defined only after Thm 14.7.1 and Prop. 14.5.2. Unplanned.

items.name: Lemma 14.8.3 (inequalities)
items.note: Immediate from Lemma 14.8.2(b) (missing). Unplanned.

items.name: Lemma 14.8.3 (equality for k large)
items.statement: For k large enough, d_i(k) = d_i^†(k) for i = 0, 1.

items.name: Lemma 14.8.4
items.statement: For all k ≥ 0 and i ∈ {0, 1}, d_i(k) = d_i^†(k). Moreover d_i^{†,′}(k) = d_i(k).
items.note: The proof is a local constancy argument from Theorem 11.3.1 and Prop. 13.4.1, together with Cor. 13.3.3.1 and Lemma 14.8.3. All are unplanned.

items.name: Hecke operators T_{p,2} and U_{Kli(p),2} on weight-(k,2) coherent cohomology
items.statement:
- T_{p,2} is the Hecke operator of the double coset GSp4(Z_p) diag(p,p,1,1) GSp4(Z_p) (§5.1.3). It is realized by a toroidal Hecke correspondence p_1: C_{p,2,Σ″} → X_Σ, p_2: C_{p,2,Σ″} → X_{Σ′} ([18], p. 253; take Σ = Σ″). C_{p,2} parametrizes isogenies p_1^*G → p_2^*G whose kernel, away from the boundary, is a totally isotropic subgroup of order p² of p_1^*G[p].
- On the p-rank ≥ 1 locus, T′_{p,2} = Tr_{p_1} ∘ (differential p_2^*Ω^{(k,2)}(−D) → p_1^*Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) and T_{p,2} = p^{−3}T′_{p,2}.
- U_{Kli(p),2} is the Hecke operator of Kli(p) diag(p,p,1,1) Kli(p) (§5.1.4), with the same normalization p^{−3}.
- They act on H^i(X, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p and H^i(X_Kli(p), Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p respectively, where X is the spherical-level toroidal compactification over Z_p.
- For spherical π_p with Hecke parameters (α,β,γ,δ), αδ = βγ, T_{p,2} acts on π_p^{GSp4(Z_p)} by α+β+γ+δ (Lemma 5.1.5.1).
- If π_p is generic spherical, π_p^{Kli(p)} is 4-dimensional and the eigenvalues of U_{Kli(p),2} on it are the Weyl orbit of α+β (Prop. 5.1.5.1).
- For general π_p with π_p^{Kli(p)} ≠ 0, the Hecke parameters are defined (§5.1.5) so that some eigenvector in π_p^{Kli(p)} has U_{Kli(p),2}-eigenvalue α+β.
items.note: AutomorphicBundles:B5 plans 'Construct pullback, coefficient identification, and trace along Hecke correspondences. State all scalar normalizations', but only on sections in characteristic 0: PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18 notes that B3–B5 'are statements about sections in characteristic zero'. ShimuraCompactifications:C3 supplies the characteristic-0 toroidal correspondence. Not planned: the operators on H^i for i > 0, the normalisation p^{−3}, and the Klingen-level U_{Kli(p),2}. The eigenvalue descriptions come from §5.1.5 (another cluster), and the Satake transform from SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.4. PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18 and PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20 route coherent Hecke operators in all degrees (hecke-operators-T-x-i) to the proposed IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes. In characteristic 0, the operators at p are the same pull–identify–trace construction.

items.name: Proposition 14.9.1 (integrality of Hecke eigenvalues)
items.note: Unplanned. Printed: 'only have eigenvalues of positive p-adic valuation'. The proof, which rules out v(α) < 0, gives valuation ≥ 0, as the item states. The proof uses Lemmas 14.9.1 and 14.9.2.

items.name: Corollary 14.9.1 (valuations of Hecke parameters of ordinary classes)
items.statement:
Assume k ≥ 1. Let π_p be an irreducible smooth admissible representation of GSp4(Q_p) contributing to either:
- e H^i(X, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) ⊗ C (e = ordinary projector of T), or
- f H^i(X_Kli(p), Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) ⊗ C (f = ordinary projector of U), with i ∈ {0, 1}.
Then its Hecke parameters (α, β, γ, δ) (§5.1.5, αδ = βγ) have p-adic valuations (0, 0, k+1, k+1) in a suitable order. In the Klingen case this holds for all k ≥ 0.
items.note: Unplanned. It needs a Newton-polygon computation with the GSp4 spin Hecke polynomial. IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.3 plans only the GL_n polynomial ('Do not assert this GL_n polynomial for a general reductive group without choosing a representation of its L-group'); PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20 routed the GSp4 spin polynomial to IHG.3 as a source.

items.name: Ideal sheaf I = det ω_G ⊗ det ω_{G′}^{−1}; formal loci 𝔛^{≥1}, (𝔛_Kli(p))^{≥1}
items.statement:
- Over X_Kli(p), with the chain G → G′ → G, the differential of the second isogeny gives det ω_G → det ω_{G′}.
- I := det ω_G ⊗ det ω_{G′}^{−1}, identified via this section with an invertible ideal sheaf of O_{𝔛_Kli(p)}.
- I defines a Cartier divisor supported in the special fibre, whose complement in the special fibre is X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_1 (p-rank ≥ 1 and H multiplicative).
- 𝔛^{≥1} is the p-rank ≥ 1 open of the formal completion 𝔛 of X.
- (𝔛_Kli(p))^{≥1} is the p-rank ≥ 1 open of 𝔛_Kli(p); it strictly contains 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p).
- Remark 14.9.2: Ω^{(k,2)}(−D) ⊗ I^{−3} is an integral structure on Ω^{(k,2)}(−D) ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p.

items.name: Lemma 14.9.1(a) (T_{p,2} is integral on 𝔛^{≥1})
items.statement:
For k ≥ 0, T_{p,2} = p^{−3} T′_{p,2} acts on RΓ(𝔛^{≥1}, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)). Precisely:
- p_1: (ℭ_{p,2})^{≥1} → 𝔛^{≥1} is finite and generically étale, and 𝔛^{≥1} is smooth hence normal, so there is a trace Tr_{p_1}: (p_1)_* O_{(ℭ_{p,2})^{≥1}} → O_{𝔛^{≥1}}.
- T′_{p,2}: (p_1)_* p_2^* Ω^{(k,2)}(−D) → Ω^{(k,2)}(−D) factors through p^3 Ω^{(k,2)}(−D).
items.note: Unplanned. PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20 needs the H^0, mod ϖ^m case of the same construction (item hecke-at-p-via-almost-ordinary-locus-and-hartogs, routed to the proposed SiegelModularFormsModPn). Its note lists as unplanned 'the Siegel and Klingen parahoric-level Hecke correspondences at p over O/ϖ^m, finite over the p-rank ≥ 1 locus' and cites Pilloni (Crelle 2012) as an alternative source. The all-degree integral action proved here is the most general form, so it should have one owner. The proof uses the Serre–Tate computations (missing) and the trace for a finite, generically étale map to a normal formal scheme (AdicSpacesPartII:R3 plans traces 'for finite locally free algebras and finite étale analytic maps' only).

items.name: Lemma 14.9.1(b) (U_{Kli(p),2} is integral on (𝔛_Kli(p))^{≥1} after twisting by I^{−3})
items.statement:
For k ≥ 0, U_{Kli(p),2} acts on RΓ((𝔛_Kli(p))^{≥1}, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D) ⊗ I^{−3}). Precisely, the map
  U′_{Kli(p),2}: (p_1)_* p_2^* (Ω^{(k,2)}(−D) ⊗ I^{−3}) → Ω^{(k,2)}(−D) ⊗ I^{−3},
built from Tr_{p_1}, the differential and Lemma 14.9.2.1, factors through p^3 Ω^{(k,2)}(−D) ⊗ I^{−3}. So U_{Kli(p),2} = p^{−3} U′_{Kli(p),2} is integral.
items.note: Unplanned. This Klingen-level integral action with the I^{−3} twist is specific to this paper.

items.name: Lemma 14.9.2 (extension from the p-rank ≥ 1 locus)
items.statement:
For n ∈ Z_{≥0} ∪ {∞} (with p^∞ = 0), the restriction maps
- H^i(X, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)/p^n) → H^i(𝔛^{≥1}, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)/p^n), and
- H^i(X_Kli(p), Ω^{(k,2)}(−D) ⊗ I^{−3}/p^n) → H^i((𝔛_Kli(p))^{≥1}, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D) ⊗ I^{−3}/p^n)
are isomorphisms for i = 0 and injective for i = 1.
items.note: The statement applies the SGA 2 depth extension (external-sga2-depth-extension, missing), using two further inputs that no layer plans: Cohen–Macaulayness of X and X_Kli(p), and codimension 2 of the complement of the p-rank ≥ 1 locus. The spherical H^0 case overlaps PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20's Hartogs step (routed to SiegelModularFormsModPn). The Klingen part with I^{−3} belongs with the higher Hida theory. External input: [SGA2] A. Grothendieck, SGA 2, exposé III, §3 (depth and local cohomology).

items.name: Integral model (𝔈_{p,2})^{≥1} of the U_{Kli(p),2}-correspondence
items.statement:
- (𝔇_{p,2})^{≥1} := (ℭ_{p,2})^{≥1} ×_{𝔛^{≥1}, p_1} (𝔛_Kli(p))^{≥1}, with analytic generic fibre (𝒟_{p,2})^{≥1} over Spa(Q_p, Z_p).
- Over it there is an isogeny p_1^*G → p_2^*G and the universal chain G → (G′)^t → G′ → G, of degrees p, p^2, p, composing to multiplication by p. H := Ker(G → (G′)^t).
- (ℰ_{p,2})^{≥1} is the union of the components of (𝒟_{p,2})^{≥1} on which the kernel of p_1^*G → p_2^*G meets H trivially, generically (away from the boundary).
- (𝔈_{p,2})^{≥1} → (𝔇_{p,2})^{≥1} is the normalization of the closure of (ℰ_{p,2})^{≥1}.
- p_2 lifts on the generic fibre to (ℰ_{p,2})^{≥1} → (𝒳_Kli(p))^{≥1}, equipping p_2^*G with the image of H. By normality it extends to p_2: (𝔈_{p,2})^{≥1} → (𝔛_Kli(p))^{≥1}.
- p_1 is finite and generically étale and (𝔛_Kli(p))^{≥1} is normal, so there is a trace Tr_{p_1}: (p_1)_* O_{(𝔈_{p,2})^{≥1}} → O_{(𝔛_Kli(p))^{≥1}}. There is also a differential p_2^* Ω^{(k,2)} → p_1^* Ω^{(k,2)}.
items.note: Unplanned. The construction uses selection of components, normalization of the closure, extension of p_2 by normality, and the trace for finite, generically étale maps to a normal base. AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.5 plans 'normalisation, schematic closure and descent of finite correspondences' generically, but not this model.

items.name: Lemma 14.9.2.1
items.statement: Over (𝔈_{p,2})^{≥1} there is a natural morphism p_2^* I^{−1} → p_1^* I^{−1}.
items.note: Unplanned. The proof uses the Fargues inverse-different identification (missing) and Stroh's boundary extension of H (missing).

items.name: Remark 14.9.3 (the map p_2^*I^{−1} → p_1^*I^{−1} at ordinary points)
items.note: Unplanned. Case 3 cites Fargues prop. 2, p. 11 (missing). External input: Case 3 cites [20] L. Fargues, J. reine angew. Math. 645 (2010), prop. 2 on p. 11.

items.name: Fargues' degree of a finite flat group scheme (with additivity)
items.statement:
- Let K be a complete valued extension of Q_p with v(p) = 1, and 𝒢 a finite flat group scheme over O_K with ω_𝒢 ≅ ⊕ O_K/a_i. Then deg 𝒢 := Σ v(a_i).
- If 𝒢 has order p^h, then 0 ≤ deg 𝒢 ≤ h.
- deg is additive in short exact sequences of finite flat group schemes. This is used as 'elementary properties of the degree map', e.g. deg L = deg pL + deg L[p]/pL + deg L/L[p].
items.note: No layer defines the degree of a finite flat group scheme over O_K, for K complete and possibly non-discretely valued, or its additivity. HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T0 is the natural owner: it plans to 'Extend that same API to the generic-fibre Tate modules and the integral differential calculations here' and to build the finite-level Hodge–Tate map. T3 (canonical subgroups) is a consumer. There is no Mathlib or Tau Ceti declaration. External input: [20] L. Fargues, La filtration de Harder–Narasimhan des schémas en groupes finis et plats, J. reine angew. Math. 645 (2010).

items.name: Fargues: degree increases along generic isomorphisms
items.statement: If f: 𝒢_1 → 𝒢_2 is a morphism of finite flat group schemes over O_K that is an isomorphism on generic fibres, then deg 𝒢_1 ≤ deg 𝒢_2.
items.locator: Proofs of Lemma 14.1.1, Lemma 14.3.1(1), (3), (5) and Cor. 14.3.1, pp. 92–94
items.note: Unplanned. It has the same owner as the degree. External input: [20] L. Fargues, J. reine angew. Math. 645 (2010), coro. 3 on p. 13.

items.name: Fargues: deg 𝒢 + deg 𝒢^D = height
items.statement: For a finite flat group scheme 𝒢 of order p^h over O_K with Cartier dual 𝒢^D, deg 𝒢 + deg 𝒢^D = h.
items.locator: Proofs of Lemma 14.1.1 and Lemma 14.3.1(2), (4), pp. 92–93
items.note: Unplanned. Cartier duality is planned (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.1) and exists over an affine base in Tau Ceti (tauceti:TauCeti.FiniteLocallyFreeCommAffineGroupSchemeCat.cartierDual, TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AffineGroupScheme/CartierDuality/FiniteLocallyFree.lean:275), but the formula deg 𝒢 + deg 𝒢^D = h is not. External input: [20] L. Fargues, J. reine angew. Math. 645 (2010), lem. 4 on p. 12.

items.name: Fargues: the cokernel of the Hodge–Tate map is killed by p^{1/(p−1)}
items.statement: For H_n ⊂ G[p^n] (étale-locally cyclic, generated by e_1) over O_K, the cokernel of HT_{H_n} ⊗ 1: H_n ⊗ O_K → ω_{H_n^D} is killed by p^{1/(p−1)}.
items.note: HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T0 plans 'Build the finite-level Hodge–Tate map using Cartier duality and differentials of characters. Prove functoriality ...' but no estimate for its cokernel. External input: [20] L. Fargues, J. reine angew. Math. 645 (2010), thm. 7, as cited.

items.name: Fargues: inverse different and conormal sheaf
items.statement: For a finite flat, generically étale group scheme H^D over a normal base, the pullback along the unit section of the inverse different 𝒟_{O_{H^D}/O} is canonically an invertible sheaf. For H^D the Cartier dual of the universal order-p subgroup H, it is identified with I^{−1}.
items.note: Unplanned. No layer constructs the inverse different of a finite flat, generically étale group scheme, or identifies its pullback along the unit section with I^{−1}. External input: [20] L. Fargues, J. reine angew. Math. 645 (2010), §§1.3–1.4 and définition 3.

items.name: Oort–Tate classification of group schemes of order p
items.statement: Over a suitable base (e.g. O_K), every finite flat group scheme of order p is of the form G_{a,b} = Spec O[x]/(x^p − a x) with ab = w_p. Its Cartier dual is G_{b,a}.
items.note: FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.1 plans Raynaud's '(p,…,p)-type classification and its tame inertia characters ... (Bull. SMF 102 (1974), §§2–3 ...)'. That is close to Oort–Tate but does not state it, nor the Cartier-dual swap G_{a,b}^D = G_{b,a}. The Tau Ceti ModularCurves roadmap explicitly schedules 'No Oort–Tate classification'. PAPER-SCHROER-23 routed its Oort–Tate item to R07.1. No library declaration. External input: [58] F. Oort, J. Tate, Group schemes of prime order, Ann. Sci. ENS (4) 3 (1970), 1–21.

items.name: Comparison / GAGA for coherent cohomology of proper schemes and their analytifications
items.statement: For a proper scheme over a complete non-archimedean field, coherent cohomology agrees with that of the associated adic space.
items.locator: Proof of Prop. 14.4.1.1, p. 94; proof of Lemma 14.8.1(1), p. 100
items.note: The reviewed AdicSpacesPartII decomposition records the gap 'Proper GAGA and analytification of group schemes for R1 have no source in the library'. The paper's citation (Scholze, thm. 9.1) is a candidate source; the paper cites it as [70], thm. 9.1 on p. 15 but as [69], thm. 9.1 on pp. 94 and 100, where [69] (Perfectoid spaces) is the wrong key for [70] (p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, Forum Math. Pi 2013) [sourceIssues E126]. AdicSpacesPartII:F0 separately plans formal GAGA. The theorem is also used on p. 15, in the proof of Prop. 3.4.1 (§3.4), where it is correctly cited as [70], thm. 9.1. There it is used in relative form for the proper toric morphism f attached to a refinement Σ′ of Σ: Rf^an_*O = (Rf_*O)^an. Together with the classical vanishing for toroidal embeddings ([40], cor. 1, p. 44), this gives Prop. 3.4.1 after inverting p. External input: Cited as [69] P. Scholze, Perfectoid spaces (2012), thm. 9.1. The same comparison is cited as [70] P. Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, Forum Math. Pi 1 (2013), thm. 9.1, in §3.4.

items.name: Lan: vanishing of higher direct images of subcanonical extensions to the minimal compactification
items.statement: For the projection π from the toroidal to the minimal compactification (Klingen level), Rπ_* Ω^{(k,2)}(−D) = π_* Ω^{(k,2)}(−D).
items.note: AutomorphicBundles:B3 plans 'Define the pushforward to the minimal compactification as a coherent sheaf and prove the exact properties used later', but no vanishing of R^iπ_* for subcanonical extensions. ShimuraCompactifications:C3 requires that such vanishing be 'a separate theorem with the relevant coefficient hypotheses'. PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20 routed the same vanishing (in ext-pilloni-vanishing-large-parallel-weight) to the proposed IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes. External input: [50] K.-W. Lan, Integral models of toroidal compactifications with projective cone decompositions, IMRN 2017, no. 11, thm. 8.9.

items.name: SGA2: sections and H^1 extend across closed subsets of codimension ≥ 2 on Cohen–Macaulay schemes
items.statement: If F is locally free on a Cohen–Macaulay scheme Y and Z ⊂ Y is closed of codimension ≥ 2, then H^i_Z(Y, F) = 0 for i ≤ 1. Hence H^0(Y, F) ≅ H^0(Y∖Z, F) and H^1(Y, F) ↪ H^1(Y∖Z, F).
items.note: Mathlib has algebraic local cohomology (mathlib:localCohomology, Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/LocalCohomology.lean:175, 'the direct limit of Ext^i(R/J^t, M)') and Rees's depth theorem (mathlib:exists_isRegular_tfae, Mathlib/RingTheory/Depth/Rees.lean:158). Together they give the affine vanishing for i < depth, but only after an argument that is not in the library. Absent from both libraries: sheaf cohomology with supports on schemes, and the extension statement. DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3 plans 'regular sequences, depth, Cohen–Macaulay rings/modules', and SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2 plans 'sheaf cohomology, localization'; neither states SGA 2 III §3. PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-19 routed its SGA 2 depth statements to SchemeAndStackFoundations (SF.0, SF.4). External input: [SGA2] A. Grothendieck, Cohomologie locale des faisceaux cohérents et théorèmes de Lefschetz locaux et globaux (SGA 2), exposé III, §3.

items.name: Stroh: the universal subgroup H extends to a finite flat group scheme at the boundary
items.statement: The universal order-p subgroup H over the Klingen-level Siegel threefold extends to a finite flat group scheme over the toroidal boundary.
items.note: ShimuraCompactifications:C5 plans 'For higher p-level normalizations, prove the precise chart and finiteness properties used by the perfectoid-tower argument', and C4 plans 'the comparison of level structures across a boundary chart'. Neither states that the universal order-p subgroup at Klingen level extends to a finite flat group scheme over the toroidal boundary. External input: [75] B. Stroh, Mauvaise réduction au bord, Astérisque 370 (2015), 269–304, lem. 2.4.3.

items.name: Faltings–Chai: Hecke correspondences on toroidal compactifications
items.statement: For a double coset (T_{p,2}, T_{ℓ,i}) and suitable polyhedral cone decompositions Σ, Σ′, Σ″, the Hecke correspondence extends to toroidal compactifications p_1: C_{Σ″} → X_Σ and p_2: C_{Σ″} → X_{Σ′}.
items.note: The prime-to-p case is planned: PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18's lan-toroidal-hecke-correspondence was marked planned in ShimuraCompactifications:C3/C5, where C3 plans 'For a morphism of data or a Hecke translation, choose compatible source and target fans and construct the extension'. The item as stated also covers the integral correspondence C_{p,2} over Z_p for diag(p,p,1,1), whose formal completion ℭ_{p,2} §14.9.2 uses. That case lies outside C3 (characteristic-0 toroidal models) and C5 (good-prime level), so the item is missing. External input: [18] G. Faltings, C.-L. Chai, Degeneration of abelian varieties, Ergebnisse 22, Springer 1990, p. 253.

items.name: Standing data of §15: level K, integer N, and the ordinary complex M_K
items.statement: Throughout §15, p is a fixed prime. K = ∏_ℓ K_ℓ ⊂ GSp4(A_f) is a compact open subgroup, neat as assumed from §5.2.1 and §6.1.1 on, with K_p = GSp4(Z_p). N is the product of the primes ℓ with K_ℓ ≠ GSp4(Z_ℓ), so p ∤ N. 𝔛 = 𝔛_K is the p-adic formal completion of a toroidal compactification X_K → Spec Z_p of the Siegel threefold of level K. 𝔛^{≥1}_{Kli}(p) = 𝔛_{Kli}(p)^{≥1}_K is the open formal subscheme of the formal completion of X_{Kli}(p)_K (Klingen level at p: a subgroup H ⊂ G[p] of order p) where the p-rank of the semi-abelian scheme is at least 1 and H is multiplicative. Equivalently, it is the moduli over 𝔛 of subgroups H ⊂ G[p] that are étale-locally isomorphic to μ_p (§9.2), and it is étale over 𝔛. D is the boundary divisor. Λ = Z_p[[Z_p^×]], and for k ∈ Z the specialisation k : Λ → Z_p extends z ↦ z^k. 𝔉^κ = (π_*O_{IG(p^∞)} ⊗̂_{Z_p} Λ)^{Z_p^×} is the sheaf of §9.3, where π : IG(p^∞) → 𝔛^{≥1}_{Kli}(p). The paper describes it as an invertible sheaf of O_{𝔛^{≥1}_{Kli}(p^∞)} ⊗̂_{Z_p} Λ-modules over 𝔛^{≥1}_{Kli}(p). ω² = det² ω_G. f is the ordinary projector attached to the locally finite action of U on RΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_{Kli}(p), 𝔉^κ ⊗ ω²(−D)) (Theorem 11.3.1(1)). M_K := fRΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_{Kli}(p), 𝔉^κ ⊗ ω²(−D)) is a perfect complex of Λ-modules concentrated in degrees [0,1] (Theorem 11.3.1(2)); it is the complex M of Theorem 1.1. For k ≥ 0 there is a quasi-isomorphism fRΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_{Kli}(p), Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) → M_K ⊗^L_{Λ,k} Z_p, where Ω^{(k,2)} = Sym^k ω_G ⊗ det² ω_G (Theorem 11.3.1(3)).
items.note: The ingredients split into planned and unplanned parts. Planned: neat compact open levels (ShimuraData:D5, 'Define neatness'); Siegel moduli (PELModuli:M5, 'Construct Siegel moduli for every dimension'); the integral toroidal compactification and its formal completion (ShimuraCompactifications:C5, 'Construct the integral toroidal algebraic spaces with their universal semi-abelian extensions ... Prove their formal completion descriptions'); Λ as a completed group ring (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1, 'R[[G]] = lim_(n,U) (R/I^n)[G/U]'; AUDIT-26 says 'No completed group ring exists in either library'); ordinary projectors on complexes (PadicFamilies:L0a, 'Apply the result degreewise to finite perfect/cohomological complexes with commuting U'); perfect complexes (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:P7). Planned nowhere: the Klingen-level formal scheme 𝔛^{≥1}_{Kli}(p), the p-rank ≥ 1 locus with H multiplicative (no stage mentions Klingen level at p or the p-rank stratification of Siegel varieties); the sheaf 𝔉^κ of §9.3 (OverconvergentAutomorphicForms O7 is Hilbert-only, and O8 treats only overconvergent Siegel coefficients on anticanonical domains); the U-operator; and M_K with Theorem 11.3.1. These are the paper's own §§9–11 constructions, extracted by other clusters. The introduction introduces M as the complex of Theorem 1.1 (§1, pp. 2–3), a perfect complex of Λ-modules of amplitude [0,1]. On pp. 3–4 it describes M as the U-ordinary part of the cohomology of the sheaf of Λ-modules 𝔉^κ ⊗ Ω^{(0,2)}(−D) on 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p)_K.

items.name: Prime-to-p Hecke correspondences and normalised operators T_{ℓ,i} on the p-rank ≥ 1 locus
items.statement:
Let ℓ ≠ p be a prime with K_ℓ = GSp4(Z_ℓ), and let i ∈ {0,1,2}. For suitable (suppressed) choices of polyhedral cone decompositions there is a Hecke correspondence X ←p2− C_{ℓ,i} −p1→ X between toroidal compactifications attached to the double coset T_{ℓ,i} ([18], p. 253). Its universal isogeny has ℓ-power degree and is therefore étale. Let ℭ_{ℓ,i} be the formal completion of C_{ℓ,i}, and form 𝔇_{ℓ,i} := ℭ_{ℓ,i} ×_{p1,𝔛} 𝔛^{≥1}_{Kli}(p).
(a) The second projection p2 : 𝔇_{ℓ,i} → 𝔛 lifts naturally to p2 : 𝔇_{ℓ,i} → 𝔛^{≥1}_{Kli}(p).
(b) Since the isogeny is étale, there is a canonical isomorphism p2^*𝔉^κ ⊗ ω²(−D) → p1^*𝔉^κ ⊗ ω²(−D).
(c) 𝔛^{≥1}_{Kli}(p) and 𝔇_{ℓ,i} are smooth, so there is a fundamental class p1^*O_{𝔛^{≥1}_{Kli}(p)} → p1^!O_{𝔛^{≥1}_{Kli}(p)}.
(d) Combining (b) and (c) gives the unnormalised cohomological correspondence T'_{ℓ,i} : p2^*𝔉^κ ⊗ ω²(−D) → p1^!𝔉^κ ⊗ ω²(−D).
(e) The normalised operators are T_{ℓ,2} := ℓ^{−3}T'_{ℓ,2} and T_{ℓ,i} := ℓ^{−6}T'_{ℓ,i} for i = 0, 1. Through the cohomological-correspondence formalism of §4 they act on RΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_{Kli}(p), 𝔉^κ ⊗ ω²(−D)).
items.locator: §15.1, proof of Proposition 15.1.1, p. 106 (footnote 28 refers to Remark 5.3.1)
items.note: Planned inputs: the Hecke extension to toroidal compactifications (ShimuraCompactifications:C3, 'For a morphism of data or a Hecke translation, choose compatible source and target fans and construct the extension'); the analytic correspondence (ShimuraVarieties:V1, 'Construct the Hecke correspondence through K∩gKg⁻¹'); and Hecke operators on sections by 'pullback, coefficient identification, and trace' (AutomorphicBundles:B5). Planned nowhere: the lift of p2 to 𝔛^{≥1}_{Kli}(p); the étale-isogeny isomorphism p2^*𝔉^κ → p1^*𝔉^κ; the coherent fundamental class p1^*O → p1^!O; and the cohomological-correspondence formalism of §4. A keyword search finds f^! only for étale sheaves and diamonds (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.1, DiamondSixOperations S3), and no stage plans coherent Grothendieck duality. CG20 routed Hecke operators on higher coherent cohomology (hecke-operators-T-x-i) to the proposed Part II IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes.

items.name: Proposition 15.1.1: action of H_ℓ on the p-adic cohomology
items.statement: Let ℓ ≠ p be a prime such that K_ℓ = GSp4(Z_ℓ). The operators T_{ℓ,0}, T_{ℓ,1}, T_{ℓ,2} of the construction define an action of H_ℓ = Z[T_{ℓ,0}, T_{ℓ,0}^{−1}, T_{ℓ,1}, T_{ℓ,2}] on RΓ(𝔛_{Kli}(p)^{≥1}_K, 𝔉^κ ⊗ ω²(−D)).
items.note: This is an action of H_ℓ on cohomology of the p-adic sheaf 𝔉^κ ⊗ ω²(−D) over 𝔛^{≥1}_{Kli}(p). It needs the missing construction item, the missing presentation of H_ℓ, and the relations among the T'_{ℓ,i} (composition of cohomological correspondences). None of these is planned. Commutativity of the action with U, needed later so that H^{Np} acts on fRΓ, is also not stated anywhere in the atlas. The paper's proof also stops once the T_{ℓ,i} are constructed. It does not verify the relations of H_ℓ, that operators for different ℓ commute, or that they commute with U [sourceIssues E147]. The construction of the operators is recorded in construction-prime-to-p-hecke-correspondences-on-p-rank-one-locus: the correspondences C_{ℓ,i}, their formal completions restricted to 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p), the fundamental class and the normalisations T_{ℓ,2} = ℓ^{−3}T′_{ℓ,2}, T_{ℓ,i} = ℓ^{−6}T′_{ℓ,i} (i = 0, 1). The level K = ∏_ℓ K_ℓ with K_p = GSp4(Z_p) is set up in setting-level-and-p-adic-ordinary-complex.

items.name: Residual representation ρ̄ and its maximal ideal m ⊂ H^{Np}
items.statement: Let ρ̄ : G_Q → GSp4(F̄_p) be a continuous Galois representation that is unramified at every prime ℓ ∤ pN and absolutely irreducible. Let Θ_m : H^{Np} → F̄_p be a ring homomorphism with Θ_m(Q_ℓ(X)) = det(1 − Xρ̄(Frob_ℓ)) for every prime ℓ ∤ Np, where Frob_ℓ is a geometric Frobenius (Remark 5.1.7.1; printed 'Fob_ℓ', sourceIssues E149) and Θ_m is applied to the coefficients. The maximal ideal of H^{Np} attached to ρ̄ is m := ker Θ_m. Correction [sourceIssues E150]: the rule fixes Θ_m(T_{ℓ,2}) = tr ρ̄(Frob_ℓ), Θ_m(T_{ℓ,0})² and Θ_m(T_{ℓ,1}) + (ℓ²+1)Θ_m(T_{ℓ,0}). For p = 2 it therefore determines Θ_m on H_ℓ, since squaring is injective on F̄_2. For p odd it fixes Θ_m(T_{ℓ,0}), and hence Θ_m(T_{ℓ,1}), only when tr ρ̄(Frob_ℓ) ≠ 0. One also imposes ℓ³Θ_m(T_{ℓ,0}) = ν(ρ̄(Frob_ℓ)), with ν the similitude character (cf. Lemma 5.1.5.1), or takes m to be any maximal ideal satisfying the rule.
items.note: This item needs the missing GSp4 Hecke polynomial Q_ℓ(X) (see recall-spherical-…) and GSp4-valued residual representations. ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1 plans continuous GL_n-valued representations with descent to a finite coefficient field, but no stage plans GSp4-valued ones or the similitude ν; CG20 routed its residual r̄ to ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7 as a source. The dictionary Θ_m(Q_ℓ(X)) = det(1 − Xρ̄(Frob_ℓ)) with geometric Frobenius is exactly IHG.3's normalization work ('Every other convention is connected by an explicit conversion theorem, including geometric Frobenius/inverse roots'), but IHG.3 covers GL_n only. CG20's non-Eisenstein maximal ideals are also missing. The item's correction (Θ_m(T_{ℓ,0}) is fixed only up to sign unless ν(ρ̄(Frob_ℓ)) is imposed) should be kept. The paper calls such an m, attached to an absolutely irreducible ρ̄ unramified outside pN, a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal (§1, p. 3; §15 introduction, p. 106). On p. 3 the definition reads: m has an associated 4-dimensional representation of Gal(Q̄/Q) that is unramified away from pN, satisfies the familiar local-global compatibility at primes not dividing pN, and is absolutely irreducible.

items.name: The Hecke algebra of the ordinary complex is finite over Λ and semi-local
items.statement: The algebra H^{Np} acts on the perfect complex M_K = fRΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_{Kli}(p), 𝔉^κ ⊗ ω²(−D)), through Proposition 15.1.1 for each ℓ ∤ Np. The Λ-subalgebra T_K of End(M_K) (endomorphisms in the derived category of Λ-modules) generated by the image of H^{Np} is a commutative, finite Λ-algebra, and in particular it is semi-local.
items.note: The general statement is planned. IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.2 says 'For a Hecke action on a bounded perfect complex define its finite image algebras ... Prove localization decompositions over complete coefficient rings'. Finiteness holds because End_{D(Λ)} of a perfect complex over noetherian Λ is a finite Λ-module, and a finite algebra over Λ (a product of p − 1 complete local rings for p odd; local for p = 2) is semi-local. The instance is missing. The H^{Np}-action on M_K needs Proposition 15.1.1 (missing) and its commutation with U, hence with f. M_K is Theorem 11.3.1 (missing). This follows CG20, which marked its Hecke algebras of specific cohomology missing (def-5-13-2-hecke-algebra-T-mu-Q).

items.name: Localisation of a perfect complex at a maximal ideal of a finite Hecke algebra ([41], Lemma 2.12)
items.statement: As used: let Λ be a noetherian ring that is a finite product of complete local rings, C a perfect complex of Λ-modules, and T ⊂ End_{D(Λ)}(C) a commutative Λ-subalgebra that is finite over Λ. Then T = ∏_n T_n is the product of its localisations at its finitely many maximal ideals n. The corresponding idempotents decompose C ≅ ⊕_n C_n in D(Λ), where each C_n is a perfect complex of Λ-modules with H^i(C_n) = H^i(C) ⊗_T T_n.
items.note: This is purely general. Λ = Z_p[[Z_p^×]] is a finite product of complete regular local rings (Z_p[[T]] factors), so the lemma applies componentwise. H^i(C_n) = H^i(C) ⊗_T T_n is exactness of the idempotent decomposition. Nothing is in the libraries: AUDIT-17 on P7 says 'No perfect complex, Perf subcategory or pseudo-coherence notion exists in either tree', and IHG.2 has no audit entry. By Remark 2.3.1 (p. 11), [41] Lemma 2.12 is stated for idempotents in End_{D}(M) with M perfect over a complete local ring, and 'rests on the property that the algebra End ... is finite over R when M is a perfect complex'. The paper uses that finiteness in both §2.3 and §15.2. External input: C. Khare and J. Thorne, Potential automorphy and the Leopoldt conjecture, Amer. J. Math. 139 (2017), Lemma 2.12 (the paper's [41])

items.name: The non-Eisenstein localisation fRΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_{Kli}(p), 𝔉^κ ⊗ ω²(−D))_m
items.statement: For m as above, M_{K,m} := fRΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_{Kli}(p), 𝔉^κ ⊗ ω²(−D))_m is the direct factor of M_K cut out, through [41, Lemma 2.12], by the idempotents of the semi-local algebra T_K belonging to the maximal ideals of T_K that lie over m. It is a perfect complex of Λ-modules concentrated in degrees [0,1]. It is zero if Θ_m does not factor through T_K, i.e. if ρ̄ does not occur in the cohomology.
items.note: This is the object of Theorem 15.2.1. The localisation itself is IHG.2/P9's general idempotent decomposition, which is planned (see ext-khare-thorne-localisation-of-perfect-complexes). The fact that a derived direct summand of a perfect complex with Tor-amplitude [0,1] again has amplitude [0,1] is DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:P7 ('Distinguish the amplitude of a chosen complex, Tor-amplitude and the degrees of nonzero cohomology'). The object itself is missing: it needs M_K (Theorem 11.3.1), the Hecke algebra T_K and the maximal ideal m, all missing. The introduction (§1, p. 3) introduces the same object as M_m, the direct factor of M obtained by localisation at a maximal ideal m of the prime-to-pN Hecke algebra. N is the product of the primes ℓ with K_ℓ ≠ GSp4(Z_ℓ) (setting-level-and-p-adic-ordinary-complex). H^{Np} is the abstract spherical Hecke algebra away from Np (spherical-hecke-algebra-gsp4).

items.name: Euler characteristic of a perfect complex of Λ-modules
items.statement: For a perfect complex C of Λ-modules, represented by a bounded complex P^• of finitely generated projective Λ-modules, χ(C) := Σ_i (−1)^i rk_Λ(P^i). This is a locally constant Z-valued function on Spec Λ. Equivalently, χ(C)(x) = Σ_i (−1)^i dim_{k(x)} H^i(C ⊗^L_Λ k(x)) for every point x. 'χ(C) = 0' means that χ(C) vanishes on every connected component. For Λ = Z_p[[Z_p^×]] there are p − 1 components when p is odd, and Λ is local when p = 2.
items.locator: §15.2, Theorem 15.2.1, p. 107 (the notion is used but not defined)
items.note: χ(C) = Σ(−1)^i rankAtStalk(P^i) is a one-line definition once perfect complexes exist. Independence of the representative, and the fibrewise formula through rankAtStalk_eq and Tau Ceti's Euler–Poincaré, are routine. What the libraries lack is perfect complexes (AUDIT-17 on P7) and the K₀ Euler class of a perfect complex (Z.6 audit: 'absent'). Mathlib's HomologicalComplex.eulerChar is not this χ over a disconnected Λ, because finrank is junk on non-free projectives. The paper uses the notion without defining it; the component count of Spec Λ comes from Z_p^× = μ_{p−1} × (1+pZ_p), with Λ from PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1.

items.name: Theorem 15.2.1 (= Theorem 1.2): vanishing of the Euler characteristic of the non-Eisenstein ordinary complex
items.statement: Assume K = ∏_ℓ K_ℓ ⊂ GSp4(A_f) is a (neat) compact open subgroup with K_p = GSp4(Z_p), and N is the product of the primes ℓ with K_ℓ ≠ GSp4(Z_ℓ). Let ρ̄ : G_Q → GSp4(F̄_p) be absolutely irreducible and unramified outside pN, and let m ⊂ H^{Np} be an associated maximal ideal. Then the Euler characteristic of the perfect complex of Λ-modules fRΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_{Kli}(p), 𝔉^κ ⊗ ω²(−D))_m is 0, on every connected component of Spec Λ.
items.note: This is the main theorem of §15 (Theorem 1.2), and nothing in the atlas plans it. Its inputs: M_{K,m} (missing); Theorem 11.3.1(3) (missing, other clusters); Corollary 15.2.3.1 and Proposition 15.2.4.1 (missing, routed to the proposed IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes); and the planned base-change property of χ (ext-euler-characteristic-base-change). A remark on the proof (p. 109, image checked): it 'specialize[s] at a very large weight k', but one specialisation k : Λ → Z_p fixes χ only on the component of Spec Λ containing ker k, namely the class of k mod p − 1 for p odd. So the argument must be run for a large k in each residue class mod p − 1 [sourceIssues E165]. The automorphic argument holds for every k ≥ R − 1, so the stated conclusion 'on every component' stands. PAPER-BCGP18 (pending roadmap AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity) consumes this theorem. This is Theorem 1.2 of the introduction (§1, p. 3): for a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal m of the prime-to-pN Hecke algebra, the complex M_m has trivial Euler characteristic. §15 opens (p. 106) by saying that it proves Theorem 1.2.

items.name: Conjecture (Remark 15.2.1): the localised ordinary cohomology is Λ-torsion
items.statement: Conjecture: if ρ̄ is not induced from a real quadratic extension of Q, then the support over Λ of ⊕_{i=0}^{1} fH^i(𝔛^{≥1}_{Kli}(p), 𝔉^κ ⊗ ω²(−D))_m has Krull dimension ≤ 1. Λ has Krull dimension 2, so this says the cohomology is Λ-torsion. If ρ̄ is induced from a real quadratic field, positive-dimensional families should come from inductions of families of Hilbert modular forms.
items.note: This is an open conjecture (Remark 15.2.1, p. 107, image checked), and no stage records it. It should become a named conjectural statement. Related commutative algebra is planned in DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:P9, which relates codimension of support, projective dimension and Tor-amplitude, and gives the 'dimension-one generic-length formula for the Euler characteristic'. Compare Khare–Thorne [41], Conjecture 7.2. The real-quadratic exception needs families of Hilbert modular forms and automorphic induction, planned in PadicFamilies L5 and ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.5; these are background only. The introduction states the same expectation as Remark 1.4 (§1, p. 3). Suppose m is associated to a Galois representation that is absolutely irreducible and stays absolutely irreducible on restriction to the Galois group of every real quadratic field. Then the H^i(M_m) should be torsion Λ-modules. By Clifford theory, an absolutely irreducible ρ̄ becomes reducible on the index-2 subgroup G_F exactly when it is induced from G_F, so the two hypotheses agree. Since dim Λ = 2, being Λ-torsion is the same as having support of Krull dimension ≤ 1. So Remark 1.4 and Remark 15.2.1 state the same conjecture. External input: Compare C. Khare–J. Thorne [41], Conjecture 7.2

items.name: The two limits of discrete series π(λ)^h and π(λ)^g for λ2 = 0, λ1 < 0
items.statement: Let λ = (λ1, 0; c) ∈ X^*(T) + (2,1;0) with λ1 < 0. Exactly two Weyl chambers are positive for λ. π(λ)^h := π(λ, C) for C the chamber of the fixed choice of positive roots (Remark 5.1.2.1: compact positive roots in 𝔪_Si, noncompact ones in 𝔤_C/𝔭_Si). It contains the holomorphic and antiholomorphic limits of discrete series of the derived group Sp4(R), and it is the holomorphic limit of discrete series in the sense of §5.1.6. π(λ)^g := π(λ, C') for the other chamber C'. Both are limits of discrete series with infinitesimal character the W-orbit of λ.
items.note: This item depends on the missing parametrisation π(λ, C) and on the Weyl chambers of GSp4, which CG20 marked missing and routed to AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups (def-weyl-chambers-C0-to-C3, def-compact-noncompact-roots-and-positive-system). The two chambers containing λ = (λ1, 0; c) are CG20's C0 and C1, whose packet is {π(λ, C0), π(λ, C1)}. The positive system of Remark 5.1.2.1 fixes which one is π(λ)^h. The identification of π(λ)^h with the holomorphic limit of discrete series of §5.1.6 is also unplanned.

items.name: h, K∞, the Cartan decomposition, and the K∞-type V_{(−λ1+1,2;−c)}
items.statement: Let λ = (λ1, 0; c) ∈ X^*(T) + (2,1;0) with λ1 < 0. The character (−λ1+1, 2; −c) ∈ X^*(T) is dominant for the Levi M_Si ≅ GL2 × G_m of the Siegel parabolic P_Si ⊂ GSp4, the stabiliser of ⟨e1, e2⟩. V_{(−λ1+1,2;−c)} is the complex irreducible representation of P_Si of highest weight (−λ1+1, 2; −c). Let h : Res_{C/R} G_m → GSp4/R be h(a+ib) = a·1_4 + bJ (printed: a1_2 + bJ), with J = [[0, A], [−A, 0]] as in §5.1. Let K∞ ⊂ GSp4(R) be the centraliser of the image of h. Let 𝔤 be the complex Lie algebra of GSp4, with Cartan decomposition 𝔤 = 𝔨 ⊕ 𝔭. The algebra 𝔨 = 𝔤^{(0,0)} is identified, by the conjugation of Remark 5.2.1.1, with the complexified Lie algebra of M_Si. Through this identification V_{(−λ1+1,2;−c)} is also a representation of 𝔨 and of K∞.
items.note: This follows CG20, which classified h (construction-hodge-cocharacter-h: D5, D1), K∞ (D2, LieGroups L9), the Siegel parabolic and Levi (ReductiveGroups L7, C1) and the K-dominant weights and representations (B2, B4, D2, ClassicalGroups L3) as planned. Caveat: the statement that 𝔨 is the complex Lie algebra of M_Si uses a Cayley-transform conjugation of K∞,C to M_Si,C, and CG20 marked the explicit Cayley transform missing (construction-basis-f-and-cayley-transform, source ShimuraData). p. 107 prints the subscript as (λ1+1,2;−c) and (−λ1+1,2;c) where (−λ1+1,2;−c) is meant (image checked).

items.name: (𝔭, K∞)-cohomology H^•(𝔭, K∞; W) of a (𝔤, K∞)-module
items.statement: For a (𝔤, K∞)-module W, H^•(𝔭, K∞; W) is the relative Lie algebra cohomology of Harris [30], §4.1.1. It is taken with respect to the parabolic subalgebra 𝔭_h = 𝔤^{(0,0)} ⊕ 𝔤^{(1,−1)} = 𝔨 ⊕ (one of 𝔭^±) of Remark 5.2.1.1, relative to K∞, and is computed by the complex Hom_{K∞}(∧^•(𝔭_h/𝔨), W). It measures the contribution of a representation to the coherent cohomology of the automorphic vector bundle attached to a K∞-type.
items.note: AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups:AF.1 plans only (g,K)-cochains, 'Define relative Lie algebra cochains Hom_K(∧^q(g/k),V)'. The (𝔭_h, K∞)-cohomology relative to the θ-stable parabolic 𝔨 ⊕ 𝔭^± (Harris's ∂̄-cohomology) is planned nowhere. AUDIT-13 on AF.1 finds 'the relative complex for a pair (g,K) is absent'. CG20 made the same classification (relative-lie-algebra-cohomology-spaces: missing, source AF). External input: M. Harris [30], Automorphic forms of ∂̄-cohomology type as coherent cohomology classes, J. Differential Geom. 32 (1990), §4.1.1

items.name: Theorem 15.2.2.1(1) (BHR): (𝔭,K∞)-cohomology of π(λ)^h and π(λ)^g
items.statement: Let λ = (λ1, 0; c) with λ1 < 0 and V = V_{(−λ1+1,2;−c)}. Then H^i(𝔭, K∞; π(λ)^h ⊗ V) = C for i = 0 and 0 for i ≠ 0. Also H^i(𝔭, K∞; π(λ)^g ⊗ V) = C for i = 1 and 0 for i ≠ 1.
items.note: The (𝔭, K∞)-cohomology of the limits of discrete series π(λ)^h and π(λ)^g (BHR Thm 3.2.1, §4.2) is planned nowhere. It needs the missing parametrisation and the missing (𝔭, K)-cohomology. CG20 marked the same theorem missing (ext-bhr-coherent-cohomology-discrete-series, ext-harris-limit-ds-lie-algebra-cohomology) and routed it to AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups. External input: D. Blasius, M. Harris, D. Ramakrishnan [4], Coherent cohomology, limits of discrete series and Galois conjugation, Duke Math. J. 73 (1994), Thm. 3.2.1 and §4.2

items.name: Theorem 15.2.2.1(2) (BHR): only π(λ)^h, π(λ)^g contribute in large weight
items.statement: There is a constant R with the following property. Let λ = (λ1, 0; c) with λ1 < 0 and −λ1 ≥ R (printed: λ1 ≥ R), and V = V_{(−λ1+1,2;−c)}. Let π∞ be an irreducible, essentially unitary representation of GSp4(R). If H⁰(𝔭, K∞; π∞ ⊗ V) ≠ 0 then π∞ ≅ π(λ)^h, and if H¹(𝔭, K∞; π∞ ⊗ V) ≠ 0 then π∞ ≅ π(λ)^g.
items.note: This is a classification of the irreducible essentially unitary representations of GSp4(R) with nonzero H^0 or H^1 (𝔭, K∞)-cohomology in large regular-enough weight. No stage plans unitary (g,K)-modules with nonvanishing (𝔭, K)-cohomology. The tempered analogue in CG20 (ext-mirkovic-tempered-cohomological) is also missing and routed to AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups. p. 108 prints 'λ1 ≥ R' where −λ1 ≥ R is meant, since λ1 < 0 (image checked; the item already records this). External input: D. Blasius, M. Harris, D. Ramakrishnan [4], Duke Math. J. 73 (1994), Thm. 3.2.1 and §4.2

items.name: Complex Siegel threefold, the bundle Ω^{(k,2)}, and the normalisation k = −λ1 − 1, c = −λ1 + 3
items.statement: S_K is the Siegel threefold of level K over C (K neat), S^{tor}_{K,Σ} a fixed toroidal compactification, and D its boundary divisor. G is the semi-abelian surface over S^{tor}_{K,Σ} and ω_G its conormal sheaf; Ω^{(k,2)} = Sym^k ω_G ⊗ det² ω_G, with cuspidal subsheaf Ω^{(k,2)}(−D) (§5.3). For λ = (λ1, 0; c) ∈ X^*(T) + (2,1;0) with λ1 < 0, set k = −λ1 − 1 (so k ≥ 0) and fix the central character c = −λ1 + 3 = k + 4, the 'correct' normalisation.
items.note: The objects are planned in characteristic 0, in line with CG20 (toroidal-compactification-hodge-bundle: C5, C3; automorphic-bundles-omega-a-b: B4, B3, C5). The numbers k = −λ1 − 1 and c = k + 4 are notation. Their meaning, that Ω^{(k,2)} is the bundle attached to the K∞-type V_{(−λ1+1,2;−c)} with the 'correct' Hecke normalisation, is the Harris/BHR bundle dictionary. CG20 marked that dictionary missing (lemma-5-4, rem-5-10-hecke-normalization) and routed it to the proposed IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes.

items.name: Interior coherent cohomology H̄^i(S^{tor}_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,2)})
items.statement: H̄^i(S^{tor}_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,2)}) is the image of the natural map H^i(S^{tor}_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) → H^i(S^{tor}_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,2)}).
items.note: This is a one-line definition from objects that are planned or in the library. Coherent cohomology of O_X-modules on schemes is in Tau Ceti (tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.Cohomology, TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Cohomology/Basic.lean:61). The canonical and subcanonical extensions are AutomorphicBundles:B3. No stage names interior coherent cohomology, however. CG20 found it 'planned nowhere' ('CompletedCohomologyPartII CC.7 defines completed interior cohomology only for Betti towers') and routed it to the proposed Part II (interior-cohomology-and-limits).

items.name: Theorem 15.2.3.1 (Harris): interior coherent cohomology in large weight
items.statement:
For every integer k ≥ R − 1 (R from Theorem 15.2.2.1(2)), with λ = (−k−1, 0; k+4):
(i) H̄⁰(S^{tor}_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,2)}) ≅ ⊕_{πf} (πf^K)^{m^h(πf)}. Here πf runs over the irreducible admissible representations of GSp4(A_f) such that πf ⊗ π(λ)^h is cuspidal automorphic, and m^h(πf) is the multiplicity of πf ⊗ π(λ)^h.
(ii) H̄¹(S^{tor}_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,2)}) ≅ ⊕_{πf} (πf^K)^{m^g(πf)}. Here πf runs over those such that πf ⊗ π(λ)^g is cuspidal automorphic, and m^g(πf) is the multiplicity of πf ⊗ π(λ)^g.
items.note: Harris's description of interior coherent cohomology through (𝔭, K)-cohomology of cusp forms (JDG 1990, Cor. 5.3.2) is planned nowhere. AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.5 is Betti-only. CG20 routed the same theorem (thm-5-2-harris-diagram, interior-cohomology-automorphic-description) to the proposed IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes. This item also needs the missing BHR uniqueness theorem and the missing multiplicities m^h, m^g. External input: M. Harris [30], J. Differential Geom. 32 (1990), Cor. 5.3.2 (combined with [4], Thm. 3.2.1)

items.name: Localisation of complex coherent cohomology at m, and congruence of Hecke characters
items.statement: Fix an isomorphism Q̄_p ≃ C. H^{Np} acts on H^i(S^{tor}_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) and H^i(S^{tor}_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,2)}) through the normalised Hecke correspondences of §5.3 ([30], Prop. 2.6). The localisation H^i(...)_m is the sum of the generalised eigenspaces for the systems of eigenvalues Θ : H^{Np} → C ≅ Q̄_p that are congruent to Θ_m. Here Θ is congruent to Θ_m when it takes values in Z̄_p and reduces to Θ_m modulo the maximal ideal of Z̄_p. For an irreducible admissible πf unramified outside Np, Θ_{πf} : H^{Np} → C is the character through which H^{Np} acts on ⊗_{ℓ∤Np} πℓ^{GSp4(Zℓ)}.
items.note: The H^{Np}-action on H^i(S^tor, Ω^{(k,2)}) and H^i(S^tor, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) for i ≥ 1 is missing. AutomorphicBundles:B5 plans Hecke operators on sections only. CG20 routed coherent Hecke operators in higher degree (hecke-operators-T-x-i) to the proposed Part II. Some pieces are planned. Localisation as a sum of generalised eigenspaces over Z̄_p-valued systems is linear algebra covered by IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.2's localisation. Θ_{πf}, the action on spherical vectors, is SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.4 ('Identify Hecke eigencharacters with unramified semisimple parameters') once the GSp4 Hecke algebra exists (missing).

items.name: Corollary 15.2.3.1, degree 0: localised H⁰ in large weight
items.statement: Let m be as in def-residual-representation-and-maximal-ideal-m, k ≥ R − 1 and λ = (−k−1, 0; k+4). Then H⁰(S^{tor}_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D))_m ≅ ⊕_{πf} (πf^K)^{m^h(πf)}. The sum runs over the irreducible admissible representations πf of GSp4(A_f) such that πf ⊗ π(λ)^h is cuspidal automorphic and Θ_{πf} : H^{Np} → C is congruent to Θ_m.
items.note: This follows from Harris's theorem (missing) and the injectivity H^0(Ω(−D)) ⊂ H^0(Ω), so H^0(Ω(−D)) = H̄^0 without localisation. It also needs localisation at m (missing). No stage plans an automorphic description of Siegel coherent H^0 in weight (k,2).

items.name: Corollary 15.2.3.1, degree 1: localised H¹ in large weight
items.statement: Let ρ̄ be absolutely irreducible and m as above, k ≥ R − 1 and λ = (−k−1, 0; k+4). Then H¹(S^{tor}_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D))_m ≅ ⊕_{πf} (πf^K)^{m^g(πf)}. The sum runs over the irreducible admissible πf of GSp4(A_f) such that πf ⊗ π(λ)^g is cuspidal automorphic and Θ_{πf} is congruent to Θ_m.
items.note: This needs Harris's theorem (missing) and the boundary-Eisenstein injectivity (missing), which gives H^1(Ω(−D))_m = H̄^1_m. It is the Pilloni counterpart of CG20's lemma-7-10-interior-equals-full and interior-cohomology-automorphic-description. CG20 routed the first to GSp4NonregularModularityLifting and the second to IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes. The same mathematics should have one owner.

items.name: Boundary restriction of Ω^{(k,2)}: pushforward to the compactified modular curves
items.statement: π_*(Ω^{(k,2)}|_D) ≅ ω^{k+2}(−cusp) if k ≠ 0, and ≅ ω² if k = 0. Here ω^{k+2} is the sheaf of modular forms of weight k + 2 on S^{(1),*}_K and cusp = S^{(0)}_K. Consequently H⁰(S^{tor}_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,2)} ⊗ O_D) ≅ H⁰(S^{(1),*}_K, ω^{k+2}(−cusp)) for k ≠ 0, and ≅ H⁰(S^{(1),*}_K, ω²) for k = 0 (printed 'if k = 2').
items.note: AutomorphicBundles:B3 plans only a general statement about the pushforward to the minimal compactification ('Define the pushforward to the minimal compactification as a coherent sheaf and prove the exact properties used later'). No stage plans the computation π_*(Ω^{(k,2)}|_D) ≅ ω^{k+2}(−cusp) (ω² when k = 0) on the one-dimensional boundary strata, or any coherent cohomology of toroidal boundary strata. CG20 found no stage mentioning 'coherent cohomology of toroidal boundary strata' and routed the Harris–Zucker boundary theory to the proposed Part II (ext-harris-zucker-nerve-spectral-sequence). p. 109 prints 'if k = 2' in the second display where k = 0 is meant (image checked; the item already records it).

items.name: Hecke compatibility of the Siegel Φ-operator: T_{ℓ,2} = 2T_ℓ on the boundary
items.statement: Let ℓ be a prime to the level K. Under the isomorphism H⁰(S^{tor}_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,2)} ⊗ O_D) ≅ H⁰(S^{(1),*}_K, ω^{k+2}(−cusp)) (resp. H⁰(S^{(1),*}_K, ω²) if k = 0), the Hecke operator T_{ℓ,2} (normalised as in §5.3) acts as 2T_ℓ, where T_ℓ is the usual Hecke operator on modular forms for GL2/Q.
items.note: AutomorphicBundles:B5 plans Fourier–Jacobi expansions at the relevant higher-dimensional boundary components and says 'Identify cuspidality with the appropriate boundary vanishing condition'. It does not plan the Hecke equivariance of the Siegel Φ-operator. In weight (k,2) the relation T_{ℓ,2} = 2T_ℓ is consistent with Klingen-type boundary eigensystems having spinor L-function L(f,s)², i.e. Galois representation ρ_f ⊕ ρ_f. The classical T_ℓ on elliptic forms is Tau Ceti existing work (ModularForms layer 2). External input: E. Freitag [22], Siegelsche Modulfunktionen, Grundlehren 254 (1983), Chap. IV, Satz 4.4

items.name: Galois representations attached to elliptic modular eigenforms
items.statement: Let f be a Hecke eigenform of weight k + 2 ≥ 2 on a modular curve component of S^{(1),*}_K. There is a continuous semisimple representation ρ_f : G_Q → GL2(Q̄_p), unramified at the primes ℓ not dividing the level and p, with tr ρ_f(Frob_ℓ) = a_ℓ(f), the T_ℓ-eigenvalue of f, for such ℓ.
items.note: R19.1 covers cuspidal eigenforms of weight k + 2 ≥ 2. AUDIT-31 finds it 'not built'. The boundary space H^0(S^{(1),*}, ω^{k+2}) also contains Eisenstein series, for instance weight-2 Eisenstein series when k = 0. Their ρ_f are sums of two characters, which comes from class field theory and cyclotomic characters (Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory and Chebotarev layer 4), not R19.1. The components of S^{(1),*}_K have congruence level determined by K ∩ M_Kli. External input: Eichler–Shimura, Deligne (invoked without citation)

items.name: Boundary coherent cohomology is Eisenstein: H⁰(S^{tor}, Ω^{(k,2)} ⊗ O_D)_m = 0
items.statement: Let ρ̄ be absolutely irreducible and m as above, and let k ≥ 0. Then H⁰(S^{tor}_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,2)} ⊗ O_D)_m = 0. The reason is that every system of Hecke eigenvalues Θ_f on this space comes from an eigenform f in H⁰(S^{(1),*}_K, ω^{k+2}), and its associated 4-dimensional Galois representation ρ_f ⊕ ρ_f is reducible, hence not congruent to ρ̄. Consequently, by the exact sequence H⁰(S^{tor}_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,2)}) → H⁰(S^{tor}_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,2)} ⊗ O_D) → H¹(S^{tor}_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) → H¹(S^{tor}_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,2)}), the map H¹(S^{tor}_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D))_m → H¹(S^{tor}_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,2)})_m is injective, and H¹(Ω^{(k,2)}(−D))_m = H̄¹(Ω^{(k,2)})_m.
items.note: The exact sequence is the long exact cohomology sequence of 0 → Ω(−D) → Ω → Ω ⊗ O_D → 0, which is in the library (tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.exact_cohomologyMap_cohomologyδ, TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Cohomology/LongExactSequence.lean:118). The vanishing H^0(Ω ⊗ O_D)_m = 0 needs the missing boundary pushforward, the missing Φ-operator Hecke relation, R19.1 (planned) and Brauer–Nesbitt/Chebotarev (planned), and no stage plans it. ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces:ALS.4 is Betti-only ('Describe conditions under which boundary localization vanishes ... by an actual eigenvalue argument'). CG20 routed its analogue (boundary-cohomology-vanishing) to GSp4NonregularModularityLifting. One owner is needed.

items.name: Brauer–Nesbitt and Chebotarev: Hecke congruence determines the residual semisimplification
items.statement: Let r : G_Q → GL4(Q̄_p) be continuous and unramified outside a finite set S ⊇ {primes dividing Np}. Suppose Θ : H^{Np} → Z̄_p satisfies Θ(Q_ℓ(X)) = det(1 − X r(Frob_ℓ)) for all ℓ ∉ S, and Θ reduces to Θ_m. Then (r̄)^{ss} ≅ ρ̄, by the Chebotarev density theorem and the Brauer–Nesbitt theorem. In particular, if r is reducible then ρ̄ is not absolutely irreducible. If only the traces Θ(T_{ℓ,2}) = tr r(Frob_ℓ) are known to agree, the same conclusion holds when p > 4.
items.note: This follows the CG20 precedent (ext-brauer-nesbitt: planned R01.1, R01.5). AUDIT-31 on R01.5 says 'Tau Ceti has the Frobenius prime sets ... but not the density theorem ... Brauer-Nesbitt is absent'. Only infrastructure is in the library, e.g. tauceti:NumberField.Chebotarev.frobeniusPrimeSet.
