The trace-only variant for p > 4 is the small-characteristic caveat R01.5 names. Applying the item to Θ through Q_ℓ(X) needs the missing GSp4 Hecke polynomial. External input: Chebotarev density theorem; Brauer–Nesbitt theorem (standard, invoked without citation)

items.name: Arthur's classification of the discrete spectrum of GSp4 (as used)
items.statement: As used: every discrete automorphic representation of GSp4(A) lies in a global Arthur packet Π_ψ of one of six types ([1], classification theorem on p. 78): (a) general ('generic') type, where ψ is a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL4 of symplectic type; (b) Yoshida type; (c) Soudry type; (d) Saito–Kurokawa type; (e) Howe–Piatetski-Shapiro type; (f) one-dimensional type. If Π is of general type, ψ is stable (trivial global component group), the archimedean packet Π_∞ is the L-packet of the archimedean parameter, and every element of Π = ⊗_v Π_v occurs in the discrete spectrum with multiplicity one. If Π is of Yoshida or Saito–Kurokawa type, its Hecke eigenvalues at unramified primes are those of a reducible 4-dimensional Galois representation: a sum of those attached to GL2 forms, resp. GL2 and GL1 forms.
items.note: This follows CG20's conservative reading (ext-arthur-gsp4-classification: missing, source ML.4). ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions:ML.4 ('Give Arthur/Mok/KMSW classification inputs explicit proof-source owners: ... packets, multiplicities') names the sources 'NEWTON-THORNE, ARTHUR-MOK, EXISTING'. Arthur's GSp(4) announcement [1] and its proof by Gee–Taïbi (J. Éc. polytech. Math. 6, 2019) are not among them. The author version does not cite Gee–Taïbi; searching the reference list for 'Taïbi' finds nothing. The introduction (§1, p. 6) also announces this use: Part IV proves that the Euler characteristic of a non-Eisenstein localisation of M vanishes 'by using results of Arthur on the theory of automorphic forms'. External input: J. Arthur [1], Automorphic representations of GSp(4), in Contributions to Automorphic Forms, Geometry, and Number Theory, Johns Hopkins Univ. Press (2004), classification theorem on p. 78 (an announcement); proved by T. Gee and O. Taïbi, Arthur's multiplicity formula for GSp4 and restriction to Sp4, J. Éc. polytech. Math. 6 (2019)

items.name: The archimedean L-packet {π(λ)^g, π(λ)^h}
items.statement: For λ = (λ1, 0; c) with λ1 < 0, the archimedean L-packet of GSp4(R) containing π(λ)^h is {π(λ)^g, π(λ)^h}.
items.note: Archimedean L-packets of GSp4(R) with a limit-of-discrete-series member are planned nowhere. CG20 marked the same packet {π(λ,C0), π(λ,C1)} missing (ext-mok-archimedean-packet) and routed it to ML.4, and archimedean local Langlands for GSp4(R) is also missing there (ext-sorensen-transfer-infinitesimal-character). External input: D. Blasius, M. Harris, D. Ramakrishnan [4], Duke Math. J. 73 (1994), Prop. 5.3.7

items.name: Packets with archimedean component π(λ)^h are of general, Yoshida or Saito–Kurokawa type
items.statement: Let Π be the global Arthur packet of a discrete automorphic representation π of GSp4(A) with π∞ ≅ π(λ)^h (λ = (λ1, 0; c), λ1 < 0, a non-degenerate limit of discrete series). Then Π is of general, Yoshida or Saito–Kurokawa type.
items.note: This is a case analysis of Arthur's six GSp4 packet types against the archimedean parameter of π(λ)^h. Its input, Arthur's GSp4 classification, is missing, and no stage plans the result. CG20's analogous exclusion of types (b)–(f) (arthur-classes-b-f-excluded) is also missing. External input: R. Schmidt [68], Packet structure and paramodular forms, Trans. AMS 370 (2018), §§1.1–1.2, compared with the archimedean parameters of π(λ)^h in R. Schmidt [67], Archimedean aspects of Siegel modular forms of degree 2, Rocky Mountain J. Math. 47 (2017), p. 11

items.name: Proposition 15.2.4.1: h/g symmetry and multiplicity one for non-Eisenstein πf
items.statement: Let ρ̄ be absolutely irreducible and m as above. Let πf be an admissible irreducible representation of GSp4(A_f) that is unramified at every prime ℓ ∤ Np, and let Θ_{πf} : H^{Np} → Q̄_p be its Hecke character. Assume Θ_{πf} is congruent to Θ_m. Let λ = (λ1, 0; c) ∈ X^*(T) + (2,1;0) with λ1 < 0 (printed: λ1 > 0). Then πf ⊗ π(λ)^h is cuspidal automorphic (equivalently, occurs in the discrete spectrum) if and only if πf ⊗ π(λ)^g is, and in that case the cuspidal multiplicities satisfy m^h(πf) = m^g(πf) = 1.
items.note: This needs Arthur's GSp4 classification, the BHR archimedean packet and Schmidt's packet types (all missing, source ML.4). It also needs reducibility of the Galois representations for Yoshida and Saito–Kurokawa packets, from GL2 forms and characters: R19.1 planned, the packet-level statement missing. It is the same mathematics as CG20's arthur-classes-b-f-excluded, case-a-cuspidal-limit-of-discrete-series and the multiplicity-one part of h1-h0-dimension-equality, which CG20 routed to GSp4NonregularModularityLifting. p. 109 prints 'λ1 > 0' where λ1 < 0 is meant (image checked; the item already records this).

items.name: Specialisation of M_m at weight k is classical Klingen-level ordinary cohomology
items.statement: For every k ≥ 0, in particular for k very large, there are H^{Np}-equivariant quasi-isomorphisms M_{K,m} ⊗^L_{Λ,k} Q_p ≃ fRΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_{Kli}(p), Ω^{(k,2)}(−D))_m ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p ≃ fRΓ(X_{Kli}(p)_K, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D))_m ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p. Their cohomology is concentrated in degrees 0 and 1.
items.note: This combines Theorem 11.3.1(3) with classicality at Klingen level and the H^{Np}-equivariance of both. All of these are the paper's own §§11–13 results (missing, other clusters). Derived base change of perfect complexes is planned (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:P7), and localisation commutes with it (IHG.2).

items.name: Automorphic description of localised ordinary Klingen-level cohomology in large weight: dim fH⁰ = dim fH¹
items.statement: Let ρ̄ be absolutely irreducible and m as above, k ≥ R − 1 and λ = (−k−1, 0; k+4). After extending scalars along Q̄_p ≃ C, f H⁰(X_{Kli}(p)_K, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D))_m ⊗ Q̄_p ≅ ⊕_{πf} f(πf^{K^p Kli(p)}) ≅ f H¹(X_{Kli}(p)_K, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D))_m ⊗ Q̄_p. The sum runs over the irreducible admissible πf of GSp4(A_f) such that πf ⊗ π(λ)^h is cuspidal automorphic and Θ_{πf} : H^{Np} → C is congruent to Θ_m. The projector f acts on πf^{K^p Kli(p)} through πp^{Kli(p)}. In particular the two cohomology groups have the same dimension.
items.note: This applies Corollary 15.2.3.1 and Proposition 15.2.4.1 (missing) at level K^p Kli(p). f acts on π_p^{Kli(p)} through the Klingen U-operators of §5.1.4–5.1.5 (missing, other clusters), and the equality of dimensions follows from m^h = m^g = 1. Klingen-parahoric fixed vectors are local representation theory, SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups (CG20 routed remark-gsp4-parahoric-oldforms there as a source). The ordinary projector formalism is PadicFamilies:L0a.

items.name: Euler characteristic of a perfect complex is invariant under derived base change
items.statement: Let C be a perfect complex over a noetherian ring Λ and φ : Λ → F a ring homomorphism to a field. Then Σ_i (−1)^i dim_F H^i(C ⊗^L_{Λ,φ} F) equals χ(C) evaluated at the point ker φ ∈ Spec Λ. Hence one specialisation determines χ(C) on the connected component of Spec Λ containing ker φ, and χ(C) = 0 as soon as each connected component contains a specialisation whose alternating sum of dimensions is 0.
items.note: Represent C by a bounded complex P of finite projectives. Then C ⊗^L F = P ⊗ F. Tau Ceti's Euler–Poincaré gives Σ(−1)^i dim H^i(P ⊗ F) = Σ(−1)^i dim(P^i ⊗ F), and rankAtStalk_eq and rankAtStalk_baseChange identify this with χ(C) at ker φ. Constancy on components follows from local constancy. The only piece missing from the libraries is perfect complexes (P7; AUDIT-17: absent). The paper uses this step implicitly (§15.2.5, p. 109). External input: Standard commutative algebra (not cited)

items.name: Short exact sequence of complexes relating the Hasse–Witt maps of G and G^D (proof of Lemma 6.3.3.1)
items.statement: Let G be a BT_1 over an F_p-scheme S and 𝓔 = Ext^1_cris(G, O_{S/F_p})_S, with Hodge filtration 0 → ω_G → 𝓔 → ω^∨_{G^D} → 0. As in Fargues [21], p. 915, there is a short exact sequence of complexes, the complexes being the rows: [ω_G →V⋆ ω_G^{(p)}] → [(ω^∨_{G^D})^{(p)} →F⋆ 𝓔 →V⋆ ω_G^{(p)}] → [(ω^∨_{G^D})^{(p)} →F⋆ ω^∨_{G^D}]. Here F⋆: (ω^∨_{G^D})^{(p)} → ω^∨_{G^D} is the dual of the Hasse–Witt map V⋆: ω_{G^D} → ω^{(p)}_{G^D}. The paper takes the long exact cohomology sequence, which implicitly uses that the middle row is exact. This relates the kernel and cokernel of V⋆_G to those of V⋆_{G^D}, so V⋆_{G^D} has rank one when V⋆_G does.
items.note:
Keep, but state it in general form as an external input from Dieudonné theory. Let G be a BT_1 over an F_p-scheme S. Then 𝓔 = Ext^1_cris(G, O_{S/F_p})_S is locally free, with Hodge filtration 0 → ω_G → 𝓔 → ω^∨_{G^D} → 0. The maps F⋆: 𝓔^(p) → 𝓔 and V⋆: 𝓔 → 𝓔^(p) satisfy Ker F⋆ = ω_G^(p) = Im V⋆ and Ker V⋆ = Im F⋆. Hence the three rows of the p. 31 diagram form a short exact sequence of complexes, and its middle row (ω^∨_{G^D})^(p) → 𝓔 → ω_G^(p) is exact. The paper cites only 'As in [21], p. 915'; hasse-witt-rank-one-for-dual lists that source as external. The proof then says 'Taking the long exact sequence in cohomology' (p. 32, image checked), which silently needs the middle row to be exact. With that exactness, Ker F⋆ ≅ Ker V⋆_G and Coker F⋆ ≅ Coker V⋆_G, which gives the rank-one conclusion. I checked on p. 32 (diagram 6.3.A) that F⋆ kills ω_G^(p) and that V⋆ lands in ω_G^(p). No existing item defines 𝓔, although hasse-invariant-Ha-prime-of-Goo, hasse-witt-rank-one-for-dual and maps-VH-W-Z all use it. The same exactness makes Z (Lemma 6.3.3.4 ff.) an isomorphism, as the proof of section-A-regular-vanishing-locus needs.
Library: none. library-coverage says 'p-divisible (Barsotti–Tate) groups do not exist in either library, and neither does Dieudonné theory of finite flat or p-divisible groups'.
Not planned. FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.2 plans 'Dieudonné modules over perfect residue fields ... Include Frobenius/Verschiebung'. CrystallineCohomology:CR.7 exports crystals 'to R07's Dieudonne crystal and Grothendieck–Messing construction'. Neither states the Dieudonné crystal of a BT_1 over an arbitrary F_p-scheme with its Hodge filtration and the exactness of F⋆ and V⋆.

items.name: Fibres of p_1 : X_Kli(p)_1 → X_1 over the p-rank 0 locus (footnote 11)
items.statement: The p-rank 0 locus X_1^{=0} has dimension 1. The map p_1 is bijective over the dense open subscheme of X_1^{=0} of abelian surfaces not isomorphic to a product of supersingular elliptic curves. Over the finite set SS of superspecial points of X_1^{=0} (abelian surfaces isomorphic to a product of supersingular elliptic curves), p_1 is a P^1-fibration. Stated without proof.
items.note:
Footnote 11 (p. 48, image checked) reads: 'The p-rank 0 locus X_1^{=0} is of dimension 1 and the map p_1 is bijective over the dense open subscheme of X_1^{=0} parametrizing abelian surfaces which are not isomorphic to a product of supersingular elliptic curves. On the other hand, the map p_1 is a P^1-fibration over the finite set of superspecial points SS of X_1^{=0}.' It is the only justification the paper gives for 'the p-rank 0 locus has codimension 1' in the proof of Lemma 7.4.2.5. Lemma 7.4.2.5 feeds the Ha′ exact sequences, Proposition 7.4.2.2 and §8. The footnote is stated without proof, but it is correct:
- A p-rank-0 abelian surface A over an algebraically closed field is supersingular.
- Its subgroups of order p are copies of α_p, parametrized by P(Hom(α_p, A)), which has dimension a(A) − 1.
- a(A) = 1 off SS (one subgroup) and a(A) = 2 on SS (a P^1).
The dimension 1 agrees with p-rank-strata-density-dimension (corrected to r + 1). Existing items do not cover this fibre description:
- lemma-7-4-2-5-second-Hasse-nonzerodivisor lists footnote 11 in its locator but does not state it.
- setup-klingen-paramodular-correspondence says only that p_1 is not quasi-finite over X_1^{=0}.
Neither library has the Klingen-level model, p-divisible groups or a-numbers (library-coverage: 'p-divisible (Barsotti–Tate) groups do not exist in either library'). No stage plans the Klingen model; klingen-level-siegel-threefold is missing.

items.name: p_1 is finite flat away from the p-rank 0 locus and the boundary; Ĉ → B̂ is finite flat
items.statement: The map p_1 : X_Kli(p) → X is finite flat away from the p-rank 0 locus and the boundary, so the cohomological correspondence can be base changed to an arbitrary (formal) scheme by §4.2.5. In particular, if Ĉ is the completion of X_Kli(p) along the étale-type component (X_Kli(p)|_{Y_{par,1}^{=1}})^{et} and B̂ the completion along Y_1^{=1}, then p_1 : Ĉ → B̂ is finite flat: B̂ is regular, p_1 is finite (the p-rank 0 locus has been removed) and dominant, and Ĉ is Cohen–Macaulay.
items.locator: §7.4.2, proof of Proposition 7.4.2.1 and footnote 10, p. 46
items.note:
Footnote 10 (p. 46, image checked) reads: 'Since the map p_1 is finite flat away from the p-rank 0 locus and the boundary, it makes sense to base change the cohomological correspondence to an arbitrary (formal) scheme by section 4.2.5.' The proof of Proposition 7.4.2.1 adds: 'the map p_1 is finite flat because B̂ is regular, p_1 is finite (because we removed the p-rank 0 locus) and dominant, and Ĉ is Cohen-Macaulay.' This is the structural input for the local computations in Propositions 7.4.2.1 and 7.4.2.2 and for base-changing the fundamental class (fundamental-class-base-change). setup-klingen-paramodular-correspondence records only the negative half, that p_1 is not finite flat over X_1^{=0} or over the boundary. The positive statement is the Klingen-level analogue of t1-finite-flat-on-abelian-locus (Lemma 10.3.1), which is an item. Proof sketch:
- p_1 is proper, and quasi-finite off X_1^{=0}, because an abelian surface of p-rank ≥ 1 has finitely many subgroups of order p; hence it is finite there.
- Y_K is smooth over Z_p, and Y_Kli(p)K is regular and lci (Proposition 6.1.4.1). Miracle flatness (ext-miracle-flatness) then gives flatness.
Neither library has miracle flatness (library-coverage: 'Neither library has the local criterion for flatness or miracle flatness') or the Klingen model.

items.name: Serre–Tate deformation theorem (lifting with prescribed p-divisible group)
items.statement: For a scheme S on which p is locally nilpotent and a nilpotent thickening S_0 ↪ S, deformations of an abelian scheme A_0/S_0 to S are equivalent to deformations of its p-divisible group A_0[p^∞] (compatibly with polarizations). Passing to the limit, a (principally polarized) abelian surface A over l lifts to Ã over W(l) with any prescribed lift of A[p^∞], here μ_{p^∞} ⊕ E[p^∞] ⊕ Q_p/Z_p.
items.note: This is a distinct external input and is not in the extraction. The existing Serre–Tate items (ext-serre-tate-local-moduli, serre-tate-local-moduli, external-serre-tate-local-computations) are Katz's canonical coordinates at ordinary points. The fixreason of ext-serre-tate-local-moduli already flags this theorem as a different statement, used on p. 47. Checked against the p. 47 image: 'Consider the lift Ã → Spec W(l) with associated Barsotti-Tate group μ_{p^∞} ⊕ E[p^∞] ⊕ Q_p/Z_p'. The paper names no theorem there. The equivalence is planned at AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A4: 'Prove the Serre–Tate equivalence for deformations of abelian schemes with endomorphism and polarization structures; identify its tangent map with the Hodge filtration'. Passing to the limit over W(l) needs algebraization of the formal polarized lift, planned at SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4: 'formal schemes, algebraization ... An algebraized object comes with a comparison to its completion'. Formal GAGA with ample-line-bundle hypotheses is also at AdicSpacesPartII:F0. This matches the routing in PAPER-MAULIK-SHANKAR-TANG-22/8 and PAPER-SHANKAR-SHANKAR-TANG-ETAL-22/27 (A4). Neither library has it: declarations.tsv has no SerreTate declaration, and library-coverage.json says '`SerreTate` has zero occurrences and there is no deformation category of abelian schemes'. The paper also uses, without comment: the splitting A[p^∞] ≅ μ_{p^∞} ⊕ G^{oo} ⊕ Q_p/Z_p over l (ext-oort-zink-splitting, missing); G^{oo} ≅ E_0[p^∞] (Dieudonné classification, FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.2); and a lift of the quasi-polarization.

items.name: Local constancy of dim (M_x)^{=h} for a compact operator (Coleman)
items.statement: Let M be a projective Banach A-module with a compact endomorphism Ũ, and h ∈ Q. Then x ↦ dim (M ⊗̂_A K_x)^{=h} is locally constant on rank one points x of Spa(A,A^+) ([14] Part A). Combined with Σ_i(−1)^i dim H^i(M^•_x)^{=h} = Σ_i(−1)^i dim(M^i_x)^{=h}, this gives Proposition 13.1.3.1.
items.note:
Keep this as an external-input item, with only its first sentence as the statement. The Euler-characteristic step belongs to the proof of Prop. 13.1.3.1.

Source. The paper cites it without a result number. p. 85 reads: 'This follows from the equality Σ_i(−1)^i dim H^i(M^•_x)^{=h} = Σ_i(−1)^i dim(M^i_x)^{=h} and the local constancy of dim(M^i_x)^{=h} (see [14], Part A).' Here [14] is R. Coleman, 'p-adic Banach spaces and families of modular forms', Invent. Math. 127 (1997). prop-13-1-3-1-euler-characteristic-locally-constant mentions it only in its xnote and note. Serre's input already has its own item (serre-slope-decomposition-of-fibres), so this should too.

Why missing:
- Neither library has p-adic Fredholm theory. The TauCeti/Analysis/Fredholm/* declarations are Banach/Hilbert Fredholm-index theory (e.g. ContinuousLinearMap.IsFredholm.adjoint), which is unrelated.
- LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L4 plans 'nuclear/Fredholm determinants in the precise compact-operator setting, slope decompositions, and compatibility with specialization on slope-adapted affinoids'. Its decomposition node L4/finite-slope-summands (from Coleman §A4 and Buzzard Thm 3.3) gives a finite projective summand of rank n from P_φ = QS.
- PadicFamilies:L2a plans 'finite-projective slope summands on adapted affinoids' (nodes strict-slope-neighborhoods and slope-polynomials).
- Together these give local constancy of dim^{≤h} at classical points of a slope-adapted affinoid. No stage or node states local constancy of dim(M ⊗̂_A K_x)^{=h} near a rank-one point of Spa(A,A^+), with neighbourhoods as in footnote 20. That statement also needs the Newton polygon of the slope factor to be locally constant near x. The note of item 454 makes the same point.
